name: Torsdagsløpet
description: The Thursday run in Sarpsborg was a real Easter treat on Maundy Thursday, with glorious weather and a well-deserved break from the long-forecast rain. The run, which takes place on Thursdays until mid-October, offers lovely routes through the extensive network of trails in Kalnesskogen. Although there were a few icy sections, conditions were generally excellent for both runners and organizers.

description: Registration is now open for the second race of the season in the Ålesund Winter Series, which takes place on 28 November. Participants can also register for the entire series until 20 February 2017. The Winter Series began in the mid-1980s in the Furmyra/Åse area, but has had a new course on Gamle Brusdals veg since 2001. From winter 2023, Ålesundløpene will be the organizer of this traditional race.

name: Arborettrimmen 1
description: Arborettrimmen is a wonderful tradition that has been held since Einar Søndeland started it in 1978. It set a participation record in 1983 with 587 participants, including Grete Waitz. The race offers distances for everyone in the beautiful surroundings of the Arboretum, where you can choose to run one (2.7 km), two (5.4 km) or three (8.1 km) laps. A 600 m Mini Run for children starts at 14:00.

name: Kristiansund Backyard Ultra
description: Welcome to Kristiansund Backyard Ultra, a unique endurance race taking place on Saturday, November 15, starting at Frei School. Participants must complete a 6.7 km loop every hour on the hour, and the race continues for 12 hours. If you cannot finish the loop within the hour or do not start the next loop, you are out of the race. This format tests both physical endurance and mental strength, pushing runners to complete “just one more loop.” Everyone who completes at least one loop receives a medal.

The race is suitable for anyone looking for an active and social experience in November.

The races take place during the winter months and provide a great opportunity for both recreational and competitive runners to compete and stay in shape. The event has a long tradition and includes several distances and classes suited to different levels. Participants aged 13 to 80 must have an athletics license, which also serves as insurance.

name: BlåmansLøpene - Etappe 3
description: Blåmansløpene 2026 consists of three spectacular races from Fjellveien to Blåmanen, with the start and finish at the same location, but on different routes featuring trails, nearby mountains and varied running challenges. Stage 3, held on 14 November, follows a demanding, technical course on trails towards Blåmanen, finishing at Tindevann. The race is suited to runners who enjoy challenging terrain and technical sections, and trail shoes are recommended. Varegg IL welcomes everyone to a great running experience in beautiful surroundings in Bergen.

description: Sognefjord Backyard is a unique backyard ultra race held in Sogndal on Saturday, 14 November 2026, starting at 08:00 from Meieriet. The race consists of a 6.7 km loop with approximately 45 metres of elevation gain, run every hour on the hour. Participants have one hour to complete each loop. The competition continues until only one participant remains who has completed one more loop than everyone else. This race challenges both endurance and mental strength, and is suited to runners who want to test themselves in a unique format with no fixed distance.
course_highlights: 6.7 km loop with approximately 45 metres of elevation gain
Start and finish at Meieriet in Sogndal
The course follows pavements and shared pedestrian and cycle paths, in both daylight and darkness
additional: Maximum 100 participants. Minimum age: 18. Start and finish at Meieriet, which also serves as a base with space for drop bags and rest. The café at Meieriet is open for food and drink purchases, but participants must arrange their own provisions. Assistance and provisions are only permitted in the start and finish area. Each participant may have one dedicated support person in the participant area. Registration is binding and non-refundable, but the entry can be transferred to another person via Racetracker. Warnings are given 3 and 1 minute before each start. One winner is declared: the participant who completes one more loop than everyone else; otherwise, there is no winner. Start at Meieriet in Sogndal at 08:00 on Saturday, 14 November 2026. If you cannot complete the loop within the hour, you are out of the race.

It is part of the Sør-Helgeland Running Series (SHLK) and offers runners of all ages and levels a great opportunity to take part in a social and active setting. Participants can enjoy a lovely running experience in the scenic surroundings of Viksjøen.

This race is part of Hvam Runners’ training and racing activities and offers a unique opportunity to test endurance and speed in a controlled indoor environment.

name: Fakkeltoget Løvstakken
description: The Løvstakken Torchlight Procession is an enjoyable mountain hike for all ages, held every year in support of the Norwegian Cancer Society. No particular level of fitness is required, and you’re welcome to come without children. The hike up Løvstakken begins as darkness falls and the city lights become visible. At the summit, there’s a medal ceremony, a barbecue and other fun activities, before everyone lights their torches for the group hike back down. Pizza, mulled wine and gingerbread are served at the finish.

Unlike the summer version, all races follow the same 5-kilometre course on lit pedestrian and cycle paths in the Prestrud area of Hamar. We keep the same officially measured 5-kilometre course for every race, making it an excellent opportunity to use as a test race. Everyone is welcome, whatever their ambitions: walkers (untimed or timed), runners (untimed or timed), those who want to compete with themselves or beat the neighbour, and active super-runners.

The main course is 6.8 km, starting at the Begbyporten clubhouse and passing Bjørneklova, heading down Alleen, going around the golf course, and returning via Bjørneklova. There is also a separate 4.6 km course for those who want to walk or jog. The event takes place every Wednesday at 18:00, and tickets are sold through Strava.com.

description: Østmarka Trail Challenge organizes tough and challenging trail races in Østmarka. This race, taking place on Saturday, August 23, 2025, is not for the faint-hearted, as it features 37 km of technically demanding terrain and nearly 1,000 metres of elevation gain. Participants will experience trails that cross rough, rocky ground, and after many hours of preparation, they will feel ready for this challenge.

name: Hodelyktløpet Østmarka
description: Østmarka Trail Challenge – The Headlamp Race is a technically demanding trail race of approximately 12 km, running mainly on blue- and red-marked trails in Østmarka. The route will be marked all the way by the organizers, but there is definitely a chance of taking a wrong turn, so it is important to pay close attention, especially at trail junctions. A good headlamp is essential! From the start at Skullerud, we follow the Flyktningeruta up to Rundvann, before taking the technically challenging blue trail downhill.

name: Hodelyktløpet i Østmarka
description: The Headlamp Run in Østmarka is a technically demanding trail race of approximately 12 km, mainly following blue- and red-marked trails in Østmarka. The race takes place in the evening, starting at 19:30, and a good headlamp is required to navigate in the dark. Runners face challenging terrain with 400 metres of elevation gain. The race offers a nature experience in beautiful surroundings, with demanding trails. There are no food or drink stations along the route, so runners must bring their own drinks.
course_highlights: Approximately 12 km of technically demanding trail running
The course follows blue- and red-marked trails in Østmarka
400 metres of elevation gain and demanding trails, with a risk of going off course
additional: Race numbers can be collected at Skullerud park between 18:15 and 19:00 on race day. There are good parking options and public transport to the start area. Indoor changing facilities and luggage storage are available. The course is marked throughout, but runners are advised to pay close attention to avoid going off course. There are no food or drink stations during the race, so runners must bring their own drinks. Participation is at your own risk. The start and finish are by the entrance towards Østmarkaporten. Start at 19:30, with space for up to 200 participants.

description: Bislett 24-hour is a unique indoor race held at the famous Bislett Stadium in Oslo. Participants have 24 hours to run as far as possible around the 542-meter track. The event attracts both experienced ultrarunners and beginners who want to test their limits in a supportive and motivating environment. The race is sold out, and prizes include a large achievement medal for those who reach 150 km (men) and 130 km (women).

name: Klubbmesterskap 5k
description: The Club Championship 5K is a running competition that is part of Tjøme Running Club’s events. The courses are officially measured, and the race is run over a distance of 5 km. This championship gives members the opportunity to compete for club championship titles and set club records. The race takes place at the beautiful Grønneset by Ånøya on Wednesday, June 25, with the start from 18:00, and is designed to challenge both beginners and experienced runners.

name: Bergen Cider Marathon
description: Bergen Cider Marathon is a unique race combining running, Bergen and cider for a different kind of marathon experience. The course goes through Fyllingsdalstunnelen, the world’s longest tunnel for pedestrians and cyclists, and continues through beautiful surroundings in Bergen. Half-marathon runners complete one lap, while marathon runners complete two laps and pass through the tunnel four times. After the race, participants are invited to a cider party featuring tastings of different ciders and food inspired by Bergen and Hardanger.

additional: All participants receive a technical running shirt included in the price. There will be no medal, but a certificate can be printed after the race. Refreshments during the race are non-alcoholic, with non-alcoholic cider, water and squash/energy drink. After the race, a separate cider party will be held at Siderbaren, with tastings of at least seven different ciders and food. It requires a separate ticket and has limited capacity. Registration is for the selected distance, and it is possible to transfer your entry to someone else. Start at 09:00. A technical running shirt is included. Aid stations serve non-alcoholic cider, water and squash or energy drink. The cider party at Siderbaren requires separate registration and has limited capacity. Age limit: 18 years.

A children’s race is also held, and no advance registration is required to participate. Race numbers are collected from the race office on race day.

The event is a great opportunity for both experienced and motivated runners seeking a demanding and rewarding racing experience in scenic surroundings.

name: Karmøy Marathon
description: Karmøy Marathon wraps up the running season in the fresh West Norwegian air. The marathon course takes you through three towns, along the coastline on both the east and west sides of Karmøy, with the North Sea as your closest neighbour. This year, IL Trio is strongly represented, with participants in both the full and half marathon, including Emil Solli Stafsnes, who is taking part in his first full marathon. Results will be posted on Trio’s Facebook page as they become available.

Geiteryggen Run 2022 was a success, with as many as 700 people registered, and we’re really looking forward to this year’s race.

The race offers two distances, 5 and 10 km, on officially measured courses heading into Brusdalen, with turnarounds after 2.5 and 5 km. The 5 km distance includes a non-timed recreational class, and there is usually little traffic on Gamle Brusdals veg.

The running group is informal, free and open to everyone.

Marathon runners complete the same loop twice. The course is gently undulating, except for a hilltop at Fana Stadium that runners must go up and down from both sides.

name: Borredalen Rundt – Juleløpet
description: Borredalen Rundt is the Fredrikstad district’s most longstanding recreational race, held since 1962. The race takes place on Tuesday evenings during the April-to-October season. Its approximately 5.5 km course winds around Borredalsdammen through scenic surroundings, along forest trails, rocky terrain and sandy paths. This is an informal weekly event with no entry fee, built on volunteer effort and a sense of community among women and men who enjoy running. Participants register at the start and set off together, keeping their own time.
course_highlights: The course follows forest trails, rocky terrain and sandy paths around Borredalsdammen
An approximately 5.5 km route with varied terrain: trails, rocky terrain, forest paths and gravel roads
Scenic surroundings in the Fredrikstad forest
additional: The race is held every Tuesday during the summer season, with a mass start. Participants register their names at the start and must keep track of their own time and report it to the official recording the times. Volunteers run the event, with a six-week rotation in the race office. The Borredalen Rundt tradition began in 1962.

name: Lierløpet 13
description: Lierløpet is an exciting race series offering different distances for both men and women of all ages. Participants can choose between 5 km, 10 km, and 21.1 km, with age categories for everyone aged 11 and up. The race takes place in scenic surroundings and follows the well-known Linnesrunden, an easy-to-run route suitable for everyone. Prizes are awarded to the top runners, and there are opportunities to set personal records.

Participants can expect a varied and exciting race experience in an active and social setting.

name: Samnanger Romjulshalvmaraton
description: Samnanger Romjulshalvmaraton is held on 27 December 2026, starting at Ådland Church in Samnanger. The race is part of Samnanger IL’s athletics events and welcomes runners of all ages to a traditional activity during the Christmas holidays. The race starts at 11:00 and gives participants a great opportunity to stay in shape during the winter break. Samnanger IL offers a wide range of sporting activities and welcomes everyone to take part.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Ådland Church
A Christmas holiday event in scenic surroundings
Part of Samnanger IL’s athletics programme
additional: The race is part of a wide range of sporting activities at Samnanger IL. Winter series races are also held in Nesodden before and after the Christmas holiday half marathon. The Samnanger IL running group offers group training for all levels, with an accessible option for recreational and experienced runners. The start time is listed as 11:00.

name: Romjulsløpet Jaktstart
description: The Romjulsløpet Pursuit Race has a flexible start in Fjellveien by “Damen” on Tuesday, December 31, between 10:30 and 11:00. The start and finish are in Fjellveien above Varegg’s clubhouse, where you must pick up your timing chip before the start. The course goes from Fjellveien, past BKK’s station, across the field to Permisjonsstien, and down to the water at the top of Munkebotn, with the option of an extra loop up to Stoltzen before returning to the start.

name: Nyttårsløpet i Egersund
description: The New Year's Eve Run in Egersund takes place on 31 December 2026 at Vannbasengene in Egersund. The race offers 1 or 3 laps in a figure-eight, with each lap measuring 1.7 km. There is also a separate children's race, making the event family-friendly and inclusive. The start is at 12:00, and the event runs until approximately 15:00.
course_highlights: The course follows a figure-eight around Vannbasengene
Each lap is 1.7 km long
Choose between 1 or 3 laps
additional: The event runs from 12:00 to 15:00. A separate children's race is also held. The race is organized by Egersunds IK - friidrett. The start time is listed as 12:00 on New Year's Eve.

name: Nyttårsløpet, Fredrikstad
description: The New Year’s Run in Fredrikstad takes place on December 31, 2026, starting and finishing at Stortorvet. The race is suitable for elite athletes, recreational runners, old and young, and offers a fun, inclusive experience for everyone. The course consists of two laps through central Fredrikstad, each 1,600 meters long. There is no entry fee or registration, and the event runs from 12:00 to 15:00.
course_highlights: Two laps through central Fredrikstad, each 1,600 meters long
Start and finish at Stortorvet
Suitable for all ages and abilities
additional: No entry fee or registration required. Tickets are sold via f-b.no. The event runs from 12:00 to 15:00. The 2026 edition starts at 12:00 on December 31. No registration information is provided.

name: Nyttårsløpet Tønsberg
description: The New Year’s Race Tønsberg has been held for many years and is a fun run for absolutely everyone. The atmosphere is relaxed, and the race is a great way to start a new year. Whether you’re in peak shape or looking for a leisurely run on the last day of the year, you’re very welcome.

name: Nyttårstrimmen
description: Nyttårstrimmen is a 10 km recreational race suitable for runners of all abilities. The race has a long tradition and is Norway’s oldest continuously held recreational race, taking place every New Year’s Eve since 1975. This year, we are celebrating Nyttårstrimmen’s 50th anniversary, with hundreds of participants expected in Grenland. Participants can look forward to a varied and enjoyable experience, despite challenges such as snow and weather conditions.

name: Grimstadvatnet Rundt
description: Grimstadvatnet Rundt is part of the Hareid winter series, with race 1 held on a Saturday in November, December, January and February, making 4 races in total. This is a 7.8 km road race, mostly on asphalt, and the course is relatively flat. The first race in the series was held on 5 December 1981, and the 110th race took place in November 2008.

name: Lierløpet
description: Lierløpet is one of Norway’s fastest courses, running along a wide footpath that is popular with runners and recreational exercisers in the Drammen area. The race offers distances of 5 km, 10 km and a half marathon (21 km), and is open to those who want to jog or walk as well as to fit, fast runners. There is also a children’s race, where all participants receive ice cream. Race numbers can be purchased at Lier Station, and the race starts at 12:00.

name: Bjørgene Løpskarusell 4. Løp
description: The athletics group welcomes you to a new running series in Bjørgene on February 4! The snow is gone and the trails in Bjørgene are in good condition. We hope to see you at the starting line!

name: Vinterkarusellen 5. løp
description: The 5th race of Vinterkarusellen was held at Fana Stadium, where the venue was crowded and 515 runners finished the 5 km, while 247 finished the 10 km. Participation increased considerably after the previous winter race, and conditions were good despite brisk winds in some places. Markus Galleberg and Eli Anne Dvergsdal were the fastest in the 5 km, while Andre Lenningsvik and Renate Galleberg won the 10 km. This race is part of Ålesund Vinterkarusell, which consists of 5 races suited to both beginners and experienced runners.

name: Samnanger Vinterkarusell - 3. løp
description: The Samnanger Winter Series is a social and inclusive running series organised by Samnanger IL Athletics. The races take place at Nesodden, with the start and finish in the same place. Participants can choose between 2 km and 5 km distances. The Winter Series is suitable for all levels, whether you want to compete, set a new personal best, maintain your fitness, or simply enjoy a pleasant run with others. Races are held approximately every other Friday throughout the winter, and participants are encouraged to wear reflective gear because of the dark season.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Nesodden
Choice of 2 km and 5 km distances
The 5 km course is officially measured by the Norwegian Athletics Federation (NFIF)
additional: Races are held approximately every other Friday throughout the winter. The running group is beginner-friendly, free, and open to all levels. Wearing a reflective vest is recommended because of the dark season. Samnanger IL Running Group also offers group training every Monday at 18:10 at Hagabotnane. The schedule lists the start time as 18:30. The Winter Series is free; remember your reflective vest.

name: Vinterkarusellen 5. løp
description: The 5th race in Vinterkarusellen was held at Fana Stadium, where it was crowded, and a total of 515 participants completed the 5 km, while 247 took part in the double distance. Participation has increased sharply since the winter race 3 weeks ago, and the running conditions were good despite brisk winds in exposed areas. Markus Galleberg and Eli Anne Dvergsdal were fastest in the 5 km, while Andre Lenningsvik and Renate Galleberg won the 10 km.

name: Polar Night Marathon
description: The Polar Night Marathon is a spectacular race during the blue hour north of the Arctic Circle. Choose from several distances, from 5 km to a full marathon (42.195 km), and experience the magic of the magnificent Arctic landscape. The race takes place in early January, during the polar night, when the sun does not rise above the horizon.

name: Magni Maraton 106
description: Magni Marathon is a popular marathon that attracts participants from various places. The course is known for its beautiful scenery and varied terrain, offering runners a unique experience. Participants can enjoy both challenging hills and flat stretches, making the race exciting for beginners and experienced runners alike.

name: Eikanger Vintarkarusell 4
description: The second race in the 2025–26 winter series takes place on Saturday 15 November at Eikanger. There will be seven races in total this season, with three before Christmas and four after New Year. The course follows the usual route around Eikangervågen, and registration opens from 14:20.

name: Askløpet
description: Askløpet is a long-standing race organized by Ask Friidrett in beautiful surroundings on Askøy in Vestland. The race brings together both local and visiting runners for a friendly and inclusive competition. It is a great opportunity for both recreational runners and competitive athletes to test their fitness early in the year. The event has a long history, and past results are available for those who want to follow previous performances.

name: Nidaros Vinterkarusell: Løp 2
description: Nidaros Winter Running Series is a winter running series organized by Strindheim IL Friidrett at Ranheimshallen. The races take place indoors and include distances such as 3,000 meters for everyone and 1,000 meters for children. The event is open to both young people and adults. Timing is provided by EQTiming, but times are not accepted for records or annual statistics. The series is part of Strindheim’s tradition of offering inclusive athletics events that bring the community together in Trondheim.
course_highlights: Indoor races at Ranheimshallen
3,000 meters for all participants
1,000 meters for children
additional: Timing is provided by EQTiming, but times are not accepted for records or annual statistics. Registration on the day of the event incurs a fee. The event is part of a series with several races in the winter running series.

name: Vinterkarusellen 3. løp
description: The 3rd Vinterkarusellen race offers two distances, 5 and 10 km, on accurately measured courses through Brusdalen. The course turns around after 2.5 km and 5 km, then returns to the start/finish. The 5 km distance has a recreational class without timing. There is usually little car traffic on Gamle Brusdals veg on Sundays, but be aware that cars may be in the area.

name: Snøkuten Nordhagarunden
description: Snøkuten Nordhagarunden takes place on October 17, 2023, and covers a distance of 9.5 km. The race is part of the Snøkuten series and gives participants the opportunity to challenge themselves in beautiful surroundings. The course is quite demanding, but takes you through beautiful scenery, and is suitable for both beginners and experienced runners. This is a popular event on Veldre Friidrett’s calendar.

name: Åsane løpskarusell 2027
description: Åsane Running Series is a recreational running series with weekly 5 km races that start and finish at IKEA in Åsane. The courses are nationally measured and suitable for all levels, led by experienced coaches. The series has a sociable and inclusive atmosphere, and also offers training sessions for those who want to join the running group. Race bibs are collected in the IKEA garage before the races, and family and individual registration are available.
course_highlights: 5 km course measured and certified by NFIF
Start and finish inside IKEA, at the back facing south
The races are held in the evening, with a 19:00 start
additional: Race bibs are collected in the IKEA garage between 18:00 and 18:45. Race bibs must be worn visibly, and the tags must not be folded or damaged. A new race bib costs 100 kr. The races are held in the evening on selected Thursdays throughout the year. Race bibs are collected in the IKEA garage between 18:00 and 18:45.

name: Vinterkarusellen 6.løp
description: The 6th race of the season in the NECON Winter Series took place on January 20, with 721 participants finishing despite torrential rain. A total of 382 runners completed the 5 km, while 169 finished the double distance. Hector Breivik from Ask was the fastest over 5 km with a time of 18:13, while Miriam Emilie Stensland Donovan from Lerøy won the women’s race in 21:31. The 10 km winners were Magne Knudsen (35:48) and Vanja Flatberg (40:26).

name: 5 Km Sport Glexe
description: Sport 1 Glexe is organizing a 10 km race on October 12 at 11:00! The race starts at MSG car wash, heading toward Gvarv from Bø. The course has been officially measured and is a fast route on new walking and cycling paths. It is easy to run, with an unattended drink station after approximately 3.4 km, 6.6 km, and at the finish. Toilets are available at Circle K, but there are no shower facilities.

name: Bislett Spring 5k
description: Bislett Spring 5K takes place at Bislett Stadium and offers a great opportunity to set a personal best over 5 km. The starting groups are divided by target finish time, and each group has a pacer to help you reach your goal. But remember, you still have to do the running!

description: Hagemanns Hill Mile 2027 is a unique last-man-standing race in Drammen where participants run laps of one English mile (1609 metres) in under 20 minutes. The race starts at 10:00 on 16 January and continues with new starts every 20 minutes. Each lap has approximately 80 metres of elevation gain, and medals are awarded to everyone who completes at least one lap. The start and finish are at Svelvik Sports Association’s clubhouse/football pitch at Solbakken, with the option to rest indoors in the changing rooms between laps.
course_highlights: Run 1609-metre laps with approximately 80 metres of elevation gain per lap
Last-man-standing format with a start every 20 minutes
Start and finish at Svelvik Sports Association’s clubhouse/football pitch at Solbakken
additional: A reflective vest is required when it is dark, but the street is lit, so a headlamp is not mandatory. There is an opportunity to heat food and drinks, and blackcurrant cordial will be available. Buying and selling race bibs is also permitted. A minimum of 50 registrations is required by 16 November 2026 for the race to go ahead. Registration is referred to via the event page.

name: Bergen 3000 Indoor
description: Gneist 3000 Indoor is an indoor 3 km race held at Gneist Arena in Bergen. The race consists of 15 laps on a soft, smooth blue athletics track, and participants may wear running shoes or spikes with blunt pins no longer than 6 mm. To ensure evenly matched heats and a smooth event, start times are assigned based on estimated finishing times, and pacers are planned for several heats. The event also includes a separate children’s race, Gneist 400 Kids, for children aged 6 to 12, covering 400 metres. A café with grandstand seating will be open during the event, and race bibs must be collected no later than one hour before the start.
course_highlights: Indoor 3 km race on a blue athletics track
15 laps on a soft surface at Gneist Arena
Choose between running shoes and spikes with blunt pins (maximum 6 mm)
additional: Race bibs must be collected at Gneist Arena no later than one hour before the start. Athletes must report to the Call Room 10–15 minutes before each heat, where their shoes will be checked. Runners will be allowed onto the track when it is ready for the next heat. Warm-ups must take place outdoors, as there is no space to warm up inside the hall. A café with grandstand seating will be open during the event. Access to the competition area is not permitted without a race bib. Warm-ups take place outdoors. Participants should report to the Call Room 10–15 minutes before their heat. A café and grandstand seating are available. Information for the 2027 date has not been confirmed on the organiser’s website.

name: HOKA Solastranden Halvmaraton
description: HOKA Solastranden Half Marathon offers a unique running experience, with distances of 5 km, 10 km, and 21 km. Half-marathon runners should note that course marshals go home after a target time of 2:40, but timing remains open for up to 3 hours. Pacers are also available for all distances, and aid stations serve both water and sports drinks. The race takes place in a scenic area, with alternative parking options nearby.

name: Gneist 3000 Indoor
description: Gneist 3000 Indoor is an indoor 3 km track race held at Gneist Arena. The race consists of 15 laps on a soft, smooth blue track surface. Participants can choose to run in running shoes or spikes with blunt pins no longer than 6 mm. The race uses eq-timing’s timing system with lap times, and heats are organized according to estimated finish times to ensure evenly matched groups. There is also a separate children’s race, Gneist 400 Kids, for children aged 6 to 12, over 400 metres. The first start is scheduled for 17:00, and a café and seating in the stands will be available during the event.
course_highlights: 3 km indoor track race on a blue athletics track surface
15 laps, timed with lap times via eq-timing
Choice of running shoes or spikes with blunt pins (maximum 6 mm)
additional: Race numbers must be collected at Gneist Arena no later than 1 hour before the start. Callroom check-in is 10–15 minutes before each heat, with shoes checked. Runners are let into the hall when it is ready for the next heat. Warm-ups must take place outdoors, as there is no space to warm up inside the hall. Each heat has approximately 15–20 participants, and pacemakers are planned for as many heats as possible. Warm-ups must take place outdoors, and race numbers must be collected at Gneist Arena no later than one hour before the start. Registration requires an estimated finish time. Gneist 400 Kids, a 400-metre race for children aged 6–12, will also be held.

name: Sørlandstesten 5
description: Sørlandstesten is an accessible fun run for everyone looking for a positive running experience, whatever their level of ambition. Whether you’re training for a bigger goal, want to experience the excitement of competition, or simply want a social and active day, this is the race for you! There’s room for both beginners and experienced runners. The start and finish are on the opposite side of the road from Gumpens Auto, along Setesdalsveien in Kristiansand. Participants follow a flat, fast route up Setesdalsveien to Strai, then turn around and run back.

name: Vinterkarusellen Løp 4
description: Vinterkarusellen is an annual running series featuring several distances, with courses officially measured and certified. This means that times achieved in the races will be recognized in statistics for both 5 km and 10 km. Participants have the opportunity to set personal records that will be recognized forever. The series has a rich history dating back to the mid-1980s, and since winter 2023, Ålesundløpene has once again been the organizer.

name: Hamarkarusellen Vinter Løp 4
description: Hamarkarusellen Winter is the winter edition of the new Hamarkarusellen. All races follow the same 5-kilometer course along illuminated walking and cycling paths in the Prestrud area of Hamar. Everyone is welcome, whatever their ambitions—whether you walk or run, with or without a time. There is no registration at the start, and the race offers an excellent opportunity to test your fitness, with 6 races during the winter.

name: Vinterkarusellen Sørlandet
description: Vinterkarusellen Sørlandet is an exciting running race held in Kristiansand. The race covers a distance of 10 kilometres and gives participants the opportunity to experience the beautiful winter landscape of Sørlandet. It is perfect for both recreational and experienced runners who want to challenge themselves in a wintry setting.

name: Bergen Vintermaraton
description: Bergen Winter Marathon will be held for the 5th time on Saturday, January 18, 2025. The start and finish area will be at Fana Stadium. The course is an out-and-back route on paved roads that are either completely free of cars or have very little traffic, and a large part of the route follows a disused railway line through idyllic rural surroundings. Each loop is exactly one half marathon, and the same loop is run twice for the full marathon. The half marathon is one loop, while the marathon is two loops.

description: Frikarusellen is a race organized by Idrettslaget Fri at Espeland sports ground in Arna, Bergen. The race features a certified 5 km course that starts north of Londalskrysset, runs to Gamle Haukeland station and returns along the same route, with the finish inside the sports ground. The event is part of a race series with several dates throughout the winter and early spring. It is a popular recreational race with a friendly atmosphere and enthusiastic participants of all ages.
course_highlights: Certified 5 km course
Start north of Londalskrysset – Gamle Haukeland station – return along the same route
Finish inside Espeland sports ground
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Espelandshallen on race day between 18:00 and 18:55. Registration is open until 18:55 on race day. A license fee is additional for participants over 13 who do not have an annual license. There is a fee of 50 kr for a forgotten race bib for those registered for all the races. Results are published at www.eqtiming.no. The race takes place at Espeland sports ground in Arna. Registration is stated to be via EQ Timing.

name: Søknad Frikarusellen løp nr.4 2027
description: The Frikarusellen is a winter running series organized by Idrettslaget Fri in Arna, with six races throughout the winter and spring. The course is certified as 5 km and runs mainly along a pedestrian and cycle path between Espeland and Gamle Haukeland station, with the start and finish at Espeland sports grounds. The race is suitable for both young people and adults, with separate prices for members and age groups. It is a social and inclusive running series that encourages people to enjoy running together through the winter months.
course_highlights: Certified 5 km course between Espeland and Gamle Haukeland station
The course runs mostly along a pedestrian and cycle path or a lightly trafficked road
Start and finish at Espeland sports grounds
additional: Race numbers can be collected at Espelandshallen on race day between 18:00 and 18:55. Registration is open until 18:55 on race day. A license fee is added for participants over 13 years old who do not have an annual license. A fee of 50 kr applies if participants who registered for all the races forget their race number. Results are published at www.eqtiming.no.

name: Brooks Winterrun Oslo

tiers.label: tier_1

description: Winterrun Oslo 2027 is the big winter running festival, taking place on Saturday, 30 January at Rådhusplassen in Oslo. The race offers a unique atmosphere, with fire baskets, torches and music along the course, as thousands of participants gather for a magical running experience through Oslo’s streets. All participants receive a medal and Vitamin Well at the finish, and great prizes are drawn after the race. This is a feel-good race for anyone who wants to test their fitness or simply have fun in the winter cold.
course_highlights: Run through Oslo’s streets with atmospheric lighting from fire baskets and torches
Start and finish at the beautiful Rådhusplassen
A unique atmosphere with music and marshals providing an extra boost
additional: Race bibs are distributed a few days before the race in the city, but can also be collected in the start area on race day. Bag storage is outdoors and requires a luggage tag. There is a dedicated women’s tent for warming up and changing. Public transport to the start area is recommended due to limited parking. Race bibs can be transferred for a fee of NOK 150 via My Page. The race takes place on winter surfaces. Costumes are encouraged, and prizes are awarded for eye-catching outfits. All participants receive a medal and Vitamin Well at the finish.

name: Necon Vinterkarusellen Bergen - løp 5
description: The Necon Winter Series in Bergen is a winter running series with eight races, where participants can choose between 5 or 10 km. The races start and finish at Fana Stadium, with a start time of 18:45. The series runs on several Mondays from October to April and offers discounts for members of IL Gneist. Registration is individual via EQ-timing, and members of the athletics groups who pay a training fee may participate for free.
course_highlights: 5 km and 10 km races
Start and finish at Fana Stadium
Evening races starting at 18:45
additional: Discounts are available for IL Gneist members, with different codes for free or reduced entry fees. An annual licence is required for participants over 13 and can be selected during registration. Registration is individual via EQ-timing. Participants are responsible for using the correct discount code and paying the correct fee. The series takes place on several Mondays during the winter half of the year. A licence fee of 50 kr may be added if you do not have an annual licence.

name: Necon Vinterkarusell 26-27 løp 5 (1. jan)
description: Necon Vinterkarusell is a winter race series consisting of 8 races held on Mondays throughout the winter, with the start and finish at Fana Stadion in Bergen. Participants can choose between 5 km and 10 km distances. The races start at 18:45, and discounts are available for IL Gneist members. Registration is individual through EQ-timing, with options for both annual-license holders and those without a license.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Fana Stadion
Choice of 5 km and 10 km distances

The course is 5 km long, first officially measured in 2000 and measured again in 2018. It runs from north of the Londalskrysset intersection via Gamle Haukeland station and back along the same route. You can register easily via EQ Timing, and race numbers are collected on race day at Espelandshallen.
course_highlights: 5 km officially measured course
Starts north of the Londalskrysset intersection and returns along the same route
Finish inside Espeland sports ground
additional: Race numbers are collected at Espelandshallen between 18:00 and 18:55 on race day. Registration is open until 18:55 on the same day. A licence fee is added for participants over 13 who do not have an annual licence. There is a fee of NOK 50 for a forgotten race number for those registered for all the races. Results are published at www.eqtiming.no. Registration via EQ Timing is available until 18:55 on race day. A licence fee may be added. Series registration is also available, with separate prices for IL Fri members.

name: Landeveisløp 8km
location: IL Skade Clubhouse, Kåsa, Nome, Telemark, Norway
description: The Lunde Road Race is a traditional 8 km road race organised by IL Skade’s athletics group. It follows the beautiful, flat route alongside the Telemark Canal, starting and finishing at IL Skade’s clubhouse at Kåsa. The race has a long history and has been held more than 50 times, previously as part of the Vinterkarusellen in Telemark. After the race, participants are invited to socialise over cordial, coffee and waffles, followed by an informal prize-giving at the clubhouse, where changing rooms and showers are also available.
course_highlights: Flat route of approximately 7.8 km alongside the Telemark Canal
Start and finish at IL Skade’s clubhouse at Kåsa
More than 50 years of tradition; one of the oldest races in the area
additional: Registration is available on race day at the clubhouse from approximately 11:00 to 12:30, or by SMS to Sveinung Håland (98 62 38 62). Changing rooms and showers are available at the clubhouse. After the race, participants can socialise over cordial, coffee and waffles, followed by an informal prize-giving. Registration on race day is at the clubhouse from approximately 11:00 to 12:30, or by SMS.

name: Vinterkarusellen i Ålesund - 5. løp
description: Ålesund Winter Series is a long-standing race series held over five races during the winter months in Ålesund. The races take place on officially measured courses in Brusdalen, over distances of 5 and 10 km, and start at BestDrive in Fremmerholen. The courses are relatively flat and follow Gamle Brusdals veg, with little traffic on race days. After the race, juice, cola, cake and coffee are served, and medals are awarded to those who take part in three or more races in the series.
course_highlights: Officially measured 5 and 10 km courses in Brusdalen
Relatively flat courses with little traffic on Gamle Brusdals veg
Start and finish at BestDrive in Fremmerholen
additional: The races start at 13:00 for the 10 km and 13:05 for the 5 km. There is a non-timed recreational category over 5 km. Gift prizes are drawn after each race. Medals are awarded to participants who complete three or more races in the series. Juice, cola, cake and coffee are served in the finish area after the race. Registration is through EQ Timing. The 5 km is also available as a non-timed recreational category. Juice, cola, cake and coffee are served in the finish area.

name: Necon Vinterkarusell 26-27 løp 7 (15. mar)
description: Necon Winter Series is a winter running series with 8 races, where participants can choose between 5 or 10 km. The races start and finish at Fana Stadium in Bergen, with a start time of 18:45. The series runs over several Mondays from October to April and offers discounts for IL Gneist members. Registration is individual via EQ-timing, and members of the athletics groups who pay the training fee may participate for free.
course_highlights: Races over 5 km or 10 km
Start and finish at Fana Stadium
Evening races starting at 18:45
additional: Discounts are available for IL Gneist members using various discount codes. Members of the athletics groups who pay the main club membership fee and training fee may participate for free. An annual licence incurs a fee of 50 kr if it has not already been paid. Registration is via EQ-timing with individual sign-up. Registration is individual via EQ-timing. Membership discounts are available for various IL Gneist memberships. The annual licence costs 50 kr if it has not already been registered.

name: Hamarkarusellen vinter Løp 6
description: The Hamarkarusellen Winter Series is a running series for everyone, whether you are an experienced runner, a recreational runner, or simply looking to get outside for some fresh air. The series consists of six races over the winter months, all on the same 5 km course, starting and finishing at Prestrudhallen in Hamar. The races focus on activity, achievement, and socializing, and everyone is welcome regardless of pace—you can run, jog, walk, or combine them. Participants who take part in at least four of the six races receive a finisher’s prize. The event offers a friendly atmosphere, with gingerbread and cordial at the finish.
course_highlights: Six races on the same 5 km course, starting and finishing at Prestrudhallen in Hamar
The course is suitable for running, jogging, and walking
A social and motivating winter series focused on achievement and activity
additional: A finisher’s prize is awarded to everyone who takes part in at least four of the six races. Participants are encouraged to wear a Santa hat, and gingerbread and cordial are served at the finish. The member price applies to members of corporate sports clubs and individual members of the Innlandet Regional Corporate Sports Association. Everyone is welcome, with an accessible format and room for all levels. Registration is available for individual races or the entire series.

name: Åsane løpskarusell 2027 | Løp 4
description: Åsane running series is a recreational running series with weekly 5 km races in Åsane, Bergen, starting and finishing at IKEA. The course is nationally certified, suits all levels, and is led by experienced coaches. The series has a social and inclusive atmosphere and also offers training sessions for those who would like to join the running group. Race numbers are collected on site before the races, and family and individual registration are available.
course_highlights: 5 km course, measured and nationally certified
Start and finish inside IKEA, at the rear facing south
The course was measured and certified by Ivar Andreas Sandø
additional: Race numbers are collected in the IKEA garage between 18:00 and 18:45. Race numbers must be worn visibly and must not be folded or damaged. A replacement race number costs 100 kr. The races take place on Thursdays. Start time: 19:00. Race numbers can be collected in the IKEA garage between 18:00 and 18:45. The start and finish are at the rear of the IKEA building, facing south.

name: Åsane Løpskarusell 2027 Løp 4
description: Åsane Running Series is a recreational running series with weekly 5 km races in Åsane, starting and finishing at IKEA. The course is nationally certified and suitable for all levels, with experienced coaches leading the way. The series has a social and inclusive atmosphere and also offers group training sessions for members. Bibs are collected in IKEA’s car park before the race, and participants can enter individual races or the full series.
course_highlights: 5 km course measured and nationally certified
Start and finish inside IKEA, at the rear on the south side
The course was measured by a certified course measurer on 19.11.2022
additional: Bibs are collected in IKEA’s car park between 18:00 and 18:45. Bibs must be worn visibly, and the tags must not be folded or damaged. Participants can enter individual races or the full series. The race is organized by I.L. Norna-Salhus. Runners use their bib at every race. The prices listed on the information page apply to 2026 and are therefore not included as prices for 2027.

name: Frozen Lake Marathon
description: Frozen Lake Marathon is a unique running event held on the frozen surface of Lake Tisleifjorden in Norway, 819 meters above sea level. Participants run entirely on ice, on a course with the flattest elevation profile in the world, making it an unforgettable experience. The race is limited to 500 participants and offers both a half marathon and a full marathon. The entry includes an official long-sleeved race shirt and a medal for all finishers, with warm soup and bread served after the race. The course is carefully monitored and laid out just days before the race to ensure safety on the ice.
course_highlights: 100% ice surface on Lake Tisleifjorden, with ice about 80 cm thick
The flattest elevation profile in the world
Energy stations at several points, offering sports drinks, water, energy bars, dried fruit, and chocolate
additional: Limited to 500 participants. Transfer is included only for participants staying at Oset Fjellhotell; shuttle service is available at a cost from Storefjell Resort. Parking near the race area is very limited; studded tires are recommended for driving. Bag-drop service is available with a bib tag. Basic changing tents and portaloo toilets are provided. Warm soup with bread is served after the race. Arrival by train to Gol is recommended; the official race hotel is Oset Fjellhotell. The entry includes an official long-sleeved race shirt and a medal, and warm soup with bread is served after the race. Transport is included for participants staying at Oset Fjellhotell; parking near the race area is very limited.

name: 6. Ekeberg Backyard Ultra
description: Ekeberg Backyard Ultra is a classic backyard ultra race held in Oslo’s “central park” at Ekeberg. The race takes place during the dark and cold time of year, giving participants the opportunity to run together with the ultra-running family in beautiful surroundings, with views of Oslo’s skyline and the Oslofjord. The event offers a unique atmosphere with live music, good vibes and facilities such as changing rooms and tents. A maximum of 110 participants can take part, and everyone who completes at least one lap receives a medal.
course_highlights: Run through beautiful scenery with views of the Oslofjord and Oslo’s skyline
The event takes place at Bekkelagshøgda Tennis Club, with access to changing rooms and tents
Live music and good vibes with the ultra-running family
additional: Participants receive a race bib and tracker for automatic live recording of lap times. Drinks, snacks and some hot food are provided. Maximum 110 participants. Everyone who completes at least one lap receives a medal. The race starts at 09:00. Registration opens on 1 December 2026 at 00:01. Participants receive a tracker for lap times, access to the venue and changing rooms, drinks, snacks and hot food. Medals are awarded to everyone who completes at least one lap.

name: Lillestrøms Høyeste Trappeløp
description: Lillestrøm’s Highest Stair Race takes place at Scandic Lillestrøm, with its 12 floors, and offers a real challenge for anyone who wants to test themselves, their friends, family, or colleagues. The race is suitable for all levels and is open to participants aged 13 and over. The event starts at 18:00, with race bibs and timing chips available for collection from 17:00. EMIT timing chips record start time, split time, and finish time, and results are displayed in real time on a large screen on the 2nd floor.
course_highlights: The race goes up 12 floors at Scandic Lillestrøm
EMIT timing chips record start, split, and finish times
Results are displayed in real time on a large screen on the 2nd floor
additional: Race bibs and timing chips can be collected from 17:00. Warm-up is self-directed, outdoors or indoors where space is available. Luggage can be left in a hotel meeting room at your own risk. Toilets are on the 1st and 2nd floors. Using public transport is recommended, as Scandic Lillestrøm is 50 metres from the train station and 150 metres from the bus station. Parking is limited, but commuter parking in the parking garage or at Varemessen (approx. 200 m away) is recommended if arriving by car. Group registration and a single invoice are available for corporate sports clubs and businesses. Timing is done using EMIT chips.

name: Påskekonrad
description: PåskeKonrad is a short race with a mass start from Brunstad, formerly Nærbutikken, in Velledalen. The race is held annually and attracts both locals and experienced veteran runners. Participants can register on race day or in advance via EQ-timing, which helps the organizer with planning. After the race, participants can shower and change at Tandstad School, where an informal gathering is also held. Everyone is warmly welcome to take part in this enjoyable event, whatever their pace.
course_highlights: Mass start from Brunstad, by the former Nærbutikken
A short race with variable weather conditions, often rain and wind
Showers and an after-race gathering at Tandstad School
additional: Registration is available on race day from 09:00 and in advance via EQ-timing. After the race, showers and dry clothes are available at Tandstad School, where a small gathering is also held. Weather conditions can vary, with rain, wind, and snow later in the day. Registration can be done on race day or in advance via EQ-timing. There is a simple after-race get-together at Tandstad School.

name: Sandtangstafetten
description: Sandtangstafetten is a traditional relay held at Sandtangen in Bryne. The race has four legs on varied surfaces, including forest floor, gravel and grass, and offers both a short and a long course for different age groups, from age 7 to seniors. The event starts in the evening and lasts approximately one hour and fifteen minutes, with a focus on team spirit and a great atmosphere. It is a family-friendly race, with many mixed teams as well as all-girls and all-boys teams competing in different categories.
course_highlights: Short course for ages 7–10, with 110 m legs on forest floor, gravel and grass
Long course for ages 11 and older, with 370 m and 420 m legs on varied surfaces
Four legs per relay team, with changeovers at Sandtangen
additional: Start times for the different categories are from 18:00 to 18:36. Participants are advised to arrive 45 minutes before the start for a course and changeover briefing. Parking is available at Vianor Bryne (north) and Storstova (south). Registration is available via a link or by emailing pamelding@brynefriidrett.no. Parking at Vianor Bryne or Storstova.

name: GIF-Joggen Backyard Ultra

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Påmelding skjer ved at du Vippser kr 150 til #609846 med info om navn, klubb/lag.

description: GIF-Joggen Backyard Ultra takes place in Gressvikmarka, starting Saturday, April 3 at 08:00. The race consists of up to 12 laps on a 6.7 km course through varied and challenging terrain. Participants run one lap every hour and continue for as long as they can, aiming to complete as many laps as possible or all 12. All participants receive a medal, and those who complete every lap can log over 80 km in their training diary. Facilities include a heated shelter, toilets, changing rooms, and some fruit and baked goods.
course_highlights: A 6.7 km course through varied terrain
Up to 12 laps, with over 80 km for those who complete them all
The course is marked with red and white ribbons
additional: Check-in and registration from 07:00 on race day. To continue, participants must be ready for the next lap at the top of each hour. A heated shelter, toilets, and changing rooms are available. Bring a change of clothes, drinks, food, and possibly a headlamp. The course may be wet and muddy; a camping chair is recommended for the break area. The previous edition had a maximum of 77 participants. The race started at 08:00, and runners had to be ready at the start at the top of each hour to continue. A heated shelter, toilets, and changing rooms were available. Sources give conflicting information about the date in 2027.

name: Holmestrand maraton
description: Holmestrand Marathon is a friendly running event that has been a regular fixture on the race calendar since 2013. The race is held every year on the Saturday after Easter and offers beautiful, easy-to-run courses along the Holmestrand Fjord and through the city’s charming streets. Distances are available for all levels, from 5 km to the marathon, and the course has been officially measured and internationally approved by World Athletics. The event is suitable for both beginners and experienced runners, and also includes a free children’s race called Miniton.
course_highlights: Easy-to-run, personal-best-friendly 5 km loop course
Course along the Holmestrand Fjord and through the city streets
Officially measured and internationally approved by World Athletics
additional: All children can take part in the free Miniton children’s race. The race offers the option to run with or without a time. There are food and drink stations, prizes, and opportunities to follow the race along the course. The race is held every year on the Saturday after Easter. Distances: 5 km, 10 km, half marathon, marathon, and the free Miniton for children. For the 5 km, you can choose to run with or without a time. The event also offers the combinations marathon + 10 km and half marathon + 5 km.

name: Drammen 10K
description: Drammen10K is Norway’s fastest 10-kilometer race, taking runners through downtown Drammen on a fast course with only 22 meters of elevation gain. The race is for everyone looking for a fast and enjoyable running experience in an urban setting. The event has an inclusive atmosphere and also offers fun digital competitions beforehand. Welcome to a great race weekend in Drammen!
course_highlights: Norway’s fastest 10K race
Fast course with only 22 meters of elevation gain
The race takes place in downtown Drammen
additional: Green race bibs indicate that a medal was purchased in advance. Children’s races are also held on the same day, including Minimila. There is no telephone contact; all communication takes place via email and the contact form. A digital triathlon with prizes and a live announcement on social media is held beforehand. Transferring a race bib or changing the participant costs 100 NOK.

name: Bergen Ultra - Maratonkarusellen
organizer: Maratonkarusellen i samarbeid med BFG Bergen Løpeklubb

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Prisene øker med kr 50,- to uker før løpsdagen

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Prisene øker med kr 50,- to uker før løpsdagen

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Prisene øker med kr 50,- to uker før løpsdagen

description: Bergen Ultra is a challenging ultramarathon organized by Maratonkarusellen in collaboration with BFG Bergen Løpeklubb. The event offers distances of 63.3 km and 100 km, as well as a half marathon and marathon, and takes place at Fana Stadium in Bergen. Maratonkarusellen places great emphasis on quality and participant enjoyment, despite the event’s tough challenges. The minimum age is 18, and the race is part of a series of long-distance events held in both spring and autumn.
course_highlights: Ultramarathon distances of 63.3 km and 100 km
Organized in collaboration with BFG Bergen Løpeklubb
The races start and take place at Fana Stadium in Bergen
additional: Kondis members receive a NOK 50 discount. A year-round license from the Norwegian Athletics Federation can be provided by giving the license number, and a one-time license does not need to be paid for. Prices increase by NOK 50 two weeks before race day, by a further NOK 50 four days before, and the price on race day is NOK 650. The minimum age for the marathon is 18. The start and finish are at Fana Stadium. The half marathon is one lap, the marathon two laps, and the 63 km race three laps. The listed start times are 09:00 for 63 km, 10:00 for the marathon, and 11:00 for the half marathon. The prices and race details apply to the published 2026 edition; information for 3 April 2027 is not provided in the sources.

name: Solsiå sentrumsløp
description: Solsiå Sentrumsløp 2027 takes place in Sandnes city centre and features a circuit where participants choose how many laps to complete within six hours. There is also a separate children’s race of approximately 600 metres in Langgata. The race has an informal, inclusive character, focusing on local runners and safe preparation. Registration and payment are handled directly by the organiser, not through Førstart.
course_highlights: A 3 km circuit in Sandnes city centre
Choose how many laps to complete within six hours
A separate children’s race of approximately 600 metres in Langgata
additional: The children’s race starts at 11:30, and the circuit race starts at 12:00. Registration and payment are handled by the organiser, not through Førstart. Limited practical information about the race is available on Førstart. Feel free to invite others to the starting line. The circuit race starts at 12:00, and the children’s race starts at 11:30. Registration and payment are handled by the organiser.

name: Fredrikstadløpet
description: The Fredrikstadløpet is held in Gamlebyen in Fredrikstad, with the start and finish at Kongstenhallen. The event offers distances of 3 km for children and youth, 5 km, and a 21 km half marathon. All courses are on asphalt and are flat, with no elevation changes. The half-marathon course consists of three identical laps of approximately 7 km each, and the courses have been officially measured by a nationally approved course measurer. The event has international status and is a quality race, with course marshals at every intersection for safety.
course_highlights: Asphalt surface, except for a little gravel in the start and finish area
Flat courses with no elevation changes or sharp turns
The half marathon is run as three identical 7 km laps, with two pedestrian underpasses
additional: The start and finish area is behind Kongstenhallen. The children’s race is approximately 500 m and takes place near the start/finish area for the other distances. The course crosses busy roads in a few places, but course marshals are stationed at every intersection. Kondis members receive a discount on the entry fee. Registration for 2027 opens in September. The start and finish area, race office, and changing rooms are at Installatøren Arena, Torsnesveien 12, Gamle Fredrikstad. The course crosses busy roads in some places, with course marshals at the intersections.

name: Norgestesten 2027 1
description: Norgestesten is an efficient and simple running event held in Jessheim, with a mass start for all distances. The course is a flat 3,146-meter loop, suitable for both beginners and experienced runners. Distances range from an 800-meter children’s race to a half marathon, with pacers to help participants maintain the right pace. The event is run by volunteers, and any surplus goes to sports for children and young people.
course_highlights: Flat 3,146-meter loop
Mass start for all distances
Pacers at several speeds, from 4:00 to 7:00 min/km
additional: The children’s race starts at 09:30 and is approximately 800 m long. Bib pickup is self-service from 09:00. Toilets are available at Jessheim Athletics Stadium and in the ice and multipurpose hall. A table for participants’ own drinks is available at the start, and water and sports drinks are provided along the course. The half marathon has a cut-off time of 2 hours and 30 minutes. The race is listed as WA-approved. Train services and parking are approximately 300 meters from the start area.

name: Fløibanen Opp

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: 650 kr for åpen gruppe eller seedet gruppe

description: Fløibanen Opp is Bergen’s most spectacular uphill race, held annually. Participants run up to Fløyen along the Fløibanen tracks. The race is open to everyone, from children and recreational runners to elite athletes, and offers a unique experience with an 820-metre course and 310 metres of elevation gain. After the finish, a celebration awaits at the top, with music, medals, T-shirts, refreshments and an awards ceremony. The event brings the joy of sport to the heart of Bergen and offers a great opportunity to challenge yourself on a spectacular uphill course.
course_highlights: An 820-metre course with 310 metres of elevation gain
Steepest section has a 26-degree incline
Run along the Fløibanen tracks up to Fløyen
additional: Race bibs are collected before the start at the entrance to Fløibanen. Participants receive an email with their exact start time and important information closer to race day. After the finish, there is a celebration at the top with music, medals, T-shirts, refreshments and an awards ceremony. Companies can receive a discount code for free employee registration and take part in the Afterrun at ToppFløyen with their own teams. Information about start times, prices and participant benefits applies to the 2026 event and has not been confirmed for 2027. In 2026, the open class started at 18:25; race bibs were collected at the entrance to Fløibanen, and everyone received a medal and a T-shirt.

name: Voss Løpskarusell 1
description: Voss Running Series is a running series for everyone, with races on Mondays at 19:00 in 2027. The course is 5 km long, starting and finishing at the sports grounds in Voss, and runs through Prestegardsmoen and along the waterfront promenade. You can register for individual races or all six races together, with a discount for early registration. This is a friendly recreational race that welcomes both joggers and runners aged 9 and up.
course_highlights: 5 km course starting and finishing at the sports grounds
Loop through Prestegardsmoen
Run along the waterfront promenade
additional: The races take place on Mondays, starting at 19:00, except for the fifth race on 20 September, which starts at 18:30. Registration is online only via eqtiming. A discount is available when registering for all six races by the second race. Registration for all six races opens on 15 November 2026 and closes on 3 May 2027. Registration is online via EQ Timing. You can register for individual races or all six races in the series; the discount applies when registering for all six by the second race.

name: Voss Løpskarusell 2027, alle løp
description: Voss Running Series 2027 is a running series for everyone, with races on Mondays at 19:00. The course is 5 km long and runs from Voss Sports Ground through Prestegardsmoen and along the promenade back to the sports ground. The series welcomes recreational runners and runners aged 9 and up to enjoyable fun runs throughout the season. Registration is online, and a discount is offered when registering for all six races by the second race.
course_highlights: 5 km course starting and finishing at Voss Sports Ground
Route through Prestegardsmoen and along the promenade
Races are held on Mondays, starting at 19:00, except for the fifth race, which starts at 18:30
additional: Registration for all six races opens on 15 November 2026 and closes on 3 May 2027. A discount is available when registering for all six races by the second race. The fifth race, on 20 September, starts at 18:30 instead of 19:00. Races usually take place on Mondays, starting at 19:00. Registration is via EQ Timing. A discount is available when registering for all the races by the second race.

name: Vårdilten 2027

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Alle andre må ut med 200 kr for å delta på Vårdilten

description: Vårdilten is a traditional race held annually in Ålesund, formerly known as Teledilten. The race starts at Rattviksvingen in Gåseid and follows a 4.27 km route along sidewalks and gravel roads, including a challenging hill on the grounds of Sunnmøre Museum. Vårdilten is a popular spring event with both competitive and recreational categories, and prizes are awarded to the fastest man and woman after the race.
course_highlights: The route follows well-marked sidewalks and gravel roads
Includes a steep hill halfway through on the grounds of Sunnmøre Museum
Total distance of 4.27 km
additional: The race starts at Rattviksvingen in Gåseid, with ample parking at the start and across the road at Rema. After the race, trophies are awarded to the fastest man and woman, along with gift prizes. The race has a long tradition and has previously served as a local qualifier for the Holmenkollstafetten. Start: Wednesday, April 7, 2027, at 18:00. Registration through EQ Timing. Parking at the start and at Rema. Trophies for the fastest man and woman, as well as raffle prizes.

name: Terrengløpskarusellen 2027 løp 1
description: The cross-country running series is an annual event organised by Haugesund Idrettslag in Haraldsvang Nature Park. The races follow gravel and forest trails, starting and finishing by the stage/pavilion in Haraldsvang. The series is popular with both children and adults, with a focus on the joy of sport and achievement on varied terrain. Results are published continuously on EQ Timing, and prizes are awarded after the final race.
course_highlights: The routes are mostly on gravel paths, with approximately 200 metres of forest-surface terrain per lap
Start and finish by the stage/pavilion in Haraldsvang Nature Park
Varied terrain with both gravel and forest trails
additional: Race numbers are handed out by class at the stage in Haraldsvang and must be used for all three races in the series. A group warm-up for the youngest participants starts at 17:30. Results are published live on EQ Timing. Prizes are awarded immediately after the final race on the stage in Haraldsvang. The 2026 edition consisted of three races, and the same race number was used throughout the series.

name: HTB Valestrandsmarka Rundt 1. løp
description: HTB Valestrandsmarka Rundt is a traditional fun run organized by Osterøy IL Friidrett. The race takes place in Valestrandsmarka over a distance of 4.4 km, starting from Furubakken sports ground in Valestrandsfossen. Several races are held during the season, with start times of 18:45 for walkers and 19:00 for the main field. Participants can enjoy a scenic course and a great atmosphere, with prizes and svele pancakes served after the race. The event has a long history, with extensive statistics and records available to participants.
course_highlights: 4.4 km course in Valestrandsmarka
Starts at Furubakken sports ground, Valestrandsfossen
Start times: 18:45 (walkers) and 19:00 (main field)
additional: Course records earn a prize of kr. 3,000 from HTB. Svele pancakes from Toro and cordial from Saftsuse are served after the race. Registration is at the venue, at Furubakken sports ground, until the start. No race license is required, and payment can be made via Vipps to 121337. Christmas and New Year's races are also held, with their own start times. Registration is open until the start. Previous races have started at 18:45 and 19:00; times may differ for the 2027 race.

name: Tunnelløpet
organizer: BFG Bergen løpeklubb og Fyllingen Friidrett
description: Tunnelløpet is a fast 5 km road race that starts and finishes at the entrance to the tunnel on the Fyllingsdalen side in Bergen. The race runs partly on asphalt and partly on a royal-blue rubber surface inside the tunnel, providing stable, ideal running conditions without wind or rain, at a temperature of around 11–12 degrees year-round. The race is World Athletics-approved and attracts runners looking to set personal records. Children’s races are also held, with free entry and wave starts to ensure a good race experience for everyone.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the tunnel entrance on the Fyllingsdalen side
Run on asphalt on the way out and a royal-blue rubber surface on the way back through the tunnel
Stable conditions of around 11–12 degrees, with no wind or rain
additional: Wave starts are based on estimated finishing time, with around one minute between each wave. Children’s race distances are 400 metres for ages 3–5 and 1,500 metres for ages 6–10. Entry is free, but registration is mandatory. Race bibs are distributed the evening before the race at Oasen Senter. Race bib transfers are handled through Eq-timing for a fee. The main race has wave starts based on estimated finishing time. The children’s race is free but requires registration. Registration for the 2027 edition will open later in 2026.

name: TUNNELLØPET BERGEN 5 KM 2027
location: Fyllingsdalen tunnel entrance near Oasen, Bergen, Norway
organizer: BFG Bergen løpeklubb og Fyllingen Friidrett
description: Tunnelløpet 5 km is a fast road race that starts and finishes at the tunnel entrance on the Fyllingsdalen side in Bergen. The race runs partly on asphalt and partly on a royal-blue rubber surface inside a 3 km long pedestrian and cycling tunnel, providing stable, wind-free conditions and a temperature of around 11–12 degrees. With a drop of approximately 17 metres from the start to the turnaround, the course is ideal for fast times and personal records. The race is World Athletics-approved and has been held since 2023 in connection with the opening of the tunnel.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the tunnel entrance on the Fyllingsdalen side
Run on asphalt on the way out and a royal-blue rubber surface on the way back through the tunnel
Wind-free, stable temperatures of around 11–12 degrees
additional: Wave starts are used, with approximately one minute between each wave based on expected finishing time to ensure a good race experience. Race bibs are distributed the evening before the race at Oasen Senter. A children's race is held with free registration and a medal for everyone, with distances from 400 metres to 1500 metres. Registration for the 2027 edition is expected to open later in 2026. Race bibs are distributed at Oasen on Thursday and Friday evening before the race. There is also a free children's race with registration.

name: Velledalen Frontyard Ultra
location: Velledalen, Sykkylven, Møre og Romsdal, Norway

name: Atlanterhavsløpet
description: Atlanterhavsløpet is organized by Idrettslaget Bryn and is a long-standing race in Averøy, Møre og Romsdal. Registration takes place at the race office in Kårvåg, with payment available in cash, via Vipps, or by payment card. The race has competition, recreational, and fitness classes with different registration times. It offers a social, inclusive running experience with strong local roots.
course_highlights: The course runs across the Atlantic Ocean Road.
The coastal landscape and exposed location make the weather and wind part of the race experience.
The race takes place in Averøy, Møre og Romsdal.
additional: Registration and payment for the competition and recreational classes take place at the race office in Kårvåg half an hour before the start. Registration and payment for the fitness class are available between 10:00 and 12:30. Payment methods: cash, Vipps, and payment card.

name: Trioløpet
description: Trioløpet is being held for the first time on Saturday, 11 April 2027, by IL Trio friidrett. The race offers several categories to include as many participants as possible, including a timed 5 km course starting at Husnes Stadium and running through the town centre and around the church. There is also an untimed 3–4 km fun run along Opsangervatnet, as well as children’s races and accessible options with adapted distances at or around Husnes Stadium. The event aims to become a community celebration on a par with the former Søralløpet.
course_highlights: Measured, flat 5 km course from Husnes Stadium through the town centre and around the church
3–4 km fun-run category along Opsangervatnet
Children’s races and accessible options at or around Husnes Stadium
additional: The race takes place at Husnes Stadium and includes both competitive and fun-run categories. The fun-run course is suitable for walking or jogging. The event aims to create a community celebration and also includes children’s races and accessible options. The available information concerns the first edition on 11 April 2026 and does not confirm details for 2027. In 2026, participants in the 5 km race category registered in advance via EQTiming, while the other categories had registration at the stadium on race day.

name: H3 Hamar Vårløp
description: H3 Hamar Spring Run is an inclusive running celebration in Hamar, inviting everyone, regardless of ability, to take part in the 5 km or 10 km race. The course is mainly on asphalt and gravel, and is almost flat, making it ideal for personal bests. The start and finish are at Skibladner Pier, and the event offers a great atmosphere along Lake Mjøsa. Prizes are also awarded to the fastest runners, with prize draws for participants.
course_highlights: A flat, fast race on asphalt and gravel
Start and finish at Skibladner Pier in Hamar
The course has approximately 44 metres of elevation gain and is ideal for personal bests
additional: Race number collection and late registration take place at Skibladner Pier before the start. Race numbers can also be collected at Sport1 CC-Stadion on the Saturday before the race. The race office and baggage drop are by the pier. Showers and changing rooms are available at Esper’n Activity Park, which also has parking. H3 Hamar lists 11 April 2027 as the event date. In previous years, the race has had one 5 km lap and two 10 km laps.

name: Necon Vinterkarusell 26-27 løp 8 (12. apr)
description: Necon Vinterkarusell is a winter race series consisting of 8 races, where participants can choose between 5 or 10 km. The races start and finish at Fana Stadion in Bergen, with a start time of 18:45. The series runs on several Mondays from October to April and offers discounts for IL Gneist members. Registration is individual via EQ-timing, and participants can run the entire series or individual races.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Fana Stadion
Choice of 5 km or 10 km distances
Evening races starting at 18:45
additional: Discounts for IL Gneist members: free for athletics members who pay the main club fee and training fee (code Gneist00), 50% off for Gneist trim (code Gneist50), and 25% off for other Gneist groups (code Gneist25). Participants over 13 must select an annual license when registering; otherwise, a license fee of 50 kr applies. Registration is individual via EQ-timing. The date has been changed from 5 April to 12 April.

name: Vestfold løpskarusell - 1. løp - Revetal
price_range: Sesongkort: 900–1 200 kr før 31.12.2026; 960–1 260 kr etter denne datoen

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: 1200 kr. for ikke medlemmer frem til 31.12.26.

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: 1200 kr. for ikke medlemmer frem til 31.12.26.

description: Vestfold Running Series 2027 is a running series consisting of 8 races in the Tønsberg region, starting at 18:00, with two distances at each race. The series offers the joy of running, a sense of community and a great atmosphere for all levels, whether you want to set a personal best or simply be social and active. The races take place in beautiful surroundings, with electronic timing by EQ Timing. You can enter individual races or buy a season pass for all races at a discounted price.
course_highlights: Two distances at each race, ranging from approximately 2.3 km to 6.9 km depending on the location
Races in beautiful surroundings in the Tønsberg region, including Essoskogen, Tønsbergmarka, Vear, Teieskogen and Revetal
Start and finish at central locations such as the Sport1 store in Revetal, the Essoskogen car park and the playground at Teie school
additional: Season-pass participants collect their race number at the first race, while participants in individual races collect theirs from the race office 10 minutes before the start. Race numbers must be kept for the entire series. Electronic timing by EQ Timing. Course descriptions and profiles are available in the Facebook group and are sent out when registering for the season. Season registration and registration for individual races are available. Season-pass participants collect their race number at the first race and use it throughout the series; race numbers for individual races are collected and returned at each race.

name: Ålgårdstafetten
