description: The Ålgårdstafetten is an annual relay organized by Gjesdal Idrettslag, bringing together recreational and elite athletics in the Gjesdal municipality. The event takes place at the athletics stadium in Ålgård, with baton exchanges at the stadium or in the immediate vicinity. The surfaces include Tartan track, asphalt and gravel. There are categories for children, youth and adults, including senior, veteran and corporate teams. The event promotes the joy of sport and community spirit, with a varied course network suited to different age groups and ability levels.
course_highlights: Baton exchanges take place at the athletics stadium or in nearby areas
Surfaces include Tartan track, asphalt and gravel
Several categories have 4 or 6 legs for different age groups and ability levels
additional: The entry fee doubles for late registration. Participants aged 13 and older need an annual licence or a one-time licence. Spiked shoes are not recommended because parts of the course are on asphalt. Categories include mixed teams aged 7–8, age-group categories for boys and girls, and senior, veteran and corporate categories for the 6-leg relay. The 2026 edition listed categories for children, youth, senior, veteran and corporate teams. Spiked shoes are not recommended. The date 15 April 2027 has not been confirmed in the available event information.

name: Sandnes Ultratrail
description: Sandnes Ultratrail is a challenging trail race in the Sandnes Alps, with distances from 10 km to 100 miles. The routes offer varied scenery, including mountains with beautiful fjord views and technically demanding trails. The longest distance climbs 28 mountains and peaks, and runners can enjoy several swimming spots along the way. After the finish, Jæder burgers are served in a social and inclusive atmosphere with a bonfire and cheering.
course_highlights: Technically demanding routes, with 28 mountains and peaks on the 100-mile distance
Varied scenery featuring mountains, fjord views and quiet forest trails
Opportunities to swim in several lakes along the routes
additional: Mandatory equipment for the 50- and 100-mile distances includes two headlamps, a GPS file, a mobile phone, a power bank, hydration containers, an emergency blanket and first-aid equipment. The start and finish for the 100 miles are at Alsvik Nature Centre. There are several aid stations along the way, staffed by experienced volunteers. Buses to the start are arranged for the 50-mile and shorter distances. After the finish, burgers are served and there is a social gathering around a bonfire. In 2027, the 100-mile race starts on Friday, 16 April, from Alsvik Nature Centre; the other distances start on 17 or 18 April. The programme mentions, among other things, race-bib and tracker collection, drop bags and shuttle buses.

name: Backyard Ultra Ålesund
description: Backyard Ultra Ålesund is a unique ultrarunning event organized in cooperation with SIF/Hessa IL, where participants run a 6.7 km loop every hour. The race tests endurance and willpower, and continues as long as runners can complete a loop within 60 minutes. The start and finish are at Skarbøvik Stadium, and the route offers beautiful views around Sukkertoppen. Participants have access to base areas for resting and refuelling between loops, with facilities such as tent pitches, toilets and basic refreshments.
course_highlights: The route is 6.7 km long and goes around Sukkertoppen, starting and finishing at Skarbøvik Stadium
Each loop starts on the hour and must be completed within 60 minutes
The base area offers places to rest, eat, drink and warm up in SIF-huset
additional: The maximum number of loops is 12, for a maximum distance of 80.5 km. Bib collection and parking times will be announced later. Toilets and changing rooms with showers are available in the changing-room building, as well as five toilets in SIF-huset. Basic refreshments including squash, cola, bananas, crisps and sweets are available from 10:30. Participants are encouraged to bring their own food and drink. Parking opens at 08:45, and participants may pitch a tent or use a car or motorhome as a base in the area around the start/finish. The start and finish are at Skarbøvik Stadium. The information in the sources relates to the 19 September 2026 edition; it does not confirm event details for 17 April 2027.

name: Bergen 5000 Challenge
price_range: 5000 meter: 250 kr; 1000 meter kids: 100 kr; 300 meter mini: gratis
description: Bergen 5000 Challenge is a fast and social 5,000-metre race held at Fana Stadium in Bergen. The race consists of 12.5 laps on a track with no uphill sections and is suitable for both recreational and more experienced runners. There are several heats with pacers for different target times, and children’s races are also held for the youngest participants. Admission is free for spectators, and all participants receive a medal.
course_highlights: 12.5 laps at Fana Stadium with no uphill sections
Pacers in several heats for different target times
Certified road-race results with EQ timing
additional: Race numbers are collected in the gym at Fana Stadium on race day. Admission is free for spectators. All participants receive a medal. The recreational race is classified as a road race with certified results. There are several heats with pacers for different target times. Children’s races are held for ages 3–6 and 6–12. All finishers receive a medal, and admission is free for spectators. The organizer’s website states that the new date for 2027 will be announced, so the date of 17 April 2027 has not been confirmed there.

name: Haugesund Backyard Ultra
description: Welcome to Haugesund Backyard Ultra 2027, a unique and social ultrarunning event held at Haraldsvang Arena in Haugesund. The race is not about running the fastest, but about lasting as long as possible, with a new lap of approximately 6.7 km starting every hour on the hour. Participants can rest between laps if they finish within the hour, and the winner is decided after the final lap. With new, modern facilities at Haraldsvang Arena, the experience will be even better for both runners and supporters.
course_highlights: The course is easy to run and gently rolling, with a mix of asphalt and gravel
Start and finish outside the new Haraldsvang Arena
Each lap is approximately 6.7 km and starts every hour on the hour
additional: All participants start at the same time. You must be ready at the starting line for each new start. There are improved facilities and more social gathering areas around the arena compared with previous years. The race sold out in 2026, so early registration is recommended. Participants can stop whenever they wish. Registering early gives you a lower price.

name: Nidaros Vinterkarusell: Løp 4 / Trønderjogg
description: Nidaros Vinterkarusell and Trønderjogg are long-standing running events in Trondheim, organized by Strindheim IL Friidrett. The races offer distances for all levels, from children’s races to a 10 km road race, creating an inclusive and social running experience. Trønderjogg marks the start of the running season with a great atmosphere at Trondheim Stadium, while the winter series provides regular running goals throughout the winter. The club has a long history and a strong community for both recreational and elite runners.
course_highlights: Trønderjogg: 5 km and 10 km road races at Trondheim Stadium
Nidaros Vinterkarusell: Races at Ranheimshallen, including a 3,000 m race and children’s races
Obstacle course for children aged 6 and under during Trønderjogg
additional: Trønderjogg starts at 18:00 at Trondheim Stadium. There is an obstacle course for children aged 6 and under, with a prize for everyone. Registration before the start is from 17:30. Nidaros Vinterkarusell races are held at Ranheimshallen, with timing via EQTiming, but times are not approved for records or annual statistics. Prizes go to the 3 fastest women and men in the 5 km and 10 km races at Trønderjogg. There are many prize draws among all participants.

name: Oslo Løpsfestival, 5'ern vår!

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Dagsbillett SOLO Deltakere kr 475,00 kr 332,50 + Adm. gebyr (25 NOK + 3%) -30%

description: Our 5K! is the first race in Oslo Running Festival and offers a fast, flat 5-kilometer course along the beautiful Oslofjord, from Frognerkilen to Bygdøylokket. You can complete the race at any time between April 9 and 18, or join the group start on Sunday, April 18 at 11:00, with pacers, music, and a great atmosphere. This race is a great way to kick off the running season in Oslo and is suitable for anyone looking to test their fitness on a fast, enjoyable course.
course_highlights: Fast, flat 5 km course along the Oslofjord
The course runs from Frognerkilen to Bygdøylokket
Option to join the group start with pacers and music
additional: Race bibs can be collected from Löplabbet Oslo sentrum from April 7. The same bib is used throughout the series. A new bib can be purchased for 75 kr. The courses are marked only for the group start. GPX files and course maps are available to download. The race can be completed at any time between April 9 and 18, 2027. Registration is offered as SOLO, DUO, and TRIO tickets; listed prices vary by ticket type and purchase date.

name: Perseløpet 5 km, 10 km, halvmaraton
description: Perseløpet is a race in Eidsvoll starting at Ås school, Hammerås, offering a simple and efficient race format for achieving fast times. The race takes place on a flat, officially measured 2,633-metre loop, where runners can leave their own bottles and gels on their personal nutrition table, which they pass each lap. Seven distances are offered, from 3 km to 100 km, including 5 km, 10 km and the half marathon. The race is known for producing many personal records and has a friendly atmosphere, with the option to ring the bell when setting a personal record.
course_highlights: Flat, officially measured 2,633-metre loop
Your own nutrition table, passed each lap
Free parking, changing rooms and toilets at the venue
additional: Race bibs are collected via self-service at Ås school approximately two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available inside the school. At selected races, ninth-grade students from Feiring school staff an official drinks station to raise money for their school trip. The race has a lap-time calculator to help plan split times. The weather forecast is updated four times daily using satellite data for the area around Ås school. Race bibs can be collected via self-service at the school from approximately two hours before the start. Changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. Registration is via RaceDays.

name: Baroniløpet
description: Baroniløpet is organized annually by Rosendal Turnlag and takes place in beautiful surroundings at Baroniet Rosendal in Kvinnherad. The race is part of the Kvinnherad cross-country running series and attracts both local and visiting runners looking for a challenging race in scenic surroundings. The terrain offers varied surfaces and beautiful nature, making the race a popular event for both recreational and competitive runners. The event has a long tradition and is well integrated into the local community.
course_highlights: Cross-country race in scenic surroundings at Baroniet Rosendal
Varied surfaces, including trails and wooded sections
Part of the Kvinnherad cross-country running series

name: Neskollen Backyard Ultra
description: Neskollen Backyard is a unique ultramarathon held at Nes Arena in Neskollen. The race follows the classic backyard format, with a new start every hour on the hour. Participants must complete a 6.706 km loop within 60 minutes to continue. They can run up to 12 loops in total, equivalent to approximately 80.5 km. The race is a demanding test of both mental and physical strength, and is suitable for experienced ultrarunners as well as those who want to challenge their limits. Food and drinks are available during the race, and prizes are awarded to participants.
course_highlights: Relatively flat course around Nes Arena
Start and finish inside Nes Arena, with a short break between loops
Up to 12 loops of 6.706 km each, approximately 80.5 km for those who complete them
additional: The race starts every hour on the hour, with a maximum of 12 loops. Participants can take a break inside Nes Arena between loops to eat, rest and prepare. Pizza, cakes, drinks and potato chips are served during the race. Prizes are awarded. The maximum is 12 loops, equivalent to approximately 80.5 kilometres. The available information applies to the 2026 edition; details for 2027 have not been confirmed.

name: Skjold på tvers
description: Skjold på Tvers is a mountain marathon and the most beautiful spring adventure in Vindafjord, Rogaland. The race offers several route options, including the full Skjold på Tvers, with 7 peaks over approximately 21.2 km, as well as shorter options such as HalvTversen and a family route. Participants are transported from Skjold Arena to the start, and chip timing and prize money are offered in the elite class. The event combines challenging terrain with beautiful scenery and is suitable for both fit runners and families.
course_highlights: The full Skjold på Tvers, with 7 peaks, approximately 21.2 km
HalvTversen, with 4 peaks (11.4 km) or 3 peaks (9.6 km)
Family route at Vikaneset, with a trail and an alternative for strollers/wheelchairs
additional: You can also register on the day via EQ Timing at Skjold Arena, but advance registration is recommended. Bus transport from Skjold Arena to the start at Hodnafjellet is included in the price. It is possible to walk half the route, with a bus to or from Dalavik. Participants receive a T-shirt, fruit and drinks at designated stations. The elite class has a mass start at 13:00, with timing and prize money. The route page has a UT.no map and GPX file. The main route runs from Hodnafjellet to Skjold Arena.

name: Perseløpet
description: Perseløpet is a simple and effective running event at Ås school in Eidsvoll, designed to help runners achieve fast times. The race takes place on a flat, officially measured 2,633-metre loop, with the option to set up your own nutrition table, passed on every lap. Seven distances are offered, from 3 km to 100 km, and the event has a friendly atmosphere where runners can celebrate personal records by ringing the bell at the finish area.
course_highlights: Flat, officially measured 2,633-metre loop
Option to set up your own nutrition table along the course
Seven distances from 3 km to 100 km
additional: Race bibs are collected self-service at Ås school from around two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. Runners can set out their own bottles and gels on the nutrition table before the start. An official aid station staffed by 9th grade students from Feiring school is available at selected races. Timing and a lap-time calculator are available for planning. The weather forecast is updated four times daily based on satellite data for the area. Race bibs are collected self-service at the school from around two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. Registration and current prices are available via RaceDays.

name: Stomperudkarusellen - løp nr 1
price_range: Enkeltløp i 2026: 110–220 kr, med lisens på 20–30 kr i tillegg
description: Stomperudkarusellen is a long-running race series organized by Sørum IL since 1981. The series consists of four races with varying distances from 800 meters to 9 kilometers, including shorter options for the youngest participants. The races take place in scenic surroundings around Sørum school and Stomperud Stadium, and the same race number is used throughout the series. This makes it easy and enjoyable for children, young people, and adults to take part in several races during the season.
course_highlights: Bingenrunden 5 km with a shorter option
Aasgaardsrunden 9 km with a shorter option
Lysløypa 6 km with a shorter option
additional: Participants use the same race number in all races in the series. Children who are members of Sørum IL can participate for free if they register at least one week before race day. The races are held in the evening and start at 19:00. Shorter options are available for the youngest participants at every race. The prices are listed for 2026 and may change before the 2027 edition. The same race number is used in all races in the series.

name: Terrengløp i Smidalen
organizer: Nidelv IL Friidrett og Nidelv IL Ski
description: The Smidalen cross-country run is an accessible event for children and young people in grades 1 to 7, organized by Nidelv IL Athletics and Ski in cooperation with Kjeldsberg Eiendom AS. The races take place on a circuit of approximately 1,000 metres in the scenic surroundings of Smidalen, Trondheim. Participants run 1 to 3 laps depending on their grade, with a mass start for everyone. The event promotes well-rounded exercise and the joy of competition among children in the local community.
course_highlights: Approximately 1,000-metre cross-country circuit
Race distance adapted to age: 1–3 laps
Mass start for all participants
additional: The races are held several times a year, with a focus on children and young people. Coaches and team leaders are encouraged to prioritize participation over their own training. The event is part of a sponsorship agreement with Kjeldsberg Eiendom. Previous race formats have been 1 lap for grades 1–3, 2 laps for grades 4–5, and 3 laps for grades 6–7. The information applies to previous editions; no information about 2027 has been provided.

name: Fjordkraft Bergen City Marathon
description: Fjordkraft Bergen City Marathon is organized by Turn og Idrettsforeningen Viking and is one of Scandinavia’s largest road races. The race brings together both Bergen residents and visitors for a festival in the heart of Bergen, with five different distances suitable for all ages and levels. The main distance is a challenging marathon consisting of two 21 km laps. The event offers an inclusive and inspiring running experience focused on activity, achievement, and community.
course_highlights: The race takes place on Bergen’s streets, with beautiful views and technical sections
The main distance consists of two 21 km laps
Five different distances for all levels and ages
additional: Registration is binding and includes an administration fee of 25 kr as well as a license to the athletics federation. It is possible to resell your race bib until 17 April 2027 via a voucher code. Official participant information will be sent out on 14 April 2027. Relay teams are also available, with separate team leader administration and a joint invoice for companies. Registration is available both individually and for companies and organizations. Company teams can be managed by a team leader and receive a joint invoice.

name: Fevik halvmaraton og 5 km
description: Fevik Half Marathon and 5 km are organized by IL Express Friidrett at Fevik Stadium in Grimstad. The race is part of the club’s annual events and offers both recreational and experienced runners a great opportunity to take part in a well-organized race in scenic surroundings. IL Express Friidrett has an active community, with weekly group runs and several races throughout the year, making this a popular event in the local area.
course_highlights: The races start and finish at Fevik Stadium
Scenic surroundings in the Grimstad area
Both half marathon and 5 km distances are offered
additional: IL Express Friidrett also organizes three annual track meets in May, August, and October. Weekly group runs take place on Thursdays at 19:00 from Fevik Stadium.

name: Vinstra Byløp
price_range: 200 kr for 5 km og 10 km; gratis for barneløp og bamseløp (2026-utgaven)
description: Vinstra City Run is an inclusive running event in Vinstra Park, welcoming participants of all ages, from 2 years and up. The event focuses on public health, diversity and the joy of running, with options including a children’s park run, an untimed fun run, and timed 5 km and 10 km races. The start and finish are in Vinstra Park, and participants are encouraged to take part in teams such as family, friends or colleagues. There are prizes and start-number prize draws, and the aim is to establish an annual running event for all levels.
course_highlights: Children’s park run and teddy bear run in the park for the youngest participants
5 km and 10 km races with electronic timing
Untimed fun-run category where participants can walk or run
additional: Participants are advised to arrive 1 hour before the start. Prize ceremony at approximately 13:00. Joint warm-up for the 5 km and 10 km at 11:30. Start of the timed 5 km and 10 km races and the fun-run category at 12:00. Previous editions have offered an untimed 5 km fun-run category and timed 5 km and 10 km races. The listed distances and prices apply to previous editions and have not been confirmed for 2027.

name: Glommaløpet
description: Glommaløpet is an annual race on a gravel path along the final kilometres of the Glomma, from Sarpefossen to Gamlebyen in Fredrikstad. The course starts in the square in Sarpsborg and passes through Kulåsparken, over Sannesund Bridge, along the eastern bank of the Glomma and under Fredrikstad Bridge, finishing in the historic fortress town of Gamlebyen. The event offers several distances and categories, including 10 miles, a relay, a recreational run and a children's race, and is suitable for both competitive runners and recreational participants. The course is flat and easy to run, with scenic surroundings and water stations along the way.
course_highlights: Run on a gravel path along the Glomma's final kilometres, from Sarpefossen to the sea at Gamlebyen
Start in the square in Sarpsborg and finish in Gamlebyen, the best-preserved fortress town in the Nordic countries
Flat course profile with water stations at 4.5, 5, 9.5 and 14.5 km
additional: Glommaløpet has one start group per event, with no wave starts. The maximum number of participants is limited to ensure smooth flow and sufficient capacity at the water stations. Race numbers can be collected in the square in Sarpsborg on race day from 11:00 to 13:30, or earlier at selected locations in Fredrikstad and Sarpsborg. Bus transport is available for participants and must be booked by 18 April at the latest. Everyone who finishes receives a medal, and prizes are awarded to category winners and relay teams. A technical running shirt with the Glommaløpet print can be purchased when registering by 24 March. The 10-mile distance is 16 km. The relay consists of ten legs ranging from 800 metres to 3 kilometres. There are three water stations, and bus transport must be booked in advance. Changing rooms and showers are available at Kongstenhallen and Sarpsborghallen.

name: Hell Backyard Ultra
description: Hell Backyard Ultra is an ultramarathon in which participants run a 6,706-meter lap in under an hour. The race continues hour by hour until only one runner remains and completes a full lap alone, known as Last Man Standing. The race takes place at Trudvang community hall in Lånke and offers a challenging but social ultrarunning experience, with the option of personal support within the start and finish area. The race record is 42 laps, set in 2026.
course_highlights: The lap is 6,706 meters long and must be completed in under an hour
The course runs from Trudvang toward Hell and Hell station, along the shore and the Stjørdal River, then back to Lånke athletics track
Start and finish at Trudvang community hall, with the option to use a tent or indoor space
additional: The race starts at 09:00, with a new start every hour on the hour. Personal support is permitted within the start and finish area, but not out on the course. Basic refreshments, including drinks and snacks, are provided, and it is possible to set up a tent near the start area. Participants must remain within the course area during the race. Start at 09:00 at Trudvang community hall in Lånke. Race director: Lars Erik Gylland.

name: Sparebank1 Østlandet-mila Moelv 2027 - 10000 meter/3000 meter på bane
Tveide Rundt
price_range: 200 kr for 10 km; barneløpet er gratis
description: Tveide Rundt is a fun run starting and finishing in Birkenesparken. The course has been officially measured and certified at 10 km, and the race takes place on the last Sunday in April. It is a great event for everyone aged 13 and over, with attractive raffle prizes and gift cards for podium finishers. Birkenesparken Rundt is also held—a free 1 km children’s race for children aged 6 to 12, with a medal for everyone.
course_highlights: Officially measured and certified 10 km course
Start and finish in scenic Birkenesparken
1 km children’s race for ages 6–12, with a medal for everyone
additional: Schedule: The kiosk opens at 11:00. Tveide Rundt 10 km starts at 12:00. Birkenesparken Rundt 1 km starts at 12:10. Attractive raffle prizes for all runners and gift cards for podium finishers. The children’s race is free, and all children receive a medal. Birkenesparken Rundt is a free 1 km children’s race for ages 6–12, with a medal for everyone. The listed schedule has the kiosk opening at 11:00, the 10 km starting at 12:00, and the children’s race at 12:10.

name: Jæren Sparebank Sentrumsløp
price_range: 125 kr for barneløp; 275 kr for 5 km
description: The Jæren Sparebank Sentrumsløp is an annual race held in Kanalparken, Ålgård, Gjesdal. The race features a 5 km loop starting outside Amfi Ålgård and passing through Torgveien, along the Figgjo River and over the Liv Godin Bridge. The scenic course combines an urban setting with beautiful natural surroundings. There is also a 700-metre children’s race. Separate start times are provided for fast runners and everyone else. Prizes are awarded to the top three in the women’s and men’s categories, and all participants receive a finisher’s prize.
course_highlights: 5 km course starting outside Amfi Ålgård
The course runs along the Figgjo River and over the Liv Godin Bridge
700-metre children’s race
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 16:30 at Ålgård Sentrum by Kanalparken. Schedule: 18:00 Children’s race, 700 m; 18:15 5 km SUPER (for runners under 18 minutes); 18:40 5 km for everyone else. Prizes for the top three in the women’s and men’s categories in the 5 km, and a finisher’s prize for everyone. Course records from 2025: Men 15:42.8, Women 18:54.1. Race bibs can be collected from 16:30 at Kanalparken. Prizes are awarded to the top three in the women’s and men’s categories in the 5 km, and all participants receive a finisher’s prize.

name: Gateløp
location: Ripateigane, Ørsta, Møre og Romsdal, Norway

name: 1. mailøpet
description: Welcome to the 64th May 1st race in Åheim, a traditional cross-country race starting and finishing at Olivinhallen. The race offers several distances for different age groups, from the youngest recruits to seniors and veterans. The event has a friendly atmosphere, with a kiosk, cakes, a tombola, and prizes after the race. The senior, junior, and veteran races start at 13:00, while the recruits start at around 14:05.
course_highlights: Cross-country race starting and finishing at Olivinhallen
Several distances from 220 metres to 3,000 metres
Courses for all age groups, including seniors, juniors, veterans, and recruits
additional: The start and finish are at Olivinhallen, which also houses the event office and changing rooms. Payment can be made by bank transfer, VIPPS, or in person, but VIPPS payments are not registered as entries. A paid athletics licence for participants aged 13 and over gives a NOK 20 discount on registration. Traveling trophies are awarded to women and men; they must be won three times to be kept permanently. The event office and changing rooms are at Olivinhallen. Earlier information states that late registration on race day costs an extra NOK 50; prices and practical details for 2027 have not been confirmed.

name: Steinsland Bygdemaraton

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Startkontingent er 400 kr. (350 kr for kondismedlem)

description: Steinsland Village Marathon is a long-standing race that starts in the farmyard of Odd Gunnar Tveit in Steinsland. The course passes through the scenic municipalities of Vennesla, Iveland and Birkenes, with a choice of distances: marathon, half marathon and 10 km. The race offers a wonderful experience in nature, with several refreshment stations along the way and kiosk sales in the start and finish area. An earlier start is available for those who wish to walk the course, and transport and accommodation can be arranged if needed.
course_highlights: The marathon course passes through Vennesla, Iveland and Birkenes
10 refreshment stations along the course
Start and finish in the farmyard of Odd Gunnar Tveit in Steinsland
additional: Start times: 08:00 marathon for walkers; 09:00 marathon for those who expect to take more than 4.5 hours; 11:00 half marathon for walkers; 12:00 start for the half marathon and 10 km. Kiosk sales are available in the start/finish area. Transport and accommodation can be arranged by contacting the organizer. Distances are marathon, half marathon and 10 km. The start and finish are in the farmyard of Odd Gunnar Tveit, with kiosk sales in the start/finish area.

name: Skifjelløpet
description: Skifjelløpet is held annually on May 16, starting at 18:00 from Lillesand IL’s clubhouse. The race is approximately 6 km long and takes place over varied terrain with natural trails and rocky sections. The course is well marked and offers a challenging route that includes steep hills and a rocky section, finishing in front of the clubhouse. Participants can register in advance or on site from 16:30.
course_highlights: Start outside the clubhouse, with an uphill section to the right of the garage
The course crosses the Skifjell rocky section on natural trails
Finish in front of the clubhouse after running around the stadium
additional: Registration is available in advance via Webscorer or on site from 16:30. The course is marked, and a GPX file is available for mobile apps. Participants must run around the stadium before finishing. The organizer’s page lists advance registration via Webscorer and on-site registration from 16:30. Previous editions have been held in May; details for 2027 may differ.

name: Hagemanns Backyard Festival 2027
description: Hagemanns Backyard Festival 2027 is a unique race in Drammen where participants run a 6.7 km loop every hour on the hour, with the first start at 10:00 on May 1. It is an endurance challenge: runners must complete each loop within an hour to continue, and the last person standing wins. Children’s races are also held on both days, along with an additional race on Sunday where participants run one loop as fast as possible. The festival offers facilities including changing rooms, showers and a kiosk. Reflective vests and headlamps are mandatory for runs after 21:00.
course_highlights: 6.7 km loop starting every hour on the hour
Children’s race of approximately 400–500 metres around the school building
Running in the dark, with reflective vests and headlamps required after 21:00
additional: Reflective vests and headlamps are mandatory from 21:00 to 06:00. Changing rooms, toilets and showers are available at Ebbestadhallen. The kiosk opens at 08:00 and is run by Svelvik Cycling Club. Pizza will be served to participants at 19:30. Start numbers can be bought and sold through Racetracker. Children’s races are held on both Saturday and Sunday. Contact: Einar Hagemann (einarhagemann@msn.com).

name: Olavstafetten
description: Olavstafetten is a traditional relay race held on historic ground in Trondheim, starting and finishing at Trondheim Stadion, Øya. The race consists of 10 legs totaling 11,300 metres and is a popular running festival that also includes the “Family and Friends of Olav” category for teams of all sizes. The event features leg times, course records and leg records in all categories, and serves as preparation for the Norwegian Athletics Championships. It is a social, informal relay suited to both competitive and recreational runners.
course_highlights: 10 legs on historic ground, totaling 11,300 metres
Leg times and course records are recorded in all categories
The course follows the Olav route, starting and finishing at Trondheim Stadion
additional: There are dedicated children’s categories (Mini-Olavstafetten and Lille-Olavstafetten) with short legs at the stadium. Family and friend teams can enter the “Family and Friends of Olav” category, with flexible team line-ups. The kiosk opens at 12:00, and prizes are awarded to the children’s and youth categories early in the day. Runners may run multiple legs for multiple relay teams. The main relay starts at 13:00 and is for participants aged 13 and over. A family and friends category is also offered.

name: Råskinnet
description: Råskinnet is a challenging trail race around Sognsvann in Oslo, featuring bogs, trails, steep hills and two water crossings. The race is known for being tough, wet and muddy, and is suitable for the whole family, with separate distances for children and young people. Everyone who finishes can call themselves a true Råskinn. The event has a long tradition and is met with great enthusiasm by participants and volunteers.
course_highlights: Two crossings of Sognsvann, with water reaching thigh or chest height
Steep hills in old ski jumps from 1942 (Kollbakkene)
The course’s most beautiful section, with old-growth forest and bogs by Godbekken
additional: Race bibs are sent by SMS and must be collected at the start area no later than one hour before the start. Showers and changing rooms are available in the basement at NIH; bring your own padlock. There is free parking at Sognsvann and paid parking at NIH. Bags and luggage can be stored in an unattended tent at the venue. Råskinnet’s 10 km race starts in waves according to expected finish time (from 13:30 to 13:50). The children’s races, Knøttetassen and Råtassen, have separate start times at 11:45 and 12:20–12:35. Distances: 900 m for ages 6–9, 3 km for ages 10–15 and 9 km from age 15. Starts are divided into waves. Sognsvann is accessible by metro line 5.

name: Nupen halvmaraton
description: The Nupen Half Marathon in Harstad is a long-standing race that marks the start of the season for the local running community. The race takes runners through the scenic surroundings of Kasfjord and offers a great half-marathon experience for both local and visiting runners. Runners of all ages and levels come together for a social and sporting day in early May.
course_highlights: Half marathon through the scenic surroundings of Kasfjord
Season opener for Harstad’s running community
The race takes place over varied terrain with great views
additional: Kasfjord is approximately 12 km from Harstad. The distance information is confirmed for 2026; information about 2027 is not provided in the sources.

name: Esefjorden Rundt

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: 13-16 år for medlemmar i BIL med heilårslisens

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: 13-16 år for medlemmar i BIL med eingongslisens ( kr.30)

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Startpengar konkurranse stafett kr 100,- Stafett 11-12 år (f. 2015 og 2014)

description: Esefjorden Rundt is a beautiful 8.5 km road race on asphalt, with no major elevation changes, around Esefjorden, part of the National Tourist Routes. The race starts at Tjugum Church and finishes at the Balahaugen festival grounds, near the centre of Balestrand. The event has a long tradition and attracts recreational runners and competitive runners of all ages, with a festive atmosphere and beautiful scenery, including the mountains Tjugatoten and Keipen around the fjord. Participants can take a shuttle boat from the centre of Balestrand to the start area, making for a unique experience.
course_highlights: 8.5 km asphalt course with no major elevation changes
Starts at Tjugum Church and finishes at the Balahaugen festival grounds
The course goes around Esefjorden, part of the National Tourist Routes, with beautiful mountain views
additional: Shuttle boats run between Holmen (Balestrand town centre) and Tjugum (the start area) from 09:00 to 16:00. Boat transport ends at 16:00. Shuttle boat tickets cost NOK 80 for adults, NOK 40 for children under 15, and NOK 200 for a family. Parking is available at the finish area, in the town centre, at Tjugum Church and at Bygdahuset. The relay competition has three legs, with a map available. Race numbers must be collected at Tjugum Church within the specified times. A licence is required for participants aged 13 to 80, with a one-time licence available when registering. Recreational and competitive categories. A shuttle boat from Holmen in Balestrand town centre to Tjugum is an option; the finish area at Balahaugen is about 1 km from the town centre.

name: SA-løpet
description: SA-løpet is an open and inclusive running event in the beautiful Kulåsparken in Sarpsborg, suitable for all ages and levels. The event offers several distances, both timed and untimed, and focuses on community, personal achievement, and the joy of running. It is well organized, with dedicated volunteers, good safety measures, and accessibility, and aims to give all participants a positive experience. Welcome to an active day filled with smiles and the true joy of running!
course_highlights: Course in the beautiful Kulåsparken, Sarpsborg
Several distances: 2.5 km, 5 km, and 10 km
Safe, well-organized event with a clear course
additional: The start and finish are in Kulåsparken. The children's race starts at 10:00, the 10 km starts at 10:30, and the 2.5 km and 5 km start at 10:35. Race numbers are handed out only on race day from 08:00. Toilets are available in the Service House in Kulåsparken. Bag storage is provided during the race. Participants must be 11 years or older to take part in the timed races; younger participants may take part without timing. Registration is listed as open from 1 February to 29 April 2027, with late registration on 30 April and until the race starts on 1 May. Timed categories have an age limit of 11; younger participants may take part without timing or in the children's race.

name: Heim FrontYard Ultra
description: Heim Front Yard Ultra is a unique ultrarace that combines speed and endurance in a social, informal atmosphere. The race takes place on a 3 km loop with a variable time limit per lap, and participants must complete each lap faster than the previous one to continue. The race starts at Sodvinhallen in Ånesøyan, and the course features a mix of gravel and asphalt with approximately 20 metres of elevation gain per lap. The event is suitable for anyone looking for a challenge in an inclusive setting, with light refreshments and facilities available.
course_highlights: 3 km loop with approximately 20 metres of elevation gain per lap
The course is 50% gravel and 50% asphalt
Start and finish at Sodvinhallen, with access to changing rooms and toilets
additional: The race starts with 30 minutes for the first lap, after which the time is reduced by one minute per lap. Light refreshments are offered during breaks. Parking is available at Sodvinplatået or by the community centre. Spaces are limited. Toilets and changing rooms are available, and light food is served during breaks. All participants receive a medal.

name: Backyard Lampeland Ultra
description: Backyard Lampeland is a unique ultrarace held in Lampeland, Flesberg. The race consists of a gently rolling 6.7 km loop run every hour on the hour, with a maximum of twelve laps in total. Participants must start each lap to continue, and the last runner to start wins the race. The event has a social focus and a low barrier to participation, and offers a rest area, refreshments and changing rooms. Everyone who completes 12 laps receives a cup, and those who run the ultra distance receive a Norwegian-made wooden medal.
course_highlights: Gently rolling 6.7 km loop per lap
Maximum of 12 laps, 80.4 km in total
The race starts every hour on the hour
additional: Bringing your own cup is mandatory. A reflective vest and headlamp are required if visibility is poor on the final lap. Baked goods, snacks, coffee, water and sausages are served after the seventh lap. A rest area and changing rooms are available in the hall. Maximum 500 participants. Race bib collection is Friday 15–20 and Saturday 08–09:15 at Friluftsbua by Lampeland Hotel, or in the hall at the start from 09:30. Using a race belt for the race bib is recommended. The start and finish are at Skattekista, the school and multipurpose hall in Lampeland. Maximum 500 participants. Bringing your own cup is mandatory; a reflective vest and headlamp are required if visibility is poor on the final lap.

name: Perseløpet 50 km, 100 km, maraton
description: Perseløpet is a race in Eidsvoll, starting and finishing at Ås school in Hammerås. It features a flat, accurately measured 2,633-metre loop offering good opportunities for fast times. Participants can choose from seven distances ranging from 3 km to 100 km, including 50 km and the marathon. The race has a unique concept, with a dedicated nutrition table passed on every lap, and a friendly atmosphere where personal records are celebrated by ringing a bell near the finish area.
course_highlights: Flat, accurately measured 2,633-metre loop
Dedicated nutrition table passed on every lap
Distances from 3 km to 100 km, with opportunities to set personal records
additional: Race bibs are collected by self-service at Ås school approximately two hours before the start. Free parking, changing facilities and toilets are available at the venue. At selected races, ninth-graders from Feiring school staff an official refreshment station to raise money for their school trip. The weather forecast is updated four times daily based on satellite data for the area. The race has a lap-time calculator for planning split times. Race-bib collection, changing facilities and toilets are at Ås school, less than 100 metres from the start. Free parking is available.

name: Ulfstindmila
description: Ulfstindmila is an annual cross-country race held on 1 May, starting at Tønsvik bridge and finishing at Skittenelv School in Vågnes. Known as the “world’s shortest 10K,” it covers 8.7 km and has a long tradition dating back to 1972. There are two categories: a recreational category without timing and a competitive category. Mini-Ulfstindmila and Mini-mini Ulfstindmila are also held for children, with shorter distances adapted for the youngest participants.
course_highlights: Cross-country race through the beautiful Tønsvik Valley
Starts at Tønsvik bridge and finishes at Skittenelv School
The race is 8.7 km long and is known as the world’s shortest 10K
additional: Ulfstindmila has two categories: a recreational category without timing and a competitive category. Mini-Ulfstindmila (approx. 2.5 km) and Mini-mini Ulfstindmila are held for the youngest children. The race has been held annually since 1972, with a few exceptions. Previous editions have offered changing facilities, parking, a café and an awards ceremony at Skittenelv School. The organizer has also offered transport for bags from the start to the finish. Practical information and prices listed for 2025 may change for 2027.

name: Konradløpet 2027
location: Velledalen, Sykkylven, Møre og Romsdal, Norway

name: Voss Løpskarusell 2
description: Voss Running Series is a running series for everyone, with 5 km races held on Mondays in 2027. The course starts and finishes at Idrettsplassen in Voss, and runs through Prestegardsmoen and along the waterfront promenade. The event welcomes recreational participants and runners aged 9 and up to enjoyable fun runs in scenic surroundings. Registration is online, and a discount is offered for registering for all six races before the second race. The races start at 19:00, except for the final race, which starts at 18:30.
course_highlights: 5 km course starting and finishing at Idrettsplassen
Loop through Prestegardsmoen
Race along the waterfront promenade
additional: The races are held on Mondays, starting at 19:00, except for the final race on 20 September, which starts at 18:30. You can register for individual races or for all six together, with a discount for early registration. The course can be viewed virtually in a video on the website. Registration is via EQ Timing. A discount is available for registering for all six races by the second race.

name: Voss Løpskarusell 2027, løp 2
description: Voss Running Series 2027 is a running series for everyone, with races on Mondays at 19:00. The course is 5 km long, starting and finishing at Voss Idrettsplass, and runs through Prestegardsmoen and along the waterfront promenade. The event welcomes recreational runners and runners aged 9 and up to enjoyable fun runs in scenic surroundings. Registration is online, with a discount for registering for all six races by the second race.
course_highlights: 5 km course starting and finishing at Voss Idrettsplass
Loop through Prestegardsmoen
Run along the waterfront promenade
additional: Registration is online only via EQ Timing. You can register for all six races at a discount by the second race. The fifth race starts at 18:30 instead of 19:00. Registration is online via EQ Timing. There is a discount for registering for all six races by race 2; otherwise, you register for each race individually.

name: Tinestafetten Gjesdal IL Friidrettsbane 2027
location: Gjesdal IL Friidrettsbane, Ålgård, Gjesdal, Norway

name: Tordenskioldløpet
description: Tordenskioldløpet is an annual running event organized by Sportsklubben Freidig, traditionally held on the first Tuesday in May at Lade in Trondheim. The event offers 5 km and 10 km races as well as a children’s race, and is suitable for all levels, from recreational runners to competitive athletes. It has an inclusive profile with an easy entry point for participants, and focuses on the joy of sport, personal achievement, and community spirit. The aim is to bring together many participants and help as many people as possible experience the joy of physical activity.
course_highlights: 5 km and 10 km routes starting and finishing at Koteng Arena
The route passes through Lade Allé, Fagerheimbakken, Olav Engelbrektssons Allé, and several local roads
Children’s race and multiple distances with an easy entry point for participants
additional: The venue opens at 17:00. The children’s race and untimed 5 km/10 km races start at 18:30. Warm-up with 3T at 18:35. Official starts: 5 km at 19:00 and 10 km at 19:15. Prize ceremony at 20:15. All participants have access to changing rooms at Koteng Arena. For the 2026 edition, the start and finish were in the Koteng Arena area at Lade, with changing rooms available at the venue. Information about the 2027 edition has not been confirmed in the sources.

name: Revetal Halvmaraton
description: Revetal Half Marathon is a race offering a fast, officially measured 21.1-kilometer half-marathon course that is almost completely flat, with only 24 meters of elevation gain. The race is suitable for both experienced runners and recreational runners, with a focus on even pacing and negative splits. The start and finish are at Re-torvet, a short distance from changing facilities, parking, and refreshments, making for a compact and pleasant race experience. A 5 km race and a children’s race are also held, giving people of all ages and abilities the opportunity to participate.
course_highlights: An officially measured 21.1 km course that is almost completely flat
Two turnarounds, with a total of 24 meters of elevation gain
Start and finish at the same location, a short distance from facilities
additional: Bib distribution from 09:00 at Sport 1 Revetal and Re-torvet. Children’s race at 10:45, with free entry and a medal for everyone. Maximum of 600 places in total. Early registration is recommended to avoid stress. The course follows Bispeveien to Real Våle and back. Events include a half marathon, 5 km, and free children’s race. Pacers are available for the half marathon and 5 km. Stated capacity is 600 participants, with registration closing one hour before the start.

name: Tjomsevannet Rundt + Backyard 12 timers
description: Tjomsevannet Rundt is held annually on Ascension Day and is a popular race for all ages and levels, starting and finishing at Søgne gamle prestegård. The event offers a social and enjoyable day with several distances, including a children’s race, a youth race, and a 6.5 km fun run. New this year is registration via EQtiming.com with live timing, and the popular Backyard 12-hour race returns, offering the opportunity to run around Tjomsevannet for up to 12 hours. Group training sessions are also held every Monday at Søgne stadium for all levels.
course_highlights: Run around Tjomsevannet, starting and finishing at Søgne gamle prestegård
Off-road races for children and youth over short distances
Backyard 12-hour race, with the opportunity to run every hour for 12 hours
additional: Group training every Monday at 18:00 at Søgne stadium for all levels. Registration for the children’s race, youth race, and untimed race takes place on-site on the day, with payment via Vipps. Live timing via EQtiming.com for the main race and the Backyard race. Start and finish at Søgne gamle prestegård. Prices vary by race, and a license fee may be added.

name: Ekebergstafetten og Ekebergløpet 2027
description: Ekebergløpet and Ekebergstafetten are an annual running festival held at Ekebergsletta in Oslo, with a long tradition and an inclusive atmosphere for runners of all ages and abilities. The event takes place on Ascension Day and offers several distances, including relays for children and youth, a children’s race, 5 km and 10 km. The event is more than just a race, with activities for children and young people, food and drinks from local vendors, as well as music and entertainment that create a lively atmosphere. Bækkelagets Sportsklub is the organizer and welcomes everyone to a day filled with activity, achievement and fun.
course_highlights: Scenic surroundings around Ekebergsletta
Several distances: relays for children and youth, a children’s race, 5 km and 10 km
Recreational race with national age-group categories for adults
additional: Start times: 11:30 Children’s relay, 12:00 Youth relay, 14:00 Children’s race for ages up to 10, 15:00 5 km, 15:10 10 km. The event includes activities for children and young people, food and drinks from local vendors, as well as music and entertainment. Previous editions have featured a children’s race of around 700 metres. Ekebergstafetten has been held as a mixed relay for 7–16-year-olds with five legs. Details for 2027 have not been confirmed in the sources.

name: Sunnhordland løpsfest
description: Sunnhordland Running Festival takes place in the centre of Leirvik on Stord and offers a wide range of distances for all runners, including 5 km, 10 km, half marathon, a children’s race and a Super Race for people with disabilities. The event is a community celebration that brings together runners of all ages and abilities for a day of running and camaraderie. The race starts on Borggata and is organised by Stord Athletics, which welcomes everyone to a great running experience in scenic surroundings.
course_highlights: Run in the centre of Leirvik, with the start on Borggata
A great choice of distances from 5 km to half marathon
An adapted Super Race for people with disabilities
additional: The children’s race is approximately 450 metres. Registration for the standard distances and the Super Race is via EQ Timing; the children’s race has its own registration form.

name: Skogvokteren Ultra
description: Skogvokteren Ultra is a demanding 88 km trail ultramarathon with 3,500 metres of elevation gain, passing through varied forest areas in Grenland. The race starts and finishes at the steps of Porsgrunn City Hall and offers a mix of trails, gravel roads and asphalt in scenic, hilly terrain. The event has an accessible, authentic profile, with a focus on personal achievement and the joy of trail running. A six-stage relay is also held, offering teams and companies a great opportunity to take part together. The race includes electronic timing, tracking via intermediate timing points, five aid stations and a Skogvokteren medal.
course_highlights: 88 km with 3,500 metres of elevation gain across varied terrain
80% trail and 20% gravel/asphalt through three municipalities and two cities
The course links Grenland’s two largest cities in a green, winding loop
additional: The race has electronic timing and tracking via approximately 15 intermediate timing points. There are five aid stations along the route. Mandatory equipment includes a GPS device with the route loaded, hydration containers holding at least 1.5 litres, a wool or technical base layer, a reflective vest for running in the dark, a phone with the race director’s number saved, first-aid supplies and an emergency blanket. Accommodation is available with a 20% discount at Comfort Hotel Porsgrunn when booked before 9 April 2027. A pasta party will be held on Friday 7 May from 17:00 to 19:00, alongside race-number collection. The relay class has six stages with handovers in marked areas, and the baton is a timing chip passed between runners. Start at 05:00 from the steps of Porsgrunn City Hall. The course is not marked and must be followed using GPX; there are five aid stations. Mandatory equipment and an age limit of 18 apply. The relay has 25 team places.

name: Fløyen - Knarvik
location: Fløyen, Bergen to AMFI Knarvik, Knarvik, Norway
description: Fløyen-Knarvik is a hiking and running event of approximately 26 km, starting at Fløyen in Bergen and finishing at AMFI Knarvik. The route follows much of the old postal road and crosses the Nordhordland Bridge, Flatøy and the Hagelsund Bridge. There is also a shorter starting option from IKEA in Åsane, covering approximately 13 km. The event is suitable both for families looking for a scenic outing and for runners seeking a challenging distance, with timing and prizes for the top finishers. The route is approximately 50% asphalt, 30% gravel and 20% trail, with a total elevation gain of 800 metres from Fløyen.
course_highlights: The route follows the old postal road and crosses the Nordhordland Bridge, Flatøy and the Hagelsund Bridge
Approximately 26 km with 800 metres of total elevation gain from Fløyen
Varied terrain: asphalt, gravel and trail
additional: The Fløibanen funicular ride up to Fløyen is included in the registration fee. It is not possible to register on the day at the start. The running class starts at 11:00 from Fløyen with a mass start, and at 11:30 from IKEA Åsane. Free buses from Knarvik bus station to Bergen depart at 08:20 and 09:30. Return by regular scheduled bus from AMFI Knarvik. The route is staffed by course marshals and has Red Cross stations. Water and bananas are available at aid stations along the way. The finish area at AMFI Knarvik offers baguettes, bananas, water and coffee. Toilets are available at the start, IKEA Åsane and the finish area. Race numbers can be collected at the lower Fløibanen station or IKEA Åsane before the start. The route is marked with kilometre markers, arrows and tape. Good running shoes that have been worn a few times and weather-appropriate clothing are recommended. The Fløibanen ride up to Fløyen is included in the registration fee. The Fløyen route is approximately 50% asphalt, 30% gravel and 20% trail. It is not possible to register on the day at the start.

name: Oslo Løpsfestival, Bygdøyrunden

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Dagsbillett SOLO Deltakere kr 475,00 kr 332,50 + Adm. gebyr (25 NOK + 3%) -30%

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Festivalpass SOLO Deltakere kr 1475,00 kr 1032,50 + Adm. gebyr (25 NOK + 3%) -30%

description: Bygdøyrunden is one of eight races in the Oslo Running Festival, which follows the capital’s lovely trails and scenic roads. The race has a mass start on Sunday, May 9 at 11:00 from Frognerkilen skatepark in Oslo. Participants can run alone or as part of a team, and it is possible to take part in several races to earn an overall medal. The course is marked only during the mass start, and timing is recorded using a chip on the race bib.
course_highlights: The race follows lovely trails and scenic roads in Oslo
Mass start on Sunday, May 9 at 11:00
The course is marked only during the mass start
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Löplabbet Oslo sentrum at Pilestredet 7 from April 7. Timing is recorded using a chip on the race bib, and participants must pass within five metres of the sensors. The course is marked only during the mass start. Participants can run alone (SOLO) or in teams (DUO, TRIO), with women’s, men’s and mixed categories. Participants who take part in at least five races can compete in the overall series. Start and finish at Frognerkilen skatepark. The race can be completed between April 30 and May 9, 2027; the mass start is on Sunday, May 9 at 11:00. SOLO, DUO and TRIO tickets are available, and the festival pass covers all eight races.

name: Strailøpet
description: Strailøpet is an inclusive spring trail race on the lit trails at Strai, Torridal, Kristiansand, organized by Torridal IL and secondary school students. The race offers four distances: a children’s race, 5 km, 10 km trail, and half marathon, all starting and finishing in the same area at Storemyråsen. The event combines competition with socializing, offers timing for those who want it, and also allows participants to walk in the recreational class. Proceeds go toward the students’ class trip and the Norwegian Cancer Society, and the whole village pitches in to create an enjoyable race day.
course_highlights: Half marathon of 22.2 km with 474 metres of elevation gain, consisting of one 5 km loop and two 10 km loops
5 km and 10 km trail courses on the lit trails at Strai
Children’s race of approximately 1 km, untimed, with a medal and ice cream at the finish
additional: All distances start and finish at Storemyråsen, allowing family and supporters to follow runners across the different distances. The start order is half marathon first, followed by the children’s race, 10 km, and 5 km. There is a group warm-up and an announcer before each start. Race bibs and timing chips are collected on race day in the start and finish area. The children’s race is untimed, but all children receive a medal and ice cream at the finish. NOK 20 of each participant’s entry fee goes to the Norwegian Cancer Society. It is possible to participate in the recreational class without being ranked. The race is organized by volunteers, with support from parents, young people, and sponsors.

name: Halsahalvøya Rundt 2027
description: Halsahalvøya Rundt 2027 takes place on Sunday, August 22, in Halsa, starting at Halsa Church. This road race offers a great opportunity to experience the beautiful Halsahalvøya amid scenic surroundings. The event is suitable for both recreational and competitive runners, offering an active, social day for all participants. Tickets are sold via EQ Timing. Follow the organizer’s channels for updates on the start time and practical details.
course_highlights: The race takes place on Halsahalvøya amid scenic surroundings
Road race on varied terrain
Start and finish at Halsa Church
additional: Tickets are sold via EQ Timing. The start time will be announced on the organizer’s channels. The event is managed by Halsa IL. The 2026 edition had a 21.7 km course, starting and finishing at Halsa Church. Both a recreational class without timing and competitive classes are listed.

name: Kanada Rundt
description: Kanada Rundt is a traditional annual road race in Sylling that has been held since 1981. The race offers 3 km, 6 km, and 12 km distances, with the start and finish at Syllinghallen. The classic 12 km course runs around Kanada and is officially measured by the Norwegian Athletics Association. The event also includes Syllingløpet for children, with no timing, and prizes are awarded for course records, sprints, and youth categories.
course_highlights: Classic 12 km course around Kanada, officially measured at 12,040 metres
The 6 km course follows the main route to Kyllerudsvingen before returning to Syllinghallen
Route: Syllinghallen, Kyllerud, Trolldalen, Kanada, Tronstad, Skjeggerud, Syllinghallen
additional: Start and finish at Syllinghallen, with changing rooms available. Participants in the recreational category can walk or run without timing, with starts between 17:00 and 18:00. Syllingløpet for children aged 0–11 starts at 18:00 without timing; all participants receive a medal. There is a sprint prize at the Learn sprint point, approximately 3 km into the course, as well as course-record prizes and youth prizes. Participants who finish multiple times receive anniversary prizes and mugs. The Lier double prize is for taking part in both Kanada Rundt/Syllingløpet and Lierskogen 6-timers. Previous editions have offered registration through EQ Timing. The start, finish, and changing rooms have been at Syllinghallen.

name: Sørdalskarusellen - Strandtorgetløpet
location: Strandpromenaden, south of Strandtorget, Lillehammer, Norway
description: Strandtorgetløpet is part of Sørdalskarusellen and takes place on the open area south of Strandtorget in Lillehammer, by the red artwork. The race offers an inclusive, accessible atmosphere where both elite runners and recreational runners can take part. The event focuses on the joy of running and togetherness, and is suitable for anyone looking for an enjoyable race experience in scenic surroundings. Race bibs can be collected at the Litrim tent by the art installation, and facilities include toilets on Strandpromenaden.
course_highlights: The race takes place on the open area south of Strandtorget by the red artwork
Race bibs can be collected at the Litrim tent on Strandpromenaden from 17:45
Toilets are available on Strandpromenaden
additional: Registration closes at 18:00 on race day, one hour before the start. Prices increase from 13:00 on race day. Parking at Strandtorget is limited to 2 hours, or 3 hours for shopping centre members. An SMS with information about race bibs and start times will be sent at approximately 16:00. Remember to bring your race bib if you have registered for the whole series. Listed with a start time of 20:00 on 12 May 2027. Virtual participation is listed for 8–11 May.

name: Søreideløpet
description: Søreideløpet is being held for the first time and offers a running festival in Søreide, Bergen. The race follows sidewalks, with a course guide on a bicycle and course marshals at crossings with vehicle traffic. Participants will receive a race bib, and a race medal will be awarded at the finish. Children and young people will also receive a buff from Fjordkraft, and gift cards for Puma products will be drawn among participants. The team with the highest percentage of its members participating will receive NOK 5,000 for its team fund.
course_highlights: The race follows sidewalks in Søreide, marked with white arrows
Course guide on a bicycle and course marshals at crossings with vehicle traffic
Start and finish at Rema 1000 Søreide
additional: Race bibs will be handed out from 18:00. The registration deadline is 18:15 on race day. Rema 1000 Søreide provides bottled water at the finish. All participants receive a race medal. All children and young people receive a buff. The team with the highest percentage of its members participating wins NOK 5,000 for its team fund. Previous editions have awarded medals to all participants. Information about the 4 km distance and price applies to the 2026 edition; information for 2027 is not provided in the sources.

name: Ølmedal Rundt
location: Bygdahuset i Ølmedal, Imsland, Vindafjord, Norway
description: Ølmedal Rundt is a traditional race that started in 1984 and attracts 500–600 participants each year. The race follows an approximately 7 km paved route around Ølmedalsvatnet through gently rolling terrain, suitable for runners, recreational participants, wheelchair users and strollers. The event also includes a children’s race, recreational and family classes, and age-group competition classes. The start and finish are at Bygdahuset in Ølmedal, where food is available, along with a drinks station, showers and changing rooms. Ølmedal Rundt is a community celebration with a wide range of participants and good facilities.
course_highlights: Approximately 7 km route around Ølmedalsvatnet on paved roads
Gently rolling terrain suitable for everyone, including wheelchair users and strollers
Children’s course of approximately 400 metres near Bygdahuset
additional: Drinks station after approximately 4 km. Medal for all children’s race participants. Prizes for the top three in the competition classes. Access to showers and changing rooms. A large food sale with grilled food, sveler, cakes and coffee at Bygdahuset. The start and finish are at Bygdahuset in Ølmedal. There is a drinks station after approximately 4 km, and food, showers and changing rooms are available. The race is traditionally held on the second day of Pentecost.

name: Vestmarkaløpet
description: Vestmarkaløpet takes place on May 15, 2027, in Vestmarka in Bærum and offers trail running in beautiful natural surroundings. The race offers two distances, 10 km and 21 km, on trails and forest roads with varied terrain and elevation changes. It is suitable both for those looking for an experience in nature and for those who want to test their fitness early in the racing season. The start and finish are at Vestmarksetra outdoor recreation parking area, with ample parking and public transport nearby.
course_highlights: 10 km course with 219 metres of elevation gain and 1 water station
21 km course with 413 metres of elevation gain and 2 water stations
Trail running on paths and forest roads in Vestmarka
additional: Start and finish at Vestmarksetra outdoor recreation parking area. Parking is available on site, and bus 245 runs to Kattås, about a 1.5 km walk from the race venue. Water, sports drinks and bananas are available at aid stations along the way. Live results will be available on race day. Information about bib collection, baggage storage and awards will be published closer to race day. Start and finish at Vestmarksetra. Parking at the race venue, or take bus 245 to Kattås, about 1.5 km away. Poles and listening to audio are not permitted.

name: Eikenosa opp 2027
location: Eikenosa, Ålesund, Møre og Romsdal, Norway

name: Perseløpet ¤2 - 2027
description: Perseløpet is a simple, fast race event at Ås School in Eidsvoll, designed to help runners set new personal records. The race takes place on a flat, measured 2,633-metre loop, with seven distances to choose from, ranging from 3 km to 100 km. Participants have their own nutrition table, which they pass each lap, making race nutrition simple and personal. The event offers good facilities, including changing rooms, toilets and free parking, and has a friendly atmosphere where everyone who sets a personal record gets to ring the bell at the finish.
course_highlights: Flat, measured 2,633-metre loop
Your own personal nutrition table along the course
Seven distances from 3 km to 100 km
additional: Race numbers are collected on a self-service basis at Ås School approximately two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. The race has a lap-time calculator to help plan split times. At selected races, 9th-grade students from Feiring School staff an official aid station, which also raises money for their school trip. The weather forecast is updated four times daily based on satellite data for the area around Ås School. The venue is close to public transport, with live bus departure information and train connections via Entur. The start and finish are at Ås School, Hammerås. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. Runners can have their own nutrition table.

name: HTB Valestrandsmarka Rundt 3. løp
description: HTB Valestrandsmarka Rundt is a traditional recreational race organized by Osterøy IL Friidrett. The race takes place in Valestrandsmarka on a 4.4 km course, with set start times for walkers and the main field. It is a social and inclusive race series with prizes, refreshments and sveler for participants. The race has a long history, with extensive statistics and records, and several races are held throughout the year, including Christmas and New Year’s races.
course_highlights: 4.4 km course in Valestrandsmarka
Start times: 18:45 for walkers and 19:00 for the main field
Course records are rewarded with NOK 3,000 from HTB
additional: Registration takes place at Furubakken sports ground until the start. Sveler from Toro, cordial from Saftsuse and prizes from Extra Valestrand are provided. The race does not require a license, and payment can be made via Vipps to 121337. A Christmas race is also held on 26.12 at 12:00 and a New Year’s race on 31.12 at 14:00. Race statistics and results are available from 1981 onward. Registration is open until the start. Start times are 18:45 and 19:00. Payment via Vipps 121337.

name: Endless Shore Ultra
description: Endless Shore Ultra Trail is an ultramarathon along the coastal path from Jeløy in Østfold to Nesodden in Akershus, offering an unforgettable journey through varied and scenic terrain. The race offers three distances: 50 km, 50 miles, and 100 miles, with challenging elevation profiles and spectacular views of the Oslofjord. It is organized by a nonprofit, volunteer-run organization that emphasizes sustainability and a great race experience for ultra-running enthusiasts. The start and finish are at Berger Stadium on Nesodden, with bus connections to the start locations and Oslo city center.
course_highlights: Varied coastal terrain with smooth rock, pine forest, and oak forest
Fantastic views of the Oslofjord and towns such as Son and Hvitsten
Run through the night on the 100-mile distance, with historic and scenic stops
additional: Bus transport is available from the finish area at Berger Stadium to the start locations (Drøbak for 50 km, Moss for 50 miles and 100 miles) and can be booked during registration. Medals are made from locally sourced wood, with ribbons made from recycled fabric. The race focuses on environmental responsibility, with no littering on the course and a requirement to bring your own cup to aid stations. The distances award ITRA points (50 km = 2, 50 miles = 3, 100 miles = 5). Registration includes a race bib, timing chip, food and drink stations, and a medal. Bag transport from the start to the finish is available, and a bus from Berger Stadium to the start in Drøbak can be booked for the 50 km distance. Bring your own cup; mandatory safety equipment is required.

name: Schjongs5ern
location: AKA Arena, Hønefoss idrettspark, Hønefoss, Norway
description: Schjonsfemmern is a friendly running event at Femmern, with distances for all levels, from 5 km to children’s races. The event offers scenic, accurately measured courses combining nature trails and asphalt along the beautiful Storelva, with the highest point in Søndre Park. It takes place by the ice hockey arena in Hønefoss Idrettspark and offers a unique atmosphere for both beginners and experienced runners. All participants receive a medal, and there are cash prizes for the 5 km race as well as many prize draws. After the race, participants can easily find photos of themselves through a photo service.
course_highlights: Fast, officially measured course combining nature trails and asphalt
Runs along the beautiful Storelva, with the highest point in Søndre Park
The children’s race starts and finishes at the venue, and all children receive a medal
additional: Race bibs are distributed at the finish area through a self-service system. The 5 km race has electronic timing, with the timing chip integrated into the race bib; the children’s races are not timed. Participants can choose to run the 5 km without timing. Cash prizes are awarded for the 5 km race (women and men). Everyone receives a finisher’s medal at the finish. Results are published on RaceDays. To comply with GDPR, photos from the children’s races are not published. The start and finish are at AKA Arena in Hønefoss Idrettspark. The 5 km can be run with or without electronic timing. The children’s races are untimed, and all children receive a medal.

description: Ulriken Opp is a popular uphill race in Bergen that takes you to the top of Ulriken, the highest of the seven mountains surrounding the city, with spectacular views of Bergen and the North Sea. The race is suitable for all levels, from competitive runners to recreational runners and families, and offers three distances: the Grieg Oppstemten Opp competitive category, the Drevelin Montana Classic recreational and fitness category, and CaniCross, for running with a dog. All start from Montana and finish at the summit of Ulriken, at 605 metres above sea level. The event offers a social and challenging experience, with a mass start and refreshments available in the finish area.
course_highlights: 1.75 km course with 420 metres of elevation gain from Montana to the summit of Ulriken
Start at Montana gravel field, via Johan Blyttsvei and Oppstemten
Finish at Ulriksmasten, at 605 metres above sea level, with views of Bergen and the North Sea
additional: All categories start together from Montana. The competitive category starts at 11:30, the recreational and fitness category at 10:30, and CaniCross at 10:00. The finish area by Skyskraperen Restaurant and Café offers refreshments and outdoor seating for 250 people. Training races are held before the main race, with prizes and an opportunity to socialise. Three categories: Grieg Oppstemten Opp (competitive), Drevelin Montana Classic (recreational and fitness), and CaniCross. CaniCross has a limited number of places. Parking at Bergen Hostel Montana is listed at 55 kr; public transport is recommended.

name: Bjørndalenmila
description: Bjørndalenmila is a World Athletics-certified road race with a measured course that meets international standards. The race offers officially certified results, making it possible to set a personal best. The course is fast and easy to run, making it perfect for runners who want to test their fitness, whether their goal is a new personal best or an enjoyable race experience.
course_highlights: World Athletics-certified, measured course
Fast, easy-to-run asphalt course
Officially certified results for personal bests

name: Namsosløpet 2027

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Namsosløpet 3,5 km/8 km uten tid kr. 200,-

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Namsosløpet 3,5 km/8 km med tid kr. 350,-

late_fee.price: 300 kr uten tid / 450 kr med tid

description: Namsosløpet is a long-standing race in Namdalen, with 3.5 km and 8 km routes, as well as a certified 21 km half marathon. The race is suitable for everyone, whether you want to walk, jog or run, and takes place in beautiful surroundings on a mix of paved and gravel roads. The start and finish are in central Namsos, and the event has been held for many years. Welcome to an enjoyable running experience in Trøndelag!
course_highlights: Routes of 3.5 km, 8 km and 21 km (half marathon)
Start and finish in central Namsos
Routes on paved and gravel roads in scenic surroundings
additional: Race bibs can be collected in the start area on Friday, June 5, from 17:00–20:00 and Saturday, June 6, from 10:00–14:00. Mass start: 3.5 km at 14:00 and 8 km at 14:10. Free parking throughout the town on race day. Businesses can request a code and pay the entry fee for their employees. All prices exclude the license fee.

name: Nordlo Sentrumsløpet Haugesund
