description: Nordlo Sentrumsløpet Haugesund is a fast, officially measured road race starting and finishing at Rådhusplassen in Haugesund. The event offers a 10 km race consisting of two 5 km laps, as well as a new 5 km race on the same route. It is suitable for all levels, from beginners to elite runners, and creates a festive atmosphere in the city centre with closed roads and lively crowds. A children’s race is also held for the youngest participants, and there are opportunities to socialise after the race.
course_highlights: The 10 km route passes through the pedestrian street in Haraldsgaten, around the city park and along Salhusvegen to Karmsund videregående skole
The 5 km route follows the same course as the 10 km race, but covers one lap
Start and finish at Rådhusplassen, with roads closed to traffic
additional: The children’s race starts at 11:00 and covers approximately 500 m for ages 0–12. There is no timing, and all participants receive a medal. The 5 km race starts at 12:00, the elite 10 km at 13:00 and the main 10 km field at 13:20. Pacers are available, and electronic timing includes gun time and split times. A water and squash station is provided halfway around the course. AfterRUN, with food and drinks for sale, takes place after the race. Race numbers can be collected in advance at Anton Sport Oasen or on race day at Rådhusplassen. Changing facilities and bag storage are available at the start/finish. Roads are closed to traffic during the race. The course is stated to be certified by World Athletics with an AIMS-B certificate. Roads are closed to traffic during the race.

name: Saudafjellet Maraton 2027
description: Saudafjellet Marathon 2027 takes place on Saturday, May 22, in Sauda, Rogaland. This unique race offers spectacular scenery across Saudafjellet, one of Norway’s most impressive mountain passes. Participants can choose between the marathon, half marathon, or Gruvemila, and every distance offers a memorable experience in beautiful surroundings. The race starts at 12:00, and everyone is welcome to enjoy a challenging and wonderful day of running.
course_highlights: Run across Saudafjellet, a spectacular mountain pass
Choose between the marathon, half marathon, and Gruvemila
Scenic surroundings in Sauda, Rogaland
additional: Tickets are sold through EQ Timing via the Aett platform. The event runs from 12:00 to 15:00. Aett offers simple registration and ticket sales administration, with the option to pay at the door. The start time is listed as 12:00. Registration is through EQ Timing, and the organizer has announced an early bird offer.

name: KK-mila
description: KKmila is a friendly race in Oslo offering two distances, 5 km and 10 km, on a flat, easy-to-run course that showcases the city at its best. Thousands of participants come together for a running festival full of good vibes, a sense of achievement and energy. The course follows the waterfront, passes through parks and urban areas, and visits iconic locations such as Aker Brygge and Bjørvika, offering a varied and memorable route. The event also focuses on community and supporting charity through its partnership with Right To Play.
course_highlights: Flat, easy-to-run course along the waterfront and through the city’s parks
Passes well-known areas such as Frognerkilen, Tjuvholmen, Aker Brygge and Bjørvika
Varied, memorable route with a maritime feel and modern architecture
additional: The 5 km starts at 12:00 and the 10 km at 14:00. The race offers pacers, timing, changing rooms, showers and toilets. Participants receive a goodie bag and this year’s medal. Bag storage and a warm-up before the start are available. The event also includes a social after-run dinner for businesses and groups. The race supports the charity Right To Play, and one lucky winner will be drawn to receive a trip to KKcamp in Portugal. The Heia class is untimed, and participants are ranked alphabetically. The listed course starts and finish locations are from 2026 and therefore cannot be confirmed for 2027.

name: 4625løpet 2027
description: The 4625 Run takes place on Flekkerøy, a gem at the edge of the open sea just outside Kristiansand. The race offers varied terrain with many beautiful viewpoints and is suitable for both beginners and elite runners. The course passes through idyllic Southern Norwegian gardens, over the iconic bridge at Skibbusundet, and along the archipelago with views of Oksøy Lighthouse. After crossing the finish line, runners can look forward to a medal, recognition and well-earned refreshments.
course_highlights: Varied terrain with Kodak-friendly viewpoints
Run across the bridge at Skibbusundet, one of the island’s most photographed spots
Views of Oksøy Lighthouse and the beautiful archipelago
additional: The children’s race starts at 10:15 and 10:30, with courses of approximately 300 metres and 1 km. Toilets and changing rooms are available at Flekkerøyhallen, and bag storage is provided in the start area. Electronic timing is used for the 4625 Run, with a minimum age of 11. A water and sports drink station is located about halfway along the course at Geitodden. All participants receive a medal and pizza from Pizzabakeren after the race. Parking is available at the sports facility. Race numbers are distributed on race day from 09:00 and must be worn visibly. Separate children’s race. The main race starts at 11:00.

name: SpareBank 1 Vartdalsstranda Halvmaraton 2027
location: Vartdal skule, Vartdal, Ørsta, Møre og Romsdal, Norway
distance_verbose: Halvmaraton, 10 km, 7 km, 5 km, 0.5 km, 0.1 km
description: SpareBank1 Vartdalsstranda Half Marathon is an inclusive race organized by the non-profit organization Team Joggis, with 100% of the entry fee going to the Norwegian Cancer Society. The race takes place on the fourth Saturday in May and runs through the beautiful valleys of Vartdal, surrounded by high mountains, making for a spectacular and memorable running experience. Participants can choose from several distances, from the half marathon and 10 km to a recreational run and the children’s race, Mini Joggis. The event combines the joy of running with support for a good cause and has strong local involvement.
course_highlights: The race runs through the beautiful valleys of Vartdal and Nordre Vartdal, surrounded by high mountains
The half marathon has 3 water stations along the route (4 km, 10 km, 20 km)
The 10 km race has a water station at 4 km
additional: The recreational category has a flexible start time between 09:00 and 11:00. There is a group warm-up with Mova Ørsta and Bjørnis before the start. Changing facilities and showers are available at Vartdal School. A kiosk serves grilled food and other refreshments. Registration for Mini Joggis and the recreational run takes place at the race office on race day. All participants are entered into prize draws, but must be present at the awards ceremony to win. The half-marathon course has three water stations, and the 10 km course has one at 4 km. Changing facilities and showers are available at Vartdal School. Mini Joggis is 100 or 500 metres, and registration for the children’s race and recreational run takes place at the race office on race day. According to the organizer’s website, 100% of the entry fee goes to the Norwegian Cancer Society.

name: Askøy-På-Langs 2027
organizer: Askøy Turlag, Askøy Orienteringslag og Ask Friidrett
description: Askøy På Langs is a spectacular running and walking event that runs from south to north across Askøy. Participants can choose between three distances: a half distance of 16 km, a full distance of 37.3 km, or an extreme marathon distance. The course offers varied terrain, including the island’s highest point and dense forests, with the start in Kleppestø and the finish at Herdla Museum at Herdla Fort. The event offers both walking and running categories, and start times are carefully planned to avoid conflicts between runners and walkers. There is also increased toilet capacity and photographers along the way to capture the experience.
course_highlights: Varied terrain over the island’s highest point
Course from Kleppestø to Herdla Museum at Herdla Fort
Start times arranged to avoid conflicts between runners and walkers
additional: The full-distance race starts at Kleppestø quay at 08:00, while the half distance (16 km) starts from Træet School at 12:00. All distances finish at Herdla Museum at Herdla Fort. Basic first-aid supplies are available at the start/finish and at the food stations. Toilet capacity has been increased at Kleppestø quay and Træet. A photographer will be present along the course at a marked location. The full distance starts at 08:00 and the half distance at 12:00. All distances finish at Herdla Museum at Herdla Fort. The event is run on a voluntary, non-commercial basis.

name: Lustraløpet
price_range: Aktiv klasse: 250 kr + eventuell lisens; trimklasse: 150 kr; familie i trimklassen: 300 kr

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Påmeldingsavgift aktiv klasse: kr. 250,-+ ev. lisens om du ikkje har heilårslisens.

description: Lustraløpet is a traditional 10 km road race on asphalt, starting at Neshøgdi and finishing at Luster oppvekstsenter. The race is held annually and is known for its beautiful scenery and excellent prizes made by local producers and artists. Great emphasis is placed on volunteer effort to ensure a successful event. In addition to the competitive class, there is a recreational class for those who want a social and scenic outing without timing.
course_highlights: 10 km road race on asphalt
Starts at Neshøgdi and finishes at Luster oppvekstsenter
Scenic surroundings and prizes featuring local art
additional: Race numbers can be collected at Nes/by the start no later than 13:45. Free shuttle buses run between Luster and Nes, but travelling by your own transport is recommended due to summer traffic. Changing rooms with showers are available in the finish area. The recreational class starts between 11:00 and 13:30. All participants receive free betasuppe (soup) with flatbread and cordial at the finish. A kiosk sells ice cream, soft drinks, lapper (Norwegian pancakes), betasuppe, cordial and hot dogs. Cash prizes are awarded for the sprint prize, best time and course record. The competitive class is for participants aged 13 and over. Free shuttle buses run between Luster and Nes, changing rooms with showers are available at the finish, and participants are served betasuppe with flatbread and cordial. Prices are based on the published information for 2026 and may change before the 2027 race.

name: Åsaneløpet 2027
price_range: 150–400 kr, i tillegg til lisens fra 13 år
description: Åsaneløpet is a traditional fun run in the heart of Åsane, Bergen, inviting the whole family to take part. The race offers 5 km and 10 km distances, as well as a children’s race where every child receives a medal and the first 800 participants receive a T-shirt. The event offers a fun race-day atmosphere with a warm-up, awards ceremony, and activities such as a bouncy castle and face painting, and is suitable for both young and adult runners.
course_highlights: Run in the heart of Åsane with a lead bicycle riding ahead of the runners
100-metre children’s race for the youngest participants, with a medal for everyone
Group warm-up with MOVA before the start
additional: Race bibs and T-shirts (children only) can be collected from 11:00 on race day outside Building A at Thon Senter Åsane. The warm-up for the children’s race with MOVA starts at 11:45. The children’s race (approx. 100 m) starts at 12:00. Group warm-up with MOVA at 12:50. The 5 km and 10 km races start at 13:00, with a lead bicycle riding ahead of the runners. Awards and activities such as a bouncy castle, face painting, and athletics trials take place after the race. Children below 3rd grade run 100 metres. There is a water station at the turnaround point on the 10 km route. All children receive a medal, and the first 800 participants receive a T-shirt.

name: Jentebølgen - Kristiansand
description: Jentebølgen in Kristiansand is an inclusive public health run taking place on 24 May 2027, with the start and finish at Tresse. The course is approximately 5 km long and suitable for everyone, whether you want to walk, jog or run. The event focuses on community, a sense of achievement and mental health, and supports Mental Helse Ungdom with NOK 10 per race entry sold. It is a colourful and lively experience with entertainment, medals for all participants, and the option to take part as a company or sports club.
course_highlights: Approximately 5 km course starting and finishing at Tresse, Kristiansand
Accessible course that also allows strollers
Colourful Color Run with costumes, a mini-concert and medals for everyone
additional: Race numbers can be collected at the event site two hours before the start, but collecting them in advance is recommended to avoid queues. Stands open one hour before the race, and entertainment begins 30–45 minutes before the start. Jackets and bags can be left in a tent by the event office; storage is at your own risk. Companions can participate for free upon showing a companion certificate. There is no official timing, but participants can use their own watch. There is no timing, and all participants receive a medal. Race numbers can be collected at the event site on race day.

name: Jentebølgen - Stavanger
description: Jentebølgen in Stavanger is an inclusive public health run organised in cooperation with Mental Helse Ungdom. The course is between 5 and 6 kilometres long, and participants can walk, jog or run on accessible terrain. The event offers a colourful and lively experience, with entertainment, a mini-concert before the start and a medal for everyone who finishes. Jentebølgen is more than a race—it is a place for people of all ages to connect through achievement, joy and community.
course_highlights: The course is 5–6 km long and accessible
Color Run with colourful costumes and colour along the course
Mini-concert featuring young artists before the start
additional: Race numbers can be collected at the venue two hours before the start, or in advance to avoid queues. Stands open one hour before the race starts. Jackets and bags can be left in a tent by the event office; storage is at your own risk. Companions participate for free upon presentation of a companion certificate. All participants receive a medal. Companies and sports clubs can register groups using dedicated group tickets. All participants receive a medal. Race numbers can be collected at the venue on race day. The venue for the 2027 event has not yet been announced.

name: Jentebølgen - Bergen
description: Jentebølgen Bergen 2027 brings together girls and women of all ages for an afternoon filled with a sense of achievement, community, and a great atmosphere. The event takes place on 26 May 2027 in Bergen and invites you to enjoy running and energy with friends, colleagues, or family. The entry fee includes insurance and the ticket fee, creating a unique sense of community on the starting line.
course_highlights: A course of between 5 and 6 km
Participants can walk, jog, or run
A handicap-accessible course
additional: The entry fee includes insurance and the ticket fee. The event runs from 17:30 to 20:00. Participants are encouraged to join with friends, colleagues, or family for a social and energetic running experience. There is no timing, and all participants receive a medal. The entry fee includes insurance and the ticket fee. The venue has not yet been announced.

name: Kodal Ultra Trail 50K

tiers.label: tier_1

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Fra 1. mars øker prisen til kr. 600,00 frem til løpsdagen.

description: Kodal Ultra Trail 50k is a challenging and beautiful trail race taking place for the very first time on Saturday, May 29, 2027, in Kodal, Sandefjord. The race consists of a gently rolling 5 km loop, with a start every hour on the hour from 09:00 to 18:00, for a total of 10 laps, or 50 km. Participants must complete each lap within the hour to be able to start the next one. The race ends at 19:00 with the winner being announced. The event is social and inclusive, with prizes for completing 25 km and 50 km, and 10% of the surplus goes to the Norwegian Association for Children with Congenital Heart Disease. There will also be activities and a children’s race at the stadium during the event.
course_highlights: Gently rolling 5 km loop through varied, technical terrain
The course runs through deep forests in the heart of Vestfold, with trails, hills, and a field
Start and finish at the sports ground, with spectators cheering runners on during the final 200 meters
additional: The race starts and finishes at the sports ground of Kodal Idrettslag. Coffee, cordial, and cold water will be served during the event, and there will be a kiosk at the stadium. Participants must have a valid license from the Norwegian Athletics Federation, either an annual license or a one-day license purchased during registration. Participants can rest and spend time on the grass between laps, but only participants may access the rest area. Support is permitted only outdoors in the start and finish area. Starts take place every hour from 09:00, with the final lap starting at 18:00. A children’s race and activities for children are planned. Ten percent of the surplus goes to the Norwegian Association for Children with Congenital Heart Disease (FFHB).

name: Energistafetten
description: Energistafetten is a festival-like relay race held in Stavanger, inspired by the atmosphere of the Holmenkollstafetten and the Tour de France. The race consists of 10 stages of varying lengths and elevation profiles, and teams can have 6–10 members, whether colleagues, friends, or neighbors. The event emphasizes togetherness, enjoyment, and team spirit, and also includes a sprint prize in collaboration with Red Bull. After the race, participants are invited to AfterRun for live music, food, and socializing.
course_highlights: 10 stages ranging from approximately 750 to 2,500 meters
Approximately 14 km total, with 112 meters of ascent and 119 meters of descent
Start and finish in the Forum area, Stavanger
additional: Teams can have 6–10 members, and some participants may run multiple stages. All participants must be at least 16 years old, and the age limit for AfterRun is 18. No license or insurance is required, but optional insurance is available. A sprint prize with a cash award is held, with the prize donated to a good cause. After the race, AfterRun features live music and food in collaboration with Fjåge i Vågen. The Red Bull sprint prize includes a gift certificate worth 10,000 kroner, which is donated to a good cause in the region. AfterRun is held in collaboration with Fjåge i Vågen.

tiers.label: tier_1

description: Stomperudløpet is a major running festival in Sørum, starting and finishing at Stomperud Stadion in Lørenfallet. The event offers four distances suitable for everyone, on varied courses featuring gravel roads, trails and some asphalt. The shortest distances take place on the athletics track, and the race has received positive feedback for its beautiful courses. This inclusive event encourages children, young people and adults to take part and enjoy an active day in scenic surroundings.
course_highlights: A mix of gravel roads, trails and some asphalt
The shortest distances take place on the athletics track
Start and finish at Stomperud Stadion in Lørenfallet
additional: Registration is open until 11:00 on race day, with a late registration fee of NOK 100 for adults and NOK 50 for children. Participants registered for the full Stomperudkarusell for women/men pay a reduced price when registering at the secretariat during race 1 or 2 of the series. Distances listed for previous editions are 15 km, 6 km, 400 m and 300 m. The prices on the organizer’s website apply to the 2026 edition and have therefore not been used as price information for 2027.

description: Bergensløpet is a traditional race that has returned after almost 30 years, originating in 1976. The race takes place in beautiful surroundings in Bergen, with the start and finish in historic Nygårdsparken. Participants can choose between two distances, 5 km and 10 km, on a fast, scenic course along Store Lungegårdsvann and Møllendal. A free children’s race is also held for the youngest participants in idyllic surroundings around the pond in the park.
course_highlights: Fast course along Store Lungegårdsvann and Møllendal
Start and finish in historic Nygårdsparken
The 10 km course consists of two laps of the 5 km course
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 09:45 at the Vitalitetssenteret by Møhlenpris sports ground. Toilets are available at bib collection and in the clubhouse buildings. The children’s race starts at 12:00, the 5 km at 13:00, and the 10 km at 14:00. The children’s race is approximately 500 metres, with no timing or rankings, and all children receive a medal. The spring edition features a 5 km, a 10 km, and a children’s race. The listed start times for previous editions are 13:00 for the 5 km, 14:00 for the 10 km, and 12:00 for the children’s race.

name: Hurdalsjøen Trail Race
location: Hurdalsjøen Hotell & Spa, Skredderbakkveien 9, 2090 Hurdal, Norway
description: Hurdalsjøen Trail Race is a trail race held at Hurdalsjøen Hotell & Spa in Hurdal, Akershus. The race offers four distances from 5 km to 23 km, across varied terrain featuring technical sections, flowing trails and spectacular viewpoints. Participants get to experience the magical natural surroundings of Hurdalsjøen, with challenges suited to both beginners and experienced runners. The event also emphasizes community, a sense of achievement and nature experiences, with the start and finish at the hotel, which offers facilities such as a spa and good food.
course_highlights: Terrain with technical sections and flowing trails
Spectacular views from Buråsen and Buråskollen (540 m above sea level)
23 km distance with 1,000 metres of elevation gain and views over Hurdal and Hurdalsjøen
additional: All participants in the same distance start at the same time. The courses are marked with colour codes that match the race bibs. Carrying a mobile phone during the race is mandatory. There are 1–3 passes by aid stations, depending on the distance, and runners may refill their own bottles. Parking is recommended at Lundbybakken or Steinerskolen. The start and finish are at Hurdalsjøen Hotell & Spa. The start and finish are at Hurdalsjøen Hotell & Spa, Skredderbakkveien 9, 2090 Hurdal. The courses are marked, and carrying a mobile phone is mandatory. Free parking is recommended at Lundbybakken or Steinerskolen.

name: Konnerudløpet
description: Konnerudløpet 2027 takes place on May 29 in the scenic surroundings of Konnerud in Drammen. The race offers distances for everyone, from a children’s race to 21 km, and is suitable both for those who want to test their speed and those looking for a pleasant run. There will be a great atmosphere, varied courses and experiences for all ages, with free childcare and prizes for all participating children. Konnerud IL looks forward to welcoming runners to a wonderful race celebration marking the club’s 100th anniversary.
course_highlights: Scenic surroundings at Konnerud
Varied courses with distances of 5 km, 10 km and 21 km
Family-friendly, with a dedicated children’s race and prizes for all children
additional: Free childcare is available for the youngest children while their parents run. Every participating child receives a prize. The organizer lists free childcare for the youngest children and a prize for every child who participates. Registration is available via the race website.

name: Trondheimstafetten
price_range: 2500-2900 kr for hovedklassene; UNG-stafetten fra 1000 kr
description: Trondheimstafetten is a traditional 10-stage relay race that runs through central Trondheim and the surrounding areas. The race brings together teams from companies, clubs, schools and groups of friends, offering a social and inclusive running experience focused on team spirit and achievement. There is also a dedicated UNG relay for children and young people, with 6 stages in Nidarø Park and Trondheim Stadion. The start and finish are in Skanseparken, and the race welcomes a wide age range, with young people able to take part in selected stages.
course_highlights: 10 stages through central Trondheim and the surrounding areas
Start and finish in Skanseparken
The UNG relay has 6 stages in Nidarø Park and Trondheim Stadion
additional: Race bibs and diplomas can be collected together at Trondheim Spektrum in the days before the race and on race day. The relay baton is handed out no later than 30 minutes before the start at Skansenparken. There are drink stations at Kristiansten Fortress and Sverresborg Museum. Toilets and showers are available at Trondheim Spektrum and at the exchange points. Runners choose a start wave based on their expected finish time to improve race flow and competition. The main relay has ten stages, while the UNG relay has six and is for children and young people aged 6 to 15. Registration involves choosing a class and start wave.

name: Kragerø Sommerløp
description: Kragerø Summer Run is a community celebration in the heart of Kragerø, with 5 km and 10 km distances and a free children’s race. The race starts at Jernbanetorget and offers a fast, scenic loop through the town centre, with a great atmosphere and entertainment along the route. This accessible street race is suitable for all levels, whether you take part alone, with family, friends or colleagues. The 700-metre children’s race is free and gives every child a fun experience and a medal. The event also includes activities, stands and socialising before and after the races.
course_highlights: A fast, scenic loop through the heart of Kragerø town centre
A spectator-friendly route with entertainment along the way
A 700-metre children’s race with a medal for every child
additional: Race numbers can be collected at Sport1 Kragerø on Friday 29 May from 16:00 to 18:00, or on race day from 12:00 at Jernbanetorget. Please collect your race number no later than 30 minutes before your start. A relaxed social run (SAYSKY Shake-Out Run) will take place on Friday 29 May at 18:00, followed by sweet buns, coffee and cordial. No registration is required for the children’s race; just show up. Participants are advised not to run with their own music in their ears. Activities and entertainment for children and spectators will be available on race day. The distances are 5 km, 10 km and a free 700-metre children’s race. The children’s race requires no registration and is recommended for children aged 2 to 10. The minimum age for timed results is 12. Prices apply to the information provided for 2026; the date 29 May 2027 is not confirmed in the sources.

name: Kvennstuguløpet 2027
description: Kvennstuguløpet is an annual race organized by Vallset IL in the beautiful surroundings around Kvennstugua in Vallset. The race attracts both young and adult runners and offers a wonderful race-day celebration with strong performances from local athletes. The event has an inclusive atmosphere focused on the joy of sport and community, and it is an important tradition in the local community. Participants can look forward to a range of distances and a great day in scenic surroundings.
course_highlights: Run in the beautiful surroundings around Kvennstugua
A range of distances, with competitions for both women and men
Strong local involvement and a wonderful race-day celebration
additional: The race includes distances such as 2.5 km and 5 km, with separate classes for women and men. The event is supported by many volunteers and has a strong club community. It takes place in glorious summer weather and is a social, inclusive race-day celebration.

name: Vestfold Historic Ultra Trail
description: Vestfold Historic Ultra Trail (VHUT) is a challenging trail ultramarathon through the best terrain in northern Vestfold, with only 6% asphalt on the long course. The race spans two counties and five municipalities, and runners pass many places of local historical significance. The course is unmarked, so participants must navigate using a GPS track, creating an authentic trail experience with the motto “challenging but fair.” Accommodation and transport are offered to make participation easier, along with drop-bag stations and aid stations along the way. VHUT welcomes you to a challenging and scenic ultrarunning experience in a historic setting.
course_highlights: Only 6% asphalt on the long course (147 km)
The course passes through 2 counties and 5 municipalities with local historical significance
Trail race with a challenging but fair course and GPS navigation
additional: Runners use GPS trackers. Accommodation is available from Friday to Saturday, with access to a WC, shower and kitchenette. Transport from Hengsrød to the start is offered for the 50 and 87 km distances. There are drop-bag stations for the 147 km (2 stations) and 87 km (1 station), with food and drinks provided. Aid stations with light refreshments are located at Hajern and Langevann, about 20 km before the finish. Parking is limited at the start/finish and checkpoints, and private support is not permitted at Hajern or Langevann. All runners must download the updated GPX files before the race. GPS trackers are used. Accommodation before the race and transport to the start for the 50 km and 87 km distances are offered; drop-bag stations are listed for the 87 km and 147 km.

description: EcoTrail Oslo is an environmentally conscious trail race offering five distances in the woodland areas near the city, with the finish at Huk, Bygdøy. The race is suitable for both beginners and experienced runners, with distances from 10 km to 80 km, and features scenic surroundings and varied terrain. The courses combine forest roads, technical trails and some paved sections, offering a unique opportunity to experience Oslo’s outdoor areas and cultural history. The event places strong emphasis on sustainability and the environment, and includes services such as baggage transport, timing, and food and drink stations along the way.
course_highlights: Varied terrain with forest roads, technical trails and approximately 9% paved sections
The course passes through Oslo’s woodland areas, including Akerselva, Maridalsvannet and Sognsvann
Panoramic views of Oslo and a stretch along the Oslofjord, with the finish at Huk, Bygdøy
additional: The entry fee includes timing, participant prizes, baggage transport from start to finish, toilet hire, marked courses, an electric bus shuttle to the 31 km start, and food and drink stations along the way. There is no drop bag, and support is only permitted at the stations. Participants receive sports drink, water and light food in the finish area. Merino wool participant shirts are also available at a reduced price. Distances offered are 10, 21, 31, 50 and 80 km, as well as a 21 km walking distance. EcoTrail Oslo is described as an environmentally conscious trail race.

name: Tromsøstafetten 2027
description: Tromsøstafetten is a new celebration of community in central Tromsø, focused on togetherness, atmosphere and enjoyment. The race consists of eight exciting and challenging legs with varying surfaces, distances and elevation. There is room for everyone, whatever your pace, and you are encouraged to take part with family, friends, a sports club or colleagues and experience the relay spirit together. The start and finish will be near central Tromsø, and the race offers a unique opportunity to run in beautiful surroundings with a great atmosphere along the course.
course_highlights: Eight varied legs with different surfaces, distances and elevation
Start and finish near central Tromsø
Several different categories to suit all levels and paces
additional: The minimum age is 13 (born in 2014). Medals will be awarded to the three best teams in each category, and prizes will also be drawn among all participating teams. Results will be published during and after the event. The course and start/finish location will be announced in early 2027. The minimum age is 13. The course and exact start and finish locations will be announced in early 2027. Medals will be awarded to the three best teams in each category, and prizes will be drawn among participating teams.

name: Farsund Maraton 2027
description: Farsund Marathon is one of Norway’s most beautiful races, running through spectacular natural and cultural landscapes. The race starts in idyllic downtown Farsund and continues out towards Lista, with distances suited to both recreational and competitive runners. The courses are designed to give participants a unique running experience, with good support from course marshals and refreshment and food stations along the way. The event has a friendly atmosphere and offers prizes to age-category winners and the fastest runners.
course_highlights: Run through spectacular natural and cultural landscapes
Start and finish in idyllic downtown Farsund
Refreshment stations every 5 km on the marathon and half marathon, serving water, cordial, cola and bananas
additional: Race administration is located in the auditorium at Eilert Sundt VGS, approximately 200 m from Torvet. Bib pickup and information hours are Friday 16:00–20:00 and Saturday 08:00–18:00. All participants receive a medal at the finish, and trophies are awarded to age-category winners, with gift prizes for the three fastest times in the marathon, half marathon, 10 km and 5 km for men and women. This year’s T-shirt is given to the first 1,000 people to register. Toilets are located at the start and finish, as well as at Lista Lighthouse and Borshavn on the marathon course. Start times may be adjusted slightly, and time recording ends at approximately 16:00. A registration fee of NOK 15 applies, and a Norwegian Athletics Federation licence is automatically added at registration for those without an annual licence. Registration for 2027 opens on 1 December 2026. A NOK 15 surcharge applies to all registrations.

name: Straumemila 2027

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Barnemila er gratis ved påmelding før løpsdagen

description: Straumemila Running Festival is an annual event offering challenging and scenic routes in the beautiful surroundings of Straume. The courses follow walking paths by Skogavatnet and Ebbesvikvatnet, through Sartorlunden park and Straume town centre, combining asphalt and trails. The festival emphasises community, fun and competition, with a wide range of events for children and adults. Events include the 10 km, 5 km and Barnemila, with officially measured courses approved by the Norwegian Athletics Federation.
course_highlights: The routes pass along Skogavatnet and Ebbesvikvatnet
A mix of walking paths and asphalt
The 10 km course consists of two figure-eight-shaped laps, passing through the spectator area five times
additional: Warm-up starts at 10:40. The 10 km and 5 km start together at 11:00. The prize ceremony starts at 12:15. The relay starts at 12:35. Barnemila starts at 13:40, with a group warm-up from 13:10. Barnemila is 2.3 km long and partly follows the same route as the 5 km and 10 km. A licence is required to participate; a one-day licence is available. There is an administration fee of NOK 25 per entry. Barnemila is free to enter before race day; otherwise, it costs NOK 100 plus fees. The event takes place at Idrettsvegen 50, 5353 Straume.

description: Grorudløpet is part of the Oslo Running Festival and offers a varied 12 km course that starts and finishes in Grorudparken. The race follows the Alna River and winds through Lillomarka’s enchanting trails, combining technical trails with gravel and asphalt. In 2027, the course will run in the opposite direction for a better experience, with trail running at the start and a downhill gravel section toward the finish. This race is suited to those looking for a scenic and challenging running experience in Oslo.
course_highlights: A varied 12 km course with trails, gravel and asphalt
Follows the Alna River and runs through Lillomarka
The course is reversed in 2027 for a better trail-running experience at the start
additional: Race bibs can be picked up from Löplabbet Oslo sentrum from 7 April. The same race bib is used throughout the series. The course will only be marked for the mass start. GPX files and course maps are available to download. A replacement race bib can be purchased for NOK 75 if yours is lost or damaged. You can run on your own from 21 to 30 May. The mass start is on Sunday 30 May 2027 at 11:00. The listed day-ticket prices are early-bird prices.

name: Jessheim Halvmaraton
description: Jessheim Half Marathon is a summer race offering both half marathon and 5 km distances, as well as a free children’s race for the youngest participants. The courses are flat and fast, run on asphalt around Jessheim, and start and finish at Jessheim Athletics Stadium. They are certified according to World Athletics criteria. The event is run by volunteers and supports sports for children and young people in Ullensaker/Kisa. It aims to provide an enjoyable experience for both recreational runners and competitive runners, with water stations and pacers for several finish times.
course_highlights: Flat and fast asphalt courses around Jessheim
Certified according to World Athletics criteria
Water stations on the half marathon course at 7 km, 10.5 km, 17 km and at the finish
additional: Children’s race for ages 0–12, approximately 600 metres, with free entry. Race numbers can be collected at Jessheim Ice and Multipurpose Hall on Saturday and Sunday. The half marathon has an early start at 10:00 for runners with an estimated finish time of over 3 hours. Pacers are available for several finish times in both the 5 km and half marathon. All distances finish at Jessheim Athletics Stadium. Distances: half marathon, 5 km, and a free children’s race of approximately 600 metres for children aged 0 to 12. The courses are stated to be certified according to World Athletics criteria. Proceeds go to sports for children and young people in Ullensaker/Kisa.

name: Risørløpet 2027
description: Risørløpet 2027 is organized by Risør idrettslag and is a trail race held at Kjempesteinsmyra in Risør. The race takes place on varied terrain and offers a wonderful nature experience for participants of all ages. The event is a tradition that brings together local and visiting runners for an enjoyable day of sport and community. The race starts on Sunday, May 30 at 11:00.
course_highlights: Trail race through varied scenery
The race takes place in the Kjempesteinsmyra area
A wonderful nature experience in Risør
additional: Organized by Risør idrettslag. The race starts at 11:00. No pricing or registration details were found on the website. No information about start waves, participant capacity, or late registration. Free 400-meter track race for children, with no ranking or timing. The children's race starts at 11:10, and registration takes place on arrival.

name: Vettisløpet

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: 18-39 år og deretter 10 års klasser kr 250

description: Vettisløpet is a traditional race held on the last Sunday in May in the beautiful Utladalen valley, Øvre Årdal. The race offers a challenging and scenic course that attracts both competitive runners and recreational participants. It is a wonderful opportunity to experience the most beautiful race of spring amid spectacular scenery, with a joint start for the competitive categories and a separate start time for the recreational category.
course_highlights: The race takes place in scenic Utladalen, with varied terrain
Joint start for competitive categories at 13:00
Recreational category starts from 11:00 at Skåri
additional: Registration for the recreational category is at Skåri. The latest possible registration is at 12:30 on race day. Prizes are awarded for the fastest time in each competitive category, the fastest time for women and men, and a new course record. The race has recreational and competitive categories. The official website lists this year’s race as starting at 13:00.

name: Jentebølgen - Molde
description: Jentebølgen in Molde is an inclusive public health run held on 31 May 2027 in collaboration with Mental Helse Ungdom. The event is between 5 and 6 kilometres long, and participants can walk, jog or run on accessible terrain. The event offers a colourful and lively experience with entertainment, a mini-concert before the start, and a medal for everyone who finishes. Jentebølgen is more than a race—it is a place for people of all ages to come together, build confidence and share in the joy of community.
course_highlights: The course is between 5 and 6 km long, with a detailed course map available
Accessible course that also allows participation in a wheelchair
Colourful Color Run with costumes, laughter and a mini-concert before the start
additional: Race numbers can be collected at the venue two hours before the start, but collecting them in advance is recommended to avoid queues. Jackets and bags can be left in a tent by the event office at your own risk. Companions may participate for free on presentation of a companion certificate. NOK 10 from each race number sold goes to Mental Helse Ungdom. There is no timing, and all participants receive a medal. Companions may participate for free on presentation of a companion certificate. The stands open at 17:00, and race numbers can be collected at the venue on race day.

name: Sørdalskarusellen - SpareBank1 Kanthaugløpet
description: SpareBank1 Kanthaugenløpet is the second-to-last race in the Sørdalskarusellen spring season, starting and finishing at Birkebeineren Ski Stadium in Lillehammer. The race has a long tradition dating back to 1984 and offers a varied route of approximately 5.75 km, including asphalt, trails, grass-covered Olympic trails, and some challenging sections in Lyshaugen. Both a mass-start race and a virtual race are held, and the event attracts a large field of participants each year. The start is usually at 19:00, with a single mass-start wave.
course_highlights: The route is 5.75 km long, with varied surfaces: asphalt, trails, and grass-covered Olympic trails
The route passes through the floodlit trail, crosses bridges, and follows the canal with views of the Mesna River
Challenging sections in Lyshaugen include some forestry work and terrain that requires caution
additional: Registration closes at 18:00 on the day of the mass start. Race numbers can be collected at the tent by the red artwork from 17:45. There is a water station in the finish area and a toilet in Skistua. Lillehammer Red Cross Search and Rescue Corps is present in the finish area. Parking is available at the ski stadium, with the Apcoa flow payment system. A virtual race is also held, starting a few days before the mass start. Listed on 2 June 2027 in the Sørdalskarusellen race calendar. The registration window is listed as 29 May–1 June. The course route may vary from year to year.

name: The Arctic Triple Lofoten Ultra-Trail®
distance_verbose: 100 miles, 100 miles, 50 miles, 50 miles, 50 km, 24 km, 10 km

name: Bergen Fjellmaraton
description: Bergen Fjellmaraton is a half marathon from Montana to Skansemyren in Bergen. The course starts with a challenging climb up to Ulriken, followed by rolling terrain across Vidden and on to Vareggen, where there is a drink station. From there, the course continues towards Rundemanen and down Blåmansveien, finishing via the floodlit trail past the upper Fløibanen station to the finish at Skansemyren. The race combines beautiful scenery with challenging terrain, and the route is available to download on ut.no and in Lommekjent apps.
course_highlights: A challenging climb over the first 3 km up to Ulriken
Rolling terrain across Vidden and Vareggen, with a drink station at Vikinghytten
Finish via the floodlit trail past the upper Fløibanen station to the finish at Skansemyren
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Vikinghallen on 2 and 3 June from 10:00 to 18:00, with collection also possible on race day (without the expo). Participants must follow the marked course. All participants receive a finisher's medal. Race bibs can be transferred to another participant until 28 May. The course is marked with signs, flags and course tape. Protecting the environment and the drinking water source is important during the race. Race bibs must be collected at Vikinghallen before or on race day, not at the start in Montana. The recreational class has two start waves, and the competitive class starts at 19:30. Registration for 2027 opens in early December.

name: Neveresting Hafjell
description: Neveresting Hafjell is a unique endurance challenge held on the ski slope in Hafjell on 4–5 June 2027. Participants hike or run up the slope, take the gondola back down, and repeat as many times as they can within the allotted time. Each lap covers 590 metres of elevation gain and 3.5 kilometres. The goal is to climb as many metres as possible, with the number of laps offering the chance to match famous mountain heights such as Galdhøpiggen, Elbrus and Mount Everest. The event is open to all ages and levels, with both individual and team competitions that encourage a sense of achievement and team spirit. It’s a festive event with race-number pickup, food stations and a social dinner for teams.
course_highlights: Ski slope with 590 metres of elevation gain per lap
3.5 kilometres per lap, with a gondola ride back down between laps
Opportunity to complete up to 27 laps over 36 hours
additional: Race-number pickup and the athletes’ meeting take place the evening before and early in the morning on race day. The 36-hour event starts Friday at 07:00 and runs until Saturday evening. On Saturday, there is also a 6-hour team competition starting at 10:00, in which teams of 4 work together to complete as many laps as possible. Food stations are available along the way, and teams are invited to a social dinner with a perpetual trophy presentation after the race. Discounted accommodation is offered to participants. Participants decide for themselves how many laps to complete and when to take breaks. A corporate and team competition for teams of four is also mentioned.

name: Osterøy på tvers 2027
organizer: Osterøy IL, Mjøsdalen IL, Fotlandsvåg IL og Bruvik IL
description: Osterøy på tvers is an annual running event from Bruvik to Hosanger on Osterøy. The race is organised in collaboration between several local sports clubs and offers a great opportunity to experience the island’s varied nature and terrain. Participants can choose between the competitive and recreational classes, and the race attracts both recreational and more experienced runners. The event has a long tradition and is well established in the local community.
course_highlights: The race crosses Osterøy from Bruvik to Hosanger
Varied terrain with both asphalt and gravel
Scenic surroundings on the island
additional: The race has both a competitive class and a recreational class. Results from previous years are published on eqtiming.com. The course map is available via Strava. The event is organised in collaboration between Osterøy IL, Mjøsdalen IL, Fotlandsvåg IL and Bruvik IL. The organiser’s website has a link to the registered participants and participant overview.

name: Hagebyløpet
location: Tennisbanen i Bergsalléen, Ullevål, Oslo, Norway

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Deltakeravgift: 200 kr. for voksne over 20 år

description: Hagebyløpet is an inclusive running festival in the heart of Ullevål, Oslo, with races for all ages and levels. The event offers three distances: a 500-meter children’s race in Halsparken, the 1609-meter Engelskmila, which is open to everyone, and a timed 5 km race for young people and adults. The courses run across grass, trails, and low-traffic streets. It’s a festive event with a great atmosphere, entertainment, and activities for the whole family. All participants receive a medal, and refreshments and various activities are available at Damplassen.
course_highlights: 500 m children’s race on grass in Halsparken, with a few hills
Engelskmila: 1609 m on trails and low-traffic streets, open to everyone
Timed 5 km race on trails and low-traffic streets with sidewalks
additional: All participants receive a medal. Hot dogs, cake, waffles, and drinks will be served at Damplassen. Entertainment and activities include a bouncy castle, a balloon clown, face painting, and a shot-speed radar. There will be stands from event partners. Public transport: Metro and bus 23 to Ullevål stadion, bus 25 to Eventyrveien, and trams 17 and 18 to John Colletts plass. Toilets are available by the start area and at the Seniorsenteret at Damplassen. The start and finish are by the tennis court in Bergsalléen. Food and drinks can be purchased at Damplass, where there will also be activities and stands. The 5 km race offers team registration for teams of at least four participants.

name: Festaløpet 2027
description: Festaløpet 2027 is a trail race in Oppdal, Trøndelag, taking place on Saturday, June 5. The race offers two distances: a challenging 17 km trail run with 650 metres of elevation gain through mountains, forests and alongside waterfalls, and a shorter 5 km route on forest trails. The start and finish are at the old Festa power station, where good, nourishing food will also be served after the race. Spectators are very welcome to cheer on the runners, and a group course run is arranged three weeks before race day to get familiar with the route.
course_highlights: 17 km with 650 metres of elevation gain through mountain terrain, forest and gravel roads
Start and finish inside the old power station, with a sprint prize after 1 km
Drinks station with sports drink and water before Rauhovden
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 10:30 on race day. Minimum age: 16. Carpooling is recommended due to limited parking. The awards ceremony is at 15:30, with prizes for the top three women and men, a sprint prize for the first woman and man through the power station, and draw prizes for all participants. Camping is available by the power station, with toilets and showers. Storbuan Gård serves food after the race, and showers and swimming in the river are available. Spectators can watch the runners at the power station after 1 km and at the finish. The race starts at 12:00, and race bibs can be collected from 10:30. The minimum age is 16. Parking is limited, so carpooling is recommended. After the race, food and a café, showers and river swimming are available; camping by the power station is also an option.

name: Fjellmaraton
description: The Beitostølen Mountain Marathon is a long-standing mountain race, held for the 46th time in 2027. The courses follow the National Tourist Route across Valdresflye, with spectacular views of Jotunheimen, and offer a unique nature experience in the mountains. The event brings together recreational and competitive runners of all ages for a celebration featuring several distances and activities. All finishers receive a medal, and prizes are awarded to the best in each category. The race starts at Sporten Beitostølen, with buses taking participants to the start areas for the longer distances.
course_highlights: The course follows the National Tourist Route across Valdresflye, with views of Jotunheimen
Start at Sporten Beitostølen, with transport to the start area at 960 m above sea level
Varied terrain with mountain scenery and fast asphalt
additional: All finishers receive a medal. Podium prizes for the top three in each category can be collected at Sporten Beitostølen. Course winners receive a free hotel stay at the following year's Fjellmaraton. There are drink stations and medical staff along the route. Baggage storage is provided by a baggage truck that leaves 15 minutes before the start. Toilets are available at the start and finish, as well as along the route. Bus transport to the start for the longer distances begins early from central Beitostølen. The race features a marathon, half marathon, Fjellbukken and Miniton. The 2027 weekend programme has not yet been published.

name: Bystrandløpet Bergen3000
location: Amalie Skram videregående skole, Bergen, Norway
description: Bystrandløpet Bergen3000 is a fast 3,000-metre race that takes place around Bergen’s upcoming city beach. The course follows walking and cycling paths around Store Lungegårdsvannet and is suitable for all levels, from children to elite athletes and people with reduced physical function. The event is family-friendly, with professional timing, medals for children and an awards ceremony. Organised by Sædalen IL, the race features a flat, fast course that is perfect for testing your fitness or setting personal records.
course_highlights: The course follows walking and cycling paths around Store Lungegårdsvannet
Flat, fast course, ideal for setting records and recreational running
AIMS-approved 3,000 metres off the track, with timing at several intermediate points
additional: Starts are staggered at one-minute intervals, with heats of 10–15 runners based on expected finish time. There are children’s races, para races, recreational races, a relay and elite classes, each with separate start times. Results are published on the website, and finish times are sent by SMS. The event includes entertainment, sales stalls, a kiosk and an awards ceremony. Participants are encouraged to join the Bystrandløpet X Torshov running group. The race is inclusive of everyone, including people with reduced physical function. A 300-metre children’s race, BERGEN300, is offered. Timing is provided by EQ Timing, and 3,000-metre runners start in groups based on their expected finish times. Children receive medals, and prizes are awarded for podium places.

name: The Arctic Triple - Lofoten Ultratrail - inkl. NM
Sommerløpet
description: Sommerløpet is Southern Norway’s largest running festival, held in Kristiansand with the start and finish at Øvre Torv. The event offers distances for everyone, from a children’s race to a half marathon, and welcomes participants of all ages and fitness levels. The courses pass through some of the city’s most attractive areas, including cultural venues, the city beach and historic Posebyen, creating a festive atmosphere with plenty of participants and spectators. Pacers are available for several distances, and there are well-stocked water stations along the way, making it an inclusive and motivating experience for everyone.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Øvre Torv in central Kristiansand
The course passes Kilden Performing Arts Centre, Kunstsilo, Kanalbyen, Odderøya and the city beach
Water stations by the pedestrian bridge over the Otra and in the finish area
additional: Pacers carrying balloons are available for various finish times in the 3 km, 5 km, 10 km and half marathon. Race bibs can be collected at Løplabbet and Clarion Ernst Hotel. T-shirts can be purchased during registration and collected at the hotel. Maximum of 5,000 participants in total; some distances may sell out. Companions can run for free using a code. The Red Cross provides first aid in the finish area. Distances include the Children’s Race (600 m), 3 km, 5 km, 10 km and half marathon (21 km).

name: Byløpet

tiers.label: tier_1

description: Byløpet is Grenland’s largest city race and half marathon, held in central Skien, starting by Arkaden. The 5 km, 10 km and 21 km courses run through scenic surroundings around Hjellevannet and offer a varied paved route with both hills and beautiful viewpoints. The event is open to everyone, from professional runners to families and school classes, and also includes a free children’s race for children up to 10 years old. Byløpet emphasizes the joy of running and public health, and provides accessibility for para-athletes. Race numbers are collected outside Sport 1, and there is plenty of nearby parking.
course_highlights: The course runs along the shore of Hjellevannet, with views of Skien city and Bakkestranda
Paved surface with challenging hills, including after the Falkum River and up towards Klosterøya
Water stations at Herkules and in the pedestrian street, as well as refreshments at the finish
additional: Start times: Half marathon at 11:00, 5 km at 13:00, 10 km at 13:30, Ibsen’s Children’s Race at 10:30. Race numbers are collected outside Sport 1. Free parking at Bygarasjen on race day. Accessibility for para-athletes with a guide or bicycle. Photos are taken during the race and may be published with consent. Ibsen’s Children’s Race is free for children aged 0 to 10. All participants receive a medal. Registration is through EQ Timing.

name: Oppegårdmila
location: Oppegård IL Clubhouse and Stadium, Oppegård, Norway
description: Oppegårdmila is an annual race organised by Oppegård IL, offering distances of 500 metres, 2 km, 5 km and 10 km. The event features varied courses, including the Installatørrunden and The Well route, and is suitable for children, young people and adults. It has a friendly atmosphere, with a warm-up at the stadium, race-number collection at the clubhouse and awards for different age groups. After the race, participants over 18 can enjoy free entry to The Well, providing a pleasant end to the day.
course_highlights: Micromila 500 m course for the youngest participants
Minimila 2 km course
Installatørrunden 5 km and The Well 10 km course (5 km x 2)
additional: Race numbers can be collected at the clubhouse on Friday, 5 June, from 19:00 to 19:30 and on race day from 09:00 to 11:30. There is a warm-up at the stadium before the start. Awards are given to the top three women and men, as well as to the 1st, 2nd and 3rd place girls and boys in the 12–15 and 16–19 age groups. All participants receive a participation prize. Participants over 18 can enter The Well for free after the race, but must sign up for this by Thursday, 4 June, at 12:00. Previous editions have offered the option to run or walk, with timing and a medal at the finish. Details for 2027 have not been confirmed by the sources.

name: Spitsbergen Marathon
description: The Spitsbergen Marathon is held in Longyearbyen, Svalbard, and is considered the world’s most beautiful running adventure. The race follows roads in and around Longyearbyen through open, challenging terrain. In early June, temperatures are usually above freezing, with melting snow and abundant wildlife along the course. The event includes a marathon, half marathon, 10 km with and without timing, and a mini marathon for children. The race office is located in Svalbardhallen, where race numbers are distributed and information is provided.
course_highlights: The course follows roads in and around Longyearbyen through open Arctic terrain
There is a chance to see reindeer, geese, and eider ducks along the course
The marathon consists of two identical half-marathon loops, passing the event venue at Svalbardhallen
additional: The race office at Svalbardhallen is open Friday 4 June from 16:00 to 20:00 and Saturday 5 June from 09:00 to 13:00 for race-number collection and information. The Mini Marathon for children starts at 10:30, with no advance registration required. Participants can choose a course of approximately 1 km or 3 km. Marathon runners must pass the turnaround point before 13:00 to continue, and the race ends at 16:00, with transport provided for those who have not finished. A licence is required for participants aged 13 and over. A one-day licence can be purchased when registering or at the race office. The start and finish are at the parking area outside Svalbardhallen, where the race office is also located. The Mini Marathon for children has distances of 1 km and 3 km. A one-day licence is an additional cost for participants who do not have an annual licence; the organiser recommends booking travel and accommodation early.

name: Skredløpet
description: Skredløpet is a trail race that started in 2007 and has grown into a popular annual event with around 370 participants. The race is 8.5 km long with 444 metres of elevation gain, and follows a scenic route from the avalanche barrier at Aga via Svartetjødn, Rogdatjødn and Rogdo, up to Kvestadstølane, Måkestadstølane and Herseter, before descending to the finish at Reisæter. The race is suitable for anyone who enjoys walking or running in nature, and includes adult competition classes, a short-legged race for children and a recreational class for those who want to enjoy nature at their own pace. Activities and social events are also held during Skredløpshelga, including an activity day and dancing.
course_highlights: 8.5 km course with 444 metres of elevation gain
Starts at the avalanche barrier at Aga and passes through scenic areas such as Svartetjødn and Rogdo
Highest point at Herseter, with great views, before descending to the finish at Reisæter
additional: The Kortbeintløpet has a bus from the car park at Aga to the start area at Rogdo at 12:00, and a return bus from Reisæter after the event. The recreational class can walk the course at their own pace, with a nature trail along the way. Freshly made waffles, coffee and squash are served at Rogdo and Reisæter. A team competition is held, with a minimum of 5 and a maximum of 10 participants per team. All participants in the Kortbeintløpet receive a participation prize, and prizes are drawn among the children. Participation earns 500 extra exercise points in the Solnuttrimmen app. The Kortbeintløpet is about 5 km and is for ages 7–15. It has not been confirmed that the stated details for the 2026 edition apply to the date 5 June 2027.

name: Graabeinløpet

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Påmelding koster kr. 300,- for både 10km og 5km.

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Påmelding koster kr. 300,- for både 10km og 5km.

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Prisen for 10km økes med 100,- til 400,- 14 dager før løpsdagen.

description: Graabeinløpet is a family-friendly race held at Sletta athletics track in Sætre. The event offers 5 km and 10 km distances, as well as a free children’s race, and is suitable for children and adults of all ages. The courses are measured and approved by the Norwegian Athletics Association, and run along both gravel and paved roads in scenic surroundings. All participants receive a medal, and prizes are awarded to class winners and the fastest boys and girls under 13. The event also has a kiosk, toilets, and medical personnel on site for a safe and enjoyable race experience.
course_highlights: The course runs along gravel and paved roads through central Sætre and the Chemring Nobel factory area
Start and finish at Sletta athletics track, with one 5 km lap and two laps for the 10 km
The course is measured and approved by the Norwegian Athletics Association
additional: The children’s race starts at 11:30, the 10 km starts at 13:00, and the 5 km starts at 13:25. There is a kiosk and indoor toilets at the stadium. The Red Cross is on site with medical personnel. An announcer makes announcements before the start, and course marshals are stationed along the entire route. Parking is available about 150 metres from the start area, with space for more than 100 cars. All participants receive a medal, and prizes are awarded to class winners in classes with at least 3 participants. The children’s race is free, and all participants receive a medal. The 2027 date has not yet been confirmed; the organizers say it will be set after summer 2026.

name: The Arctic Run
description: The Arctic Run is a unique island marathon held on Hadseløya in Vesterålen, Northern Norway. The race offers a scenic and varied course with a maximum elevation of 300 meters, suitable for both beginners and experienced runners. Participants can choose between a full marathon, a half marathon with views of the sea and mountains, and a 10K route that combines urban and natural landscapes. The event highlights the region’s stunning natural beauty, including views of Langøya, the Lofoten Wall, and the mountains in Bø, making it a memorable experience for all runners.
course_highlights: Marathon route around Hadseløya island with 300 meters maximum elevation
Half marathon with views of the sea, Langøya, and the Lofoten Wall
10K route through the city center, residential areas, and natural landscapes, with 79 meters of elevation
additional: The event includes a free 600-meter TAR Family Run at 10:00 AM on race day, with no timekeeping. Bib pickup is available from 08:00 to 09:45 AM at Hurtigrutemuseet. Food and drink stations are located at several points along the course and offer energy drinks, juice, water, bananas, nuts, chocolate, cookies, and dried fruit. Toilets are available at the start, finish, and along the course. Camp TAR offers drop-in showers, with passes available for purchase. Photographers will capture moments from the race, which will be available to purchase after the event. Shuttle buses run from several hotels to the race. The information page also covers food and drink stations, toilets, baggage storage, and pacers. A free 600-meter family run is also held.

name: Skurdalen Trail 2027
description: Skurdalen Trail is a trail race in scenic surroundings near Fagerli Leirskole in Skurdalen. The course offers challenging mountain terrain with spectacular views of Hallingskarvet and Hardangervidda, including the well-known Hovdetrappa. The event offers distances for the whole family, from a fun Kids Trail to a challenging 18 km course with demanding trails and mountain scenery. After the race, participants can enjoy a social gathering with a barbecue buffet, sauna and concert, making it a complete experience for runners and spectators alike.
course_highlights: The course passes via Hovdetrappa, with great views of Hallingskarvet and Hardangervidda
Trail running in challenging mountain terrain with bogs, climbs and mountain farms
Shared start and finish at Fagerli Leirskole, followed by a social get-together and After Trail
additional: Shared start and finish area at Fagerli Leirskole. Soup is served at the finish. GPS tracking of the races is available. After Trail includes a sauna at Bygdebadstua and a barbecue buffet at Fagerli, with a concert and social gathering. Mandatory equipment for the 12 km and 18 km includes a downloaded GPX course file and first-aid equipment. Participants must bring a mobile phone with the organizer’s number. Pacing and outside assistance are not permitted. Participation is at your own risk. The start and finish are at Fagerli Leirskole. Accommodation is available at Fagerli for race weekend. The race distances listed are 18 km, 12 km, 5 km and Kids Trail.

name: Lyngstadfjellet rundt
description: Lyngstadfjellet Rundt is a long-standing race organised by Hustadvika Sportsklubb that goes around Lyngstadfjellet. The race is approximately 12 km long, starting and finishing at the clubhouse in Lyngstad. It is a recreational class with timing, and all participants receive a commemorative pin. The top three in the women’s and men’s classes receive prizes.
course_highlights: Race around Lyngstadfjellet
Approximately 12 km
Start and finish at the clubhouse in Lyngstad
additional: All participants receive a commemorative pin. Prizes are awarded to the top three women and men. Recreational class with timing. The race began in 1976 and returned in 2026 after a long hiatus. The date 5 June 2027 is not confirmed in the sources.

name: Haugesunds Avis halvmaraton 2027
description: Haugesunds Avis Half Marathon and Fun Run is a long-standing recreational race held in Haugesund, with the start and finish at Haugesund Athletics Stadium. The event offers several distances, including a half marathon, relay, 5 km fun run, and a children’s marathon for the youngest participants. The course runs partly along sidewalks and inside the stadium, offering recreational and more experienced runners alike the chance to take part in a well-organized race in scenic surroundings. The event is inclusive, with options for all ages and ability levels.
course_highlights: The half marathon and relay start at Haugesund Athletics Stadium
The 5 km fun run follows a certified-distance loop, starting and finishing on the athletics track
Children’s marathon of approximately 750 metres for children aged 0 to 12, starting at the stadium
additional: The children’s marathon starts at 11:30, the 5 km fun run starts at 12:00, and the half marathon and relay start at 13:00. The 5 km course is a loop on the same route as the half marathon, adjusted to the correct distance inside the stadium. Previous editions have also included a 5 km, relay, and children’s race. Information about the 2027 edition has not been confirmed by the organizer.

name: Stomperudløpet 2027
description: Stomperudløpet is an annual race held at Sørum Stadium in Akershus. The race offers two distances, 6 km and 15 km, with the longer course recently changed from 16.5 km to 15 km following positive feedback. The course passes through varied terrain, including gravel roads, trails and sections of the old route, and offers scenic surroundings, including Flaenhytta and the shelter at Jultonåsen. This race is suitable for both recreational and more experienced runners looking for a challenging and enjoyable race experience.
course_highlights: The course runs from Lørenfallet via Aasgaardveien (gravel road) to Bølerteiet
Trail up to Tømtekoia and onward to Svartputtveien
Up to Flaenhytta and the shelter at Jultonåsen before returning to Lørenfallet
additional: Information about the distances and course applies to the 2026 edition; details for 2027 have not been confirmed.

name: Rekordmila
description: Rekordmila is a fast, flat 10-kilometer race in beautiful Buvika, perfect for anyone looking to set a new personal record. The course starts in central Buvika, follows the old road towards Øysand and returns. It is optimized for fast running, with a small roundabout at the turnaround to minimize time loss. In addition to the main race, there is a children’s race of approximately 500 meters, suitable for children of all ages. Rekordmila is also a race with heart: participants are encouraged to do good deeds in their local community as part of the event.
course_highlights: Fast, flat 10 km course from central Buvika to Øysand and back
The start has been moved 350 meters back, with a net downhill
Children’s race of approximately 500 meters along the path towards the water
additional: The children’s race starts at 11:00, approximately 90 minutes before the main race. Race bibs for the 10 km can be collected at Skaunhallen from 09:30 on race day. There are changing facilities at Skaunhallen. Water, squash, buns and bananas are served in the finish area, but there is no water station along the course. The course is closed to car traffic during the race. Pacers are available for various finish times, and photographers on the course offer photos for purchase. Cash prizes go to the top three men and women, with bonuses for a course record and for running under 30 minutes. A children’s race is also held. Previous editions have offered the option of paying the entry fee with a good deed in the local community.

name: Steinkjermila
description: Steinkjermila is a fun run and a festive event for the whole family, held in the heart of Steinkjer city centre, with the start and finish at Steinkjer Square. The course winds through many of the city’s most beautiful spots and offers a varied and enjoyable route. The event includes the Mila and 5`ern distances, as well as the children’s race Minimila, which is free for children aged 0–12. It is a social and inclusive event with a group warm-up, prize-giving and activities for all ages.
course_highlights: The course runs through Steinkjer city centre, starting and finishing at the square
The Mila distance consists of two laps of the same course
The children’s race Minimila crosses the bridge, goes through Holmen and returns to the square
additional: Race numbers can be collected in advance at Steinkjer Kulturhus on Friday 4 June and Saturday 5 June from 11:00 to 17:00, and on race day from 09:30. There is a group warm-up for children at 10:30 in the square. Bag storage is available in the Sparebank 1 SMN tent by the church tower. Everyone who finishes receives a medal. Gift cards are awarded to the top three men and women in the Mila and 5`ern. The Red Cross and race marshals ensure safety during the event. Water, cordial and bananas are available at aid stations in the finish area and along the Mila course. Toilets and showers are available at Samfunnshuset. Minimila is approximately 700 metres and is free for children aged 0–12. Race numbers can be collected at Steinkjer Kulturhus on Friday 4 June and Saturday 5 June from 11:00 to 17:00.

name: Voss Løpskarusell 2027, løp 3
description: Voss Running Series 2027 is a friendly running series for everyone, with races on Mondays at 19:00. The course is 5 km long, starting and finishing at Voss Sports Ground, and runs through Prestegardsmoen and along the waterfront promenade. The race is suitable for both recreational runners and runners aged 9 and up, and a discount is available when registering for all six races in the series. This is a great recreational race in the beautiful surroundings of Voss.
course_highlights: 5 km course starting and finishing at Voss Sports Ground
Loop through Prestegardsmoen
Run along the waterfront promenade
additional: All races start at 19:00, except the fifth race on 20 September, which starts at 18:30. Registration is online only via EQ Timing. A discount is available when registering for all six races before the second race.

name: Borgenløpet
description: Borgenløpet is organized by Borgen IL and offers an inclusive running experience for all ages and ability levels. The event includes a 7 km trail route called Åsmarkarunden, as well as a shorter 4 km route for those who prefer it. A children’s race is also held as the finale of the sports school’s running series. The event features an open kiosk, an announcer and a great atmosphere, inviting everyone to a pleasant community celebration at Borgen.
course_highlights: 7 km trail route called Åsmarkarunden
Shorter 4 km route for those who prefer it
Children’s race for the youngest runners as the finale
additional: An open kiosk, an announcer and a lively atmosphere throughout the event. The race is open to everyone, from recreational runners to elite athletes. The event concludes the sports school’s running series with a children’s race. The information found applies to the 2026 event and does not confirm details for 9 June 2027.

name: Birkebeinerløpet
description: Birkebeinerløpet is Norway’s largest trail race and will be held on Saturday, 12 June 2027, for the 29th time. The race starts at Birkebeineren Ski Stadium in Lillehammer and finishes at Håkons Hall. It offers varied forest terrain, with trails, cart roads and ski trails from the Olympics. The course is 20.2 km long, with 337 metres of ascent and 569 metres of descent, giving participants a wonderful nature experience and the joy of running. Anyone aged 16 or older in 2027 can take part, and the race is part of Birkebeinertrippelen.
course_highlights: Varied terrain including trails, grass, cart roads and ski trails from the 1994 Olympics
The course is 20.2 km long, with 337 metres of ascent and 569 metres of descent
Finish at Håkons Hall in Lillehammer
additional: Intermediate timing points are located at Sjøsetervegen (approx. 7.7 km) and Kroken (approx. 14 km). The course may have some wet sections and steep descents, so take extra care in wet conditions. The race is part of Birkebeinertrippelen. Participants must be at least 16 years old as of 31 December 2027. Participants must be at least 16 years old as of 31 December 2027. The race is part of Birkebeinertrippelen.

name: LøpeBirken 12km
description: LøpeBirken 12 km is a trail race being held for the 20th time on Saturday, June 12, 2027. The race runs from Birkebeineren Ski Stadium to the finish at Håkons Hall in Lillehammer, with varied terrain including trails, gravel roads, and ski trails from the Winter Olympics. Participants can enjoy the true Birken atmosphere, challenges, and beautiful nature in a race that combines the joy of running with a sense of achievement. The race is open to everyone aged 16 and over with timing; 15-year-olds may participate without timing.
course_highlights: Starts at Birkebeineren Ski Stadium (525 m above sea level), with varied surfaces including grass, trails, and a wide ski trail
First refreshment station at 4.14 km, with water and Maxim
The course includes gently rolling terrain, steep hills, and marsh sections, and finishes at Håkons Hall
additional: Participants aged 16 and over may take part with timing; 15-year-olds may participate without timing. The course has two refreshment stations, and participants are advised to watch out for wet conditions and traffic when crossing local roads. The race finishes at Håkons Hall in Lillehammer. Participants aged 16 and over may run with timing; 15-year-olds may participate without timing. Food and drink along the course and at the finish are included in the entry fee. A free shuttle bus runs from Håkons Hall to Birkebeineren Ski Stadium.

name: UltraBirken løp
description: UltraBirken Run is a 60 km ultramarathon from Sjusjøen Cross-Country Arena to the finish at Håkons Hall in Lillehammer. The race offers a tough running challenge across varied and demanding terrain, and is suited to runners who want to test their limits. It is held annually and is part of the Birkebeiner Triple, is approved as a qualifier for the UTMB 50K, and awards 2 ITRA points. The race continues to attract more participants and has a rich tradition of achievement and community.
course_highlights: Starts at Sjusjøen Cross-Country Arena, with 2 km of gravel road before the trail crosses high-mountain terrain over Sjusjøfjellet and Lunkefjell
The route crosses Krigsfjell, Hitfjell, Pellestova and Nevelfjell, the course’s highest point at 1,072 metres above sea level
The course ends with demanding, rocky and steep sections before reaching the finish on a gravel road outside Håkons Hall in Lillehammer
additional: The race awards 2 ITRA points and qualifies for the UTMB 50K. Participants must be at least 18 years old as of 31 December 2027. The race is part of the Birkebeiner Triple. The route has a total of 1,258 metres of elevation gain and 1,873 metres of descent. There may be muddy and wet sections, as well as steep and rocky sections where reducing your pace is recommended. Start time: 08:00. Participants must be 18 years old by 31 December 2027. The race awards 2 ITRA points and is approved as a UTMB 50K qualifier. Food and drinks at the stations are included in the entry fee.

name: UngdomsBirken løp
description: The UngdomsBirken Run is an approximately 5 km race for young people aged 12 to 16, starting at Stampesletta and finishing at Håkons Hall in Lillehammer. The race gives participants the chance to experience the true Birken atmosphere and cross the same finish line as thousands of other participants. It will be held for the 22nd time in 2027 and focuses on achievement, community and the joy of running, whether it is your first time or you have taken part before. The course passes through varied terrain, including gravel paths, a floodlit trail and scenic surroundings near Maihaugen.
course_highlights: Approximately 5 km from Stampesletta to Håkons Hall
