The course follows gravel paths, crosses Finnabrua and runs alongside the Mesna River
Finish at Håkons Hall in the true Birken atmosphere
additional: There is a drinks station with squash and water after approximately 2.5 km, as well as a food and drinks station at the finish serving water, squash and sausages from Gilde. Participants with special dietary needs are advised to bring their own packed meal. Everyone is encouraged to drink plenty of fluids before and during the race. Elevation figures for the course vary depending on GPS equipment and map data. For participants who turn 12–16 by 31 December 2027. Drinks are available at approximately 2.5 km, with food and drinks at the finish.

name: Haslummila
description: Haslummila is a road race starting and finishing at Bekkestua in Bærum, offering distances of 400 metres for children, 5 km for ambitious runners and 10 km for keen runners. The event is an inclusive, energetic running celebration focusing on time, personal achievement and the local community. The course winds through varied streets and paths, with several underpasses and scenic areas, and there are drink stations along the way. All participants receive a medal, and children receive ice cream as a prize. The event encourages the use of public transport and offers good parking options nearby.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Bekkestua, with the 400 m children's race in Bærumsveien
The 5 km course passes through underpasses beneath Kirkeveien and Bærumsveien, and by Haslum Klubbhus and Nadderud VGS
The 10 km course consists of two laps of the 5 km route
additional: Drinks will be available at the finish and at one station along the course (5 km runners pass it once; 10 km runners pass it twice). All participants receive a medal, and children receive ice cream. Participants are encouraged to use public transport; both a bus station and a metro station are within walking distance of the start/finish. Several parking garages are located nearby. Information about race bibs, clothing storage, toilets and AfterRun will be provided later. Drinks are available at the finish and at a station along the course. All participants receive a medal, and children also receive ice cream.

name: Fana Backyard
price_range: 600 kr individuelt; 1000 kr per lag på to
description: Fana Backyard Ultra is organized by Gneist Friidrett and follows the classic Backyard Ultra rules, with a start every hour on the hour. The course is 6.706 km long and consists of asphalt, trails and gravel, with a total of 12 laps run within a time window from 09:00 to 21:00. The event takes place at Gneist Arena in Bergen and offers a challenging, sociable ultra-running experience with both individual and team classes. All participants have access to a base camp with facilities such as snacks, drinks, changing rooms and toilets, and finishers receive T-shirts.
course_highlights: 6.706 km course with asphalt, trails and gravel
Starts every hour on the hour, following Backyard Ultra rules
12 laps in total, covering 80.472 km
additional: Teams consist of 2 runners who take turns running every other lap throughout the competition. All 12 laps must be completed for a valid overall time. The final lap must be completed by 21:00. Everyone who completes 1 to 11 laps receives an official participant T-shirt, while everyone who completes all 12 laps receives an exclusive black T-shirt. Spectators are welcome outside and inside Gneist Arena, but do not have access to the runners’ base camp. Pedestrian crossings must be used when crossing roads, and marshals direct traffic at some points. The start and base camp are at Gneist Arena. The base camp has snacks, drinks, toilets and changing rooms. Minimum age: 15 (born in 2011 or earlier).

name: Hell Løpefestival
organizer: Hell Ultraløperklubb, med bistand fra flere idrettsklubber i Stjørdal
description: Hell Running Festival takes place on 12–13 June 2027 at Øverlands Minde in Stjørdal and offers a wide range of races for all levels. The festival includes Stjørdalsmila, with 5 km and 10 km distances, as well as ultrarunning events of 6, 12 and 24 hours and a marathon. The races are held on certified courses with asphalt and tartan surfaces, and Øverlands Minde offers good facilities, including showers and changing rooms. With the Trøndelag midnight sun as a backdrop, this is a highlight for running enthusiasts in the region.
course_highlights: Stjørdalsmila: certified 5 km and 10 km courses through central Stjørdal and along the promenade at Tangen
Ultrarunning on a 1,185.6 m loop with asphalt and tartan surfaces at Øverlands Minde
The races take place outdoors, with facilities including showers and changing rooms at Øverlands Minde
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Øverlands Minde on Friday 11 June from 18:00 to 21:00, on Saturday 12 June from 09:00, and on Sunday 13 June until 12:45. Registration for Stjørdalsmila closes at 12:00 on race day. The ultrarunning events have a support area with tables and tents, and the running direction is reversed every 6 hours. All participants must have a licence (insurance). The race takes place outdoors, with the midnight sun as a backdrop. The festival runs over two days, 12–13 June 2027.

name: Moan5ern
organizer: Sprek Treningssenter, Berg Eiendom, Intersport, Alti Magneten og Markabygda IL
description: Moan5ern is an inclusive race in Levanger, Trøndelag, offering a running festival for all ages and levels. The event is organized in collaboration with local partners such as Sprek Treningssenter and Markabygda IL, and aims to provide a wide range of recreational running opportunities. The race includes a children’s race, a untimed fun run, and competitive waves for the fastest runners. Moan5ern is a great opportunity for both recreational and competitive runners to take part in a social and active event.
course_highlights: 5 km course in Levanger
500-meter children’s race
Competitive waves based on expected finish time
additional: The children’s race starts at 12:00, with free entry and no registration required. The untimed fun run starts at 12:30. Competitive wave 1 (faster than 20 min) starts at 13:00, and wave 2 starts at 13:05. Previous editions have had wave starts for competitive runners. The children’s race has been free and has not required registration.

name: Gjesdal Backyard
location: Gjesdal IL stadion, Ålgård, Gjesdal, Norway
price_range: 800 kr; stafett fra 1500 kr per lag

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Pris: 800,- kr. Dette inkluderer bevertning og pleie gjennom hele dagen.

description: Gjesdal Backyard is a unique and different kind of race where participants run a 6.7 km loop up to twelve times, starting and finishing at Gjesdal IL stadium in Ålgård. The course offers varied terrain, including asphalt, farm tracks and flowing trails, as well as a challenging hill and scenic valleys. Each lap starts on the hour, and your pace determines the length of your breaks between laps. The event also offers a relay option, with teams of 2–6 people sharing the 12 laps. Refreshments, entertainment and good facilities are available at the stadium.
course_highlights: Start and finish on the tartan track at Gjesdal IL stadium
Varied terrain with asphalt, farm tracks and flowing trails
The course’s toughest and longest hill comes early in the lap
additional: Bib collection from 07:30. Group information and race briefing at 08:45. A new lap starts every hour from 09:00 to 20:00. A personal chair in the “Storsalen”, with refreshments, entertainment and surprises. Good changing-room and toilet facilities. Medical staff on site. Food and drink included: water, fruit, cordial, crisps, jelly sweets, cola, filled sandwiches, hot food after lap 6 and a Jæder burger after lap 12. Minimum age: 16. Runners must bring suitable shoes, a headlamp and weather-appropriate clothing. Start and finish at Gjesdal IL stadium in Ålgård. The race is limited to 12 laps (80.4 km) and has a minimum age of 16. Relay teams can consist of 2–6 people, and each participant must run at least two laps. The official website lists 12 September 2026 as the race date, not the stated date of 12 June 2027.

name: Hovlandsnuten Opp
description: Hovlandsnuten Opp is a traditional uphill race from Risvoll School to the summit of Hovlandsnuten, 931 metres above sea level. The approximately 6.7-kilometre course offers varied terrain, with Sherpa steps, beautiful views over the fjord and a challenging climb. The race is suitable for everyone, young and old, and family entertainment is provided at Trollplassen. The event also has a dedicated Sherpa/firefighter class with additional weight to carry. After the race, there is a social gathering with music, awards and activities for the whole family.
course_highlights: The course passes through Sherpa steps built by Sherpas from Nepal
Water stations at Skreivane, Hovlandsstølen and Hovlandsnuten
Panoramic views from the summit at 931 metres above sea level
additional: The recreational walk starts at 08:30 from Risvoll School, with the option to start from the alternative parking area in Nordstøldalen. The competition starts at 12:00. Race numbers (vests) are handed out before the start. Medals are presented by Mayor Håvard Handeland. There is a race announcer and several family activities at Trollplassen, including face painting, a pirate show and music. Participants in the Sherpa/firefighter class must carry at least 20 kg of additional weight. Competition participants must bring a wind jacket and trousers, and poles are not allowed on the Sherpa steps or in the open mountain terrain. The course is marked, and there are Norwegian Red Cross stations with defibrillators along the course. Water stations are listed at Skreivane, Hovlandsstølen and Hovlandsnuten. Competition participants must bring a wind jacket and windproof trousers; poles are not allowed in the competition class. The Sherpa/firefighter class requires at least 20 kg of additional weight, and all participants must have a licence.

name: 3 toppsløpet på Jeløya (3TL)
description: 3toppsløpet on Jeløya is a trail race held annually around Midsummer, starting and finishing at Sølystranda on Jeløya in Moss. The race offers four distances: Mini 1TL (1 km), 1TL (10 km), 2TL (20 km) and 3TL (30 km). Runners alternate between forest trails and scenic beaches. The course includes the three well-known peaks Rødsåsen, Bjørnåsen and Rambergtoppen, offering a technically challenging and varied terrain experience. The event is run by volunteers and has a low entry fee. Any surplus supports children affected by war and conflict through a partnership with Right To Play.
course_highlights: Trail race on paths, forest roads, beaches and some paved sections
Includes three well-known peaks: Rødsåsen, Bjørnåsen and Rambergtoppen
The course follows much of the shoreline around Jeløya
additional: Mass start for 1TL (10 km), 2TL (20 km) and 3TL (30 km) at 10:00 from Sølystranda. Mini 1TL (1 km) starts at approximately 09:30. An early start for 3TL and the marathon is available at 09:00 for runners expecting to take longer. 3TL requires runners to check in at all three peaks; 1TL requires a check-in only at Rødsåsen. There are no aid stations for 3TL, so participants must bring their own food and drink. 1TL has an aid station at Kasekilen. Carrying a charged mobile phone is mandatory, and running with a backpack is recommended. The 2027 edition will take place on Saturday, 12 June, with the regular start from 10:00 at Sørlystranda.

name: Ålesund Maraton
distance_verbose: Maraton, Halvmaraton, 10 km, 5 km, 2.5 km, 0.8 km, 0.5 km
description: Ålesund Marathon is an annual celebration in the city centre of Ålesund, offering races for all ages and abilities. Participants can choose from 5 km, 10 km, half marathon, marathon, 5 km relay, and the Children’s Mini Marathon, which has two distances. The courses run through the city streets, starting and finishing at Skansekaia, with spectators creating a great atmosphere along the route. The event encourages both personal bests and the enjoyment of running together, with starting groups suited to different expected finish times. The Children’s Mini Marathon gives the youngest participants a fun and inclusive start to the race-day festivities.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Skansekaia in central Ålesund
The half marathon is run over two laps; the marathon over four laps
The 5 km relay course has three possible changeover points
additional: Starting groups for the 5 km, 10 km, and half marathon are based on expected finish times. The Children’s Mini Marathon has two distances (500 m and 800 m), with the option to change distance during the event. Free entry to Bybadet for children on 6 and 7 June upon presentation of a medal, race bib, or receipt. Relay teams can have 2–6 participants, with at least 40% women required on mixed teams. Traffic and parking in the city centre will be affected during the event; public transport and parking at Aksla are recommended. The Children’s Mini Marathon distances are 500 and 800 metres. Registration for the 2027 race has not yet opened.

name: Backyard Larvik Ultra
description: Backyard Larvik is a unique ultrarace where participants run a 6.7 km loop on the hour, up to a maximum of twelve loops. The race combines strategy and endurance: the last runner to start a loop wins. The event has a social focus and a low barrier to entry, with break facilities offering food and drink in a warm indoor venue. Participants who complete twelve loops receive a cup, and those who complete seven loops receive a wooden medal. The race takes place at Fagerli School in Larvik, with race bib collection and a race briefing on the day before and on race day.
course_highlights: 6.7 km loop run on the hour
Maximum 12 loops, 80.4 km in total
Break facilities with food and drink in a warm indoor venue
additional: Race bibs and ankle chips can be collected at Fagerli School on Friday, June 12, from 18:00 to 20:00, and on Saturday, June 13, from 07:45 to 08:30. The race briefing starts at approximately 08:30 in the hall at Fagerli School. Bringing your own cup is mandatory. The ankle chip and Velcro strap must be returned after the race; a fee applies if they are not returned. The Red Cross will be present with an ATV to provide assistance. The maximum number of participants is 350. A race bib can be attached with a race belt to make changing clothes during breaks easier. Maximum 350 participants. Bringing your own cup is mandatory. The organizer’s information about the race format and price reflects the published details and may change before the 2027 edition.

name: Sommernattsløpet Bergen
description: Sommernattsløpet Bergen is a summer road race held in beautiful surroundings around central Bergen. The course offers fast and relatively flat laps around Lungegårdsvann, with the start and finish in Nygårdsparken. Participants can choose between 5 km and 10 km, with the 10 km consisting of two laps of the same course. The race is suitable for all levels and offers a festive atmosphere with music, cheering, and the chance to set a new personal best.
course_highlights: Course around beautiful central Bergen and Lungegårdsvann
Minimal elevation gain; a fast, flat course
Start and finish in Nygårdsparken, with music and cheering
additional: Pacers are available in several pace groups from 4:00 to 6:30 min/km. Race bibs can be collected at Löplabbet Bergen or on race day for participants travelling from farther away. All participants receive drinks and a medal at the finish. Prizes from partners are drawn after the race. The 5 km start time is listed as 19:00. The 10 km has wave starts at 20:00 for an expected time under 50 minutes and at 21:30 for over 50 minutes. Race bibs can be collected at Löplabbet Bergen or on race day for travelling participants. Participants receive drinks and a medal at the finish.

name: Bergsdalen Halvmaraton
description: Bergsdalen Half Marathon is held annually, starting at Bergsdalen Church, and brings runners together for a wonderful half-marathon experience in scenic surroundings. The race has a reputation for being well organized and welcomes both recreational and more experienced runners. The event is organized in collaboration with Stanghelle IL, which also offers several activities for children and adults in the local community. Bergsdalen Half Marathon 2027 is planned for June 12, and runners can look forward to a day with a great atmosphere and a challenging course.
course_highlights: Measured and well-marked courses
Reported to have around 90 meters of elevation gain
Start and finish at the church in Bergsdalen
additional: Previous editions have featured a half marathon, a 10 km race, and a relay. The 2027 edition is planned for June 12.

name: Kvammen halvmaraton 2027
description: Kvammen Half Marathon is organized by Kvammen Sports Club and takes place on Saturday, June 12, 2027. This is a challenging and exclusive half marathon that gives participants the opportunity to experience much of Kvammen. The course passes through scenic areas such as Høgda, Hegreneset, the school, Løvika and Leknes, before finishing back at Høgda. This race is suited to runners looking for a challenging distance in beautiful surroundings.
course_highlights: The course passes through Høgda, Hegreneset, the school, Løvika and Leknes
Scenic surroundings in the Kvammen area
A challenging and exclusive half marathon with varied terrain
additional: The course information is for the 2026 edition; a detailed course map and video were announced but have not been confirmed for 2027.

name: Perseløpet 5 km, 10 km, halvmaraton
description: Perseløpet is a simple and efficient running event at Ås school in Eidsvoll, designed to help runners achieve fast times. The race takes place on a flat, accurately measured 2,633-metre loop, with the option to set up your own nutrition table along the way. Seven distances are offered, from 3 km to 100 km, including 5 km, 10 km and the half marathon. Race bibs are collected at a self-service station at the venue, which also has free parking, changing rooms and toilets. Perseløpet has a friendly atmosphere, and runners who set a personal best get to ring the bell by the finish area.
course_highlights: Flat, accurately measured 2,633-metre loop
Personal nutrition table passed on every lap
Venue at Ås school with free parking, changing rooms and toilets
additional: Race bibs are collected at a self-service station about two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. Runners can place their own bottles and gels on the nutrition table before the start. At selected races, ninth-grade students from Feiring school staff an official drinks station and raise money for their school trip. A countdown feature and lap-time calculator are available for planning. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets at the venue. Registration is via RaceDays, and half-marathon runners can arrange their own drinks and nutrition.

name: Trollheimsløpet
description: Trollheimsløpet is a traditional race held in central Rindal, starting and finishing at Trollbanen. The course is mainly on trails, with sections of grass, asphalt and gravel, and takes in the scenic surroundings of Igltjønna. There are several distances and categories, including a children’s race, competitive classes and a recreational class, making the event accessible to all ages and abilities. The event also has a welcoming atmosphere, with refreshments for sale, changing facilities and awards for both children and adults.
course_highlights: The course is mainly on trails, with sections of grass, asphalt and gravel
Around picturesque Igltjønna in central Rindal
The recreational class can take an extra loop for a total distance of 8 km
additional: The children’s race (200 m) starts at 11:45 and is not timed. The 1 km competitive classes for ages 11–14 start at 12:20, and the 6 km race for older classes starts at 12:45. The untimed recreational class offers a choice of 1, 3 or 8 km, with start times between 10:30 and 12:00. All children’s race participants receive awards, and class winners aged 15 and over receive cash prizes. Participants celebrating milestones receive awards for taking part over several years. The race office is located at the start, changing facilities are at Rindalshuset, and toilets are available at the venue. Previous editions have included an untimed recreational class and a children’s race. Information about registration and prices for 2027 is not available in the sources.

name: Perseløpet
description: Perseløpet is a race in Eidsvoll starting at Ås school, offering a simple and efficient setup for achieving fast times. The race takes place on a flat, accurately measured 2,633-metre loop, with the option of having your own nutrition table along the course. Seven distances are offered, from 3 km to 100 km, so both beginners and experienced runners can find a suitable challenge. The event emphasizes personal-record attempts and community, with the option to celebrate personal records near the finish area.
course_highlights: Flat, accurately measured 2,633-metre loop
Your own nutrition table, passed on every lap
Seven distances from 3 km to 100 km
additional: Race bibs are collected by self-service at Ås school approximately two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms, and toilets are available at the venue. At selected races, 9th-grade students from Feiring school staff an official drinks station to raise money for their school trip. The race has a lap-time calculator to help plan split times. The weather forecast is updated four times daily using satellite data for the area around Ås school. Race bibs are collected by self-service at the school from approximately two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms, and toilets are available at the venue. Registration and current prices are available from RaceDays.

name: Sørdalskarusellen - Mesnaelva opp

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: For klassene 0-11 år, 12-15 og 16-19 år kr 80,-

tiers.label: tier_3
tiers.description: Familie koster kr 250,- pr løp pr familie

description: Mesnaelva Uphill is a challenging uphill race held in scenic surroundings along the Mesna River in Lillehammer. The course climbs 360 metres over approximately 4 km, starting at Strandtorget and finishing at Kanten kro. It is the first uphill race in the Sørdalskarusellen and has been held since 2008. In addition to the main course, there is a shorter 2.3 km course for younger participants with 241 metres of elevation gain. The event offers both virtual participation and evening mass starts in waves.
course_highlights: 4 km course with 360 metres of elevation gain, from 123 metres above sea level to 483 metres above sea level
The course follows the Mesna River through scenic areas of Lillehammer
Short course for younger participants: 2.3 km with 241 metres of elevation gain and a 10.2% gradient
additional: Mass start in waves: Wave 1 starts at 19:00 for men aged 12–39; Wave 2 starts at 19:01 for women aged 12–39 and men aged 40–49; Wave 3 starts at 19:02 for the remaining categories; and Wave 4 starts at 19:00 for the youngest participants on the short course. There is a drinks station in the finish area, clothing transport from the start to the finish, and medical services at the finish area. Results are sent to participants' mobile phones immediately after they finish. Participants can also take part virtually from 15–17 June and record their time via My Page under the self timing tab. There is also a short course for children, starting at Badedammen.

name: Vikersundbakken Trappeløp. Vegard Hjelmesæths minneløp 2027
description: Vikersundbakken Stair Run. Vegard Hjelmesæth Memorial Run 2027 takes place on Friday, June 18, 2027, in Modum. This unique race offers 6-, 12- and 24-hour events, where participants run up the stairs in the ski jump and down the road on a loop of approximately 2.3 km with 200 metres of elevation gain per lap. The goal is to complete as many laps as possible within the chosen time limit. There is also an option for a children's race and a single lap for those who wish to take part.
course_highlights: Run up the stairs at the Vikersundbakken ski jump
A loop of approximately 2.3 km with 200 metres of elevation gain per lap
Run down the road after the ski jump
additional: Tickets are sold via racetracker.one. The event includes 6-, 12- and 24-hour races, as well as a children's race and the option to run a single lap. The loop has 200 metres of elevation gain and goes both up the stairs in the ski jump and down the road. Registration via racetracker.one. There is also a single-lap competition and a children's race.

name: Skagerrakmila
description: Skagerrakmila is a summer race in Arendal that passes through the city centre and along the waterfront. The course offers varied terrain, with both flat sections and challenging climbs, including a tough hill by the kayak club. The start and finish are in Pollen, and the race is suitable for recreational runners looking for a challenging 10 km in beautiful surroundings. The event is organised by IK Grane Arendal Friidrett and has a pleasant summer atmosphere.
course_highlights: Start and finish in Pollen, in central Arendal
The course runs along the waterfront with lovely views and passes several landmarks, including Barbu Church and Arendal Old Town Hall
A challenging climb up to Vollenetoppen and a steep hill by the kayak club
additional: The children's race starts in Pollen and follows a shorter route through the city centre. The start and finish have been moved approximately 100 metres to improve flow in the finish area. There is a key point on the course with crossing traffic between 5.5 and 6.5 km, where runners must keep to the right. A children's race is also held. The course information is based on the 2025 map, so the route for 2027 may be different.

name: Midnight Sun Marathon
description: The Midnight Sun Marathon in Tromsø is an Arctic running adventure beneath the midnight sun, with five distances offering a unique experience in the light of the sun that never sets. The race brings together thousands of participants from around the world and creates a festival atmosphere, with the whole city cheering on the runners. With spectacular mountain and fjord scenery, and an intimate atmosphere that only Tromsø can offer, this is one of the world’s northernmost marathons and a highlight of the racing calendar.
course_highlights: Run beneath the midnight sun, with daylight all night
Spectacular mountain and fjord scenery
A festival atmosphere, with cheers from across the city
additional: Bib distribution and the MSM Expo take place before the race. Bag storage is available at Kulturhuset and Havneterminalen. Changing facilities and showers are available at Gyllenborghallen. Refreshment stations are located approximately every 5 km and offer water, sports drinks and bananas. The Tromsø Red Cross Search and Rescue Corps has a medical station every 5 km and provides assistance and transport when needed. Warm-ups take place 15 minutes before the start of all distances. Bibs can be transferred in the event of illness or injury with a doctor’s certificate and an administration fee. The event offers five distances. The courses are officially measured and certified, and the Midnight Sun Marathon is a member of AIMS.

name: Sentrumsgateløpet

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: 5 km kr 50,- (Under 12 år) + 10 kroner i adm.gebyr

description: Sentrumsgateløpet in Kongsvinger is an annual city festival and running event offering certified 5 km and 10 km distances, as well as a children’s race. The course runs on both sides of the Glomma, with the start and finish at Rådhusplassen by the library. The event combines the joy of sport with activities and a lively atmosphere in the town centre, and is suitable for all ages and levels. All finishers receive a participant medal, and prizes are awarded to the top runners in various categories.
course_highlights: The course runs on both sides of the Glomma
The 10 km is run as two laps of the same course
Certified distances measured by an authorised course measurer
additional: Race numbers are distributed on event day, with distribution monitored. Water stations are available during the race. Toilets and changing rooms/showers are available near the start/finish area. Results are published on EQ Timing, the local newspaper Glåmdalen, kondis.no and the race website. A children’s race is held in Byparken, with distances of up to 500 metres. Start times for 2027 have not been confirmed in the sources.

name: Sommernattsløpet Oslo
price_range: Fra 490 kr per distanse, pluss gebyrer
description: Sommernattsløpet Oslo is the most fun street race of the summer, with fast courses and beautiful surroundings at Filipstadkaia. Choose between 5 km and 10 km, both with minimal elevation gain and a good chance of setting a new personal best. The race takes place at sunset, with music and cheering, and all participants receive a drink and a great medal at the finish. It is a social and inclusive event for both recreational and more experienced runners.
course_highlights: The 5 km course is a fast-paced loop
The 10 km course passes Filipstadkaia and includes an extra loop
The courses have minimal elevation gain and fast sections
additional: Start and finish at Filipstadkaia by Skur 13. Race numbers can be collected the day before or on race day from 17:00. Pacers are available for various finish times in the 5 km and 10 km races. All participants receive a drink and a medal. Group registration is available for companies, with separate administration and a VIP package for more than 100 participants. The listed start times are 5 km at 19:00, 10 km for runners finishing under 50 minutes at 20:00, and 10 km for runners finishing over 50 minutes at 21:30. Start times may change depending on the number of entrants. Runner’s World will provide pacers in Oslo.

name: HOKA Norefjell Trail
description: HOKA Norefjell Trail is a spectacular trail race held at Norefjell Ski & Spa. The event offers three distances: 12 km, 22 km and 42 km, all featuring varied terrain with trails, gravel roads and mountain areas. Participants can expect challenging climbs, technical sections and beautiful views, especially on the 22 km and marathon distances, which reach the summit of Høgevarde at 1,450 metres. The event also includes a free children’s event with games and running around a small lake, making it a family-friendly experience.
course_highlights: Varied terrain with gravel roads, technical trails and open mountain areas
Challenging climb to Høgevarde at 1,450 metres (22K and 42K)
Beautiful mountain views and a downhill stretch towards the finish area
additional: Free parking at Norefjell Ski & Spa. Bus transport is offered from Oslo and Gardermoen and can be booked when registering. Aid stations are available on all distances with snacks, sports drinks and water, but participants must bring their own cup or bottle (at least 0.5 L). Age limits apply, and gear checks may take place. The children’s event is free and requires no registration. After the race, there will be a social gathering with an awards ceremony and an evening party. The race takes place on 19 June 2027 at Norefjell Ski & Spa. A free children’s race is also planned, and the participant limit is 1,200. The race weekend programme includes social runs, including a 5 km run.

name: Kristinaløpet og Kristinastafetten

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: 1500,- pr lag frem til og med 30. april 2026

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: 500,- pr lag frem til og med 30.april 2026

tiers.label: tier_3
tiers.description: 2500,- pr lag fra 1. mai til 19. juni 2026

tiers.label: tier_4
tiers.description: 1000,- pr lag fra 1. mai til 19. juni 2026

description: Kristinaløpet and Kristinastafetten are traditional races held on the streets of Tønsberg, starting and finishing at Bystranda on Kaldnes. The event offers 5 km and 10 km distances, an untimed fitness class, a relay with five short legs, and the 500-metre Children’s Kristinaløpet. The courses feature a scenic loop that includes a full circuit out to Ilene, and the relay route passes through Slottsfjelltunnelen, among other places. Runners start in waves based on their expected finish time, and electronic chip timing begins when they cross the start line.
course_highlights: The 10 km course includes a full loop out to Ilene
The relay consists of five legs, covering 5 km in total, and passes through Slottsfjelltunnelen, among other places
Start and finish at Bystranda on Kaldnes, with wave starts to prevent runners from mixing together
additional: Race numbers can be collected at the Olympia Sport store at Jarlsberg from 15 to 18 June and on race day from 10:00. The pedestrian bridge between central Tønsberg and Kaldnes closes shortly before the start. Runners start in waves based on their expected finish time to prevent them from mixing together. Timing begins only when the chip on the race number crosses the start line. The 500-metre Children’s Kristinaløpet is open for registration on the day. Children’s Kristinaløpet is approximately 500 metres, with registration on race day. A 40% discount on the main race is offered to participants taking part in both Kristinaløpet and Kristinastafetten, subject to further terms.

name: Nøsen Hundreds Ultramarathon
description: Nøsen Hundreds is an ultramarathon offering distances of 21 km, 50 km, and 100 km through beautiful and challenging mountain terrain in Valdres, Norway. The race follows historic trails in Stølsvidda, an area with a rich cultural heritage dating back to the Stone Age. Participants experience spectacular landscapes of mountains, rolling hills, and traditional trails that have been a lifeline for people for centuries. The race combines a physical challenge with experiences in nature and a sense of being part of a long tradition. In 2025, Nøsen Hundreds celebrates its fifth anniversary and promises an unforgettable experience for all participants.
course_highlights: Historic trails in Stølsvidda with cultural heritage dating back to the Stone Age
Varied terrain with mountains, rolling hills, and gravel roads
Challenging climbs and mountain crossings, especially on the 50 km and 100 km distances
additional: All races start and finish at Nøsen Yoga and Mountain Hotel. Mandatory equipment is required for the 50 km and 100 km distances, including a backpack/vest, windproof and waterproof jacket and trousers, a GPS device with a GPX file, a mobile phone with the emergency number saved, and first-aid supplies. Participants in the 100 km race receive drop bags. An optional Salomon Shakeout Session and an introduction to sports psychology are also offered on the evening before the race. Several accommodation options are available at a discount for participants, including the option to camp at the hotel. For the 100 km course, information from 2026 states that runners must navigate using a GPS device and a physical compass, and download the official GPX file before the start.

name: Solnedgangen
description: Solnedgangen is a fast 5 km race held annually in June, starting and finishing at Sola Strand Hotel. The race is suitable for everyone over 10, whether you are a beginner or an experienced recreational runner. The course is flat and follows the cycle path by the beach, with a short gravel section at the turn. Participants can follow pacers targeting different times, and everyone who finishes receives a medal and an official time from electronic timing.
course_highlights: Flat 5 km course along the cycle path by the beach
Runs on pavement, with a gravel section at the turn
Start and finish at Sola Strand Hotel, with views of the beach
additional: Race bibs can be collected in advance at Anton Sport Forus or at the start area from 20:30 on race day. Parking is recommended at Regestranden, about 1 km from the start/finish. Toilets are available at the hotel and the parking area. Pacers are available for 20, 25, 30 and 35 minutes. There are refreshments, a great atmosphere and an awards ceremony at the finish. The listed race arrangements include electronic timing, pacers for 20, 25, 30 and 35 minutes, a medal for everyone who finishes, refreshments and an awards presentation. The organizer’s page mentions a race on 20 June 2026; the date 19 June 2027 is not confirmed there.

name: Nordmarka Skogsmaraton 2027
price_range: Halvmaraton: 590–1 090 kr; maraton: 690–1 090 kr; ultra: 790–1 200 kr
description: Nordmarka Forest Marathon is a traditional race being held for the 34th time in 2027. The race takes place in the beautiful Nordmarka, starting and finishing at Sognsvann Snow Park in Oslo. The courses are mainly on gravel roads with some trails, offering a hilly, scenic route that is gentle on the legs. The event offers three distances: marathon, half marathon, and ultra. The ultra combines the marathon and half-marathon courses. The race is known for good refreshments and a friendly atmosphere in the forest.
course_highlights: The course is mostly on gravel roads, with approximately 1.5 km of trail on the marathon course
The marathon course has approximately 770 metres of elevation gain; the ultra has approximately 1,195 metres
Beautiful natural surroundings in Nordmarka, with fresh air and good refreshments along the way
additional: Start and finish at Sognsvann Snow Park, with easy public transport access via the metro to Kringsjå station. Bag storage with staff on hand. Self-seeding, with wave starts based on expected finish time. A race shirt can be ordered during registration until 8 March. Ultra runners have a separate turnaround point, with the option to access their own food and drink and receive a medical check. There is no time limit for the marathon, but ultra runners must pass the turnaround by 13:30. The minimum age is 15 for the half marathon and 18 for the marathon. Race-day registration is possible if places are available.

name: Chicken Race / Bootcamp Survivor
description: Chicken Race is Norway’s largest obstacle race for the whole family, held at a former military camp at Helgelandsmoen near Hønefoss. The course is approximately 2 km long, with over 40 different obstacles suitable for both adults and children, including optional challenges and shortcuts for younger participants. Bootcamp Survivor also offers challenging obstacle races over 5 km, 8 km and 16 km, including elite classes that are official qualifying races for the OCR European Championships and OCR World Championship. The event is a celebration filled with excitement, fun and a sense of achievement for all levels and ages.
course_highlights: 2 km family course with over 40 different obstacles
5 km obstacle course with 70 challenging obstacles, including a military obstacle course and mud
8 km and 16 km courses with up to 90 obstacles, water, fire and challenging obstacles
additional: All obstacles are optional, with easier alternative exercises available. Children get free admission to Ringeriksbadet. The event includes wave starts, smoke effects, explosions and medals. Participants are advised to be able to swim for the water obstacles, and safety personnel are present. The event takes place at Helgelandsmoen Næringspark, 3512 Hønefoss. The 5 km course has a non-timed recreational class, and challenging obstacles have alternative exercises. The ability to swim is recommended for Bootcamp Survivor.

name: Lyngdal 5km
description: Welcome to the Lyngdal 5 km road race, a great and inclusive event held in central Lyngdal in early summer. The race features a flat, fast, officially measured course that starts in the town centre, heads down towards Kvavik, crosses towards Rosfjord, and returns to the centre. The event is suitable for both experienced and new runners. There is also a children’s race of approximately 1 km in the town centre. We follow the athletics federation’s age limits for road races and welcome everyone to a running celebration.
course_highlights: Flat and fast 5 km course
Start and finish in central Lyngdal
The course runs via Kvavik and Rosfjord
additional: A children’s race of approximately 1 km is held in the town centre at 10:00 before the main race. The race follows the athletics federation’s age limits for road races. Registration has been listed through EQ-timing. Sources relate to previous editions and do not confirm details for 2027.

name: RunwayK 2027
description: RunwayK is a unique race held on the active runway at Kjeller Airport, one of the oldest active runways in the world. The course is very fast and flat, with minimal elevation gain, making it perfect for both first-time runners and those looking to set a new personal best. Participants can run or roll 5 km or 10 km, and there are also dedicated para categories and a children’s race, Runway Mini. The event offers an exclusive opportunity to run on a runway, with air traffic suspended during the race.
course_highlights: The course runs on the active runway at Kjeller Airport
The 5 km course is fast and flat, with only 4 metres of elevation gain
The 10 km course is among the flattest in the world, with only 7 metres of elevation gain, and includes both the runway and streets
additional: Race bibs can be collected at the airport on race day from 8:00 a.m. Pacers will be available for both the 5K and 10K. All finishers receive a medal, and the top three women and men in each distance receive prize money. Outdoor luggage storage is available at the venue. The Runway Mini children’s race has distances of 200 and 900 metres, and adults can run for free with the children if they line up at the back of the field. The event is open to all ages and levels, including wheelchair users and para categories. Pacers will be available for the 5 km and 10 km. All finishers receive a medal. The 2027 course is under development, and details may be adjusted.

name: Bamford Frontyard
description: Bamford Frontyard is a unique race held in Asker at Vollen Sports Hall. The race consists of a relatively flat 3 km loop, and each loop must be run faster than the previous one. You must complete all previous loops to continue. The race ends when only one runner completes the final loop, and everyone who completes the first loop receives a medal. This makes for an exciting, tactical competition suitable for runners of different levels.
course_highlights: Relatively flat 3 km loop
The race starts with a 30-minute loop; each subsequent loop must be run 1 minute faster
The course runs around Vollen Sports Hall and is well marked
additional: Race bibs can be collected at the start/finish from 15:00 to 16:30. Light refreshments are available: water, cola, crisps, chocolate, oranges and bananas (bring your own cup). Toilets are available in the GUI hall, 50 metres from the start/finish. Participants are encouraged to bring their own chair, food and anything else they need between loops. Bib collection is listed as 15:00–16:30 at the start/finish. Light refreshments are available; bring your own cup, chair and food. Toilets are in the GUI hall, about 50 metres from the start/finish. Everyone who completes the first loop receives a medal.

name: HTB Valestrandsmarka Rundt 5. løp
description: HTB Valestrandsmarka Rundt is an annual recreational race organized by Osterøy IL/Athletics, with a 4.4 km course through the scenic surroundings of Valestrandsmarka. The race has a long tradition and is part of a race series with several events throughout the year. The start is at Furubakken sports ground, with two start times: one for walkers and one for the main field. Participants can look forward to a friendly and inclusive atmosphere, with prizes, cordial and sveler served after the race. Course records earn a cash prize from HTB.
course_highlights: 4.4 km course around Valestrandsmarka
Start and finish at Furubakken sports ground
Scenic surroundings and varied terrain
additional: There are two start times: 18:45 for walkers and 19:00 for the main field. Times in the walking group are recorded only if they are 30 minutes or more. After the race, sveler from Toro and cordial from Saftsuse are served. Course records earn a prize of NOK 3,000 from HTB. The race is part of a series with several races throughout the year, including a Christmas race and a New Year's race. Start for walkers at 18:45 and the main field at 19:00. No race licence required. Course records in regular races are awarded NOK 3,000 from HTB.

name: Preikestolen Backyard Ultra 2027
description: Preikestolen Backyard Ultra 2027 is held at Jørpelands Brug in Jørpelandsvågen. Participants run a fixed 6.7 km loop at the start of every hour, with a maximum of 12 loops, corresponding to approximately 80 km in total. The course offers varied terrain, including asphalt, a pier, gravel road and easy-running trail, and is suitable for ultrarunners looking for a challenging, tactical competition. The event includes a practical briefing before the start, and food and drinks are available in the rest area. The start and finish are at Jørpelands Brug, with good parking and public transport options nearby.
course_highlights: The 6.7 km loop includes asphalt, a pier, gravel road and easy-running trail
Maximum of 12 loops, approximately 80 km in total
Start and finish at Jørpelands Brug, Jørpeland
additional: Bib numbers are collected at the specified location and time. Parking is available by the municipal building on Oldeidevegen in Jørpeland. Bus route 100 stops at the start area. The rest area offers water, squash, cola, sandwiches, fruit, crisps and hot food later on. Toilets and changing facilities are available. A loop starts at the beginning of every hour from 09:00 to 20:00, with the prize-giving at 21:15. The start and finish are at Jørpelands Brug, Sagholmen 4. Parking is available by the municipal building on Oldeidevegen, and bus route 100 stops at Jørpeland Brug. The rest area offers drinks, sandwiches, fruit and crisps, among other things, with hot food later on.

name: Kristiansund Havmaraton
price_range: 50 kr for barneløpet; 300–500 kr for 6, 12 og 23 km
description: Kristiansund Sea Marathon offers a unique coastal running experience with beautiful sea views. The courses follow coastal trails, quays, rocky shoreline and coastal heath, with waves and sea spray close by. Choose from several distances for the whole family, from a children’s race to 23 km around Kirklandet and Gomalandet. The event combines spectacular scenery with technically challenging courses and good facilities at the start and finish.
course_highlights: Course along coastal trails, quays and rocky shoreline, with sea spray
23 km route around Kirklandet and Gomalandet with great views
Varied terrain including asphalt, gravel and coastal trails
additional: Race numbers can be collected at Norodd’s premises at Atlanten stadium (3rd floor). Changing rooms with showers and toilets are available. Luggage storage is at your own risk. Water and sports drinks are available at aid stations along the course. Free parking is available at several locations near the start/finish. Medical staff will be present. The event has an environmental focus, with rubbish bins at aid stations. GPX files are available for the courses. Start times: children’s race at 10:00, 23 km at 10:30, 12 km at 11:00 and 6 km at 11:30. Age limits: 23 km from age 15, 12 km from age 13 and 6 km from age 11. Changing rooms, showers, toilets and aid stations are available.

name: Ottaløpet
description: Ottaløpet is a local recreational race held in the centre of Otta in Gudbrandsdalen. The event offers 10 km, 5 km, an untimed 5 km recreational run, and a 10 km relay, with the start and finish in the park in central Otta. The event has a friendly atmosphere, with prizes for the top three finishers in the 5 km and 10 km, as well as class winners in the 10 km, and a challenge trophy for the male and female 10 km winners. There is also a children’s race for children aged 1 to 12, as well as a company competition to find the fittest company in Nord-Gudbrandsdalen. Ottaløpet has a long history: it began in 1993 and was revived in 2021 with great local enthusiasm.
course_highlights: The course runs mainly on asphalt and gravel
Start and finish in the park in central Otta
The 10 km runners complete two laps of a 5 km course that includes a tartan running track and a riverside promenade
additional: There is a group warm-up in the park led by instructors from Spenst Otta. The relay can be divided into up to five legs. The children’s race is free, and every child receives a prize. The company competition awards a challenge trophy to the company with the most participants finishing. The course is clearly marked, and marshals ensure safety during the race. The 5 km course is one lap, while the 10 km is run over two laps. The relay can be divided into up to five legs of distances chosen by the team. The children’s race is free, and a group warm-up is offered in the park.

name: Ecotrail Bergen
description: EcoTrail Bergen is an environmentally conscious trail race offering four distances through beautiful scenery with spectacular views of the fjord and city. The courses range from 27 km to 91 km and feature challenging terrain, including trails, boggy sections, mountains and cultural landscapes. The race is suitable for both beginners and experienced runners looking to enjoy a sense of achievement and community in scenic surroundings. The event emphasizes the environment and sustainability, and participants receive, among other things, merino wool race shirts from Devold.
course_highlights: Varied terrain with trails, boggy sections and bare rock
Spectacular views of the fjord, city and cultural landscapes
Cultural heritage sites and historic areas along the course
additional: Aid stations provide water, sports drinks, salty and sweet snacks, but no hot food. Mandatory equipment includes a cup or soft flask, an emergency blanket, a mobile phone and a bank card/ID. There are cut-off times along the way on the longer distances. Bib pickup takes place before the race, including at Intersport at Thon Senter Bergen. The organizer states that the courses have drink and food stations. For the 27 km, a cup or soft flask, mobile phone and bank card or ID card are listed as mandatory equipment.

name: Jotunheimen Trail Run
description: Jotunheimen Trail Run offers an unforgettable trail running experience in Norway’s stunning high-alpine landscapes. Participants can choose from several distances, including 12K, 16K, 21K, Marathon, and an epic 73K Ultra that loops around Lake Bygdin. The race features challenging elevation gains, flowing mountain trails, and breathtaking panoramic views, all in a friendly and welcoming atmosphere suitable for runners of all levels. The event includes well-organized check-in, aid stations, and post-race activities such as sauna and swimming at Bygdin.
course_highlights: Ultra: 73 km loop around Lake Bygdin with demanding elevation and runnable high-mountain plateau sections
Marathon: 40 km trail with a scenic detour via Skjetning and a final sprint to the finish line in Bygdin
Half Marathon: 17 km trail with a major climb to panoramic ridge views and a fast downhill finish in Beitostølen
additional: Check-in and bib collection at Beito Resort Hotel and Bygdin Høyfjellshotell. Pre-race pasta dinner at Lodge 900 (booking required). Post-race sauna and swimming available at Bygdin. Shuttle buses provided for Ultra and Marathon runners. Award ceremony for top finishers at Bygdin Høyfjellshotell. Social shake-out run and shoe testing with La Sportiva before race day. The race is part of the Norway Trail Series. The program also includes race briefings, meals, shuttle buses, and award ceremonies; some dinners and bus tickets must be booked in advance.

name: Lofoten Skyrace
description: HOKA Lofoten Skyrace is a spectacular trail race held in Svolvær, with three distances: 15 km, 32 km and 42 km. The courses offer varied, technical terrain, panoramic views, challenging ridges and experiences in nature whatever the weather. The race takes place over two days, with the marathon distance on 2 July and the shorter distances on 3 July 2027. A dedicated SkyCrew helps ensure a great race experience and safety along the way. Participants must be self-sufficient with drinks and nutrition, and must carry the mandatory equipment.
course_highlights: 42 km with approximately 2,000 metres of elevation gain over Matmora, Isvatnryggen and Tjeldbergtinden
Technical, varied terrain with panoramic views and challenging ridges
Natural and staffed drink stations along the way on all distances
additional: Registration opens on 15 September 2026 at 12:00, with a queue system to ensure fair allocation. Bib collection takes place at Sport1 in Svolvær in the days before the race. A HOKA shake-out run and Kids race are also held beforehand. Bus transport to the marathon start is available. Runners must bring a fully charged mobile phone, drinks and nutrition, and mandatory equipment may be checked before the start. Registration for 2027 opens on 15 September 2026 at 12:00. Participants in the 42 km race must be at least 18 years old and must provide their own drinks and nutrition. Bus transport to the start can be selected during registration, and the courses may be changed at short notice due to weather or other unforeseen circumstances.

name: Jølster Maraton
description: Jølster Marathon is a popular race that brings runners from all over the country to beautiful Jølster. The race starts and finishes at Jølstrahallen in Vassenden and offers four distances: marathon, half marathon, 10 km and 5 km. The route follows scenic stretches in the area, and places are limited, so early registration is recommended. The event also includes extra activities for the whole family and a music and marathon quiz the evening after the race.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Jølstrahallen in Vassenden
The route follows beautiful stretches in Jølster
Refreshment stations with water, squash, cola, sports drink and bananas
additional: Maximum 1,300 participants. Prize-giving at 13:00 for all distances. 5% of the proceeds go to a good cause. A pink T-shirt can be purchased, partially sponsored by Enivest. Cars are not allowed to drive to the event office on race day. Race numbers should be collected on Friday or well before the start. Extra activities, including a cycling event and a mini race for children, are held. Great prizes from sponsors are drawn among all participants. The top three in each category and distance receive prizes.

name: Bitihorn Opp
price_range: 150 kr under 17 år; 300 kr fra 17 år
description: Bitihorn Opp is an informal, laid-back uphill race up majestic Bitihorn in Øystre Slidre. The race is suitable for everyone, whether you walk or run, fast or slow, and focuses on an enjoyable outing in spectacular nature. The course follows stone steps and trails on the “front side” of Bitihorn, offering a unique nature experience with 450 metres of elevation gain over 2 kilometres. The event supports local sport, and all participants receive a prize, with extra prizes for the fastest man and woman.
course_highlights: The course follows majestic stone steps and trails on the front side of Bitihorn
450 metres of elevation gain over 2 kilometres
A spectacular nature experience in mountain terrain
additional: Bib distribution from 11:30 at the start of the stairs. Parking at Båtskaret, with signs on race day. The proceeds go to Øystre Slidre IL. All participants receive a prize, with extra prizes for the fastest man and woman, as well as fun draw prizes. Registration via EQ Timing. All participants receive a prize, with extra prizes for the fastest woman and man. Parking is listed at Båtskaret or Båtskardstølen.

name: Hornindal Rundt
location: Hornindal, Volda, Møre og Romsdal, Norway

name: Oslo Løpsfestival, Maridalsvannet rundt

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Dagsbillett SOLO Deltakere kr 475,00 kr 332,50 + Adm. gebyr (25 NOK + 3%) -30%

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Festivalpass SOLO Deltakere kr 1475,00 kr 1032,50 + Adm. gebyr (25 NOK + 3%) -30%

description: Maridalsvannet Rundt is one of eight races in the Oslo Running Festival, which follows the capital’s beautiful trails and roads. The race has a mass start on Sunday, July 4 at 11:00, with the start and finish at Frysja, a lovely area with good facilities and opportunities for swimming, barbecuing, and relaxing after the race. The course is 13.5 km long and offers scenic surroundings around Lake Maridalsvannet. The Oslo Running Festival gives you the flexibility to run alone or with others, and you can take part in several races with a festival pass or day tickets.
course_highlights: The 13.5 km course goes around Lake Maridalsvannet
Start and finish at Frysja, with good facilities such as a café and grocery store
Lovely start and finish area with opportunities for swimming and barbecuing
additional: Race bibs can be picked up at Löplabbet Oslo city centre from April 7. The same race bib is used throughout the series. The course is marked only for the mass start. Timing is recorded by a chip attached to the race bib, which must be visible on your chest. There are good public transport connections and several parking spaces near the start area. The race can be completed at a time that suits you during the period June 25–July 4, 2027. An early-bird price is listed; prices vary by ticket type.

name: Perseløpet 5 km, 10 km, halvmaraton
description: Perseløpet is a simple, fast race event at Ås school in Eidsvoll, featuring a flat, measured 2,633-metre loop. The race offers seven distances from 3 km to 100 km, including 5 km, 10 km and the half marathon, and is suitable for anyone looking to chase a personal best. Participants can set out their own bottles and gels on their personal nutrition table, which they pass each lap, giving them good control over their nutrition during the race. The event has good facilities, with changing rooms, toilets and free parking at the venue.
course_highlights: Flat, measured 2,633-metre loop
Each participant’s own nutrition table at every lap
Good facilities, with changing rooms and toilets inside Ås school
additional: Race numbers are collected at the school using self-service, approximately two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. The race has a lap-time calculator for planning lap times. At selected races, 9th grade students from Feiring school staff an official drink station and raise money for their school trip. Participants who set a personal best can ring the bell near the finish area. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. Race numbers are collected at the school using self-service from approximately two hours before the start.

name: Perseløpet ¤5- 2027
description: Perseløpet is a simple, fast race event at Ås School in Eidsvoll, featuring a flat, accurately measured 2,633-meter loop. The race offers seven distances from 3 km to 100 km, giving runners the opportunity to set personal records in a well-equipped setting with a dedicated nutrition table. Bibs are collected via self-service at the venue, which has free parking, changing rooms, and toilets. The race is organized by Feiring IL and has a tradition of many personal records, with a friendly atmosphere where runners can celebrate their personal records by ringing the bell at the finish.
course_highlights: Flat, accurately measured 2,633-meter loop
Dedicated nutrition table passed on every lap
Flat road races with the opportunity to achieve fast times
additional: Bibs are collected via self-service about two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms, and toilets are available at the venue. Runners can place their own bottles and gels on the nutrition table before the start. At selected races, 9th-grade students from Feiring School staff an official refreshment station to raise money for their school trip. A lap-time calculator is available to help plan split times. The weather forecast is updated four times daily based on satellite data for the area. Registration via RaceDays. Free parking, changing rooms, and toilets are available at the venue. Bibs are collected via self-service at the school, and runners can place their own drinks and nutrition at the nutrition table.

name: Feriespretten 2027
description: Feriespretten is the most beautiful and fun summer trail race, organized by Hope IL in Risør, Agder. The race offers two distances over varied, hilly terrain, with the start and finish in the same place. The long course of approximately 9 km is suited to those looking for a proper workout in beautiful natural surroundings, while the short course of approximately 5 km is perfect for beginners, children and families, or as an untimed fun run. Feriespretten is a family-friendly event that brings experienced runners and beginners together for an enjoyable race experience.
course_highlights: Two distances over varied, hilly terrain
Start and finish in the same place
The course runs through beautiful natural surroundings on the Sandnes Peninsula
additional: The race takes place on Tuesday, 7 July 2026 at 18:00. The short course can be run untimed as a fun run. The organizer is Hope IL. Results and statistics from previous years are available on the website. Untimed recreational classes are offered for the 5 km and 9 km distances. The time is provided in the organizer’s channels.

name: Hestane Skyrace
organizer: Lars Øvrebø og Torstein Bolstad Blikra, med Gaular IL
description: Hestane Skyrace is a demanding skyrace over the spectacular peaks of Storehesten and Lisjehesten in Bygstad. The race features technical climbing, an exposed ridge and magnificent panoramic views in dramatic natural surroundings. There are two distances: 32 km with 1,900 metres of elevation gain and 26 km with 1,400 metres of elevation gain, both across challenging mountain terrain. The event is a celebration for the whole village, with activities for participants and spectators alike.
course_highlights: Technical climbing and an exposed ridge over Storehesten and Lisjehesten
Magnificent panoramic views and challenging mountain terrain
Two distances: 32 km (~1,900 m elevation gain) and 26 km (~1,400 m elevation gain)
additional: Mandatory equipment: mobile phone, 1 L of water, emergency ration and wind jacket. Cutoff at Skaraly at 15:30; final finish at 19:00. Parking at Langeland Ski Centre costs 50 kr. Race bibs can be collected on Friday 9 July and on race day from 07:00. There are staffed stations with water and first aid along the route. After-run gathering at Tønna in Bygstad from 20:00, with food and socialising. Start and finish at Langeland Ski Centre. Start at 09:00. Registration via Racedays.

name: Black Lake Race
description: Black Lake Race is a challenging mountain trail race held in Vågstranda, Norway, featuring stunning views over Norwegian fjords. The main 29 km course combines runnable terrain, steep climbs, and exposed ridge running, including a demanding ascent to Trollstolen and a high mountain ridge section. There is also a faster and more accessible 20 km course that mixes gravel roads, forest trails, alpine terrain, and technical descents. The race offers a unique experience in spectacular natural surroundings with aid stations and mandatory GPX navigation for the longer course.
course_highlights: Steep climbs, including more than 850 vertical meters of ascent to Trollstolen
Exposed mountain ridge running with panoramic fjord views
Technical descents and alpine terrain
additional: The 29 km race requires mandatory GPX navigation loaded onto GPS watches. Aid stations with food and drinks are available along the course. A 5-hour cut-off applies at Checkpoint 3 on the 29 km course, with an alternative route for late participants. Running poles are permitted. Free camping is offered for participants at Hjelvik Idrettsplass, with assistance available for campervan/caravan parking upon request.

name: Melbuløpet
location: Melbu torg, Melbu, Hadsel, Nordland, Norway
description: Melbuløpet takes place at Melbu Square and offers three officially measured distances: 2.5 km, 5 km and 10 km on a very flat, fast course, offering good opportunities to achieve fast times. A children’s race of approximately 600 metres is also held for the youngest participants. The race is part of Sommer-Melbu, a long-running summer festival held since 1986 and characterised by broad local involvement and a strong volunteer spirit.
course_highlights: Very flat and fast course
Three officially measured distances: 2.5 km, 5 km and 10 km
Children’s race of approximately 600 metres
additional: The children’s race starts at 15:30 and the competitive race categories start at 16:00. Children’s race participants register on site. The race is held as part of the Sommer-Melbu festival, which lasts ten days and is run by volunteers. The listed start location is Melbu Square. Registration for the competitive race categories is via EQ Timing, while children’s race participants register on site.

name: Hornindal Rundt
description: Hornindal Rundt is a demanding mountain ultramarathon through the spectacular scenery of Hornindal, surrounded by some of the finest mountains in the Nordic region. The race covers 75 kilometres with 5,600 metres of elevation gain and includes 20 mountain checkpoints. Participants experience a tough and varied course with views of Jostedalsbreen, the Sunnmøre Alps and the sea, and are challenged both physically and mentally in one of Norway’s most demanding trail races.
course_highlights: 75 km ultramarathon with 5,600 metres of elevation gain
20 mountain checkpoints along the route
Views of Jostedalsbreen, the Sunnmøre Alps and the sea
additional: The 75 km ultramarathon starts at 07:00 from Honndalshallen. There are cut-off times along the course to ensure safety, with the first at Horndøla Bru and the second at Holskarsætra (checkpoint 13). Participants in the 75 km race must carry mandatory equipment, including a headlamp, clothing and a mobile phone. For the 75 km race, the start is at Honndalshallen at 07:00, and mandatory equipment includes a headlamp, clothing and a mobile phone. The 38 km race starts at Horndøla Bru at 11:00 and finishes at Honndalshallen. The race information on the website applies to 2026; the date and details for 2027 have not been confirmed in the available sources.

name: Sommerkarusell Ålesund - 2. løp
description: The Summer Series in Ålesund is a long-running race series held in scenic surroundings along Vasstranda by Lillevatnet and Brusdalsvatnet. The courses are relatively flat and run on asphalt with little traffic, offering good conditions for both the 5 km and 10 km distances. The races start from the car park by the walking trail at the western end of Lillevatnet in Spjelkavik. The atmosphere is friendly, with prizes and medals for participants who take part in multiple races. The Summer Series has a long history in Ålesund and is now back under the organisation of Ålesundløpene.
course_highlights: The courses run along Vasstranda on the south side of Lillevatnet and Brusdalsvatnet
Relatively flat asphalt courses with little traffic
Start and finish at the car park by the walking trail at the western end of Lillevatnet in Spjelkavik
additional: The 10 km starts at 18:00 and the 5 km at 18:05. The courses have been officially measured by Kondis. Gift prizes are awarded after each race. Medals go to participants who take part in 2 or 3 races in the series. Course records for both the 5 km and 10 km distances are listed. The participation record is 132 finishers. Registration is through EQ Timing. Participants who finish at least two races in the series receive a medal at the final race of the season.

name: Yttersia Skyrace Senja
description: Yttersia Skyrace Senja is a rugged and accessible skyrace held on the spectacular outer side of Senja, starting and finishing at Yttersia Base in Skaland. The course takes participants through dramatic coastal mountain terrain with long ridgelines, steep cliffs and fantastic views of Bergsøyene, Steinfjorden and Okshornan. The race features a continuous, runnable climb to Husfjellet, followed by narrow, exposed ridges and challenging technical terrain. It finishes with a social atmosphere, music and an after-run gathering at the finish area. This race is for those who want to experience authentic Senja terrain and a day filled with community and good spirits.
course_highlights: Dramatic coastal mountain terrain with long ridgelines and steep cliffs
Continuous, runnable climb to Husfjellet (632 m above sea level) with spectacular views
Technical, untouched terrain at Nonshaugen, home to a historic graphite mine
additional: The race starts with a short stretch of gravel road before continuing onto trail and uphill terrain. There is one drinking station at Litjebrusen. The finish area at Yttersia Base offers music, an announcer, awards, food, drinks and an after-run gathering with a social atmosphere into the afternoon and evening. For 2026, the course is listed as running over gravel road, trail and technical mountain terrain, with one drinking station. These details are not confirmed for 2027.

name: Blefjells Beste
description: Blefjells Beste is a trail race on Blefjell that passes several of the most beautiful places on Store-Ble. The race offers distances of 92, 53, 24, 10 and 5 km, and is a social, informal event for everyone who enjoys being outdoors in the forest and mountains. The start and finish are at Bestebu, a private cabin at Klengstøl. The courses are mainly on trails and mountain terrain, with the final kilometres on gravel roads. Participants must carry all their own food, drink and equipment, as there are no food or drink stations along the way.
course_highlights: Trail race with distances of 92, 53, 24, 10 and 5 km
The courses are mainly on trails and mountain terrain, with 150 to 3,150 metres of elevation gain
Start and finish at the Bestebu cabin at Klengstøl, along Store-Bleveien
additional: The Storetroll course (92 km) consists of completing the other distances—53+24+10+5 km—in sequence. For the 92 km race, there are time limits for passing through the event area: after 1 lap (53 km) by Saturday at 12:00, and after 2 laps (53 + 24 km) by Saturday at 18:00. The 53 km and 24 km courses are not marked by the organiser, while the 5 km and 10 km courses are well marked. Name changes cost 150 kr for the 92, 53 and 24 km distances, and are free for the 10 and 5 km distances. The race requires participants to respect wild reindeer and leave no litter. There are no food or drink stations along the way, but clean water is normally easy to find in the mountains. Participants must carry their own food, drink and equipment; there are no food or drink stations. The event is listed for 23–24 July 2027, with registration opening on 1 December 2026.

name: Rondane Backyard Ultra
description: Rondane Backyard Ultra is a unique ultrarun in the beautiful natural surroundings of Rondane, held at Stormoegga Ski Arena in Folldal. The race follows a scenic and varied loop through the Kroktjønna area, with pine forest, trails, gravel roads and idyllic ponds, and the Rondane mountains as a spectacular backdrop. The competition is a “Last Man Standing” race, with a new loop starting every hour, and continues until only one runner remains. In 2027, a separate night course will be introduced, offering participants a different experience in the dark. The arena’s service building offers facilities such as showers, changing rooms and a lounge for runners and supporters.
course_highlights: A varied route on forest trails, gravel paths and tractor roads in scenic surroundings
The course passes the Kroktjønna swimming area twice per lap
Night course on gravel road and asphalt between midnight and 06:00
additional: The race starts on 24 July 2027 at 09:00 and continues as long as runners complete the lap in under one hour. The service building at Stormoegga Ski Arena offers toilets, changing rooms, showers and a lounge. Participants may pitch their own tents and park caravans/campervans on site. A reflective vest is mandatory between 23:00 and 04:00, and a headlamp is recommended between 00:00 and 03:00. The race takes place on private gravel roads with some vehicle traffic, and runners must run on the left-hand side. First aid is available, and the race director can be contacted by phone on 909 56 674. Race bibs and timing chips are used. All places are sold out, but there is a waiting list to take over resold race entries. The start and finish are at Stormoegga Ski Arena, which has a lounge, kitchen, toilets, changing rooms and showers. Camping or parking a campervan/caravan at the arena is permitted.

name: Bleik Backyard Ultra - Last Man Standing
Kyststien Trail Ultra

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Preliminärt pris for løpet 2027 er 500 kr pluss eventuelt 100 kr for transport.

description: Kyststien Trail Ultra is an unforgettable 50 km ultramarathon along the Coastal Trail from Helgeroa to Gon Camping. The race offers varied terrain, including idyllic sandy beaches, technical trails along cliffs and coves, and spectacular panoramic views of the sea and lush countryside. It is a challenge that requires good preparation, with demanding climbs and descents, but also offers the joy of running and a wonderful sense of community among participants. The race celebrates nature and a passion for running, and encourages respect for the surroundings.
course_highlights: 50 km along the Coastal Trail over varied terrain: sand, grass, mountains, stairs, rocks, roots and gravel
Spectacular panoramic views of the sea, cliffs and lush countryside
Technical coastal trails with demanding climbs and descents
additional: Race bibs can be collected the evening before or on race day. The finish at Gonhytta offers water, drinks, snacks and hot soup. Prizes for the top 3 women and men, plus a race-bib raffle. All finishers receive a locally made birch medal. There is an opportunity to take a free hot shower and a cold sea swim. The race has 5 staffed aid stations with first aid, toilets, drinks and snacks. The course is marked with blue blazes and additional signs; a GPX file is recommended for navigation. Maximum 180 participants; a waiting list will be available if the race fills up. The start is at Blokkebukta camping, with the finish at Gonhytta at Gon Camping. Participants are provided with refreshments and a free hot shower, and all finishers receive a medal made from local birch.

name: Mefjellet Opp 2027
description: Mefjellet Opp is a traditional uphill race organized by Valldal Idrettslag in Fjørå, Valldal. The race features a challenging climb up Mefjellet and attracts both local and visiting runners looking for a demanding and scenic experience. The event is a great opportunity to test your fitness in beautiful surroundings and experience the welcoming atmosphere of Valldal IL.
course_highlights: Steep uphill climb up Mefjellet
Scenic surroundings in Fjørå, Valldal
A traditional race with strong local roots
additional: The event is organized by Valldal Idrettslag. No specific information about the start time, price, or registration was found. Contact person for the event: leiar@valldalil.no. A village brunch is also held at the clubhouse in November, and the clubhouse is available for private use in June, but these are not directly related to the race. Previous editions have had a recreational start from Fjørå town center or Hauge, and a mass start for the competition classes. There have been two water stations along the course.

name: Kvitfjell Stuttlaup
description: Kvitfjell Stuttlaup is a 13-kilometre trail race featuring technical trails and varied terrain in beautiful Kvitfjell. The race starts at Kvitfjelleggen and finishes at Tyrihanstunet, with approximately 240 metres of elevation gain. Known for its challenging and fun trails, the race is part of Lauparfestivalen, which also includes several other races and activities. Participants can look forward to a great mountain running experience, a lively atmosphere and the option to buy food in the finish area.
course_highlights: 13 km with approximately 8 km of trail and 5 km of gravel road
Technical and fun trail on the west side of Svinåa
240 metres of elevation gain over varied terrain
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 11:00 at the start. There is a drinks and food station at Svinslåvangen after 8.5 km. Parking is not available at the start. Recommended parking locations are Skitorget, by Tyrihans, along the roads towards the top (west side), or at Gudbrandsgard Hotel (east side). Carpooling is organised, with participants meeting at 10:00 in the parking area at the bottom of Vestsideløypa. Food can be purchased from Tyrihanstunet in the finish area. The race does not provide sports drinks or gels, in order to keep the event simple and affordable. The festival website lists the event as 24–25 July, which does not match the stated race date of 30 July 2027.

name: Kvitfjell Langlaup
description: Kvitfjell Running Festival offers three challenging races through varied terrain in Ringebu, Innlandet. Kvitfjell Opp is a brutal uphill race up the Olympic downhill course, climbing 838 metres over 3.2 km. Langlaupet is a 25 km long-distance race with 19 km of trail and 6.5 km of road, offering an extra challenge for those who want more after the uphill race. Stuttlaupet is a 13 km race with technical trails and gravel roads, perfect for those looking for a shorter but challenging mountain run. All races finish at Tyrihanstunet, where good food and a social atmosphere are also on offer.
course_highlights: Kvitfjell Opp: 3.2 km uphill race climbing 838 metres up the Olympic downhill course
Langlaupet: 25 km through varied terrain, with 19 km of trail and 6.5 km of gravel road; highest point approximately 1,100 metres above sea level
Stuttlaupet: 13 km with approximately 8 km of trail and 5 km of gravel road; a technical and enjoyable course
additional: Race bibs are distributed at the start of each race. Kvitfjell Opp starts by the lift at the bottom, while Langlaupet and Stuttlaupet start from Kvitfjelleggen behind the summit café. There are refreshment stations along Langlaupet and Stuttlaupet, as well as a refreshment station on Kvitfjell Opp at the mid-station. For Kvitfjell Opp, parking is recommended at the mid-station; for Langlaupet and Stuttlaupet, parking is recommended at Skitorget or Gudbrandsgard Hotel. A children’s race starts at 13:00 on Saturday during the festival, with a medal and drink at the finish. Talks and an after-run event are also part of the festival. Langlaupet is part of Kvitfjell Running Festival, which also includes Kvitfjell Opp and Stuttlaupet. Weather conditions can change in the mountains.

name: Kvitfjell Lauparfestival 2027
description: Kvitfjell Running Festival 2027 takes place in Kvitfjell from 27 to 31 July 2027. The festival offers a varied programme of sport and culture, with tickets available through EQ Timing. The event starts early in the day and continues until late in the evening, offering participants a great experience in beautiful surroundings.
course_highlights: Kvitfjell Uphill follows the former Olympic downhill course up the mountain.
The approximately 25 km long-distance race traverses varied terrain, including trails and gravel roads.
