The short race offers a shorter 13 km trail-running distance.
additional: Tickets are sold through EQ Timing. The event runs from early morning until late evening. It takes place in Kvitfjell, with a map and directions available on the website. The programme also includes an uphill race for children, talks at Tyrihanstunet, and an after-run.

name: Jordbærdilten 2027
location: Valldal, Fjord, Møre og Romsdal, Norway

name: Voss Løpskarusell 4
description: Voss Running Series is a running series for everyone, with 5 km races that start and finish at Idrettsplassen in Voss. The course goes through Prestegardsmoen and along the waterfront promenade, and is suitable for both recreational runners and runners aged 9 and up. The races are held on Mondays, starting at 19:00, and you can sign up for individual races or all six races together. This is a friendly recreational race that welcomes everyone to take part and enjoy Voss’s running community.
course_highlights: 5 km course starting and finishing at Idrettsplassen
Route through Prestegardsmoen
Run along the waterfront promenade
additional: Registration is online via EQ Timing. A discount is available when registering for all six races by the second race; otherwise, you can register for each race individually. The fifth race starts at 18:30 instead of 19:00. Search for “Voss Løpskarusell 2027” on EQ Timing to register.

name: Voss Løpskarusell 2027, løp 4
description: Voss Running Series 2027 is a running series for everyone, with races on Mondays at 19:00. The course is 5 km long, starting and finishing at Voss Sports Ground, and runs through Prestegardsmoen and along the promenade. The event welcomes recreational runners and runners aged 9 and up to enjoyable fun runs in scenic surroundings. Registration is online, with a discount for signing up for all six races by the second race.
course_highlights: 5 km course starting and finishing at Voss Sports Ground
Loop through Prestegardsmoen
Run along the promenade
additional: Registration is online only via EQ Timing. You can register for all six races together at a discounted rate if you sign up by the second race. The fifth race starts at 18:30, while the others start at 19:00. You can register for individual races or get a discount by signing up for all six races by race 2.

name: Stranda Fjord Trail Race
description: Stranda Fjord Trail Race offers a spectacular series of trail races in the beautiful landscape around Stranda, Møre og Romsdal. The races range from a fast and challenging 7 km on gravel paths to extreme 95 km ultramarathons with significant elevation gain. Participants experience technically demanding trails, magnificent fjord views and varied terrain, including alpine sections and bogland. After crossing the finish line, runners are invited to a barbecue and concert, creating a sociable and festive atmosphere. This is a race for both beginners and experienced mountain runners looking for a unique nature experience.
course_highlights: 7 km course with 370 m ascent and 500 m descent, with views of the Geirangerfjord
12 km course with 848 m ascent and descent, offering panoramic views of the fjord
25 km of technically demanding terrain with 1,800 m of elevation change, previously part of the Golden Trail World Series
additional: Registration includes admission to the barbecue and live concert after the race. GPX files for the courses are available in the race guide. The races range from 7 km to 95 km, with significant elevation changes and technically demanding terrain. The race guide contains course information and GPX files. The other distances are 7 km Ljøbrekka Express, 12 km Skurahornet Up ’n Down, 55 km and 95 km.

name: Meråker Mountain Challenge
distance_verbose: 100 miles, 50 miles, 70 km, 50 km, Halvmaraton, 8 km, 2 km
description: Meråker Mountain Challenge is a demanding ultramarathon offering distances from 2 km to 161 km, including a spectacular 100-mile loop around Meråker Municipality. The courses feature varied terrain with mountains, forests, marshland and several peaks over 1,000 metres, and are suitable for both experienced ultrarunners and recreational runners. The event has a long tradition and also includes the Norwegian Championships in trail ultrarunning. The start and finish are at Teveltunet, and the race places a strong emphasis on safety, good logistics and runner support along the way.
course_highlights: The course crosses varied terrain with mountains, forests and marshland
The 70 km distance passes nine peaks over 1,000 metres in Meråker Municipality
The 100-mile loop goes around the entire municipality and features spectacular mountain sections
additional: All races start on Saturday, 1 August, except the 100 km and 100-mile races, which start on Friday evening. Race bibs are collected primarily at Teveltunet, and transport to and from the start is available by free bus with advance registration. Personal support is permitted on the 100K and 100M distances. Drinking water sources are not publicly monitored, and using a water filter is recommended. The event has offered several distances, including 8 km, 20 km, 50 km, 70 km, 100 km and 100 miles. On the 100-mile course, one drop bag may be handed in before the start and collected at Nøstmo after approximately 93 km.

name: Craft Syv Søstre Skyrace
description: Craft Seven Sisters Skyrace is a challenging and spectacular mountain race on the Helgeland coast in Nordland, traversing the iconic De Syv Søstre mountain range. The race features technical terrain with steep climbs and descents, and offers fantastic views of the Helgeland coast. There are two distances: Syv Søstre, approximately 23 km with 2,900 metres of elevation gain, crossing all seven peaks, and Dronningruta, approximately 13 km with 1,300 metres of elevation gain, crossing the two northernmost peaks. Both distances are ISF-certified and UTMB Index races, making this an internationally recognised skyrace. The race takes place on 7 August 2027 and offers a memorable day in the mountains for local and visiting runners alike.
course_highlights: Technical terrain with steep climbs and descents
Fantastic views of the Helgeland coast from several peaks
ISF-certified course and UTMB Index race for both distances
additional: The race has two distances: Syv Søstre (23 km, 2,900 metres of elevation gain) and Dronningruta (13 km, 1,300 metres of elevation gain). All participants are required to download and use a GPX file on a suitable device. There are cutoff points along the course to ensure safety and emergency preparedness. A minimum of 1 litre of fluid is recommended at the start. Wool base layers are recommended in cold weather. The descent from Botnkrona requires extra concentration, and fixed ropes are in place at some points. The minimum age for Dronningruta is 14; participants under 18 must be accompanied by a guardian. The race is organised by Stigningsløp AS, with the aim of providing a safe and well-organised mountain race. It takes place on 7 August 2027 in Alstahaug. Both distances are certified by the International Skyrunning Federation and are included in the UTMB Index.

name: Solan Gundersens Bergmaraton
description: Solan Gundersen’s Mountain Marathon is organized by Alvdal Sports Club and offers challenges for all ages and levels, from a children’s race to demanding distances for those looking to push themselves further. The race follows Alvdal’s popular hiking trails, starting and finishing at Steimoegga Sports Complex. Great atmosphere and enjoyable experiences for the whole family are a priority, with both recreational and competitive categories available. Participants may encounter familiar characters such as Solan Gundersen during the race, which also features food and drink stations along the course.
course_highlights: The race follows Alvdal’s well-used hiking trails
Start and finish at Steimoegga Sports Complex
Food and drink stations along the course and at the finish
additional: Participants can enter the recreational or competitive category. Distances include 1 km, 6 km, 22 km (half marathon) and 48 km (marathon+). Age limits apply: 15 years for 22 km and 18 years for 48 km. Changing rooms and showers are available at Steimoegga. Bibs must be worn visibly on the chest. A license must be purchased when registering. Food and drink can be purchased at the kiosk at the start/finish. Free parking is available at Steimoegga. Dogs are allowed in the recreational category for 22 km. There will be cutoff times for 48 km. The entry fee is paid when collecting the race bib or invoiced after the race. Participants can opt out of having their photos used in marketing. Registration is open until the start. The entry fee is paid via Vipps when collecting the race bib or invoiced after the race. Food and drink stations are available along the course, and free parking, changing rooms and showers are available at Steimoegga.

name: Oslo Løpsfestival, Østmarka halvmaraton

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Dagsbillett SOLO Deltakere kr 475,00 + Adm. gebyr (25 NOK + 3%)

description: Østmarka Half Marathon is part of the Oslo Running Festival and offers an exceptional nature experience through some of the most beautiful areas of Oslomarka. The race follows scenic forest roads through varied terrain and past idyllic lakes, and is suitable both for those looking to run a good time and for those who want to enjoy a fantastic day outdoors in the forest. This is the first-ever half marathon in the Oslo Running Festival, with a mass start on August 8 at 11:00 at Rustadsaga Sportsstue in Oslo.
course_highlights: Course through beautiful areas of Oslomarka
Scenic forest roads and varied terrain
Idyllic lakes and nature experiences all the way to the finish
additional: Race bibs can be collected from Löplabbet Oslo sentrum from April 7. The same race bib is used throughout the series. A new race bib can be purchased for 75 kr. Courses will only be marked for the mass start. GPX files and Strava links for the course are available to download. Registration is binding, with no refunds or transfer of race bibs. The race can be completed during the festival period from July 30 to August 8; the mass start is on August 8 at 11:00. Early-bird prices are listed and may increase on January 1.

name: Perseløpet 5 km, 10 km, halvmaraton
description: Perseløpet is a simple, fast race event at Ås School in Eidsvoll, featuring a flat, officially measured 2,633-metre loop. The event offers seven distances from 3 km to 100 km, including 5 km, 10 km and the half marathon, and helps runners achieve fast times with a dedicated nutrition table along the course. Race bibs are collected using self-service at the venue, which has free parking, changing rooms and toilets. The race is known for its great atmosphere and the many runners who set personal records; it is a tradition to ring the bell at the finish to celebrate a new PB.
course_highlights: Flat, officially measured 2,633-metre loop
Dedicated nutrition table passed on every lap
Venue at Ås School with free parking, changing rooms and toilets
additional: Race bibs are collected using self-service approximately two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. The race has a dedicated nutrition table where runners can leave their own bottles and gels. At selected races, ninth-graders from Feiring School staff an official drinks station, which also raises money for their school trip. It is a tradition to ring the bell at the finish area to celebrate a new personal record. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. Registration is via RaceDays; half-marathon runners can arrange their own drinks and nutrition.

name: Perseløpet ¤6 - 2027
description: Perseløpet is a race in Eidsvoll, starting and finishing at Ås School in Hammerås. The event features a flat, officially measured 2,633-metre loop and offers seven distances from 3 km to 100 km, designed for fast times. Participants can set up their own nutrition table, which they pass each lap, giving them easy access to their own supplies without the need for aid-station logistics. The event has a friendly atmosphere where personal bests are celebrated by ringing the bell near the finish area.
course_highlights: Flat, officially measured 2,633-metre loop
Seven distances from 3 km to 100 km
Own nutrition table passed each lap
additional: Race bibs are self-service pickup at Ås School from around two hours before the start. Free parking, changing facilities and toilets are available at the venue. At selected races, ninth graders from Feiring School staff an official drinks station, which also raises money for their school trip. The weather forecast is updated four times daily using satellite data for the area around Ås School. Runners can have their own nutrition table.

name: Stomperudkarusellen- løp nr 3
location: Stomperud Stadion, Lørenvegen 2, Sørum, Lillestrøm, Norway
price_range: Enkeltløp: 220 kr for voksne og 110 kr for barn, med lisens i tillegg
description: Stomperudkarusellen is a long-established series of races organized by Sørum IL since 1981. The series consists of four races with varying distances from 800 meters to 9 kilometers, including shorter options for children and young people. The races take place in scenic surroundings, with the start and finish at Stomperud Stadion and nearby areas. Participants use the same race number throughout the series, and the event is open to both adults and children. Children who are members of Sørum IL can take part for free when they register.
course_highlights: Race 3: Lysløypa, 6 km with a shorter option
Start and finish at Stomperud Stadion, Lørenvegen 2, Sørum
Varied terrain with gravel roads, trails, and an athletics track for shorter distances
additional: Participants use the same race number in all races in the series. Children who are members of Sørum IL can take part for free if they register no later than one week before race day. The races have shorter options for the youngest participants. Start locations vary between Sørum Skole and Stomperud Stadion depending on the race. Race no. 3 meets at Stomperud Stadion, Lørenvegen 2, Sørum. The prices listed by the organizer apply to 2026.

name: Stomperudkarusellen 2027. Bare løp 3 (Lysløypa)
description: Stomperudkarusellen is a long-running race series organized by Sørum IL since 1981. The series consists of four races over varying distances, including Lysløypa, a 6 km race that is part of this year’s Race 3. The races are suitable for both adults and children, with shorter options for the youngest participants. Participants use the same bib number for all the races, which take place at Stomperud Stadion and in the surrounding areas of Sørum.
course_highlights: Race 3 Lysløypa: 6 km, with a shorter 500 m option
Traditional routes in the local area around Stomperud Stadion
Shorter distances for children and young people
additional: Participants use the same bib number for all races in the series. Children who are members of Sørum IL can participate for free if they register no later than one week before race day. The races offer shorter options for the youngest participants. The events take place at Stomperud Stadion and in the surrounding areas, which have a well-maintained network of walking trails and running routes. The prices and race dates listed on the organizer’s website apply to 2026 and do not confirm the 2027 edition. In 2026, the same bib number is used for all races in the series.

name: Sommerkarusell Ålesund - 3. løp
location: Vestenden av Lillevatnet, Spjelkavik, Ålesund, Norway
description: The Summer Series in Ålesund is a long-running race series organized by Ålesundløpene. The races take place in scenic surroundings by Lillevatnet and Brusdalsvatnet in Vasstranda, on relatively flat, paved courses measured by Kondis. Participants can choose between 5 km and 10 km distances, starting from the western end of Lillevatnet in Spjelkavik. The series has its own prizes and awards a medal to those who take part in multiple races, attracting both recreational runners and competitive runners.
course_highlights: The courses run along Lillevatnet and Brusdalsvatnet in Vasstranda
Relatively flat paved courses with little traffic
Measured 5 km and 10 km distances
additional: The 10 km starts at 18:00 and the 5 km at 18:05. The races have their own prizes, with gift prizes awarded after each race. Participants who complete 2 or 3 races in the series receive a medal at the final race. Course records for both the 5 km and 10 km distances are documented. The participation record is 132 finishers. Distances: 5 km and 10 km. Registration is through EQ Timing. Participants who complete two or three races receive a medal at the final race.

name: HTB Valestrandsmarka Rundt 7. løp
description: HTB Valestrandsmarka Rundt is an annual recreational race organised by Osterøy I.L. Friidrett. The race takes place in Valestrand and covers a distance of 4.4 km. It is a social and inclusive event, with evening start times for walkers and the main field. Traditionally, sveler, cordial and prizes are served, and course records are rewarded with cash prizes from HTB.
course_highlights: A 4.4 km course in Valestrand
Start times: 18:45 for walkers and 19:00 for the main field
Course records are rewarded with NOK 3,000
additional: Start times are 18:45 for walkers and 19:00 for the main field. Times in the walking field are recorded as 30 minutes or more. Traditionally, sveler from Toro, cordial from Saftsuse and prizes from Extra Valestrand are provided. The race is part of a series of races held throughout the year, including a Christmas race and a New Year’s race. Registration takes place at Furubakken sports ground, and payment can be made via Vipps 121337 or to account 3632.54.56676. In 2026, the start times were 18:45 and 19:00, with payment via Vipps. Participants received sveler, cordial and prizes.

name: Bringebærløpet 2027
description: The Raspberry Run in Vollen is a family-friendly race offering distances for all ages and ability levels. The start and finish are at Vollenhallen, and the course runs through a scenic area, with only minor changes from previous years. The youngest runners complete a lap of approximately 1 km on the roller-ski track, while older participants run 2.5 km or 5 km. The event focuses on participation and enjoyable sporting experiences, and participants can also attend the Raspberry Festival held in conjunction with the race.
course_highlights: The course follows the roller-ski track at Arnestad through scenic surroundings
A race of approximately 1 km for the youngest participants
A 2.5 km and 5 km race course with a mass start
additional: Schedule: 11:00 bib number collection opens; 13:00 mass start for 5 km; 13:30 mass start for 2.5 km; 14:00 start of the 1 km children’s race, with multiple starts; 15:00 awards ceremony for competition classes aged 11 and up. The listed distances and start/finish area apply to the 2026 edition; details for 2027 have not been confirmed.

name: Grue Backyard 2027
description: Grue Backyard is a unique endurance race featuring 6.7 km loops through technical forest terrain. The race starts a new wave every hour, continuing until only one runner remains standing. Participants can complete one loop to earn a medal or push further for the finisher cap and the win. The event also includes the Grue Half Marathon, known as one of Norway's fastest half marathon courses, and the Gruemila 10 km race.
course_highlights: 6.7 km loops through technical forest terrain
New start every hour until one runner remains
Flat and fast 21.1 km half marathon course
additional: The race features hourly starts for the backyard loops, with medals awarded for completing one loop and a finisher cap for those who continue until the end. Previous editions have had up to 12 rounds, and participants who completed at least seven rounds have been able to receive a Grue Backyard Ultra Finisher T-shirt. This information is from previous editions and does not confirm details for 2027.

name: Ringeriksmaraton
description: Ringeriksmaraton is an annual running festival that began in 1995 and has grown to become Norway’s largest marathon relay. The race runs through the beautiful municipalities of Hole, Ringerike and Jevnaker, and offers distances and categories for everyone, including 8-person and 4-person relays, a pair marathon, half marathon and marathon. The event attracts recreational runners from all over the country and offers a sociable, active experience in beautiful surroundings. Children’s Ringeriksmaraton is also a popular part of the event, making it a family-friendly occasion.
course_highlights: The course runs through the municipalities of Hole, Ringerike and Jevnaker
Beautiful natural scenery, including Norway’s largest apple orchard
Varied terrain with asphalt, footpaths, forest roads and residential areas
additional: A mass start for all categories at Vik at 11:00, with an early start at 10:00 for runners using technical aids or with a finish time over 5 hours. Drink stations with squash and water at each relay exchange, as well as a muesli bar with salt at exchanges 3 and 6 for the half marathon and marathon. Toilets are available at several locations, but there are no shower facilities at Jevnakerhallen due to renovation. Løperbanken makes it possible to find a team if you are missing teammates. Race numbers and relay batons are handed out together. Registration is final, with no refund if you withdraw. Course maps, GPX files and practical information are available on the organizer’s website.

name: Bergen Skogsmaraton - Maratonkarusellen
description: Bergen Forest Marathon is an annual forest race held in Hordnesskogen, with the start and finish at the parking lot. The race features a loop of approximately 5.3 km, run multiple times depending on the distance: 8 laps for the marathon, 4 for the half marathon, and 2 for the 10 km. The event is suitable for both experienced runners and recreational runners, offering a wonderful nature experience in the forest and good facilities, including changing rooms, water stations, and food in the finish area. The focus is on enjoyment and quality for all participants.
course_highlights: Loop course in Hordnesskogen, starting and finishing at the parking lot
Each lap is approximately 5.3 km long
Two water stations, passed three times per lap
additional: Race headquarters opens at 08:00 for race-number collection and bag drop. Start times: 10 km at 09:00, marathon at 10:00, half marathon at 11:00. Food and drink for everyone who finishes. Changing rooms and toilets are at Bjarghallen, approximately 250 metres from the start. Parking is available at Bjarghallen, but capacity is limited; public transport or carpooling is recommended. Clothing can be stored in a tent in the start area at your own risk. Late registration is possible up to the start, subject to availability. The start and finish are at the parking lot in Hordnesskogen. Bjarghallen is approximately 250 metres from the start. Registration is through EQ Timing, and late registration is possible up to the start if places are available.

name: Level-løp
description: Level Løp is a trail race for everyone, held in beautiful surroundings in Hommersåk. The race offers distances of 5 km, 10 km and 23 km, as well as a 1000-metre children's race, with varied terrain and elevation changes suited to both recreational and experienced runners. The race starts at Riska Church and features scenic trails, forest and challenging climbs. After finishing, participants can enjoy hot food and drinks, and prizes are awarded to the top men and women in all main distances.
course_highlights: Trail race through the varied and beautiful terrain of Hommersåk
23 km with 1100 metres of elevation gain, 10 km with 246 metres, and 5 km with 87 metres
Aid stations on the 10 km and 23 km distances
additional: Bib collection is on Friday, 14 August, from 15:00 to 19:00 at Amboltveien 9, and on race day from 08:00 at the start area. Registration at the start area is open from 08:00 to 12:45 on race day. The children's race is divided into age-based waves. Hot food and drinks are provided for all participants in the 23 km race. A kiosk offers hot food, snacks and drinks. Parking is at Riska Church, not at the start area. Toilets and changing rooms are available at the start/finish. Live results with finish times are available. Prizes are awarded on an ongoing basis after runners finish. One prize is drawn at random from the bib numbers. Parking is at Riska Church. The stated start times are 09:00 for 23 km, 10:00 for 10 km, 10:20 for 5 km and 13:30 for the children's race. The 10 km and 23 km races are for participants born in 2012 or earlier.

name: Skånevik Skyrace
description: Skånevik Skyrace is a spectacular mountain race on a challenging 24-kilometre circular course with 1,600 metres of elevation gain across varied and technical terrain. The race offers fantastic views of fjords and mountains, combining raw nature with the joy of running for both recreational runners and elite athletes. The start and finish are in Skånevik town centre, where activities create a lively atmosphere both on the course and in town. The event features official timing, several drink stations, and a wide range of participant amenities, including access to a pool, sauna and massage after the race.
course_highlights: 24 km circular course with 1,600 metres of elevation gain
Steep climbs and technical terrain with flowing trail sections
Fantastic panoramic views from Håfjellet (932 m above sea level) and Nepo (610 m above sea level)
additional: Start and finish at Skånevik Fjordhotell, with a Base Camp for race-number collection, information, music, food and a great atmosphere. Three drink stations along the course and several timing checkpoints. Free access to Sjøkanten Trivsel, including a pool, sauna and massage after the race. Minimum age: 16; runners must pass Juraskar by 3:00 p.m. Accommodation is available at Skånevik Fjordhotell and nearby Airbnb properties, camping and boat moorings. Registration for 2027 is sold out, but places may become available in May 2027. The 2027 edition is sold out; any available places may be released in May 2027. Minimum age: 16, and runners must pass Juraskar by 3:00 p.m. Participants receive food and drinks at 3–4 drink stations, a medal and a buff.

name: Kniveåsen Rundt
location: Pumpehuset ved Solumstrand renseanlegg, Drammen, Norway
description: Kniveåsen Rundt is a forest race around Kniveåsen in Drammen that welcomes everyone to participate. The race is free and suitable for both recreational and experienced runners looking for an outdoor experience in forest terrain. The event has an inclusive atmosphere and is held annually, offering great opportunities to enjoy running in beautiful surroundings.
course_highlights: Forest race around Kniveåsen in Drammen
Natural terrain with varied surfaces
Suitable for all levels
additional: The race is free to enter. Results from previous years and event videos are available on the website. The race is open to everyone. Registration is linked from the official website.

name: Budor løpefest 2027
description: Budor Running Festival 2027 takes place on Saturday, August 14, at Budor Gjestegård and offers 5 km, 10 km, and half-marathon distances. The race offers an inclusive atmosphere for both experienced runners and beginners, with the start and finish at Gjestegården. The courses pass through scenic surroundings on trails and gravel roads, offering a spectacular running experience with beautiful panoramic views. The event also includes a free children’s race, Koiedalen Rundt, with a medal for participants. Prizes are awarded to the three fastest runners in each category in the 5 km, 10 km, and 21 km races.
course_highlights: The courses run mainly on trails and gravel roads through scenic surroundings
Start and finish at Budor Gjestegård, with panoramic views
The half marathon has only 250 places and offers a memorable running experience
additional: Race numbers can be collected between 09:00 and 10:30 at Gjestegården. The half marathon starts at 10:00, the 10 km at 10:30, and the 5 km at 10:40. Toilets and a few showers are available in the basement of Gjestegården, and swimming is possible in Koiedalsvannet near the finish area. The children’s race, Koiedalen Rundt, starts at 13:00 and is free. You can sell your place by contacting the organizer by email. All distances start and finish at Budor Gjestegård. Published schedule: half marathon at 10:00, 10 km at 10:30, and 5 km at 10:40. Race numbers can be collected at Gjestegården. The half marathon has 250 places, and the children’s race, Koiedalen Rundt, is free.

name: Backyard ultra Golsfjellet

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Backyard Deltakere kr 750,00 + Adm. gebyr (25 NOK + 3% transaksjonsgebyr)

description: Backyard Ultra Golsfjellet is a unique trail race with no asphalt, offering participants a full experience of fresh mountain air and scenic surroundings. The race is based at Oset Fjellhotell, which is exclusively booked for the event and filled with runners, supporters, and a great backyard atmosphere throughout the weekend. This is more than just a race; it is also a social weekend experience focused on food and spending time together, with all meals for runners prepared by the hotel’s renowned kitchen. The race is suitable for anyone looking for a challenging and social experience in the mountains.
course_highlights: The race takes place entirely on mountain terrain with no asphalt
Start and finish at Oset Fjellhotell, exclusively booked for the event
Delicious refreshments and food prepared by Oset Fjellhotell’s kitchen during breaks
additional: Race bibs and ankle chips can be collected at Oset Fjellhotell on Friday, August 14, from 19:00 to 21:00 and Saturday, August 15, from 07:30 to 08:30. The entire hotel is booked for the event, and a 20% discount is available for a two-night stay with discount code BYOSET. A pasta party is held on Friday evening and a gala dinner on Saturday evening, but neither is included in registration. A hotel buffet on Saturday evening is available to participants for 495 kr when reserved. Food and drink are central to the race, with easy access to refreshments during breaks. Accommodation and some meals are not included in the entry fee. The 2027 registration is listed with an Early Bird price.

name: Saudehornet Rett Opp 2027
location: Havna i Ørsta sentrum, Ørsta, Norway
description: Saudehornet Rett Opp is an annual uphill race in Ørsta that starts at the harbour in the town centre and climbs to the summit of Saudehornet, 1,303 metres above sea level. The course is 5.7 km long with a challenging climb, attracting amateurs, recreational runners and some professional athletes. The race has a rich history, including John Tvedt’s record run in 2007. It is a challenging and spectacular summit route that can also be hiked when there is no snow on the mountain.
course_highlights: 5.7 km course with 1,303 metres of elevation gain
Starts at the harbour in central Ørsta and finishes at the summit of Saudehornet
Challenging uphill race suitable for recreational and professional runners
additional: The route can be tried as a moderately challenging summit hike when there is no snow. Participants are mainly amateurs and recreational runners, but some professional athletes also take part. The event includes a recreational class and a separate children’s race to Skåla.

name: Olsokløpet 2027
location: Ålvundeid, Sunndal, Møre og Romsdal, Norway
description: Olsokløpet is an annual race held in Ålvundeid, Møre og Romsdal. The race covers a distance of 9.7 km and starts at 13:00. Prizes are awarded to the top three women and men, as well as to category winners, who receive a modest prize. The event also includes activities for children in the form of a track and field fun run, and food sales with grilling organized by Ålvundeid Bygdekvinnelag.
course_highlights: The race takes place in Ålvundeid, Møre og Romsdal
Distance of 9.7 km
Activities for children and a track and field fun run
additional: Prizes are awarded for 1st, 2nd and 3rd place, as well as to category winners. The top three women and men receive 1,000, 500 and 300 kroner, respectively. Food sales and grilling from 11:00 to 15:00. Previous editions have included prizes for the top three and category winners, as well as activities for children and food sales/grilling. This information applies to previous editions and may differ in 2027.

name: Vestfold løpskarusell - 6. løp - Revetal

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: 1200 kr. for ikke medlemmer frem til 31.12.26.

description: Vestfold Running Series 2027 is a series of 8 great races in the Tønsberg region, offering the joy of running, community and a great atmosphere for all levels. Each race has two distances and starts at 18:00, with electronic timing via EQ Timing. Participants can choose to run individual races or buy a season pass for all the races at a discounted price. The courses take runners through varied and beautiful surroundings in Vestfold. Course descriptions are shared in a Facebook group and when registering for the season.
course_highlights: Two distances at each race, typically around 3 km and a double lap
Courses cover varied terrain, including residential areas, lit trails and gravel roads
Start and finish at central locations such as the Sport1 store in Revetal
additional: Season-pass participants collect their race number at the first race. Participants running an individual race collect theirs from the race office 10 minutes before the start. Race numbers must be kept for the entire series. Electronic timing via EQ Timing. Course descriptions and profiles are shared in the Facebook group and when registering for the season. Start at 18:00. Season passes and registration for individual races are available.

name: Sørdalskarusellen - Fløymyrløpet
description: Flømyrløpet is the seventh race in Sørdalskarusellen and has been held since 2001. The start and finish are at Skurvbrua on Nordseterveien, 6 km above Lillehammer. The race offers a tough, wet trail run over challenging terrain, including marshy sections and trails. There are two distances: a long course of 5.4 km and a short course of 2.81 km. The short course follows the long course up to Flømyra and then descends to the finish. The race offers a mass start and a virtual option, and is a traditional part of Sørdalskarusellen, with an awards ceremony after the race.
course_highlights: A challenging 5.4 km trail run with wet and marshy sections
Start and finish at Skurvbrua, 6 km from Lillehammer city centre
The course follows a ski-trail route up to Flømyra shooting range, then returns via trails and roads
additional: All mass starts are at 18:30. The virtual race takes place August 15–18. The low-price registration deadline is 13:00 on race day, and the final registration deadline is 18:00 the same day. The awards ceremony is at approximately 19:15. The under-12 class uses the short course. It is possible to run the short course without timing. The course was adjusted in 2023 to avoid the worst of the marsh. Participants must enter their time on My Page under the Self Timing tab. Flømyrløpet is part of Sørdalskarusellen, a series of ten recreational races in the Lillehammer area. There is a long course of approximately 5.4 km and a short course of approximately 2.8 km. The information from the organisers applies to previous editions, so details for 2027 may differ.

name: Blodomløpet 2027
organizer: Røde Kors Blodprogram, i samarbeid med Blodbanken Ahus og lokale friidrettslag
description: Blodomløpet is a fun run organized by the Norwegian Red Cross Blood Programme in cooperation with local blood banks and athletics clubs. The event focuses on raising awareness of blood donation and promoting a healthy lifestyle. Participants can walk, jog or run 500 metres, 5 km or 10 km, and proceeds from registration go to local athletics clubs that support children and young people. Inspired by Sweden’s largest fun run, the event aims to help create a healthier Norway without blood shortages.
course_highlights: Choice of 500-metre, 5 km and 10 km distances
The courses are clearly marked and include both paved and gravel surfaces
Proceeds go to local athletics clubs that support children and young people
additional: Registration is binding and entitles participants to a place in the event and a one-time licence where required. Participants may enter individually or as part of a team (maximum 5 participants). Photos and videos will be taken during the event and may be used for documentation and marketing. By registering, participants enter into an agreement with the organizing clubs and partners.

name: TMC (Tromsø Mountain Challenge) HalvUltra 25km
description: Tromsø Mountain Challenge is a weekend featuring four trail races in Tromsø’s unique mountain landscape, spread over two days. The HalvUltra 25 km starts at TUIL Arena and follows a demanding course through Tromsdalen, up Djupdalen to Bønntøva (760 m above sea level), and down Fjøyfjellet to Fjellstua before finishing at TUIL Arena. The race combines spectacular scenery with challenging terrain and attracts both new and experienced runners seeking a true Arctic running challenge.
course_highlights: Start at TUIL Arena and run through Tromsdalen
Climb to Bønntøva at 760 m above sea level, the race’s highest point
Spectacular descent via Fjøyfjellet and finish at TUIL Arena
additional: Bib pickup takes place at TUIL Arena in Tromsdalen. The HalvUltra 25 km has a time limit of 6 hours. Transport to the Ultra 50 km start is available by bus from TUIL Arena at 07:45. Bag storage is available at TUIL Arena. A self-declaration form must be completed before the start for the Ultra and HalvUltra. The time limit is 6 hours. Bib pickup takes place at TUIL Arena, and HalvUltra participants must complete a self-declaration form before the start. Places are limited.

name: Vikerfjell Challenge
description: Vikerfjell Challenge is a trail race for all levels, with distances of 21 km and 11 km, plus a separate 2.5 km children’s race. The courses pass through the beautiful Vikerfjell Nature Reserve, over varied terrain including gravel roads and trails. Start and finish locations are Ringerudsetra, Tossviksetra and Skarrudsetra. The event offers fantastic scenery and a great atmosphere, and is suitable for both beginners and experienced runners.
course_highlights: The courses pass through Vikerfjell Nature Reserve
Terrain includes gravel roads, trails and varied surfaces
Start and finish locations are Ringerudsetra, Tossviksetra and Skarrudsetra
additional: The race offers distances of 21 km, 11 km and a 2.5 km children’s race. Start and finish locations are at several mountain farms in the area. The courses offer varied terrain and scenic experiences. Aid stations, toilets, showers and baggage storage are available. Parking and transport information can be found on the website. The event also includes a 2.5 km children’s race. Start and finish locations vary by distance.

name: Hornindalsrokken Skyrace
location: Horndøla bru, Volda, Møre og Romsdal, Norway
description: Hornindalsrokken Skyrace is a challenging 17.5 km mountain race with 1,300 meters of elevation gain, held annually in Volda, Møre og Romsdal. The race starts at Horndøla bru and features a mix of gravel roads, rough off-road tracks, and technical alpine trails, including a steep ascent up Rokkeråsa with scrambling sections. Participants experience varied terrain and stunning natural scenery. Mandatory safety equipment is required due to the alpine conditions. The race emphasizes safety, sportsmanship, and respect for the environment.
course_highlights: 17.5 km distance with 1,300 m of elevation gain
Steep 1.3 km ascent up Rokkeråsa with 506 m of climbing and technical scrambling
Aid station at the top of Rokkeråsa (6.4 km)
additional: Registration and bib pickup at Horndøla bru from 07:30 to 09:15. Mandatory safety briefing from 09:15 to 09:30. The start and mandatory safety briefing are at Horndøla bru. Prize ceremony at Horndøla Camping at 15:00. Bus transportation is available from the finish at Trondstad Grendahus back to Horndøla Camping. Minimum age: 15 years. Maximum 200 participants. Mandatory equipment includes trail shoes with good grip, a windproof jacket, warm clothing, a warm buff or hat, gloves, an extra wool shirt, a first aid kit, a whistle, a charged phone, water, nutrition, and a climbing harness with a locking carabiner if the direct route is used. The organizer’s website lists different dates for 2027: 21 August in the main listing and 22 August in the practical information.

name: Skåbu fjellmaraton (Jotunheimvegen Ultra)
description: Jotunheimvegen Ultra is a spectacular ultramarathon starting at Bygdin Høifjellshotell on Valdresflya and following Jotunheimvegen, with fantastic views of the peaks of Jotunheimen. The race follows a gravel road past idyllic mountain farms along Vinstervatna, and from around 38 km follows the marathon course to the finish in Skåbu town centre, with a tough final climb up Kamfossbakken. This race offers a challenging and scenic experience in high mountain terrain, with several food and drink stations along the way. Skåbu Fjellmaraton also offers several distances suitable for all levels, but Jotunheimvegen Ultra is the highlight for ultrarunners.
course_highlights: Start at Bygdin Høifjellshotell on Valdresflya, approx. 12 km from Beitostølen
The race follows Jotunheimvegen, with views of the peaks of Jotunheimen and idyllic mountain farms along Vinstervatna
Finish with a tough 3 km climb up Kamfossbakken to the finish in Skåbu town centre
additional: Race bibs not collected in Skåbu are sent by bus in the morning and can be collected at the start. Luggage can be sent by bus to the finish and collected at the event office. Six food and drink stations along the route serving sports drink, water, bananas and cola. Cut-off time at the Slangen aid station is 14:00; runners arriving later may continue at their own risk or get a ride to the finish. Timing is provided by eqtiming.no, with split times at Slangen and Kamfossbakken. The “King and Queen of Kamfossen” climbing competition takes place at the Kamfossbakken split-time point. Late registration is possible up to 1 hour before the start. Parking is at Skåbu school, not by the finish area. Toilets and showers are available at the school. There are six food and drink stations along the route, with the first after 14 km. The cut-off time at Slangen is 14:00. Bus transport between Skåbu and Bygdin can be booked as an add-on when registering.

name: Høyjord Rundt og Rundt
description: Høyjord Rundt og Rundt is a varied race suitable for all levels, with distances from 6.1 km to 77 km. The course features technically challenging terrain with approximately 470 metres of elevation gain per lap, including trails, gravel roads and beautiful viewpoints. The event also includes a children’s race with an obstacle course and an untimed recreational run, so the whole family can take part and have fun. Everyone who finishes receives a medal, and food and drinks are available in the start/finish area. The race is organised by Høyjord Idrettslag and emphasises the joy of running, community and a great atmosphere.
course_highlights: Approximately 470 metres of elevation gain per 11 km lap, with technically challenging trails
Beautiful viewpoint at approximately 7 km on the course
Snack station with snacks and drinks at 2.5 km
additional: Dogs are not allowed on the technical courses, but dogs on a leash are permitted in the recreational run. Pacing is not allowed. The children’s race takes place on the artificial turf pitch and includes an obstacle course and a separate medal. The extra service offers the option to walk or run shorter distances without timing during the week before the race. Food and drinks are available in the start/finish area, including snacks, broth, coffee, cola, hot food and fruit. The race has a zero-tolerance policy for littering and requires mandatory equipment according to the equipment list. Registration is via Racetracker. The children’s race includes an obstacle course. The untimed extra service is available on Thursday or Friday of race week.

name: Langhusløpet
organizer: Langhusløperne i samarbeid med Langhus IL Alliansen
description: Langhusløpet 2027 is an inclusive race for all ages and abilities, held at Haugjordet Lower Secondary School in Langhus. Participants can choose between a children’s race, 5 km and 10 km. Everyone receives a medal, and all children receive a bun. The race combines asphalt with forest roads and trails, and offers a friendly, social atmosphere focused on the joy of running and community. Bag storage is available, and race bibs can be collected both the day before and on race day.
course_highlights: 10 km course with 75% asphalt and 25% forest roads and trails
400-metre children’s race, with a medal and a bun for every child
Start and finish at Haugjordet Lower Secondary School, with bag storage available
additional: Race bibs can be collected on Friday 13 August at Löplabbet in Ski Storsenter from 10:00 to 19:00, and on race day from 9:30 to 10:45 at the race office at Haugjordet Lower Secondary School. Prizes will be awarded to the top three men and women in the 5 km and 10 km races. All participants take part at their own risk, and parents are responsible for children who participate. The minimum age is 10 for the 5 km and 13 for the 10 km. The children’s race is open to all. Race bibs can be collected on race day at Haugjordet Lower Secondary School or at Löplabbet in Ski Storsenter.

name: Tromsø Mountain Ultra 50km
description: Tromsø Mountain Challenge is a weekend featuring four trail races in Tromsø’s unique mountain landscape, including the 50 km La Sportiva Ultra, which starts from Snarbyeidet. The races offer challenging trails, spectacular mountain and plateau views, and finish with a wonderful descent through Tromsdalen to the finish at TUIL Arena. The event attracts runners from all over the world and offers a true Arctic running experience in the fresh autumn air and beautiful fall colors. This is a race for both new and experienced trail runners looking for a challenging and scenic experience.
course_highlights: Start from Snarbyeidet on runnable mountain terrain, climbing to approximately 760 m above sea level
Pass nine checkpoints along the way during the ultra race
Spectacular descent through Tromsdalen to the finish at TUIL Arena
additional: Bib pickup takes place at TUIL Arena in Tromsdalen. The cutoff time for the 50 km ultra is 9 hours, with a checkpoint at Tromsdalselva (32 km) where the cutoff is 5.5 hours. Transport to the start from TUIL Arena is by bus at 07:45. Bags can be stored at TUIL Arena and transported by bus to the finish area. A self-declaration form must be completed before the start for the Ultra and HalvUltra. The maximum time is 9 hours. The cutoff at the Tromsdalselva checkpoint, after 32 km, is 5.5 hours. The organizer provides a bus from TUIL Arena to the start at 07:45, and Ultra runners must complete a self-declaration form. The number of start places is limited.

name: Nordvest Maraton

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Pris: 200 kroner for mosjon utan tid

description: Nordvest Marathon is a traditional race that has been held annually since 1991 in the beautiful and varied surroundings of Hareid Municipality in Sunnmøre. The race offers distances for everyone, including the full marathon, half marathon, 5 km and an untimed recreational class. The course offers scenic experiences along Grimstadvatnet and around Snipsøyrvatnet, with a varied route combining asphalt, gravel and tartan, over gently rolling terrain. The event is known as one of Norway’s most beautiful races and attracts both experienced and recreational runners.
course_highlights: The course runs along Grimstadvatnet and around Snipsøyrvatnet
Varied surfaces: asphalt, gravel and tartan
Gently rolling terrain in scenic surroundings
additional: Prize ceremony at 15:30 at the clubhouse. Medals for all finishers. Prizes for the top third in each class, with up to three prizes. Untimed participation is available at all distances, with a preferred start time of 11:00. Members of Hareid IL receive a NOK 100 discount, and those with an annual licence receive a NOK 50 discount. Registration is open on a rolling basis via RaceResult until the race starts. Start and finish are at Hareid Stadium. The recreational class is untimed.

name: Dalheim Rundt
description: Dalheim Rundt is a family-friendly trail race that starts and finishes at TUIL Arena in Tromsø. The course follows the network of trails and the floodlit ski trail through beautiful Tromsdalen, with a water station at Dalheim. This race is part of Tromsø Mountain Challenge, which offers spectacular nature experiences in rugged Northern Norwegian terrain, with challenging trails and great views. The event takes place in late August, when Northern Norway displays its finest autumn colours.
course_highlights: Start and finish at TUIL Arena in Tromsdalen
The course follows the network of trails and the floodlit ski trail through Tromsdalen to Dalheim
Water station at Dalheim amid scenic surroundings
additional: Race bibs are distributed at TUIL Arena in Tromsdalen. The number of starting places is limited, and registration is open while race bibs are available. The race is part of a weekend featuring several trail races in Tromsø, and several of the races finish with a spectacular descent through Tromsdalen to the finish at TUIL Arena. The race is part of Tromsø Mountain Challenge and the TMC Triple. The start time is listed as 12:00 on Saturday, 21 August 2027.

name: Vossaton

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Barneløp (3-11år) Påmelding opnar i mai: Kr 35 – Påmelding

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Rabatt, kr 50, for medlemmer i Voss IL fram til 17.08. (gjeld ikkje for barneløp)

description: Vossaton running festival is an annual race held at Voss sports ground, starting on 21 August 2027. The event offers several distances, including a half marathon starting at Gjernes, as well as a children’s race for the youngest participants. It is an inclusive running festival, with cash prizes for the fastest times and extra prizes for course records. Participants can enjoy a varied course with several water stations along the way, and there is also an informal corporate relay with several legs.
course_highlights: Half-marathon start at Gjernes, approximately 1.5 km from the sports ground
Water stations at 5.2 km, 11.3 km, 16.4 km and the finish
Group jog to the start from the finish area before the half marathon
additional: The half marathon has a minimum age of 15. There are toilets at the start at Gjernes School. Clothing can be handed in in a separate bag or sack when collecting race numbers and will be transported back to the finish area. The corporate relay has 5–10 runners per team, with legs of approximately 2.5 km and just over 1 km. Late registration for the children’s race is possible until 15 minutes before the start. The three fastest times for women and men in each race receive prizes. An extra prize is offered for a course record: NOK 1,000 in the half marathon and NOK 500 in the 5 km. Members of Voss IL receive a discount.

name: Sami Maraton

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Pris: kr 100,- Deltakere 7-13 år får kr 50,- i rabatt.

description: Sámi Marathon is mainland Norway’s northernmost marathon and is held in the centre of Tanabru in Deatnu-Tana. The race offers compact, sociable courses with several passes by the stadium, creating a great atmosphere and bringing runners close to the spectators. Distances include the marathon, half marathon, 10 km, Run4Fun and MiniMarathon, with dedicated categories for para-athletes and children. All participants receive a medal at the finish, and prizes are awarded in several categories, with additional prizes for the fastest times over each distance. The race has a strong focus on community and the joy of running in the centre of Tana.
course_highlights: The marathon consists of 4 laps and the half marathon of 2 laps on officially measured courses
The courses are compact and close to the town centre, with several passes by the stadium
Suitable for all ages, with dedicated courses for children and para-athletes
additional: Race numbers and Emit timing chips can be collected at the stadium the day before the race between 18:00 and 19:30, or from 08:30 on race day. Please arrive at least 30 minutes before the start, or 1 hour beforehand if you have not collected your race number and chip. All participants receive medals. Family discount with a maximum combined entry fee of NOK 1,500 per family. Additional prizes for the three fastest times in the 10 km, half marathon and marathon. An earlier marathon start is available for participants expecting a running time of over 5 hours. The information page lists medals for all participants and changing facilities at Tana multi-purpose hall. Distance and price information applies to the published 2027 registration; the date 21 August 2027 has not been confirmed on the source pages.

name: Romerikes Råeste 2027
description: Romerikes Råeste is an action-packed obstacle race held in Nannestad’s unique, muddy ravine landscape. The race offers two courses of different lengths and difficulty levels, suitable for children, young people, recreational runners and competitive athletes. The main course is 6 km long with more than 60 obstacles, and there is also a family-friendly children’s course called Råtassen. The event combines challenges, a sense of achievement and community, and is a spectacular outdoor event near Gardermoen.
course_highlights: 6 km main course with more than 60 obstacles
Course through a muddy ravine landscape
Children’s course for ages 3–10 with exciting obstacles
additional: Starts are in groups of approximately 20–30 participants every 5 minutes, with 10–20 in the elite classes. Start and finish at Nannestad Idrettspark. It is possible to pick up your race pack before race day to avoid queues. There is a water station on the main course, but not on the children’s/family course. Romerikes Råeste caps in children’s and adult sizes are available to order when registering. Parking costs 100 kr and is paid via Vipps. The organiser’s website describes the 2026 edition but does not confirm race details for 2027. Råtassen is for children aged 3 to 10; guardians may accompany the children without a separate ticket.

name: Sørkedalsløpet
location: Idrettslokalet i Sørkedalen, Sørkedalen, Oslo, Norway

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Alle klasser 22 år og yngre (nedre aldersgrense 8 år) kroner 285

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Alle klasser fra 23 år og eldre kroner 435

description: Sørkedalsløpet is a real cross-country race on forest trails in Nordmarka, organised for the whole family. You can choose between a challenging, hilly 11 km course or a shorter 3 km course, both starting and finishing at Idrettslokalet in Sørkedalen. The race offers fresh air, a great atmosphere, and homemade elk soup and buns in the finish area. It is a friendly, local weekday race suitable for runners of all ages.
course_highlights: Cross-country race on forest trails and gravel roads in Nordmarka
Hilly 11 km course and shorter 3 km course
Start and finish at Idrettslokalet in Sørkedalen
additional: Wave starts: 11 km at 18:00 and 3 km at 18:20. Race bibs can be collected at Idrettslokalet from 16:00 to 18:15. Homemade elk soup and buns are served in the finish area. Sausages, cinnamon buns, coffee, and squash are also sold to spectators. Parking is not available at the venue, but there is parking about 700 m away at Sørkedalen utfartsparkering. Bus 41 stops at the venue. Previous editions have served refreshments at the finish, including elk soup and buns.

name: HTB Ole Bull-løpet 2027
description: HTB Ole Bull Run is a traditional fun run organised by Osterøy IL Athletics. The race is part of a series of fun runs and running events in beautiful surroundings on Osterøy in Vestland. Participants can look forward to a well-organised race experience starting at Furubakken sports ground, with options for walkers and the main field. The event has a friendly atmosphere, with prizes and refreshments for participants.
course_highlights: The course is 4.4 km long
Starts at Furubakken sports ground, Valestrandsfossen
Start times: 18:45 for walkers and 19:00 for the main field
additional: Prizes are provided by local sponsors such as Extra Valestrand and Toro. Sveler (Norwegian pancakes) and squash are served to participants. The race is part of a series with several events throughout the year, including a Christmas run and a New Year’s run. Registration is available at the start at Furubakken sports ground or via Vipps 121337. The series lists start times of 18:45 for walkers and 19:00 for the main field. Previous editions have featured 4 km and 6 km courses, but distances for 2027 have not been announced.

name: Sognefjord Trail Run
description: Sognefjord Trail Run is a spectacular trail-running experience in beautiful Kaupanger, Vestland. Choose from the 17K, 27K, 45K Ultra or a 1 km Kids Race. The courses offer varied terrain, including forest trails, mountain sections and fantastic views of the Sognefjord. The event has an inclusive atmosphere, with well-marked courses, helpful volunteers and a social post-race gathering in central Sogndal.
course_highlights: Varied terrain with forest trails, mountains and technical sections
Fantastic views of the Sognefjord and mountain peaks such as Søre Gråbrørne
Flowing trails and challenging climbs, including up to Amlaholten and Store Haugmælen
additional: Start times: 08:00 for 45K Ultra, 11:30 for 17K, 12:00 for 27K, 15:00 for Kids Race. Bib collection and check-in Friday 16:00-21:00 in Sogndal and Saturday morning in Kaupanger. Post-race gathering with music and an awards ceremony in central Sogndal from 20:30. The courses include asphalt, gravel and trails. Kids Race for children aged 2-13 over 1 km. Food available for purchase after the finish. The 2027 edition is part of the Norge Trail Series (NTS), and registration is open.

name: Arctic Alta Ultra 2027
description: Arctic Alta Ultra is a challenging ultrarun held in Tverrelvdalen, starting and finishing at Ungdomshuset. The race offers several distances from 6 km to 100 miles, with well-marked courses and aid stations along the way. Participants can use bag-drop points on the longer distances, and the finish area has facilities including a café, changing rooms and showers. The event combines nature experiences with challenging terrain in the beautiful surroundings of Alta.
course_highlights: Aid stations on all distances, with several unmanned stations on the 50 km, 100 km and 100-mile distances
Bag-drop points for the 50 km, 100 km and 100-mile distances
Start and finish at Ungdomshuset in Tverrelvdalen, with facilities including a café and showers
additional: Participants in the 50 km, 100 km and 100-mile races must sign a runner's declaration before the start. Race manuals are available for the 16 km, 29 km, 50 km, 100 km and 100-mile distances. The start and finish address is Sønvismoen 44, 9537 Tverrelvdalen. For the 2026 edition, a café, changing rooms with showers and an awards ceremony at Ungdomshuset in Tverrelvdalen are listed. These practical details have not been confirmed for 2027.

name: Mandalsmaraton
location: Giert Karis Plass, Bryggegata, Mandal, Norway
description: Mandalsmaraton is one of Norway’s oldest marathons, first held in 1980. The race runs through Mandal’s charming town-centre streets and scenic surroundings, including Furulunden and its idyllic beaches. The course is flat and consists of a 10 km loop, run multiple times depending on the distance. The event aims to be inclusive of everyone, whether you run, jog or walk, and offers a lively atmosphere with music and an enthusiastic crowd.
course_highlights: Flat 10 km loop with a national C certificate
The course runs through the town centre and Furulunden, with beautiful natural scenery
Three aid stations with water, sports drink, cola and bananas
additional: The start and finish are in Bryggegata by Giert Karis Plass. Pacers are available for all distances. Bag storage is offered at Kirkesenteret in Gågata, near the start area. After the finish, Hr. Redaktør invites participants to an After Run with food and drinks. Changing rooms and showers are available at Mandalshallen nearby. Free parking is available at Speidertomta and Mandal Videregående Skole. All participants must have a licence, either an annual licence or a one-time licence when registering. Red Cross medical personnel are present on the course. The start and finish are in Bryggegata by Giert Karis Plass. Aid stations are located at 4.2, 7 and 9.8 km. Changing rooms and showers are available at Mandalshallen, and bag storage is at Kirkesenteret. Strollers and dogs are not allowed on the course.

description: Porsgrunn Half Marathon is an inclusive road race for all levels, with distances including a children’s race, 5 km, 10 km and half marathon. The start and finish are at Franklintorget outside Down Town shopping centre, where there will also be entertainment, stalls and a free children’s race. The courses are officially measured, and there is a great atmosphere along the route, with entertainment for both runners and spectators. All participants receive a medal, and the event is a community celebration focused on making participation accessible to individuals, families, friends and businesses.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Franklintorget outside Down Town shopping centre
600-metre children’s race through the shopping centre
Officially measured courses with entertainment along the route
additional: Race bibs can be collected on Friday, 27 August, from 16:00 to 19:00 at Down Town shopping centre, and on race day from 09:30 outdoors at Franklintorget. The 600-metre children’s race is free, requires no registration and awards a medal to everyone. Registration is binding, but entries may be resold via EQ timing. A 35 NOK registration fee is added. Register by 8 August 2027 to have your name printed on your race bib. The event offers a 5 km, 10 km, half marathon and a free 600-metre children’s race. The course and distance information refers to details published for the 2026 edition.

name: Lyderhorn Opp
description: Lyderhorn Opp is an uphill race organized by Laksevåg Turn og Idrettslag, finishing at the summit of Lyderhorn, 396 metres above sea level. The course is approximately 3.8 km long and is suitable for both competitive and recreational runners. Participants receive a race bib and T-shirt, and everyone who finishes receives a medal and a T-shirt. Prizes are awarded to the three fastest men and women, and gift prizes are drawn among participants.
course_highlights: Approximately 3.8 km course finishing at the summit of Lyderhorn (396 metres above sea level)
Uphill race over varied terrain
Race bib and T-shirt for all participants
additional: Race bibs and T-shirts can be collected at Sport1 Vestkanten on the Friday before the race. Participants receive a 10% discount on one item of their choice at Sport1 Vestkanten when collecting their race bib. There are relatively good parking options, but walking, cycling or using public transport is recommended. First-aid personnel and defibrillators are available along the course. Gift prizes are drawn using race bib numbers during the event. The organizer's website states that the event has been cancelled and welcomes participants back in 2027.

name: Fjordkraft Bergen City Milen
description: Fjordkraft Bergen City Milen is a 10 km road race through the heart of Bergen city centre, starting and finishing at Torgallmenningen. The course offers a varied route that includes city streets, walking and cycling paths, tunnels, and scenic areas such as Småpudden and Nygårdsparken. The event is a community celebration that brings together local and visiting runners and is suitable for all levels and ages. With a long tradition dating back to 2012, the race is organised by Turn og Idrettsforeningen Viking, which emphasises community, activity, and quality.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Torgallmenningen in Bergen city centre
The course passes through Kronstadtunnelen and includes a turnaround
Passes scenic areas such as Småpudden and Nygårdsparken
additional: Race bibs and T-shirts can be collected at JUICE Galleriet. Race-bib distribution closes at 14:00 on race day. Changing rooms and clothing storage are available at Vikinghallen. The children's race, Mini-Milen, starts at 15:00. The awards ceremony is at 17:00. All participants receive a medal, drinks, and light refreshments. An administration fee of NOK 25 is charged in addition to the entry fee, along with a licence fee for the athletics federation. A children's race is also held. The official race website lists 18 September 2027, which differs from the date in the race listing.

name: Ledenløpet (Fåvang–Øyer)
distance_verbose: 27 km, 17 km, 7 km, 5 km, 3000 meter, 1 km
price_range: Gratis for 1 og 3 km; 250–500 kr for øvrige distanser
description: Ledenløpet is a race through the cultural landscape in the heart of Gudbrandsdalen, with six distances suitable for different ages and levels. The races start at various locations and finish at Nermo Hotell in Øyer. It is an inclusive event, with both timed races and free distances for children, and promotes environmental friendliness by being cup-free. Ledenløpet also offers carpooling to the start and nutrition packages tailored to runners.
course_highlights: Run through the cultural landscape of Gudbrandsdalen
Finish at Nermo Hotell for all distances
Several starting locations, with distances ranging from 1 km to 27 km
additional: Race bibs are distributed at the start, no later than 15 minutes before the race begins. Ledenløpet is cup-free, so runners must bring their own cup or bottle for the drink stations. Bus transport to the start from Nermo Hotell is available for Langleden and Mellomleden. The maximum total number of participants is 250 runners. Prizes for the top three in the men's and women's categories at each distance: a model of their choice of ON running shoes from Sport 1 Hafjell. Distances: 27 km Langleden, 17 km Mellomleden, 7 km Stuttleden, 5 km Ekstrastuttleden, 3 km and 1 km Bringebærleden. Bringebærleden for the youngest participants is untimed. The race is cup-free, so bring your own cup or bottle. Race bibs are collected at the start.

name: Kolbotnvannet Rundt
location: Kolbotn Kulturhus (Kolben), Kolbotn, Nordre Follo, Norway
organizer: Kolbotn IL Allianse og Kolbotn Run
description: Kolbotnvannet Rundt is an annual race organized by Kolbotn IL Allianse, with the start and finish at Kolbotn Kulturhus (Kolben) in Nordre Follo. The race offers a scenic loop around Kolbotnvannet and attracts both recreational and competitive runners. The event has a friendly atmosphere and also includes children’s races, making it family-friendly. Results from previous years show strong performances in both the 5 km and 10 km distances.
course_highlights: A route around Kolbotnvannet in scenic surroundings
Start and finish at Kolbotn Kulturhus (Kolben)
Suitable for both recreational and competitive runners
additional: The organizer is Kolbotn IL Allianse. The start and finish are at Kolbotn Torg, Strandliveien 4, 1410 Kolbotn. Children’s races are also held as part of the event. A 1 km race is offered for participants aged 6 and up, as well as a children’s race of approximately 500 meters. The start area is near Kolbotn station.

name: Damvegen Opp
description: Damvegen Opp is a challenging uphill race in Ålvik, with a 4.5 km course and a total elevation gain of 600 metres. The race follows a gravel road and offers a test of both fitness and willpower, rewarded with fantastic views. Participants can run, jog, walk or “gog” at their own pace, but must finish within the 2-hour cut-off time. Two aid stations along the way provide hydration, and refreshments and a medal await everyone who finishes at the top. The Red Cross is on hand to help ensure a safe experience for everyone.
course_highlights: 4.5 km course with 600 metres of elevation gain
Gravel road throughout
Two aid stations along the way and refreshments at the top
additional: The cut-off time is 2 hours. Everyone who finishes receives a medal. The Red Cross is present throughout the race for safety. The Red Cross helps ensure safety along the course, and everyone who finishes receives a medal. Previous information gives a participant limit of 50.

name: Kodalmila
location: Kodal IL Stadion, Kodal, Sandefjord, Norway
price_range: 50-300 kr (+ lisens på 5 km og 10 km)
description: Kodalmila is Vestfold’s oldest recreational race and is being held for the 47th time. The event offers several distances, including road and trail races, starting from Kodal town centre and Kodal IL Stadium. It is family-friendly, with a children’s race and shorter trail races, and is a traditional community celebration for runners of all ages. Race bibs can be collected at the clubhouse on race day, and registration is via EQ Timing.
course_highlights: 10 km road race starting at 14:00
5 km trail race starting at 14:05
2.5 km trail race and children’s race starting from Kodal IL Stadium
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Kodal IL’s clubhouse at Rismyrveien 10b on race day from 12:00. The start for the 10 km, 5 km and 2.5 km trail races is at the bus stop in Kodal town centre, while the children’s race starts at Kodal IL Stadium. Registration opens on 1 December 2024. Registration is via EQ Timing. Race bibs can be collected at Kodal IL’s clubhouse on race day.

name: Forest Run Elverum
description: Forest Run Elverum organizes obstacle trail runs and activity days in and around Elverum, with its main base at Starmoen. The course features approximately 20 obstacles of varying difficulty and is suitable for all kinds of recreational runners, from beginners to more experienced obstacle runners. The event emphasizes teamwork, togetherness, and a sense of achievement, and aims to foster good relationships between participants. Forest Run also offers team participation and tailored activities for schools, businesses, and private groups.
course_highlights: Obstacle trail run with approximately 20 obstacles
Course through woodland at Starmoen, 10 km east of Elverum town centre
Obstacles of varying difficulty, suitable for both beginners and experienced runners
additional: The course and obstacle course are rebuilt, and the facilities can be rented by schools, stag parties, birthday groups, and for team building. The focus is on teamwork and a sense of achievement, with activities for both recreational runners and more professional obstacle runners. The team also organizes group trips to other obstacle races. To register as a team, participants register individually and select the same team. Shoes with good tread are recommended; expect to get wet and muddy.

name: Stavanger Marathon
location: Mariero Station cycle path, Stavanger, Norway
description: Stavanger Marathon is a well-organized race offering distances for everyone, from a children’s race to a full marathon. The courses combine asphalt and gravel and take runners through scenic surroundings around lakes and fjords in Stavanger. The start and finish are in the city centre by Stavanger Cathedral, with a lively festival atmosphere on the last Saturday in August. The race has pacers, good facilities, and prizes for both the best times and course records.
course_highlights: The marathon course goes around three lakes and along Hafrsfjord and Gandsfjorden, with approximately 130 metres of elevation gain
80% asphalt and 20% gravel
Start and finish by Stavanger Cathedral; the 5 km starts at Mariero station
additional: Race numbers can be collected at Radisson Blu Atlantic Hotel on Friday 27 August and Saturday 28 August. The 5 km starts at Mariero station; the other distances start by Stavanger Cathedral. The half marathon is divided into 8 waves, starting 3 minutes apart. Bags can be left at Kongsgård School. Free showers are available at Stavanger Swimming Hall after the race. Prize ceremonies take place at different times for the various distances. Prizes are awarded for course records and for the best youth and teenage runners. Sports drink and bananas are available along the course and at the finish. The start is by the cycle path at Mariero station. Race numbers can be collected at Radisson Blu Atlantic Hotel. The marathon course has approximately 280 metres of elevation gain.

name: Nordre Follo Maraton
description: Nordre Follo Marathon is the municipality’s own marathon, starting and finishing in Ski town centre. The race takes place on Saturday, 28 August 2027 at 12:00 and offers several distances, including the marathon, half marathon, 10 km, 5 km and a children’s race. The course showcases the municipality from Oppegård to Kråkstad and serves as a natural tune-up race for the Oslo Marathon. Ski town centre is easily accessible by the Follobanen, which takes eleven minutes from Oslo S.
course_highlights: Course from Oppegård to Kråkstad
Start and finish in Ski town centre
A great showcase of Nordre Follo municipality
additional: The race is organised by Puls Samfunn and Ung300. Registration has not opened yet; check with the organiser for updates. The event is scheduled about a month before the Oslo Marathon as a natural tune-up race. Ski town centre is eleven minutes from Oslo S by Follobanen. Registration has not opened yet. Ski is around 11 minutes from Oslo S by Follobanen.

name: 4. Backyard Ås
description: Backyard Ås is a unique endurance race based on the backyard ultra format, where participants run a 6.7 km loop every hour on the hour. The race continues until only one runner remains, testing both physical endurance and mental strength. The course follows scenic trails in Ås, Norway, and offers a varied mix of asphalt, gravel, and forest trails. The event takes place in scenic surroundings just 30 minutes south of Oslo and is an official Backyard Ultra Association race, with results counting toward international rankings.
course_highlights: 6.7 km loop every hour on the hour
Course with approximately 50% asphalt and the rest trails and gravel for the first 9 loops
More technically challenging course with 100 metres of elevation gain per loop from loop 10 until the end of the race
additional: Two different courses are used: Course 1 (loops 1–9) is flatter, with 64 metres of elevation gain and approximately 50% asphalt, the rest trails and gravel. Course 2 (loop 10 onward) is more technically challenging, with 100 metres of elevation gain per loop. A fully equipped aid station at the start/finish offers basic nutrition and space for personal supplies. Headlamps are required for night loops. The event offers free parking and is easily accessible by train. Registration is coming soon, and places are limited. The venue is approximately 30 minutes south of Oslo.

name: Røykenmila 2027
price_range: 400 kr for 5 km og 10 km; gratis for deltakere under 16 år og Minimila

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Vi øker prisene med kr 100 et par uker før av hensyn til anslag på bestilling av startnummer med chip.

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Alle deltakere under 16 år løper gratis. Minimila er gratis.

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Aktivitetsløypa som Hyggen Speidergruppe setter opp koster kr 100 per familie (Vipps ved oppmøte).

description: Røykenmila is a challenging trail race in Kjekstadmarka, taking place on Sunday, 29 August 2027. The race offers scenic surroundings with gravel roads and trails, and is suitable for the whole family, with activities and a market day. It is a social event aiming to encourage exercise and support good causes in the local community. The start and finish are at Kjekstad farm. Distances of 5 km and 10 km are offered, as well as the Mini Mile for children.
course_highlights: Trail race through scenic surroundings on gravel roads and trails
Water station on the 10 km course at Haukelia, about halfway around the route
Start and finish at Kjekstad farm, about a 15-minute walk from Røyken station
additional: The Mini Mile starts at 11:30, with prizes for all children. Family activity trail with a quiz and canoeing. Several stalls and entertainment throughout the day. Free treatment and storage of valuables for participants. Course marshals ensure the routes are clearly marked and safe. Strollers can be used on the Mini Mile and activity trail, but a child carrier backpack is recommended. Registration for the 2027 edition has not yet opened. The activity trail costs NOK 100 per family. The organiser says all proceeds will be donated to good causes.

name: Norgestesten 2027 2
description: Norgestesten is an efficient and simple running event held in Jessheim, with a mass start and many experienced pacers. The course is a flat 3,146-meter loop, suitable for both beginners and experienced runners. Distances range from an 800-meter children’s race to a half marathon, and the event focuses on community and an enjoyable running experience. Proceeds support sports for children and young people in the local community.
course_highlights: Flat 3,146-meter loop
Mass start with pacers at several paces
The race is held in Jessheim, with convenient logistics and parking nearby
additional: The children’s race starts at 09:30 and is approximately 800 m long. Self-service bib pickup is available from 09:00 in the start area. Toilets are available at Jessheim Friidrettsstadion and in the ice and multi-purpose hall. A table for runners’ own drinks is provided at the start, along with water and sports drink along the course. The half-marathon cutoff time is 2 hours and 30 minutes. Mass start with pacers. The train station and parking are approximately 300 meters from the start. Proceeds support sports for children and young people.

name: Terrengløp i Smidalen
organizer: Nidelv IL Friidrett og Nidelv IL Ski
description: Terrengløp i Smidalen is an accessible cross-country race for children and young people in grades 1 to 7, organized by Nidelv IL Friidrett og Ski in collaboration with Kjeldsberg Eiendom AS. The race takes place on a loop of approximately 1,000 meters, with distances adapted to each grade level. All participants start together, and the event encourages well-rounded training and competition in an inclusive environment. It is an important offering for children at Nidelv IL and a popular event with strong participation.
course_highlights: A roughly 1,000-meter cross-country loop
Race distance adapted by grade: grades 1–3 (1 lap), grades 4–5 (2 laps), grades 6–7 (3 laps)
All participants start together
additional: The races are held several times a year, with a focus on children and young people at Nidelv IL. Coaches and team leaders are encouraged to prioritize participation over their own training. The event is part of a sponsorship agreement with Kjeldsberg Eiendom AS. Details about the course and laps come from coverage of the 2026 edition; the information does not confirm that the 2027 edition will follow the same format.

name: Arnaløpet
