price_range: 170-600 kr (+ lisens); gratis for barn 0–12 år

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Familie: kr 600 (+ lisens og inntil fem personer). Alle med færre enn fem familiemedlemmer kan ta med en venn for å "fylle opp" maks-antallet på fem.

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Gratis for barn 0-12 år! (Født 2014 og senere)

description: Arnaløpet is a long-running race that was first held in 1977 on a challenging 13 km course. Since 1984, the course has run around Haukelandsvatnet, and since 1988 there has also been a shorter 3.4 km family course. The event is a major family gathering in Arna, combining competition and social activities, including music and a warm-up before the start. The race is suitable for both children and adults, with free entry for children under 12.
course_highlights: Course around Haukelandsvatnet
3.4 km family course
Historic course starting at Londalskrysset (former route)
additional: The Family Race starts at 19:00; the 10 km race starts at 19:30. The registration deadline for family and individual entries is Monday, August 31 at 18:30. Registration is online only. Race numbers can be collected at Øyrane Torg and Espelandshallen before and on race day. There will be music, socialising and a warm-up before the start. Many great gift prizes will be drawn using race numbers. Participants must use different race numbers when registering for both courses. The stated distances, prices and start times are from the 2026 edition and may differ in 2027. In 2026, the family course started at 19:00 and the 10 km race at 19:30.

name: Stomperudkarusellen- løp nr 4
description: Stomperudkarusellen is a long-running race series organized by Sørum IL since 1981. The series consists of four races with varying distances, from 800 meters to 9 kilometers, and includes shorter options for the youngest participants. The races take place in scenic surroundings around Sørum, with the start and finish at Stomperud Stadium for most races. Participants use the same race number throughout the series, and the event is open to children, teenagers, and adults.
course_highlights: Bingenrunden, 5 km with a shorter option
Aasgaardsrunden, 9 km with a shorter option
Lysløypa, 6 km with a shorter option
additional: Participants use the same race number in all races in the series. Children who are members of Sørum IL can participate for free if they register no later than one week before race day. The races are held at different locations in Sørum, with Stomperud Stadium as the main venue. The meeting point is listed as Stomperud Stadium, Lørenvegen 2, 1923 Sørum. The distance, start time, and registration details for 2027 have not been confirmed in the sources.

name: Vestfold løpskarusell - 7. løp - Essoskogen
price_range: Sesongkort: 900–1200 kr ved påmelding innen 31.12.2026; deretter 960–1260 kr

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: 1200 kr. for ikke medlemmer frem til 31.12.26.

description: Vestfold Running Series 2027 is a series of 8 great races in the Tønsberg region, offering the joy of running, community and a great atmosphere for all levels. Each race has two distances, and starts at 18:00. The races take place in varied and beautiful surroundings, with electronic timing via EQ Timing. Participants can choose to enter individual races or buy a season pass for all the races at a discounted price. Season-pass holders collect their race number at the first race; individual entrants collect theirs from the race office before the start.
course_highlights: Start and finish right by the car park in Essoskogen
Two distances: 3 km (one lap) and 5.6 km (two laps)
After 200 metres, the course turns sharply right and runs down along the edge of the field
additional: Electronic timing via EQ Timing. Season-pass holders collect their race number at the first race; individual entrants collect theirs from the race office before the start. Course descriptions and profiles are available in the Facebook group. Everyone can take part, regardless of level. The season pass offers a discount, and race numbers are handed out at the first race. Start at 18:00. Registration is available with a season pass or for individual races.

name: Knarvikmila 2027 - Sparebanken Norge Stafetten
description: Knarvikmila is a long-standing running event that has grown since 1983 into a major community celebration featuring both sports and cultural activities. The event runs over several days and includes various races, seminars, concerts and family activities. The Sparebanken Norge Relay is a social and intense relay with five short legs, perfect for team-building and having fun together. The start and finish are at Knarvik Stadium, with good facilities such as changing rooms, showers and baggage storage in Nordhordlandshallen. After the relay, participants gather in the hall for food and mingling, with an awards ceremony for the top teams.
course_highlights: The relay consists of 5 legs between 400m and 1700m
Start and finish at Knarvik Stadium, with the relay exchange near the stadium
The course goes through Knarvik ungdomsskule, the car park, Juvikstølen and Brekkeløypa
additional: Race numbers and the relay baton can be collected at Nordhordlandshallen on Friday 16:00 - 17:45. The baton must be returned in the finish area. Changing rooms, showers and toilets are available at Nordhordlandshallen. Free parking in the area around the stadium. After the relay, there will be an awards ceremony and a social gathering with food and mingling at Nordhordlandshallen. The event address provided is Knarvik Stadion, 5916 Isdalstø.

name: Knarvikmila Halvmaraton
location: Knarvik Stadion, Knarvik, Alver, Vestland, Norway
description: Knarvikmila Half Marathon is being held for the 17th time and offers a beautiful, traffic-free course consisting of four laps of a 5.275 km route, with the start and finish at Knarvik Stadium. The course runs on asphalt and gravel, through the beautiful natural surroundings of Brekkeløypa and around Knarvik. There are 12 drink stations along the way, clear course markings, around 20 course marshals and Red Cross personnel on site. After finishing, participants receive water and bananas. Prizes are awarded to class winners, with cash prizes for the top finishers.
course_highlights: Traffic-free course, starting and finishing at Knarvik Stadium
Asphalt and gravel course through Brekkeløypa
12 drink stations along the way
additional: Race numbers can be collected at Nordhordlandshallen, which is open Friday at 16:00, Saturday at 09:30 and Sunday at 09:00. Late registration is possible but should be avoided. It takes place at Nordhordlandshallen on Friday, Saturday and Sunday during the specified hours. Free parking is available at several locations in Knarvik, with parking attendants on site. Changing rooms and toilets are available at Nordhordlandshallen. The Red Cross and an event doctor will be on site for emergencies. Waste and recycling stations are available. Knarvikmila T-shirts are also available for purchase when registering and at the hall. Drink stations are provided along the course. The half marathon has a minimum age of 15 and is part of FjordViking.

name: Numedalsløpet 2027
organizer: Lyngdal IL, Svene IL og Flesberg IL
description: Numedalsløpet 2027 is a traditional race first held in 1936, making it one of the oldest sporting events in Numedal. The race follows easy forest terrain for approximately 12 km from Høgheim in Lyngdal to Flesberg community centre. It is an inclusive event for both competitive runners and recreational participants, organised in cooperation by Lyngdal IL, Svene IL and Flesberg IL. The race offers opportunities to enjoy nature and community, and has grown into a popular event attracting participants from across the region.
course_highlights: 12 km route on easy forest terrain
Start at Høgheim in Lyngdal and finish at Flesberg community centre
384.4 metres of elevation gain on the course
additional: The untimed recreational run starts from 11:30. The race and timed recreational run start at 13:00. The event is organised in cooperation by Lyngdal IL, Svene IL and Flesberg IL. The race and timed recreational run start at 13:00. The untimed recreational run starts from 11:30. The registration deadline is Thursday, 2 September 2027.

name: Vestfold Maraton
description: Vestfold Marathon is an inclusive running event that encourages recreational runners of all ages to be physically active, starting in Larvik and finishing at Jahn Teigens plass in Tønsberg. The event offers both a full and half marathon, as well as a relay with multiple legs, and emphasizes physical activity and social interaction. The courses are officially measured by Kondis, and the relay format allows everyone to take part, regardless of ability. The event creates a running celebration from Larvik to Tønsberg, with beautiful natural scenery along the way.
course_highlights: Start at Hegdal industrial area in Larvik and finish at Jahn Teigens plass at Tønsberg brygge
Relay with 8 legs for the marathon and 4 legs for the half marathon
The courses are officially measured by Kondis and include varied legs through urban and natural areas
additional: Relay teams can be women’s, men’s, or mixed teams, with at least one woman per team. Wheelchair racing with spiked wheels is permitted when registering. Water, bananas, and sports drinks are available at several aid stations. Changing rooms with showers are available at Tønsberg guest harbor. Race numbers can be collected in advance at Nortura Tønsberg or at the start venue on race day. No refunds are given for withdrawals or failure to finish. Photographers document the race, and images may be used for marketing. Anti-doping rules apply. The course and leg details provided refer to the 2026 information and may change for 2027. Registered participants can take part individually or as a relay team.

name: Jentemila
organizer: Jentemila, Christiania Glasmagasin og Anton Sport
description: Jentemila is a long-running, accessible girls’ race held at Bislett Stadium in Oslo on the first weekend of September. The race brings together thousands of girls of all ages and fitness levels for a weekend of running, walking or jogging 5 or 10 km, alongside entertainment, shopping, gifts and a well-stocked goodie bag for all participants. The event offers a unique running festival with music, competitions and socialising, and wraps up with bubbles and a lively atmosphere after the finish. Jentemila welcomes everyone to an inclusive and magical experience at Bislett Stadium.
course_highlights: A route on asphalt, gravel and trails, with challenging and varied sections
Choose between 5 km and 10 km distances
Start and finish at iconic Bislett Stadium, with Oslo streets closed to traffic
additional: Participants are divided into waves based on their expected finish time and distance. Waves start two minutes apart. It is possible to collect race bibs for several people by showing a QR code or giving their names. Goodie bags are handed out after the finish in exchange for a voucher. Medals are available to pre-order or buy at the stadium. Bag storage is available; luggage tags are attached to race bibs. After-run drinks are available to participants over 18. Discounts are offered for registering without a T-shirt and for group registrations (more than 4 people). A 15% student discount is available by sending proof of student status to the organiser after registering. Race bibs can be selected with or without a T-shirt; choosing no T-shirt gives a 100 kr discount. Groups of more than four get a 50 kr discount per participant. The 10 km is listed as starting at 14:00, and the 5 km and 10 km waves start two minutes apart.

name: Drammen Halvmaraton
description: Drammen Half Marathon is a spectacular running adventure that takes participants around a lightning-fast 10-kilometer loop twice. The race takes place in Drammen, Buskerud, and offers a fast, scenic course suitable for both experienced runners and recreational runners. The event has a limited number of race bibs to ensure a good experience for all participants. In addition to the half marathon, a children’s race and other running activities are held under the same umbrella.
course_highlights: The course consists of a fast 10-kilometer loop run twice
The race goes through central Drammen and the surrounding areas
A limited number of race bibs ensures a good running experience
additional: A green race bib indicates that a medal was purchased in advance. A maximum of 8,000 race bibs are available for the Drammen Half Marathon. A children’s race, Minimaraton, is also held on the same day. No phone number is provided for contact, but inquiries are answered by email and through the contact form. The organizer states that a maximum of 8,000 race bibs are available for 2026. Race times can be followed live via Ultimate Sport Service LIVE.

name: Balestrand Trailrun
description: Balestrand Trailrun is a race run on a circular course starting and finishing at Kreklingen Stadium in Balestrand. The race follows beautiful trails and offers a scenic experience in the area. There are both competitive and recreational categories, so both fast runners and recreational runners can take part. The distance is 5.4 km, and the race is suitable for anyone looking for a challenging and enjoyable trail run.
course_highlights: Circular course on beautiful trails in Balestrand
Start and finish at Kreklingen Stadium
Terrain with maintained trails and scenic surroundings
additional: The race has both competitive and recreational categories. The start and finish are at Kreklingen Stadium. The race is a 5.4 km circular trail course. Previous races such as Balestrand Opp and Rundt are now combined under Balestrand Trailrun, with a new route from 2025. Previous editions have had a competitive course, a recreational course, and a free mini-run. Course distances and practical information may vary from year to year.

name: Fløymila
description: Fløymila is a fun run held on Flekkerøy in Kristiansand, with distances suited to both children and adults. The event includes a 600-metre children’s race, as well as 5 km and 10 km distances. It is a popular event that brings together many participants for an enjoyable running experience in scenic surroundings. Fløymila welcomes everyone to take part and enjoy running on Flekkerøy.
course_highlights: Run on Flekkerøy amid scenic surroundings
Distances for children and adults: 600 m, 5 km and 10 km
A fun run with a great atmosphere and broad participation
additional: Distances include a 600 m children’s race, 5 km and 10 km Fløymila. Race bib collection and registration take place at the event. The race attracts many participants and is a fun run focused on community and enjoyment.

name: Nordmarkstravern
description: Nordmarkstravern is a traditional forest race in Nordmarka, Oslo, offering several distances for different ages and ability levels. The courses follow trails and gravel roads through some of Nordmarka’s most beautiful areas, with start points at Stryken, Skar, Hammeren and Nordberg school. The event offers everything from short, child-friendly routes to challenging ultra-distances, with an emphasis on clear course marking, refreshment stations and safety, including medical personnel and first aid. The race has an inclusive atmosphere, with categories for runners, people with strollers and wheelchair users.
course_highlights: Heltravern 30 km on trails and gravel roads from Stryken to Kringsjå by Sognsvann
Dobbeltravern 60 km, following the Heltravern course out and back
Kvarttravern 7 km, with 2.5 km on trails and the rest on gravel roads, suitable for children and families
additional: Start times: Dobbeltravern 60 km at 07:30; all other distances at 11:00. Prices include a race bib with timing, marked courses, prizes and category prizes. Bus transport to start areas is provided except for the 30 km, 60 km and 1.2 km distances. Bag transport from start to finish is available for all distances. Food and drink stations along the route. A mandatory NOK 50 licence fee for the Norwegian Athletics Association applies to participants without an annual licence. Registration is binding, but race bibs may be sold or transferred to another participant. Registration prices vary by distance and date. A mandatory one-time licence fee of NOK 50 is added for participants without an annual licence. The entry fee includes timing, marked courses, prizes, bag transport, and food and drink stations. Bus transport to the start areas is included for several distances.

name: Lovundmila
description: Lovundmila is a friendly race on beautiful Lovund, offering several distances, including 10 km, 5 km, and shorter races for children and young people. The race combines scenic surroundings with an inclusive atmosphere and attracts both local and visiting runners. The event is known for its great atmosphere, volunteer effort, and support from the local community. Lovundmila is more than just a race; it is a social event celebrating the joy of running in scenic surroundings.
course_highlights: Race on beautiful Lovund with wonderful scenery
Several distances: 10 km, 5 km, and shorter races for children
Great atmosphere with support from volunteers and spectators
additional: Previous editions have started and finished at Lovundmila Flerbrukshall.

name: Furusjøen Rundt-løpet/marsjen
description: Furusjøen Rundt-løpet is a traditional race that has been held since 1966, offering beautiful natural surroundings near Rondane. The event offers several distances, including a half marathon, a 9 km walk and a children’s obstacle race, making it family-friendly. The course starts at Rudland Fjellsenter and crosses varied terrain, including gravel roads, trails, forest roads and asphalt, as well as scenic areas such as Frydalen Landscape Protection Area. Welcome to the mountains and to the Adventure in Rondane!
course_highlights: The course passes through Frydalen Landscape Protection Area, with beautiful scenery and reindeer habitat
The course’s longest uphill stretch is approximately 1.3 km long, with 35 m of elevation gain
Varied surfaces include gravel roads, trails, forest roads, marshland and asphalt
additional: The half marathon starts at 12:00, and the 9 km walk starts at 12:20. Late registration is available at the stadium until the start. There are age categories from 11 years old, as well as a family category. There are several aid stations along the course. The terrain includes wet marshland; stepping on tussocks and rocks is recommended for better grip. The start and finish are at Rudland Fjellsenter on Kvamsfjellet. The event also includes the Snipp-Snapp children’s obstacle race. Registration is through the organizer’s website.

name: Herdla Backyard Ultra
description: Herdla Backyard Ultra is an ultramarathon that challenges both beginners and experienced runners to test their limits in a unique community. The race is organized by an experienced ultrarunner and focuses on safe participation, good facilities, and a course that gives participants the best possible conditions for success. Participants run a 6.7 km loop every hour, and the race continues until only one runner remains. Herdla Backyard Ultra is not just about winning, but about challenging yourself and sharing the experience with others.
course_highlights: The course is 6.7 km, with varied terrain and 135 metres of elevation gain
The start and finish area are the same for every loop
Each loop must be completed in under an hour, and the next loop starts on the hour, exactly
additional: Each participant receives a bib number and a timing chip for tracking. A reflective vest and headlamp are mandatory in the dark. Support is only allowed in the finish area between loops. The winner receives NOK 5,000, and prizes are drawn based on bib numbers. The race does not end until the last runner completes the final loop. All participants receive a medal. Timing and tracking are provided by Racetracker Norge.

name: Toughest
description: Toughest Oslo 2027 offers an unforgettable obstacle course racing experience in the spectacular terrain of Holmenkollen. The main race covers approximately 8 km with 30–40 varied obstacles, including the iconic Holmenkollen ski slope as the grand finale. Participants can choose between the full main race, a lighter 4 km Xplore course designed for fun and beginners, or a 2 km family-friendly course. The event welcomes everyone from amateurs to elite athletes, with options for fast lanes and penalty rounds to tailor the challenge.
course_highlights: Varied and challenging terrain in Holmenkollen
Approximately 30–40 obstacles of varied size and difficulty
Finish on the legendary Holmenkollen ski slope
additional: Fast lanes are available on selected obstacles for an extra challenge. Penalty rounds allow participants to skip difficult obstacles with a short jog penalty. Registration closes about one week before the event or when capacity is reached. Health care benefits can be used for registration via Benifex & Epassi. The main race has an optional Double Distance add-on of approximately 16 km. Registration closes about one week before the race or when capacity is reached, and prices vary depending on when you register.

name: Jentemila
description: Jentemila is a long-standing, accessible race for girls and women of all ages and fitness levels, held at Bislett Stadium on the first weekend of September. The event offers both 5 km and 10 km distances, and participants can choose to run, walk or jog. There are two days of entertainment, shopping, gifts, competitions and a well-stocked goodie bag for every participant. After crossing the finish line, participants can enjoy sparkling drinks and celebrate in an inclusive, festive atmosphere. Known as Norway’s friendliest women’s race, Jentemila brings together thousands of participants for a unique running festival.
course_highlights: The courses run on asphalt, gravel and trails, with a challenging and varied profile
Start and finish at Bislett Stadium, with streets in Oslo closed to traffic for the event
Wave starts every 2 minutes, based on the chosen distance and expected finish time
additional: Participants can choose a race bib with or without a T-shirt; choosing no T-shirt gives a discount of NOK 100. Groups of more than 4 people receive a discount of NOK 50 per participant. Bag storage is available, with baggage tags included. Medals can be pre-ordered or purchased at the stadium. After the race, participants over 18 can attend an after-run with alcoholic or non-alcoholic drinks. Wave starts are 2 minutes apart, and participants can submit the same expected finish time to run together in the same wave. Goodie bags are handed out after the finish line in exchange for the coupon attached to the race bib. Race bibs can be ordered with or without a T-shirt; choosing no T-shirt gives a discount of NOK 100. Groups of more than four receive a discount of NOK 50 per participant. The 5 km and 10 km waves start 2 minutes apart.

name: Stordløpet
description: Stordløpet is a long-standing race organized by Stord Friidrett, a subgroup of Stord Idrettslag, which has a history dating back to 1914. The race takes place at Stord Stadium and brings together runners of various ages and abilities for a running festival in central Leirvik. The event is an important part of local sporting life and offers a great opportunity to take part in a well-organized race with a welcoming atmosphere.
course_highlights: The race takes place at Stord Stadium and in central Leirvik
Suitable for runners of all ages and abilities
Part of a local running festival with a great atmosphere
additional: Stord Friidrett also organizes other races, such as Parkløpet, with distances suited to children and young people. The club has members of all ages and offers a broad range of athletics events. A fun run and children's races of 400 or 800 metres have also been held. Information about distances and the course is from previous editions and does not confirm the details for 2027.

name: Lyderhorn Opp 2027
description: Lyderhorn Opp is an annual uphill race organized by Laksevåg Turn og Idrettslag, finishing at the summit of Lyderhorn, 396 meters above sea level. The course is approximately 3.8 km long and suitable for both competitive and recreational runners. The event takes place in scenic surroundings in Bergen, and everyone who finishes receives a medal and a T-shirt. It is a traditional autumn event that brings together runners of all ages and ability levels.
course_highlights: Uphill race finishing at the summit of Lyderhorn, 396 meters above sea level
Course length: approximately 3.8 km
Scenic surroundings in Bergen
additional: Race bibs and T-shirts can be collected at Sport1 at Vestkanten on Friday, September 4, from 16:00 to 21:00, with a 10% discount on any product. Race bibs can also be collected at the start, but collection in advance is recommended. There is ample parking, but using public transport, walking, or cycling is recommended. First-aid personnel and defibrillators are available along the course. Cash prizes are awarded to the three fastest men and women. Many gift prizes are drawn by race bib number. The organizer says Lyderhorn Opp will return in 2027. Distance and course details are based on previous editions; details for 2027 have not been provided.

name: Melshornløpet 2027
location: Sivert Aarflot-plassen, Volda, Møre og Romsdal, Norway
organizer: Foreininga Melshornets Venner og VTI Friidrett
description: Melshornløpet is an annual uphill race from Volda town centre to the summit of Melshornet, 807 metres above sea level. The course is approximately 7 kilometres long and offers a wonderful experience in nature, with a challenge from fjord to mountain. The race is open to competitive runners, recreational runners and participants in the non-competitive fitness run, with cash prizes in the junior and senior categories. The start is at Sivert Aarflot-plassen in Volda, and the finish is at the summit of Melshornet, with spectacular views of Voldafjorden and the Sunnmøre Alps. All participants receive a medal, and prize draws are held during the awards ceremony in the start area.
course_highlights: Approximately 7 km from sea level to 807 metres above sea level
Scenic surroundings from fjord to mountain
Spectacular views of Voldafjorden and the Sunnmøre Alps
additional: The recreational category has a start window from 09:00 to 11:00, while the competitive categories have a mass start at 11:00. All participants in the competitive categories must carry a backpack with the required equipment. Random checks will be carried out at the summit, with a time penalty for missing equipment. The awards ceremony takes place at 14:30 in the start area, and you must be present to win a draw prize. The fitness run is an alternative with no timing or competitive pressure, starting between 09:00 and 11:00. The fitness run supports the Norwegian Cancer Society, and it is possible to shorten the route by starting from Bratteberg school. Recreational starts are between 09:00 and 11:00; the competitive categories have a mass start at 11:00. The recreational category is unranked. Participants in the competitive categories must carry a backpack with the required equipment.

name: Trondheim Maraton
distance_verbose: Maraton, Halvmaraton, 10 km, 5 km, 2 km, 0.6 km
description: Trondheim Marathon is Norway’s oldest marathon and is held annually on the first weekend of September in central Trondheim. The course runs through the city centre and offers beautiful, spectator-friendly surroundings, with the start and finish at Torvet. The event offers distances for all levels, from children’s races to the full marathon, and also includes relay races. The focus is on public health and the joy of running, with a wide range of training plans and support for participants throughout the year.
course_highlights: The course runs through central Trondheim, with the start and finish at Torvet
The full marathon consists of two laps; the half marathon is one lap
Scenic, spectator-friendly routes extend to Lade and Tempe
additional: Start and finish at Torvet in Trondheim. Relay races have four legs for both the half marathon (4 × 5 km) and the full marathon (4 × 10.55 km). All participants must have a licence, either an annual licence or a one-time licence purchased during registration. Bag storage is available inside City Hall. Pacers adjust their pace to the conditions and inclines. Medical support and first-aid training for race officials are provided. Participants must finish within the time limit to be recorded as having completed the race. The range of distances also includes the 2 km Children’s Marathon, the 600 m Children’s Mini Marathon, and relay races. The half-marathon relay has four 5 km legs, and the marathon relay has four 10.55 km legs.

name: Rødseterpytten Rundt 2027
description: Rødseterpytten Rundt 2027 is a running event for all ages in Asker, Akershus. The main race is a 9 km trail course for adults, with children’s races starting at 400 metres and up. The event is suitable for both recreational and competitive runners, and a kiosk is open during the race. This is an inclusive and enjoyable running experience in scenic surroundings.
course_highlights: 9 km trail course for adults
Children’s races starting at 400 metres and up
Suitable for both recreational and competitive runners
additional: A kiosk is open during the event. The race is organised by Tofte Fremad IF. A kiosk is open.

name: Blodslitet
description: Blodslitet is an international ultra-long-distance orienteering race and a long-standing season finale in Norway, organized annually by Fredrikstad Ski Club. The race offers challenging and varied courses in beautiful terrain, with mass starts in all classes, including the Norwegian Ultra-Long-Distance Championships. The terrain at Gillingsrød consists of open spruce and pine forest, marshland, and demanding hilly sections, and is suitable for elite athletes, recreational runners, and young participants alike. Blodslitet is known for its lively arena atmosphere and exciting battles on the course.
course_highlights: Ultra-long-distance race with mass starts in all classes
Varied terrain featuring spruce and pine forest, marshland, and hilly sections
New orienteering map at a scale of 1:15000, 1:10000, or 1:7500
additional: Parking is available in fields 200–700 meters from the arena, with a parking fee of 75 NOK payable via Vipps. Race office with collection of bib numbers and maps. EmiTag is used for timing; rental of an EmiTag costs 50 NOK. Kiosk serving food and drinks, as well as sports equipment for sale at the arena. Childcare and a Småtroll program are available. Poor mobile coverage, but a guest network from NOF is available. First aid at the arena. Start and finish at the arena, with mass starts in all classes.

name: Sørdalskarusellen - Tverrløpet
location: Kleivbakken above Håkons Hall, Lillehammer, Norway
description: Sørdalskarusellen - Tverrløpet is the season finale of Sørdalskarusellen, a series of ten recreational races held from April to September. The race is suitable for everyone, regardless of fitness, age or ambitions, and focuses on the joy of running, community and personal achievement. The event offers an enjoyable race experience with a mass start and the option to run virtually. The start is at Kleivbakken above Håkons Hall in Lillehammer, and the distance is approximately 3.9 km.
course_highlights: Approximately 3.9 km course
Start at Kleivbakken above Håkons Hall in Lillehammer
Season finale of Sørdalskarusellen, with a mass start
additional: You can participate virtually from 5 to 8 September. The race is part of a series of ten recreational races suitable for all levels and ages. The organisers are Innlandet Corporate Sports Association and Tele BIL. The event emphasises the joy of running, community and personal achievement. Tverrløpet can also be completed virtually. The listed 2027 event is dated 8 September, but the date and time of the mass start should be confirmed with the organisers’ latest information.

name: Kongskleiva Opp
description: Kongskleiva is Bekkjarvik’s most popular hike, a refreshing and scenic walk that rewards you with 360-degree views from the top of Kongsfjellet. The route passes through beautiful scenery via a fine Sherpa trail and includes a stop at Taushaugen, with views over Bekkjarvik. It is ideal for both exercise and enjoying nature, and offers the chance to spot wildlife from western Norway, such as white-tailed eagles and feral sheep. The official record time is an impressive 05:31.
course_highlights: A fine Sherpa trail through beautiful scenery
360-degree views from the top of Kongsfjellet
A chance to spot white-tailed eagles and feral sheep
additional: Parking is limited at the start of Kongskleivo; parking at Selbjørn Primary School, Bekkjarvik Torg or Leirvikjo is recommended. The hike can start from Bekkjarvik Torg or Leirvikjo and includes steps up to the summit. It suits all levels if you adjust your pace. Kongskleiva Opp is listed as 5 km. A results overview for 2026 lists the race as cancelled; information about the 2027 edition is not available in the sources.

name: Grimstad Maraton
price_range: Gratis barneløp; 250–600 kr for individuelle distanser; maratontrippel 950 kr; stafett 300 kr per deltaker

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Avgift: 250,- Passer for deg som vil løpe eller gå uten tidtaking.

description: Grimstad Marathon is an inclusive running festival taking place on 11 September 2027 in beautiful Grimstad. The event is suitable for all levels, from beginners to experienced runners, and offers distances from a 3 km fun run to a full half marathon, including a relay and a triple challenge. The start and finish are at Grimstad Library in Byhaven, and the course offers scenic surroundings, with sections through the town centre and cheering spectators. All participants receive medals, and there is also a free children’s race, Sparrisløpet.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Grimstad Library – Byhaven
The course passes through beautiful Groos and charming town-centre streets
Pacers are available for the 10 km and half marathon at various finish times
additional: Race numbers can be collected at the Library in Byhaven on Friday from 16:00 to 18:00 and on Saturday from 08:00. Changing facilities and lockers are available; bring your own padlock. EQ Timing handles registration, payment, timing and results. Pacers are available for the 10 km and half marathon at various finish times. The 3 km fun run is suitable for running or walking and is untimed. The 3 km distance is untimed and can be run or walked. All participants receive medals.

name: Nærsnes Backyard
description: Nærsnes Backyard is a social, accessible race held in Nærsnes, Asker. It is suitable for all levels, from beginners to experienced runners, and has both a children’s course and a longer adults’ course. The event focuses on participation and inclusion, and aims to be climate-neutral. It is a pleasant day with activities for the whole family, including a market, bouncy castle and face painting.
course_highlights: The course starts at the sports field and follows footpaths, trails and gravel roads in the area around Nærsnes.
Includes a steep hill of approximately 500 metres leading up to a farm.
Finishes with a lap of the football field and a finish beneath the finish arch.
additional: Race numbers can be collected at Sport1 (Rortunet) in the days before the race. The children’s race starts at 12:15, with a medal and ice cream from Joker Nærsnes. Activities include a market, bouncy castle, face painting and Wipe out for children and adults. The evening ends with lit fire pans from 19:00 to 23:00. Registration for 2027 is mentioned on the organiser’s website.

name: TFS FrontYard Festningen
description: TFS FrontYard Festningen is a unique race held at the historic Kristiansten Fortress in Trondheim. The race consists of a challenging 3 km loop course, with each lap needing to be run faster than the previous one, creating an exciting and tactical competition. The event offers a lively atmosphere, with the option to set up your own camp, and food and drinks available for both participants and spectators. This race is for anyone looking for a fun and challenging experience in the city's most iconic surroundings.
course_highlights: 3 km loop course at Kristiansten Fortress
Start and finish inside the fortress
Challenging race with the pace increasing each lap
additional: On race day, participants are advised to arrive well before the start. You can set up your own camp on Friday evening. Food and drinks are sold on site, but you must bring your own race nutrition or buy it at race bib collection. There is no parking at the fortress, and participants are encouraged to use public transport, cycle or walk. Spectators can follow the race live via RaceTracker. Camps can be set up from Friday evening. Parking is not available at the Fortress; the organizer encourages people to walk, cycle or use public transport. Registration via RaceTracker.

name: Jentebølgen - Steinkjer
description: Jentebølgen in Steinkjer is an inclusive race for girls and women of all ages, held as part of the Vi bryr oss run. The event brings participants together for an energising experience focused on achievement, community and mental health. Held at Steinkjer Torg, it offers a welcoming setting for taking part with friends, family and colleagues. Participation also supports Mental Helse Ungdom through a contribution for each race entry sold.
course_highlights: The race takes place at Steinkjer Torg
Focus on community, achievement and mental health
Open to girls and women of all ages
additional: The race entry includes access to the race, insurance and a ticket fee. The event supports Mental Helse Ungdom with NOK 10 for each race entry sold. The event is a meeting place focused on safety, inclusion, entertainment and activities. An earlier local Vi bryr oss race listing stated that 50% of ticket revenue goes to Mental Helse Ungdom. Prices and details for 2027 have not been confirmed.

name: Skjervøy 20:1000
description: Skjervøy 20:1000 is a challenging mountain race combining a 20 km distance with 1,000 metres of elevation gain in scenic surroundings on Skjervøy, at the edge of the open sea at 70 degrees north. The race features steep, technically demanding trails, cart tracks and boardwalks across marshland, with spectacular views and varied terrain around Skjervøy centre. It is suitable both for the fittest runners and for those looking for a manageable challenge, with recreational and competitive classes. A shorter 10 km course with 500 metres of elevation gain is also held, as well as a 1 km children’s race. The event has a social focus and aims to inspire more people to experience the island’s wonderful routes.
course_highlights: Steep, technically demanding trails with narrow sections
Cart tracks in hilly terrain and boardwalks across marshland
Wonderful views at 70 degrees north and a varied course around Skjervøy centre
additional: The 1 km children’s race is free, with registration on race day. Race bibs can be collected at Sporten Skjervøy on Thursday, Friday and Saturday before the race. Aid stations with water and cordial are located at 8 km and 12 km on the 20:1000 course, and at 3 km on the 10:500 course; runners must bring their own bottle or cup. Poles are allowed, but runners are responsible for their own safety. Headphones are not allowed. The time limit is 7 hours for the recreational class and 5 hours for the competitive class on the 20:1000. Prizes include cash prizes for the three fastest runners in the competitive class, a prize for a new course record, and draw prizes for all finishers. There is also a sprint prize (Seppalaspurten) on the final 160 metres. The programme lists separate starts for the recreational and competitive classes in the 20:1000 and 10:500. The children’s race is 1 km.

name: Valdresløpet
description: Valdresløpet is a challenging trail race that truly puts your running fitness and trail skills to the test. The half-marathon course offers varied terrain and a wonderful experience in the traditional mountain-farm region. There are also shorter distances, including a quarter marathon, and several mini-races for children in different age groups, so the whole family can take part and enjoy a sense of achievement.
course_highlights: Half marathon of 21.1 km with 570 m of elevation gain on varied terrain
Quarter marathon of 10.3 km, starting at the same place as the half marathon, but following its own route up Knippesetvegen
Several mini-races for children from 450 m to 3.9 km, adapted to different age groups
additional: The race bib must be attached visibly to the front of the chest, with two timing chips on the back. Race headquarters opens at 10:00 on race day. The Red Cross will be on standby with an ATV patrol and a treatment tent. Awards are given in 10-year age groups, with medals and Valdres Ost for the top three in each group. Refreshment and food stations on the half-marathon course are at 7.3 km, 12.9 km and 17.7 km. The quarter marathon has a refreshment station after 6.7 km. Start location: Vasetgrende 1, 2960 Røn. The event also includes three distances for children.

name: Kyststien Rundt 2027
location: Bud, Hustadvika, Møre og Romsdal, Norway

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Preliminärt pris for løpet 2027 er 500 kr pluss eventuelt 100 kr for transport.

description: Kyststien Trail Ultra is an unforgettable 50 km ultrarun along the Coastal Trail, from Blokkebukta Camping to Gon Camping. The race offers varied terrain, including sandy beaches, technical trails along cliffs and coves, and spectacular panoramic views of the sea and lush landscape. It is a challenge for adventurous runners looking to test their physical and mental limits while experiencing the beauty of nature. The race celebrates community and a shared passion for nature and running, with locally made medals for everyone who finishes.
course_highlights: 50 km of varied terrain with sand, grass, mountains, stairs, rocks, and roots
The course follows the blue-marked Coastal Trail, with extra signage and a GPX file available
Spectacular views of the sea, cliffs, and lush landscape
additional: Race bibs can be picked up the evening before or on race day. The finish is at Gonhytta, where water, snacks, and hot soup will be served. Prizes for the top 3 women and men, plus a race-bib draw. All finishers receive a locally made birch medal. Free hot showers and the option of a cold sea swim after finishing. Five staffed aid stations along the course with first aid, toilets, drinks, and snacks. The sports drink is homemade and contains sugar, salt, honey, and lime juice.

name: Urke Challenge Saksaløpet 2027
location: Urke, Ørsta, Møre og Romsdal, Norway

name: Ålesund Trail 2027
description: Ålesund Trail 2027 is a trail race offering challenges in some of Norway’s most beautiful surroundings, with Borgundfjorden and the Sunnmøre Alps as a backdrop. The event offers three distances: a 15 km main race that starts in the city and climbs into the mountains to around 450 metres above sea level, a demanding 2.75 km uphill race with 313 metres of elevation gain, and a short 500-metre children’s race. The event is suitable for all levels, from recreational runners to competitive athletes, and emphasizes a friendly atmosphere, safety, and sustainability. Mandatory equipment is required for the 15 km race, and staffed aid stations are available along the route and at the finish.
course_highlights: 15 km trail race with a highest point of around 450 metres above sea level
Demanding 2.75 km uphill race with 313 metres of elevation gain and a 20% gradient
Panoramic views of the Sunnmøre Alps and Borgundfjorden
additional: Start times: Uphill race 10:00, children’s race 11:00, 15 km main race 12:00. Mandatory equipment for the 15 km race: a fully charged mobile phone, at least 500 ml of drink, trail shoes, and clothing suitable for the conditions; food/energy is recommended. A staffed aid station is located halfway through the 15 km race, and another is at the finish of the uphill race. Equipment checks may take place at the start and along the route. Medical personnel are present at the start, finish, and aid stations. The organizer may stop the race in the event of safety threats. Participants are required to help injured runners. The event emphasizes leaving no trace and sustainability. The uphill race starts at 10:00 and the children’s race at 11:00. Participants in the 15 km race must bring a mobile phone, at least 500 ml of drink, trail shoes, and clothing suitable for the conditions. Course maps, elevation profiles, and GPX tracks are available, and registration is via the website.

name: Torvikbukt 6 topper 2027
location: Torvikbukt, Gjemnes, Møre og Romsdal, Norway
description: Torvikbukt 6 Topper is a challenging mountain race held in Torvikbukt, with several distances tailored to different age groups. The race offers spectacular scenery and six peaks that together involve considerable elevation gain. It is suitable for youth, junior and senior runners. The event has a long tradition and attracts both recreational and competitive runners looking for a challenging experience in scenic surroundings.
course_highlights: The course includes six mountain peaks with up to 2,000 metres of elevation gain in total
Scenic surroundings in Torvikbukt with varied terrain
Several distances for youth, junior and senior runners, with varying lengths and elevation gain
additional: Start times vary by category: Tour class at 08:00, recreational at 10:00, senior at 11:00, junior and recreational at 11:30, and youth at 11:40. Registration is through EQTiming or on site for the tour class. Elevation profiles and maps of the course are available on the Instagram page. The listed distances and course information are from previous editions and may differ from 2027. Previous start and finish locations have been at Gjemneshallen.

name: Jentebølgen - Hitra
description: Jentebølgen Hitra 2027 is an inclusive race for girls and women of all ages, taking place on 12 September 2027. The event focuses on achievement, community and a great atmosphere, and aims to create a meeting place filled with energy and the joy of running. The race is held every other year on Hitra and Frøya, and invites participants to a morning of activities and entertainment. The race bib provides entry to the race, including insurance and the ticket fee.
additional: The race bib includes insurance and the ticket fee. The event supports Mental Helse Ungdom with NOK 10 per race bib sold. There is also registration for businesses and sports clubs, with separate prices and terms. NOK 10 from each race bib sold goes to Mental Helse Ungdom. The event venue has not yet been decided.

name: Neskollen løpsfestival 2027
description: Neskollen Running Festival 2027 is Hvam Runners’ signature race, offering a trail run with fantastic views of Romerike. The race is suitable for all levels and includes distances of 4.5 km, 0.5 km, and 1 km for children. The event takes place on September 12, 2027, and offers a great opportunity to enjoy running in scenic surroundings.
course_highlights: Trail run on varied terrain
Fantastic views of Romerike
Races for all levels, including children’s races
additional: The race includes distances of 4.5 km, 0.5 km, and 1 km children’s races. The organizer is Hvam IL Friidrett. The starting point is Neskollen. The race is Hvam Runners’ signature event, with a focus on community and the joy of running. Registration is stated to open on June 1, 2027.

name: Terrengløp i Smidalen
organizer: Nidelv IL Friidrett og Nidelv IL Ski
description: Terrengløp i Smidalen is an accessible cross-country race for children and young people in grades 1–7, organized by Nidelv IL Friidrett og Ski in collaboration with Kjeldsberg Eiendom AS. The race takes place on a circuit of approximately 1,000 meters, with distances adapted to the participants’ grades. Everyone starts together, and the event encourages varied training and competition in an inclusive environment. It is an important offering for children at Nidelv IL and part of the club’s sponsorship agreement. The race is held several times during the year, with the season’s final race on 15 September.
course_highlights: A cross-country circuit of approximately 1,000 meters
Race distance adapted by grade: grades 1–3 (1 lap), grades 4–5 (2 laps), grades 6–7 (3 laps)
All participants start together
additional: The races are held several times a year, with a focus on children and young people at Nidelv IL. Coaches and team leaders are encouraged to prioritize participation over their own training. The event is part of a sponsorship agreement with Kjeldsberg Eiendom AS. Previous race formats had one lap for grades 1–3, two laps for grades 4–5, and three laps for grades 6–7.

name: TronFjellet Ultra 2027
description: TronFjellet Ultra is a challenging, self-navigated mountain ultramarathon of approximately 50 km with 3,000 meters of elevation gain in Østkjolen, Alvdal. The race offers a rugged and technically demanding route with long sections off-trail, steep descents, and exposed high-mountain terrain. Participants must navigate using a GPS track with no course markings, be self-sufficient throughout, and face challenges such as rapidly changing weather and demanding terrain. With a maximum of 25 participants and a 24-hour time limit, this is a race for strong, experienced ultrarunners seeking an iconic mountain challenge in Østerdalen.
course_highlights: Approximately 50 km with 3,000 meters of elevation gain
Self-navigated on unmarked trails, using GPS
Technically demanding mountain terrain with steep descents and exposed sections
additional: Maximum 25 participants. 24-hour time limit. No course markings; the race requires GPS navigation using a GPX track. 100% self-sufficient throughout, with no aid stations or drop bags. Pacers and pets are not allowed. Live tracking for safety. The race is 100% self-sufficient, with no food stations or drop bags, and has a 24-hour time limit. Live tracking; maximum 25 participants. No pacers or pets.

name: BMW Oslo Maraton inkl. NM maraton

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Pris for deltagelse på 10 for Grete er 800 kroner. Administrasjonsgebyr på 6,75% + 3 kr er inkludert i prisen. Engangslisens (50 kr) vil komme i tillegg.

description: DNB Oslo Marathon is one of Norway’s largest road races, with over 29,000 participants, and offers distances for all ages and levels, including the marathon, half marathon, 10 km, and the children’s event Extra Oslo Mini Marathon. The race takes place in central Oslo on a varied course with beautiful city and fjord views. It is an inclusive event with dedicated para categories and a wheelchair race, and places great emphasis on a positive participant experience, with aid stations, pacers, and a wide range of services. The race takes place on September 18, 2027, and has a new registration system for 2027.
course_highlights: The marathon course has approximately 350 metres of elevation gain and consists of two laps of the half-marathon course
The half-marathon course has approximately 175 metres of elevation gain and runs through central Oslo
The 10 km course has approximately 50 metres of elevation gain and is suitable for all levels
additional: There are aid stations approximately every 5 kilometres, with Maxim energy drink and water included in the registration fee. Pacers carrying flags guide runners toward various finish times and provide motivation. Group registration is available, with discounts for groups of at least 10 participants and consolidated invoicing. Cancellation insurance is also available when registering. GPX files for the courses are available to download. Previous editions have also offered the half marathon, 10 km, and Oslotrippelen.

name: BERGAN BYGG Brakvatnet halvmaraton + stafett
description: Bergan Bygg Brakvatnet Half Marathon is a traditional half-marathon organized by Osterøy IL Friidrett. The race takes place around Brakvatnet on Osterøy, on a course of eight laps of 2,595 metres plus 337.5 metres, with the start and finish by the bathing area. The event also includes a relay and a children’s race, and provides changing and toilet facilities as well as food in the finish area. It attracts both recreational runners and competitive athletes, offering beautiful scenery and a challenging course in picturesque surroundings.
course_highlights: The course consists of 8 laps around Brakvatnet plus 337.5 metres to the start/finish
Start and finish by the bathing area at Brakvatnet
Course records: Espen Borge Joensen 1.18,02 (2024) and Hilde Aasheim 1.24,29 (2013)
additional: The children’s race starts at 11:00. Changing tents and toilets for women and men are available in the finish area. Food is served in the finish area, with Vipps as the preferred payment method. Parking is limited; parking at Valestrand school or Valestrandsvatnet is recommended. Cars cannot be driven from the start area. The course is 2,595 metres per lap around Brakvatnet. Previous editions have had the half-marathon and relay start at 12:00. Changing tents, toilets and a dining room are listed in the finish area. Parking is recommended at Valestrand school or the car park at Valestrandsvatnet; it is not possible to drive all the way to Brakvatnet.

name: Bryneløpet
description: Bryneløpet is an annual race organized by Bryne Friidrett for primary school children in grades 1 to 7. It has been held since 2013 and takes place during the Potetfestivalen in Bryne. The race starts between M44 and Brynesenteret and follows a route around the lower part of Fritz Røed Park, covering approximately 400 meters. Participants are divided into groups by age and gender for a safe and enjoyable running experience.
course_highlights: The route starts between M44 and Brynesenteret
Around the lower part of Fritz Røed Park
Approximately 400 meters, with the start and finish in the same place
additional: Participants start in groups by grade and gender: girls and boys in grades 1–2, girls and boys in grades 3–4, and girls and boys in grades 5–7. Race numbers are handed out in the play area at the start/finish. The race is held in connection with the Potetfestivalen. For the 2026 edition, race numbers could be collected outside Jordbærpikene in M44; corresponding practical information for 2027 has not been provided.

name: Sandnes Halvmaraton
description: Sandnes Half Marathon takes place on 18 September 2027, starting and finishing at Bogafjellhallen. The courses are officially measured and offer beautiful scenery around Stokkalandsvatnet, Sandvedparken and Bogafjell, with varied terrain including a steep hill up to Bogafjell Church. The event offers distances for everyone, from a children’s race to a half marathon, with drink stations along the way. It is a great opportunity for both recreational and experienced runners to enjoy the scenic surroundings of Sandnes.
course_highlights: Officially measured 21.1 km course with two laps around Stokkalandsvatnet and Sandvedparken
Steep hill up to Bogafjell Church on the 5 km and children’s race courses
Drink stations after approximately 3 km (for the 5 km and 10 km/half marathon) along the course
additional: You can travel to the start by public transport by taking the train to Ganddal station and walking 30 minutes to Bogafjell, or by taking the bus to Bogafjell. The children’s race starts at 12:00 and can also serve as a warm-up for adults who want to run with the children. The half marathon starts at 13:00. The start location may be adjusted due to work at the venue. Ganddal station and the bus to Bogafjell are the stated public transport options.

name: Fýri Trail by Salomon
description: Fýri Trail by Salomon invites you to a unique trail-running experience in the Norwegian mountains at Fýri Resort in Hemsedal. This race is the final event in the Salomon Golden Trail Nordic Series and offers three distances: 29 km, 18 km, and a 56 km ultra. The race combines demanding technical trails with spectacular scenery, including the challenging “Queen of the Hill” climb and the fast “Max Effort” descent. After the race, participants can celebrate at the “Mud & Champagne” party, creating a social and inclusive atmosphere for all runners.
course_highlights: Queen of the Hill: 3 km technical climb with 550 m of elevation gain
Max Effort: 4 km descent with 600 m of elevation loss
Start just outside Fýri Resort on varied surfaces including asphalt, gravel, and wide trails
additional: The race has two start groups based on expected finish time, with an Elite group for the top 50 men and women starting in a separate wave. Shuttle buses run from Fýri Resort before the start. After the race, the “Mud & Champagne” party features live music and a Superhero Celebration Hour to honour the final runners. Fýri Resort is the festival’s meeting point. The programme may include test runs, talks, an awards ceremony, and the Fýri Trail Party.

name: Ulvøyløpet
organizer: Ulvøy Challenge (Melbu Idrettslag, Stokmarknes Idrettslag og Lekang Ski- og Bygdelag)
description: Ulvøyløpet is a beautiful trail race through Hadseløya’s stunning landscape in the heart of Lofoten and Vesterålen. The race offers two distances, 13 km and 26 km, with varied terrain featuring technical trails, forest roads and open mountain trails. Whether you’re looking for a challenge or a wonderful experience in nature, Ulvøyløpet offers spectacular views and flowing trails that let you pick up the pace. The event has a long tradition and is organised by volunteers in support of local sports clubs and children and young people.
course_highlights: 13 km course with 450 metres of elevation gain, featuring technical and steep trails, forest roads and open mountain trails
26 km course with 1,000 metres of elevation gain and varied terrain, including forest roads, technical trails and mountain landscape
Flowing trails between Moan and Barheia are a highlight of the long course
additional: The recreational class starts between 09:00 and 11:00. Race numbers can be collected at Corner Sport in Stokmarknes or at Stokmarknes Stadium on race day from 08:30. Drop-bag transport from the start to the finish and return transport from Melbu to Stokmarknes after the race are available. There is ample parking at the start and finish, and toilets are available. The café in the finish area is open from 11:00 to 16:30. The prize-giving ceremony takes place at approximately 14:30 at Havfisk Arena, Melbu. The courses are marked with flags and signs, and downloading the GPX file for navigation is recommended. Aid stations offer bananas, cordial, sports drink and water (bring your own cup). Littering along the course is prohibited. A recreational walk along the 13 km course is also available. Walking participants register at Stokmarknes Stadium and may start between 09:00 and 11:00.

name: Bergan Bygg Brakvatnet Halvmaraton
description: Bergan Bygg Brakvatnet Half Marathon is a traditional half-marathon held at Brakvatnet on Osterøy. The course consists of eight laps around Brakvatnet plus an extra 337.5-meter section, with the start and finish at the bathing area. The event also includes a children’s race and a relay. Changing and toilet facilities are available in the finish area, and food is for sale. The race attracts both local and visiting runners and offers a scenic, varied route around the lake.
course_highlights: The course consists of 8 laps around Brakvatnet plus 337.5 meters
Start and finish at the bathing area by Brakvatnet
Scenic course approximately 2 km from Valestrandsfossen on Osterøy
additional: The children’s race starts at 11:00, and the half marathon and relay start at 12:00. There are changing tents and toilets for both women and men in the finish area. Food is for sale in the finish area; Vipps or cash is preferred. Parking is limited, and participants are encouraged to park at Valestrand School or by Valestrandsvatnet. Cars are not driven from the start area. The finish area has changing tents, toilets, and a dining room. Parking is at Valestrand School or the parking lot by Valestrandsvatnet.

name: Lina Roindt

late_fee.price: 100 kr gebyr ved påmelding på løpsdagen

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Kr 30,- i tillegg for engangslisens for de som ikke har helårslisens

late_fee.price: 100 kr gebyr ved påmelding på løpsdagen

description: Lina Roindt is a traditional race organized by Rindal IL, bringing competitive runners, recreational runners, and walkers together for a major family day at Torshall in Bolme, Rindal. The 10.8 km route is on asphalt and forms a loop around Rindal town centre, with a 6.7 km option for the recreational class. The event includes competitive classes for different age groups, an untimed recreational class, and a school cup for grades 5–10. There is an awards ceremony, sprint prizes, prizes for course records, and raffle prizes in the recreational class. Lina Roindt attracts high participation and is known for its great atmosphere and efficient organization.
course_highlights: 10.8 km asphalt route around Rindal town centre
Recreational class with a 6.7 km option via Sunnabrua and Elvepromenaden
Course records are rewarded with NOK 1,000
additional: Start and finish at Torshall in Bolme. Race office at the start. Changing facilities at Rinnvollen Football Stadium. Awards ceremony for competitive classes at 15:00 at Torshall. The recreational class starts between 11:00 and 12:30. The «Bjergpris» sprint prize of NOK 300 is awarded after 2.7 km. One-third of participants receive prizes in each class, including cash prizes for the top three overall, regardless of class. The school cup is for grades 5–10, with a prize for the class with the highest participation. An untimed recreational class and a school cup for pupils in grades 5–10 are offered. The stated distances and practical details apply to previous editions and may change for 2027.

name: Gjesdalmilå
description: Gjesdalmilå is an annual race organized by Gjesdal Idrettslag and held in Ålgård. The event offers distances for children, 5 km and 10 km, as well as a double distance for those who want to run both the 5 km and 10 km. The courses pass through scenic surroundings, with the start and finish at Sentralidrettsanlegget, and feature varied terrain with both easy-running sections and some hills. The event is a natural choice for both recreational and elite athletes in the region and promotes the joy of sport for all ages.
course_highlights: The 5 km course is easy to run, with fewer hills, and consists of several loops around Solås skole and Åfaret.
The 10 km course crosses the E39 through the underpass and follows Edlandsvatnet over varied terrain.
The finish is on the athletics track at the finish line at Sentralidrettsanlegget.
additional: Schedule: The children's race starts at 12:00, the 5 km starts at 12:30, and the 10 km starts at 13:30. The double distance involves running both the 5 km and 10 km. The children's race is 650 metres and takes place in the area around Ålgård Stadion. For 2027, the schedule is: children's race at 12:00, 5 km at 12:30, and 10 km at 13:30.

name: Storehornet 497 - 2027
location: Godøy, Giske, Møre og Romsdal, Norway

name: Voss Løpskarusell 2027, løp 5
description: Voss Running Series 2027 is an inclusive running series for everyone aged 9 and up, with five races throughout the year. The races are held on Mondays, starting at 19:00, except for the fifth race on 20 September, which starts at 18:30. The course is 5 km long, starting and finishing at Voss Sports Ground, and passes through Prestegardsmoen and along the waterfront promenade. This is a friendly recreational race that welcomes both casual runners and competitive runners.
course_highlights: 5 km course starting and finishing at Voss Sports Ground
Route through Prestegardsmoen
Run along the waterfront promenade
additional: A discount is available when registering for all six races before the second race. Registration for all six races opens on 15 November 2026 and closes on 3 May 2027. Registration for individual races is available via eqtiming.no. The races take place on Mondays. Start time: 18:30. Registration takes place online via EQ Timing. You can register for an individual race or get a discount by registering for all six races before the second race.

name: Birken Gateløp 10 km
description: Birken Street Run in Lillehammer is a running festival in the heart of the city, offering distances of 10 km, 5 km and the BarneBirken Street Run. The race is for everyone, whether you’re chasing a personal best, trying your first 5 km race or looking for an active experience with family and friends. Music, cheering crowds and lively support along the course create a festival atmosphere for both fast runners and those taking a more relaxed pace. The start and finish are centrally located at Sigrid Undsets plass, and the 10 km course follows parts of the historic route of the Olympic Dayrun from the 1980s and 90s.
course_highlights: The course runs through central Lillehammer on paved city streets
The 10 km course follows parts of the former Olympic Dayrun route
Music, bands and cheering crowds bring the course to life
additional: Music, bands, drums, majorettes and a DJ create a lively atmosphere along the course. The race welcomes both fast runners and those who prefer a more relaxed pace. BarneBirken Street Run supports a charitable cause by collecting donations for Right To Play. The 10 km distance is open to participants who turn at least 13 in 2027. The course returns to the finish just south of Mesna Bru.

name: Hagemanns rundbaneløp 2027
description: Hagemanns Backyard Festival 2027 is a unique race held on Svelvik Cycling Club’s loop course. The challenge is to complete a 6.7 km loop within one hour, with a start every hour on the hour from 10:00. Participants who fail to finish within the time limit are eliminated, and the aim is to be the last one standing. A children’s race is also held, and participants can choose to run a single loop at any time. The festival offers medals for all participants, changing rooms, showers and refreshments. Reflective vests and headlamps are mandatory after 21:00.
course_highlights: 6.7 km loop course, with a start every hour on the hour
Children’s race of approximately 400–500 metres around the school building
Changing rooms and showers at Ebbestadhallen available all weekend
additional: Reflective vests and headlamps are mandatory from 21:00 to 06:00. Pizza is served to participants at 19:30. The kiosk opens at 08:00 and is run by Svelvik Cycling Club. Buying and selling race bibs is possible. Changing rooms and showers at Ebbestadhallen are available all weekend. Children’s races are held on both Saturday and Sunday at 15:05. A children’s race is also held at Ebbestad Primary School. Information about course distance and elevation gain is from the 2025 edition.

name: Nattland Backyard Ultra
description: Nattland Backyard Ultra is a unique ultramarathon held in Bergen, Vestland. The race consists of multiple laps on a set course, with participants running for as long as they can in an effort to be the last one to finish. The event takes place on Saturday, 25 September 2027, and attracts local and international ultrarunners looking for a challenging and social running experience.
course_highlights: The race takes place on a set course repeated every hour
A demanding ultramarathon focused on endurance and tactics
Held in scenic surroundings in Bergen
additional: Registration is via Eqtiming.no. The race takes place on Saturday, 25 September 2027, in Bergen. No specific start times or price details were found on the available pages. Registration via EQTiming.no.

description: Backyard Stavanger is a unique ultrarunning event held at Dyrsnes Nature Centre in Stavanger. The race consists of a gently undulating loop of approximately 6.7 km, run on the hour every hour, with a maximum of 12 laps in total. Participants must start each lap to continue, and the last person to start wins the race. The event offers a friendly and inclusive atmosphere with a low barrier to entry, welcoming both beginners and experienced ultrarunners. Simple refreshments and places to rest are provided. A headlamp and reflective vest are required for safety.
course_highlights: Gently undulating loop of approximately 6.7 km per lap
Runs start on the hour, with a maximum of 12 laps (80.4 km in total)
Social event with places to rest in a tent and barn
additional: You must bring your own drinking cup, headlamp and reflective vest. Attaching your bib with a race belt is recommended. Simple refreshments include snacks, coffee, tea, broth and water. Support is not permitted indoors or on the course, only in the start/finish area. Everyone who completes 12 laps receives a cup and a wooden medal for the ultradistance (longer than a marathon). Maximum 210 participants. Your own drinking cup, headlamp and reflective vest are mandatory.

name: Gruemila
description: Gruemila is a challenging 10 km race held in Kirkenær as part of the Grue Half Marathon event. The race features technically demanding forest terrain on 6.7 km loops, where participants can compete for the win or finish for a medal and finisher cap. The event also includes a fast, flat half marathon, considered one of Norway’s fastest courses. This is a great race for both competitive and recreational runners looking for a varied and exciting running experience in scenic surroundings.
course_highlights: Technically challenging forest terrain on 6.7 km loops
Medal available for completing a loop
Flat and fast half marathon
additional: The race is run on 6.7 km loops through technically challenging forest terrain, with a new start every hour until only one runner remains. Complete one loop for a medal, or compete for a finisher cap and the win.

name: Loddefjordløpet
description: Loddefjordløpet is held at Alvøen Sports Park in Bergen and is an annual race featuring distances including a 5 km and children’s races of 2 km or 600 metres. It is a popular event for both children and adults, with a focus on athletics and recreational running in a welcoming atmosphere. Loddefjord IL Friidrett, which organises the race, also offers a range of training activities for children and young people in the area. For the latest information, follow the race’s Facebook page.
course_highlights: 5 km course in Alvøen Sports Park
Children’s races of 2 km and 600 metres
Held in scenic surroundings in western Bergen
additional: Loddefjordløpet includes both a 5 km race and children’s races over shorter distances. The organiser is Loddefjord IL Friidrett, which also offers athletics training for children and young people. Historical results from previous years are available on the website. Previous editions have offered free children’s races for pupils in grades 1–4, with a medal for participants. Information about the 2027 edition is not provided in the sources.

name: Norgesløpet 2027
description: Norgesløpet 2027 is held as a road race at Jessheim Stadium, with distances of 5 km (Norwegian Championships) and 10 km. The race starts on Kanalveien and finishes inside Jessheim Athletics Stadium. Registration is available in an elite start wave, and pacers are provided for the most popular finish times. The event also includes children’s races with multiple waves for different age groups, creating an enjoyable day with a great atmosphere for the whole family.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Jessheim Athletics Stadium
Course along Kanalveien marked with red and white ribbons
Water stations at approximately 5 km and at the finish
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Jessheim Ice and Multi-Use Hall. Bag storage is available with a baggage tag. Toilets and changing rooms are located in several nearby buildings. Train travel is recommended, with several parking areas nearby. Pacers run with visible flags or T-shirts. Children’s races are held at 11:30 and 14:00, with waves grouped by age. Fantorangen and the NRK Super Bus will be there for families. Children’s races are also held. Race bibs can be collected at Jessheim Ice and Multi-Use Hall. Train travel is recommended; parking costs 50 NOK via Vipps.

name: Skoppums Råeste 2027
price_range: 200–400 kr for 10–16 år; 350–550 kr for øvrige deltakere, lisens kan komme i tillegg
