description: Skoppums Råeste is a challenging and fun obstacle-course trail race suitable for everyone, from beginners to experienced OCR runners. The race takes place at Skoppum Idrettsplass and features mud obstacles, climbing over car wrecks, water crossings, muddy streams, tire obstacles, and crawling zones. Participants can choose to run 2.5 km with approximately 15–20 obstacles, or double the distance to 5 km by completing an extra lap. The race is accessible to all and includes timing, but everyone who finishes receives a medal and is considered a winner. There is also a separate MiniRåeste for children under 10, with a shorter obstacle course.
course_highlights: Obstacle-course trail featuring mud obstacles, climbing over car wrecks, and water crossings
Approximately 2.5 km course with 15–20 obstacles; participants can run 5 km by completing two laps
Accessible race with timing and a medal for all participants
additional: Race registration opens at 10:00 for bib pickup. Skoppums MiniRåeste for children under 10 starts at 11:00. Participants can choose a start group based on an expected lap time of under or over 30 minutes. Changing rooms and washing facilities are available, as is a kiosk that accepts payment via Vipps. Parking costs NOK 50 and is paid via Vipps. All participants receive a medal. The course can be walked before the start, but obstacles must not be tested. Timing and medals are provided. Start groups are divided by expected lap time: under or over 30 minutes. The prices found apply to 2027 registration on the page for the 2026 event.

name: Runfest
description: Runfest is an ambitious three-day road-running festival in Sandnes, the hometown of Olympic champion Jakob Ingebrigtsen. The festival will be held for the second time from 30 September to 2 October 2027, with race days on Friday 1 October and Saturday 2 October. Runfest combines elite competition with the joy of running and focuses on public health, physical activity and community. Participants of all ages and abilities are welcome to take part in a wide range of races and activities in beautiful surroundings.
course_highlights: Run in Sandnes, on the edge of Norway, with start locations suited to the 1500 m, 5 km, 10 km and 21 km distances
Aid stations with sports drink and water approximately every 5 km
Pacers available for several distances to help runners reach their goals
additional: Race numbers can be collected before and on race day; collecting them the day before is recommended to avoid queues. Changing facilities and bag storage are available at Thon Senter Sandnes. The official AfterRun, with a bar, street food, live concert and DJ, will be held on Saturday 3 October. Runfest Summit takes place on 30 September as a professional gathering focused on public health. Runfest Summit takes place on 30 September 2027. All finishers receive a medal.

name: Oslo Trail Challenge
description: Oslo Trail Challenge is a trail ultramarathon that takes place in the forest areas of Lillomarka, Nordmarka and Romeriksåsen, north of central Oslo. The race offers demanding and scenic trails suited to ultrarunners looking for a challenging experience in varied Norwegian forest terrain. The organizer, Langt og Lenge, has extensive experience with ultramarathons and offers a race focused on enjoying nature and the joy of running.
course_highlights: Trail ultramarathon in the forest areas of Lillomarka, Nordmarka and Romeriksåsen
Varied and demanding forest terrain north of central Oslo
Scenic trails with challenging sections
additional: Previous editions have used GPS navigation on unmarked courses.

name: Austevollsløpet
description: Austevollsløpet hosts a flexible relay for businesses, with up to five participants per team and a total course of approximately 21 km. The race runs from Kalve to Austevoll Sports Ground, and participants can divide the distance as they wish, making the relay accessible to many. The event creates a festive atmosphere, with spectators cheering along the course, and all participants receive a specially designed medal. Proceeds from the event go towards the athletics group’s activities and training camps in Austevoll.
course_highlights: A relay course of approximately 21 km from Kalve to Austevoll Sports Ground
Up to five participants per team, with flexible leg distribution
Spectators along the course with flags and music, and changeover points at food stations approximately every 5 km
additional: A bus leaves Austevoll Secondary School at 11:45 and stops at the changeover stations for drop-off and pick-up. All participants receive a medal. The event is supported by Austevoll Kraftlag as its main sponsor. Teams may have fewer than five participants if they wish. Distance options have varied between editions. In 2026, the business relay cost NOK 1,000 per team, and the Mini-Mini Marathon was free.

name: Tromsø Backyard Ultra
description: Tromsø Backyard Ultra is a unique Arctic ultrarun in the heart of Tromsø, where participants run a 6.7 km loop every hour. The race challenges endurance and tactics, as each loop must be completed within an hour to continue. It is suitable for all levels, whether you want to test your limits or take part in a social and motivating training session. The race takes place on Tromsdalen’s beautiful network of trails, mostly on gravel roads with some asphalt, offering a special experience in Northern Norwegian nature.
course_highlights: 6.7 km loop in Tromsdalen
The course is mostly on gravel roads, with some asphalt
Start/finish outside TUIL Arena in Tromsdalen
additional: Race bibs must be collected well before the race. Parking is available at Entrance A or Elvestrand Cemetery. Discounted accommodation may be available at Tromsø Lodge and Camping. Participants run one loop every hour and must be ready at the start line when the next loop begins. All starters receive a participant medal. The winners in the women’s and men’s categories are determined after 24 loops. Distances build up over the loops: 4 loops is approximately 26.8 km, 7 loops approximately 46.9 km, 12 loops approximately 80 km, and 15 loops approximately 100.6 km.

name: Nesbyen Backyard 2027
description: Nesbyen Backyard takes place on the first Saturday in October, featuring 6- and 12-hour Backyard Ultra races in beautiful Nesbyen, Hallingdal. The race offers a flat, fast 6.7 km loop that runs mainly on asphalt, with some sections on gravel and trail, challenging runners to complete one loop every hour. This unique race combines endurance, tactics and community in a social and motivating atmosphere, with prizes for everyone who completes the race and door prizes from local sponsors. The race starts at Nesbyen Sports Hall at 10:00 and is suitable for both beginners and experienced ultrarunners.
course_highlights: 6.7 km loop with less than 30 metres of elevation gain
The course runs mainly on asphalt, with some sections on gravel and trail
Flat, fast course through Nesbyen town centre amid beautiful autumn scenery
additional: Start and finish at Nesbyen Sports Hall, with changing rooms, showers, toilets and an indoor lounge. A kiosk with food and drinks is available. The race’s Backyard area serves as a social gathering place between loops. More than 20 door prizes from local sponsors. The train station is a 20-minute walk from the start area. The course is Norway’s flattest Backyard loop, with less than 30 metres of elevation gain. Accommodation is available along the course, including at Hagaled Guesthouse. Starts at Nesbyen Sports Hall on 2 October 2027 at 10:00. Registration via EQ Timing. Prices increase in stages as the registration deadline approaches. Prizes for everyone who completes at least one loop, as well as placement prizes and door prizes.

name: Perseløpet 5 km, 10 km, halvmaraton, maraton
description: Perseløpet is a race at Ås School in Eidsvoll, offering a simple and efficient race format focused on fast times. The course is a flat, measured 2,633-meter loop, with distances ranging from 3 km to 100 km. Participants can set up their own nutrition table, which they pass each lap, making it easy to manage nutrition in a personal way. The event offers good facilities, with race bib pickup, changing rooms and toilets inside the school, as well as free parking. Perseløpet is known as a race where many participants set personal records, and runners are encouraged to celebrate by ringing the bell at the finish area.
course_highlights: Flat, measured 2,633-meter loop
Your own nutrition table, passed each lap
Race from Ås School with facilities including changing rooms and toilets
additional: Race bibs are collected via self-service at the school approximately two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. At selected races, 9th graders from Feiring School staff an official drink station to raise money for their school trip. The weather forecast is updated four times daily using satellite data for the area around Ås School. The race has a lap-time calculator for planning split times. All distances take place in the same area and use the same weather forecast. Registration is via RaceDays. Race bibs are available for self-service pickup at the school from approximately two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. The course is AIMS-certified.

name: Steinkjer Skogsmaraton
description: Steinkjer Forest Marathon is a demanding trail race with a tough and challenging course featuring steep climbs and descents. The route follows the beautiful trails of Oftenåsen and gives participants a sense of achievement amid scenic surroundings. The start and finish are at Lerkehaug, by Steinkjer Shooting Range, where facilities include parking, bib collection and bag storage. At the venue, participants can enjoy campfire coffee and freshly made waffles while waiting for the start.
course_highlights: A tough and challenging trail course with steep climbs and descents
The route follows the beautiful trails of Oftenåsen through scenic surroundings
Start and finish at Steinkjer Shooting Range, with good facilities and a friendly atmosphere
additional: Participants can choose to race with or without timing in both distances. Bib collection and bag storage are available at the venue. Campfire coffee and freshly made waffles are sold by the fire. There is a water station on the course at Sagkorsen. Half-marathon runners complete two laps of the course, while quarter-marathon runners complete one lap. The start and finish are at Lerkehaug, by Steinkjer Shooting Range. Participants can choose to race with or without timing. The listed prices apply to previous editions and have not been confirmed for 2027.

name: RE-MILA 2027
description: RE-MILA is a fun run for all ages, starting and finishing in central Revetal. Distances include 600 metres for children, 2.5 km for youth, and 5 km and 10 km for adults and youth. The event has wave starts with pacers and follows Kondis’s recommended age-group categories. All participants receive a medal, and prizes are awarded to age-group winners and the top runners at each distance. Race numbers can be collected the day before or on race day in Revetal.
course_highlights: Start and finish in central Revetal, by the Sport1 store
Wave starts with up to 8 waves and pacers
Free parking in nearby parking garages and open-air parking spaces
additional: Race numbers can be collected at the Sport1 store in Revetal on the Saturday before the race from 12:00 to 15:00, or on race day from around 12:00. All participants in the children’s race receive a free T-shirt and medal. Wave starts are 15–30 seconds apart, with the fastest wave first. The official website states that all participants receive a medal. A free T-shirt is mentioned for children’s race participants. Details for the 2027 edition have not been confirmed in the sources.

name: Perseløpet ¤7 - 2027
description: Perseløpet is a simple and efficient running event at Ås school in Eidsvoll, designed to help runners achieve good times. The race takes place on a flat, officially measured 2,633-metre loop, with seven distances from 3 km to 100 km. Participants have their own nutrition table, which they pass each lap, giving them full control over their nutrition without the need to manage aid-station logistics. The event has a welcoming atmosphere, where personal records are celebrated by ringing the bell at the finish area. Perseløpet is organized by Feiring IL and attracts both recreational and competitive runners.
course_highlights: Flat, officially measured 2,633-metre loop
Your own nutrition table by the course for personal refuelling
Seven distances from 3 km to 100 km, with opportunities to achieve good times
additional: Race bibs are collected on a self-service basis at Ås school approximately two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. At selected races, ninth-grade students from Feiring school staff an official drinks station to raise money for their school trip. The event has a lap-time calculator to help plan split times. Weather forecasts and the course elevation profile are available via the website. Race bibs are collected on a self-service basis at the school from approximately two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. Registration is via RaceDays.

description: Bergensløpet celebrates an anniversary with a double running festival in beautiful surroundings in Bergen. The race starts and finishes in historic Nygårdsparken and runs along Store Lungegårdsvann, Fløen and Møllendal. Two distances are offered, 5 km and 10 km, both on a fast, officially measured course. A free children's race is also held for children up to 11 years old, with a medal for every participant.
course_highlights: Start and finish in historic Nygårdsparken
The course runs along Store Lungegårdsvann, Fløen and Møllendal
Fast, officially measured 5 km course; the 10 km runners complete two laps
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 09:45 at Vitalitetssenteret by Møhlenpris sports ground. Toilets are available at the collection point and in the clubhouses. The children's race starts at 12:00, the 5 km at 13:00, and the 10 km at 14:00. The children's race is approximately 500 metres, free, and has no timing or rankings; all children receive a medal. The autumn edition is listed as taking place on Saturday, 10 October. The date for the 2027 edition matches the race date of 9 October in the listing.

name: Flisa Backyard
description: Flisa Backyard is a friendly autumn event held at beautiful Myrmoen in Flisa. The race welcomes everyone who wants to challenge themselves, test their fitness or simply enjoy a fantastic day in beautiful surroundings. The event is open to everyone born in 2013 or earlier and offers an inclusive, magical atmosphere. The race is organised by Flisa Allianseidrettslag, which has a long tradition as a sports club in the area.
course_highlights: The race takes place at beautiful Myrmoen in scenic surroundings
Open to everyone born in 2013 or earlier
One of the autumn’s friendliest events, with an inclusive atmosphere
additional: Everyone born in 2013 or earlier may participate. The event is organised by Flisa Allianseidrettslag, which has used Rubic as its membership system. Registration is via racetracker.no. Flisa Backyard is an inclusive, social race in the scenic surroundings of Myrmoen. The listed registration price is 450 kr, increasing to 550 kr from 18 January, 650 kr from 1 April and 750 kr from 1 August. Registration includes a choice of single-event or annual licence, and camping can be reserved.

name: Gausta Challenge
location: Gausta Fjellresort, Gausta, Tinn, Telemark, Norway
organizer: Rjukan IL – Friidrett & Triathlon og Gaustablikk Fjellresort
description: Gausta Challenge is a low-key race held on Saturday, October 9, 2027, at Gausta Fjellresort. The race runs around Kvitåvatn on an approximately 6 km gravel road, starting and finishing by the paddle tennis courts. The race is suitable for all ages and levels, with wave starts and timing, and participants can run, walk, or take it easy. The event is a collaboration between Rjukan IL - Friidrett & Triathlon and Gaustablikk Fjellresort, and aims to promote physical activity in beautiful autumn surroundings.
course_highlights: Approximately 6 km gravel course around Kvitåvatn
Start and finish at Gausta Fjellresort, by the paddle tennis courts
The course is hilly, with a long downhill section and flat stretches
additional: Wave starts with timing. The children’s race for ages 0–10 starts at 14:00. The 6 km race is open to participants aged 10 to 99. The start and finish are by the paddle tennis courts near the floating saunas. The course is run counterclockwise. Gausta Challenge 2027 takes place on Saturday, October 9, at 13:00. The children’s race starts at 14:00. The 6 km course is for participants aged 10 and over.

name: Fredrikstadmarka Rundt 2027
description: Fredrikstadmarka Rundt is a traditional forest race that has been held since 1974. The course is 20 km long and is considered one of the true classics among Norwegian forest races, with a runnable route featuring pleasant trail sections and good gravel roads. The start and finish are at FIF-huset in Fredrikstad, and the course includes both flat terrain and some steep climbs, especially in the final section toward Skihytta. A shorter distance called Markatier'n is also held, using the same start and finish area and sharing the 20 km route for the first 5.5 km.
course_highlights: 20 km forest race on a runnable route of trails and gravel roads
Three drink stations along the route at approximately 5.5 km, 10 km, and 14 km
Steep climbs and challenging terrain, especially between 9 and 14 km
additional: There are 3 drink stations with water and cordial along the route, as well as drinks at the finish. The start and finish are at FIF-huset, Ilaveien 132, Fredrikstad. Markatier'n is a shorter distance that uses the same start and finish area and shares the 20 km route for the first 5.5 km. The course has remained largely unchanged since 1974. Course records are 1:07:08 for men and 1:16:17 for women. The start and finish are at FIF-huset at Ilaveien 132, Fredrikstad. Registration and results services are stated to be provided in cooperation with EQ Timing.

name: Rosa Sløyfe-løpet Kristiansand
organizer: Kreftforeningen og Brystkreftforeningen, i samarbeid med Springtime Group

description: The Pink Ribbon Run in Kristiansand is an annual event held to support the breast cancer cause. The run starts and finishes at Aquarama in the city centre, and the course passes through beautiful areas around Kristiansand. Participants can choose between a short course of approximately 3.4 km or a long course of approximately 5.5 km. There is also a separate children’s race for children aged 3 to 9. All participants receive a race pack with a bib, neck warmer, bag and medal, and the event brings together thousands of people in a sea of pink for a good cause.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Aquarama in central Kristiansand
Short course of approx. 3.4 km without timing
Long course of approx. 5.5 km with timing
additional: The race pack includes a bib, neck warmer, bag and medal. The Mini children’s race is free and approximately 400 metres long, with activities in the start area. The short course is untimed, while the long course is timed. Race numbers can be collected in the start area from 2 hours before the start, or in advance to avoid queues. Participants in the short and long courses are insured through a licence with the Norwegian Athletics Association, which also supports the cause. Companies can register using separate registration forms and manage participants through My Page. The race pack contains a bib, neck warmer, bag and medal. NOK 250 of the race entry fee goes in full to the Pink Ribbon campaign.

name: Ivar Formos Minneløp 2027
description: Ivar Formos Minneløp is a traditional cross-country race in Oslo, offering scenic and challenging courses in Nordmarka. The race has distances for both children and adults, including a tough 17 km course that follows the terrain where Ivar Formo trained to become an Olympic champion. The start and finish are at Sognsvann Snøpark, and the courses feature beautiful trails, panoramic views of the city, and several aid stations along the way. The event is a sweaty pleasure for everyone who enjoys running in the forest, with a new 10 km course that is undulating and challenging without steep climbs or descents.
course_highlights: 17 km course starting and finishing at Sognsvann Snøpark, with panoramic views of Oslo from Vettakollen and Frønsvollen
The course passes well-known places such as Båntjern, Skjennungstua, Ullevålseter, and Lynhytta, with aid stations
New 10 km course on beautiful forest trails, with challenging, undulating terrain and no steep hills
additional: Start and finish at Sognsvann Snøpark. Timing chip included in the race bib, except for the children's race, which is untimed. Late registration is available on race day via the EQ Timing app. Registration is binding, with no refunds in case of illness or injury. Race bibs can be resold via EQ Timing. No T-shirts will be sold in 2027 due to low interest. In 2027, the race will be held for the 15th time. Late registration is available on race day via the EQ Timing app. The timing chip is included in the race bib, and the children's race is untimed. Registration is binding, and a one-off licence from the Norwegian Athletics Federation is required if you do not have an annual licence.

name: Volda Bakgårdsultra 2027
description: Volda Bakgårdsultra is a social and inclusive ultramarathon based on the backyard ultra concept, where participants run 12 laps of 6.7 km, with a new start every hour on the hour. The race starts in the SpareBank 1 Hall at Volda Stadium and is suitable for all levels, from those who want to complete one lap to those aiming to finish the classic ultra distance of 50 miles (80.4 km). The event has been a success since 2025 and offers a unique running experience focused on community and personal challenge. Between laps, participants can rest in the hall, with access to a drop bag area and kiosk. Registration for 2027 opens on 16 January at 20:00 via EQ Timing.
course_highlights: 12 laps of 6.7 km, with a start every hour on the hour
The course is mostly gravel road with little elevation gain
Start and finish in the SpareBank 1 Hall, with access to a rest area and drop bag area
additional: The race has a basic aid station with water, sports drinks, fruit and salty snacks. Participants can also bring their own food and drinks and set up personal drop bags by the start/finish area. Free parking is available at Volda Stadium, and Volda town centre is within walking distance of the venue. Volda Airport Hovden is a 10-minute drive away. The hall has a kiosk selling coffee, soft drinks, chocolate and other light refreshments. Participants must have a valid licence from the Norwegian Athletics Federation or purchase a one-day licence when registering. The provisional date is 16 October 2027, with a start at 08:00. Registration has not opened yet; the final date and registration information are to be confirmed in January 2027.

name: Furumomila 2027
description: Furumomila is a traditional cross-country race held for the 44th time at Furumo Idrettspark. The event offers several distances, including a 10 km cross-country race, MiniMil, a recreational walk and SpareBank1 Modum’s cross-country race. Participants can look forward to generous cash prizes, gift cards, medals and pins. This autumn adventure welcomes both recreational runners and competitive athletes.
course_highlights: 10 km cross-country race over varied terrain
Several distances: 10 km, 5 km, 1.5 km, MiniMil and a recreational walk
Start and finish at Furumo Idrettspark
additional: Race numbers can be collected in the tent by the clubhouse before the start. Showers and changing rooms are available. Parking and a shuttle bus are provided. Prizes are awarded shortly after the finish for the various distances. A one-time licence is required for those without an annual licence, in accordance with the rules of the Norwegian Athletics Federation. Previous editions have distributed race numbers by the clubhouse. Distances and practical information for 2027 have not been confirmed.

name: Hytteplanmila
description: Hytteplanmila is an annual fun run held at Svensrudmoen in October. The race features a fast, gently undulating 10-kilometre course, known as one of Norway’s fastest 10K road race routes. Participants can experience a varied course with both easy and challenging sections, including a demanding finish on Pulsbakken. The event attracts both recreational runners and elite athletes, with separate start groups for the elite field.
course_highlights: Fast, gently undulating 10-kilometre course
The race’s challenging finish on Pulsbakken
Great views over Steinssletta and historic sites such as Mo gård
additional: Registration opens in November. Entry fees are non-refundable and cannot be transferred. Those who register by the deadlines receive a buff and running socks, distributed on race day. It is possible to pre-order a race pack with energy products. Elite athletes can register by email for separate start groups. Buses to the race are arranged from Oslo and Gardermoen. The time limit is 1 hour and 40 minutes. Registration for 2027 opens in November; information about the entry fee has not yet been published.

name: Gjesdal Trailrun
location: Gjesdal IL athletics facility, Solås, Ålgård, Gjesdal, Norway

description: Gjesdal Trailrun is a true trail race held in beautiful natural surroundings in Ålgård, starting from Gjesdal IL’s athletics facility at Solås. The race mainly follows trails in the terrain northeast of the facility, climbing Kodlifjellet and Håfjellet. It suits both those looking for an enjoyable mountain hike and those who want to compete. Three distances are offered: 10 km, 6 km, and a 1.3 km children’s race. The course follows regular hiking trails that can be challenging, with rocky and slippery sections, so good trail shoes are recommended.
course_highlights: Trail race on paths in the terrain northeast of Gjesdal IL’s athletics facility
The main course climbs Kodlifjellet and Håfjellet
Challenging sections with rocks and slippery areas
additional: Race bib collection opens at 10:00 at the Gjesdal IL clubhouse. The children’s race starts at 11:30. Both timed and untimed starts are available for the 6 km and 10 km distances. The 10 km has a time limit, with participants required to pass Kodlifjellet within approximately 35 minutes and the junction between the 6 km and 10 km courses within 40 minutes. The online registration fee of NOK 20, plus any NFIF one-time licence, is additional. Previous editions have featured 10 km, 6 km, and a 1 km children’s race. Good trail shoes with good grip are recommended. The 2027 distances have not been confirmed in the sources.

name: Neskollen Frontyard 2027

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: inkludert servering av snacks, drikke, frukt og pizza

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Barneløp med inntil 5 runder rundt tjernet

description: Neskollen Frontyard 2027 is a unique race organized by Hvam IL, where participants run 3 km laps that must be completed faster and faster. The race combines competition with a family-friendly, social atmosphere, with indoor breaks at Nes Arena where snacks, drinks, fruit, and pizza are served, included in the price. Frontyard challenges both running capacity and tactics, and prizes are awarded to the best woman, the best man, and the fastest overall time after 15 laps. The start and finish are at Nes Arena, with convenient facilities such as toilets and parking right outside.
course_highlights: 3 km laps that must be run faster with each lap
Start and finish at Nes Arena, with indoor breaks
The course consists of approximately 700 meters of gravel, with the rest on asphalt
additional: Snacks, drinks, fruit, and pizza are included in the price. The start, finish, and breaks are indoors at Nes Arena, with 12 toilets and parking right outside. The course consists of approximately 700 meters of gravel, with the rest on asphalt. Remember to wear your race bib visibly on the outside of your clothing. The children's race starts at approximately 10:01. Previous editions have served snacks, drinks, fruit, and pizza during breaks at Nes Arena.

name: Necon Vinterkarusell 27-28 løp 1 (18. okt)
description: Necon Winter Series is a winter running series consisting of 8 races held at Fana Stadium in Bergen from November to April. The races have a mass start and offer two distances, 5 km and 10 km. Participants can choose their distance during the race at the turnaround point. The start and finish are at Fana Stadium, and the races follow varied terrain, with intermediate times available along the way. The series is suitable for both recreational and experienced runners looking for a social and challenging winter series.
course_highlights: Mass start for the 5 km and 10 km, with the option to choose a distance during the race
The course starts at Fana Stadium, with turnarounds at Sandsli and Plantasjen in Kokstad
Intermediate times are recorded at 2.5 km, 5 km and 7.5 km for the different distances
additional: Start and finish at Fana Stadium from 18:45. Start waves are based on expected finish times to avoid crossing Grimseidvegen. Wave 0 starts at 18:45 for 10 km runners expecting to finish in over 55 min. Wave 1 starts at 19:00 for 5 km runners expecting to finish in under 22:30 min and 10 km runners expecting to finish in under 45 min. Waves 2–4 start at 2-minute intervals, based on expected finish times. Participants register for the 5 km when signing up; the distance is chosen automatically during the race at the turnaround point.

name: Rosa Sløyfe-løpet Oslo lørdag
organizer: Kreftforeningen og Brystkreftforeningen, i samarbeid med Springtime Group
price_range: 500 kr + 30 kr i administrasjonsgebyr og 3 % transaksjonsgebyr; Mini er gratis

description: Rosa Sløyfe-løpet Oslo is an annual race held in support of the Pink Ribbon campaign. On Saturday, the event offers a short untimed course from Nedre Foss gård to Nydalen. On Sunday, participants can choose between timed 5 km and 10 km races, starting and finishing at Rådhusplassen. The course passes through some of Oslo’s most iconic areas, including Aker Brygge, Tjuvholmen and Akershus Fortress, offering an urban and atmospheric experience. The event is for everyone, whether you want to race for a time, run with colleagues or simply be part of the sea of pink.
course_highlights: Course through Aker Brygge, Tjuvholmen and Akershus Fortress
Start and finish at Rådhusplassen in central Oslo
Urban, atmospheric course with beautiful views
additional: Saturday’s short course is untimed and suitable for anyone looking for a more relaxed experience. The race packet includes a race bib, neck warmer, bag and medal. Pacers will be available for Sunday’s 5 km and 10 km races at different paces to help participants maintain a steady speed. Race bibs can be collected in advance or from two hours before the start on race day. Participants are insured through a licence provided by the Norwegian Athletics Federation, and half of the entry fee goes directly to the Pink Ribbon campaign. Timing is available for the 5 km and 10 km. The free Mini Run, approximately 400 metres, is for children aged 3 to 9. The participant package includes a race bib, neck warmer, bag and medal.

name: Bergen Maraton- Maratonkarusellen
organizer: Maratonkarusellen i samarbeid med BFG Bergen Løpeklubb

description: Bergen Marathon will be held for the 40th time on Saturday, October 23, 2027, with the start and finish at Fana Stadium in Bergen. The race is part of Maratonkarusellen, which offers both full and half marathons, and aims to ensure that all participants enjoy themselves despite the challenges of the race. Maratonkarusellen works with BFG Bergen Running Club and places great emphasis on the quality of its events. The minimum age for the marathon is 18.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Fana Stadium
Events include both full and half marathons
Organized in collaboration with BFG Bergen Running Club
additional: Kondis members receive a NOK 50 discount. A year-round license from the Norwegian Athletics Federation can be provided to avoid the one-time license fee. Participants without a license must purchase a one-time license. The minimum age for the marathon is 18. The event offers a half marathon and a marathon. The minimum age for the marathon is 18. Listed prices apply to the 2026 edition and may change before the 2027 race.

name: Backyard Sandefjord Ultra

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Backyard Deltakere kr 750,00 + Adm. gebyr (25 NOK + 3% transaksjonsgebyr)

description: Backyard Sandefjord is a unique ultrarun being held for the 14th time in 2027. The race consists of a gently rolling loop of approximately 6.7 km, run on the hour every hour, with a maximum of 12 loops in total. Participants must start each loop to continue, and the last runner to start the final loop is declared the winner. The event has a social atmosphere and a low barrier to entry, with facilities including snacks, hot drinks and places to rest in the hall. Everyone who completes 12 loops receives a cup, and those who reach the ultradistance receive a Norwegian-made wooden medal.
course_highlights: Gently rolling loop of approx. 6.7 km
The course is marked with yellow arrow signs, red marker flags and white arrows on asphalt
Maximum of 12 loops, totalling 80.4 km if completed
additional: Bringing your own cup, headlamp and reflective vest is mandatory. Bib collection is Friday 17:00–18:30 and Saturday 08:30–09:30. Support is allowed outdoors only. Snacks, coffee, sweet tea, broth, cold/hot water and hot dogs are offered after the 7th loop. Participants must bring their own chair; there is no room for sun loungers. Enter through the large gate at the back of the hall; parking is available. Start and finish at Runarhallen, Klavenesveien 20. Maximum 350 participants. Bringing your own cup, headlamp and reflective vest is mandatory. Snacks, coffee, sweet tea, broth and water are offered.

name: Fredrikstad Multiconsult Maraton 2027
description: The Fredrikstad Multiconsult Marathon takes place in Fredrikstad and consists of three identical 14 km laps, followed by an extra 195-metre finishing section so that the kilometre markers are in the same place on each lap. The course starts and finishes at FIF-huset and includes asphalt, gravel and forest roads in Fredrikstadmarka. There are aid stations along the route with water, squash and sports drink, as well as cola and bananas on the final laps. The race has been held since 2001 and offers a varied, scenic course with marshals at important intersections.
course_highlights: The course consists of three 14 km laps, plus an extra 195 metres to ensure the kilometre markers are in the same place on each lap
The first half is on asphalt; the rest is on gravel and forest roads in Fredrikstadmarka
Three aid stations per lap with a range of drinks and food
additional: An early start at 10:00 is available for runners who expect to take more than 5 hours. The race office and bib collection open at 09:00 on race day at FIF-huset. Parking is at Stjernehallen, about a 5-minute walk from the start/finish. Changing rooms and toilets are available at FIF-huset. There are no pacers during the race. Online registration is open until 1 hour before the start. There are three aid stations per lap. The race office, changing rooms and toilets are at FIF-huset; parking is at Stjernehallen.

name: Snipsøyrvatnet Rundt
price_range: 100–200 kr, i tillegg til eingongslisens for dei utan heilårslisens

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Startavgift: 200kr for senior (født på eller før 31.12.2005)

description: Snipsøyrvatnet Rundt is one of Sunnmøre’s most traditional recreational races, organised by Hareid IL. The race goes around Snipsøyrvatnet, starting at Ward1 in Bjåstad, and marks the beginning of the autumn season. Participants register at Hareid Clubhouse before the race and can warm up with a 3 km jog to the start area. The race is open to both seniors and juniors, with a friendly and inclusive atmosphere.
course_highlights: The race goes around Snipsøyrvatnet
Start and finish at Ward1 in Bjåstad
A 3 km warm-up jog from registration to the start
additional: Registration takes place at Hareid Clubhouse from 12:00 to 13:45. Participants must make their own way from registration to the start area, either with a 3 km warm-up jog or by car. Changing facilities are available at Hareid Clubhouse. A one-time licence from the Norwegian Athletics Federation is an additional cost for those without an annual licence for road running. Parking is available at Ward1, Bigset Bedehus or Kulturoasen. Start time is 14:00; participants must make their own way approximately 3 km from registration to the start.

name: Ottestad løpsfestival
description: Ottestad Running Festival is organized by Ottestad Idrettslag and consists of three races: HOKA Ottestad Rundt over 17 kilometers, the Spenst Run over 5 kilometers, and the Sport1 Sprint for children, with distances of 400 meters, 1 km, and 1.8 km. The race starts and finishes at Ottestad Idrettspark, which has excellent facilities, including a café, refreshments, changing rooms, and showers. The course follows Ottestadstien, a scenic hiking trail through a cultural landscape of wooded areas and farmland, with beautiful views of Mjøsa. The event is family-friendly and offers both timed and recreational races.
course_highlights: The course follows Ottestadstien through a cultural landscape of wooded areas and farmland
Fantastic views of Mjøsa during the race
Start and finish at Ottestad Idrettspark, with a café and changing-room facilities
additional: The HOKA Sprint is a separate 430-meter segment on the 17 km course where participants can compete to be the fastest on Strava and win HOKA shoes. The segment has its own refreshment station, music, and spectators. A one-time race license is an additional cost for those without an annual license, and athletes up to age 12 are covered by NIF's child sports insurance. The 5 km and 17 km races can be run with or without timing. Listed prices apply to 2026, and a one-time race license is an additional cost where applicable.

name: Norgestesten 2027 3
description: Norgestesten is an efficient and inclusive running event held at Jessheim Athletics Stadium. The event offers distances ranging from an 800-metre children’s race to a half marathon, all with a mass start on a flat, fast 3,146-metre loop course. Many experienced pacers help participants find the right pace, and the event emphasizes convenient logistics, with parking and the train station nearby. Proceeds support sports for children and young people, and race bibs can be collected via self-service from 09:00 on race day.
course_highlights: Flat 3,146-metre loop course
Mass start for all distances
Many experienced pacers available
additional: The children’s race starts at 09:30 and is approximately 800 metres. Race bibs can be collected via self-service from 09:00 in the start area. Toilets are available at Jessheim Athletics Stadium and in the ice rink and multipurpose hall. A table for participants’ own drinks is provided at the start, along with water and sports drink along the course. The half-marathon cut-off is 2 hours and 30 minutes. The race is organized by volunteers, and proceeds support sports for children and young people. Information about dates and distances relates to different editions; the 2027 edition has not been confirmed in the sources.

name: Perseløpet 5 km, 10 km, halvmaraton
description: Perseløpet is a race focused on fast times, held at Ås school in Eidsvoll. The race takes place on a flat, accurately measured 2,633-metre loop, where participants can set out their own bottles and gels on their personal nutrition table. Seven distances are offered, from 3 km to 100 km, including 5 km, 10 km and the half marathon. Race numbers are collected from a self-service station at the school, and the venue has good facilities, including changing rooms, toilets and free parking. The race has a friendly atmosphere, with personal records celebrated by the ringing of a bell at the finish area.
course_highlights: Flat, accurately measured 2,633-metre loop
Participants’ own nutrition tables along the course
Good venue facilities, including changing rooms, toilets and free parking
additional: Race numbers are collected from a self-service station about two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. The race uses a lap-time calculator to plan split times. At selected races, the 9th grade class at Feiring school staffs an official drinks station to raise money for their school trip. The weather forecast is updated four times a day using satellite data for the area around Ås school. Public transport to the venue is available by train and bus, with real-time departures. Race numbers are collected from a self-service station at the school from about two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. Registration is through RaceDays.

name: HA Ottestad løpsfestival 2027
description: HA Ottestad Running Festival is an annual event held at Ottestad Idrettspark, with the start and finish in the same place. The festival consists of three races: HOKA Ottestad Rundt (17 km), the Spenst Race (5 km), and the Sport1 Sprint for children, with distances of 400 m, 1 km, and 1.8 km. The course follows Ottestadstien, a scenic walking trail winding through a cultural landscape of wooded areas and farmland, with splendid views over Lake Mjøsa. The event offers good facilities, including a café, food and refreshments, changing rooms, and showers in the clubhouse.
course_highlights: The course follows Ottestadstien through a cultural landscape of woodland and farmland
Fantastic views over Lake Mjøsa
Start and finish at Ottestad Idrettspark, with good facilities
additional: The HOKA Sprint is a separate 430 m segment on the 17 km course where participants can compete to be the fastest on Strava and win HOKA shoes. There is music, spectators, and a dedicated drinks station at the sprint segment. A one-day race license is an additional cost for those who do not have an annual license. Athletes up to age 12 are covered by NIF’s child sports insurance. The festival features HOKA Ottestad Rundt (17 km), the Spenst Race (5 km), and the Sport1 Sprint for children. The 17 km and 5 km races can be run with or without timing. The start and finish are at Ottestad Idrettspark, which has a café, food and refreshments, and changing rooms with showers.

name: MartinCrossen Trail Run
description: MartinCrossen Trail Run is a trail race starting and finishing at Voksenjordet in Oslo, inspired by the Martincrossen ski race and Martin Johnsrud Sundby. The race offers a unique course with challenging technical terrain, particularly on the longest distance, which ends with a tough finish. The event takes place in the evening in November, and the darkness and use of headlamps on the 3 km and 8 km distances make for a special experience. The race is inclusive, with categories for children, young people, para athletes, recreational runners and competitive runners. There will also be a show with pyrotechnics, flames, lights and music in the spirit of Martincrossen.
course_highlights: Trail running on challenging technical terrain
Start and finish at Voksenjordet
Evening race, with headlamps required on the 3 km and 8 km distances
additional: The 500-metre children’s race for ages 3–5 and the para category are free and do not require registration. Companions for para participants are free; contact mari@roail.no. Medals for all participants. A show with pyrotechnics, flames, lights and music. A limited number of race bibs are available for late registration, which opens on 2 November at 12:00. The sources describe the 2026 edition, listed as taking place on 4 November 2026, and do not confirm the date or registration details for 2027.

location: Espeland idrettsplass, Espeland, Arna, Bergen, Norway

description: Frikarusellen 2026/27 takes place at Espeland sports grounds in Arna and consists of six races on a certified 5 km course. The course starts north of Londalskrysset, runs via Gamle Haukeland station and returns along the same route, finishing inside the sports grounds. The races are suitable for both young people and adults, with separate prices for members and age groups. The event has a long tradition and offers easy registration through EQ Timing, with race bibs distributed on race day.
course_highlights: Certified 5 km course (first measured in 2000, revised in 2018)
Starts north of Londalskrysset and returns via Gamle Haukeland station
Finishes inside Espeland sports grounds
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Espelandshallen on race day between 18:00 and 18:55. Registration is open until 18:55 on race day. A licence fee is additional for participants over 13 without an annual licence. There is a fee of NOK 50 for forgetting your race bib if you have registered for all the races. Results are published at www.eqtiming.no. The series consists of six races: 14.10.2026, 04.11.2026, 25.11.2026, 27.01.2027, 17.02.2027 and 10.03.2027. Registration is open until 18:55 on race day; race bibs can be collected at Espelandshallen from 18:00 to 18:55. A licence fee is additional for participants over 13 without an annual licence.

name: Ledlenser Nightrun Bergen
location: Fløysletten, Fløibanen Upper Station, Bergen, Norway
description: Ledlenser Nightrun Bergen is a unique trail race held in the dark, where all participants run with headlamps. The race offers an exciting experience along Bergen’s forest trails at night, with reflective markers along the course to help runners. Separate men’s and women’s categories are held across several age groups, and all participants receive a medal. The race has a sociable atmosphere, with luggage storage available and prizes for the top finishers.
course_highlights: Trail race through dark forest trails
The course is marked with reflective markers
Headlamps are required
additional: Ledlenser provides a limited number of headlamps for testing and loan during the race, available on a first-come, first-served basis. Self-service luggage storage is available in the start area. There are separate men’s and women’s categories for ages under 25, 25–39, 40–54, and over 55. All participants receive a medal and can enter a draw for spot prizes. A headlamp is required; reflective markers along the course help you find your way. Race numbers can be collected at Löplabbet Bergen, Strandkaien 6, November 1–3, 10:00–19:00, or at the race venue from 17:00 on race day. Self-service luggage storage is available in the start area.

name: Nightrun Oslo
description: Ledlenser Nightrun Oslo is an exciting night race held at the Norwegian School of Sport Sciences at Sognsvann. The race offers an atmospheric experience, with headlamps lighting the trail and reflectors along the course helping participants find their way to the finish. There are separate men’s and women’s categories in several age groups, and all participants receive a medal and the chance to win great prize-draw prizes. The event has a friendly social atmosphere, with self-service baggage storage and awards for the top runners.
course_highlights: The course passes through scenic surroundings at Sognsvann
Headlamps light the trail in the dark
Reflectors along the course provide visibility and help runners find their way
additional: Ledlenser provides a limited number of headlamps for testing and borrowing during the race, on a first-come, first-served basis. Self-service baggage storage is available in the start area, and the baggage tag from your race bib must be attached to your bag. There are separate men’s and women’s categories for the age groups under 25, 25–39, 40–54 and over 55. The top three men and women overall receive prizes. The start and finish are at the Norwegian School of Sport Sciences at Sognsvann. Race bibs can be collected at Löplabbet Oslo, Pilestredet 7, or at the race venue on race day. All participants receive a medal, and a limited number of headlamps are available to borrow.

name: Samnanger Vinterkarusell - 1. løp
description: Samnanger Winter Series is a social and inclusive running series organised by Samnanger IL Running Group, with races held approximately every other Friday at Nesodden throughout the winter. Participants can choose between 2 km and 5 km courses, with the 5 km course officially measured by NFIF. The races suit all levels, from beginners to experienced runners, and focus on the joy of running and community. The start and finish are at Nesodden, and participants are encouraged to wear reflective gear because of the winter darkness. The Winter Series is a great opportunity to stay in shape and take part in a welcoming running community.
course_highlights: Race at Nesodden, with the start and finish at the same place
Choose between 2 km and 5 km courses; the 5 km course is officially measured by NFIF
Races are held approximately every other Friday during the winter at 19:00
additional: The running group is informal, free, and open to all levels. Wearing a reflective vest is recommended because of the winter darkness. The Winter Series is held approximately every other Friday at 19:00 at Nesodden.

name: Renna Rundt Borredalen
description: The race has the same start and finish as Borredalen Rundt. A few hundred metres from the start are on a gravel road, before the rest of the course continues on a trail. There is a steep, uneven hill after the gravel-road section, followed by relatively flat terrain, apart from the downhill stretch towards the finish.

Løpere klare for start i et terrengløp. En mann med megafon foran en gruppe løpere.
Løpere i vinterlandskap.
Løpere i snødekt terreng, muligens ved start eller mål for et terrengløp i Borredalen.

name: Lierløpet 14
description: Lierløpet is one of Norway’s fastest courses. The race takes place on a wide path that is popular with runners and recreational athletes in the Drammen area. It offers 5K, 10K, and half-marathon distances, making it accessible to both experienced runners and beginners.

images.alt_text: Løpere i Lierløpet 14 på gangvei, med startnummer og sponsorer langs løypen.
Løpere på sti i skogen.
Lier stasjon, mål for Lierløpet 14. Togstasjon med perrong, spor og tunnel.
Kart over løypen for Lierløpet 14, med start- og målpunkter og avstander.

name: Barfrostløpet
description: Barfrostløpet on 7 November 2026 offers three distances: 1,500 m, 5,000 m and 10,000 m, as well as a 4.3 km fun run, Run4Fun. The start and finish for all distances are outside Tanabru kindergarten, opposite the health centre, on marked, paved routes in central Tanabru. Age limits apply to the different competition classes, with participants ranging from 4 to 85 years old. Changing rooms will be open at Tana multipurpose hall. Food will be served, and there will be a season-opening chat after the race at Tanabru school, near the multipurpose hall.

images.alt_text: Luftfoto av elv og bro i Tanabru, muligens løypa for Barfrostløpet.

Løper i Barfrostløpet, iført startnummer 181, på en snødekt vei.

name: 3-Sjøersløpet
description: 3-Sjøersløpet is one of Norway’s most enjoyable events to take part in, and takes place in Stavanger with 5,200 participants. The course is varied and beautiful, offering a great sightseeing experience of some of the best Stavanger has to offer. Follow one of our skilled pacers, who will help you maintain the right pace along the way, and experience the excitement of the crowds, flags, and music along the course.

description: Ålesund Winter Series consists of 5 races throughout the winter, starting at 14:00 from BestDrive in Fremmerholen every other Saturday from November to March. The first race in the 2025/2026 Winter Series takes place on Saturday, 8 November 2025. Participants can choose between two distances, 5 and 10 km, on accurately measured courses heading inland through Brusdalen. The 5 km distance also has a non-timed recreational class, and there is little car traffic on Gamle Brusdals veg.

name: Refleksløpet Kristiansand
description: The Reflective Run in Kristiansand invites you to a magical evening run with headlamps on Thursday, November 13. The start and finish are at Fant Olsen in Baneheia, with registration opening at 16:30. Participants can start from 17:00, while the mass start with timing is at 18:00. The course is 4.1 km long and follows the outer edge of Baneheia, marked with reflective markers. Participants must bring a headlamp, and mulled juice and porridge will be served after the finish.

name: Fagerstrand Backyard Ultra Maraton
description: Fagerstrand Backyard Ultra Marathon 2026 is organized by Fagerstrand IF at Myklerud, Fagerstrand. This unique race starts on Saturday, November 7 at 09:00 and follows a simple but demanding format: a new 6.7 km lap starts every hour. The race continues on a “last man standing” basis until only one runner remains, or is decided on lap 12 if several runners are still competing. Participants can choose their strategy: run fast for a longer break or take it easier to conserve energy. There will be a banquet for runners and their companions.

A service fee of NOK 15 per ticket is added at checkout (maximum NOK 30 per order). Race starts at 09:00, with doors opening at 08:00. Limited number of tickets. Banquet ticket sold separately.

description: Grimstadvatnet Rundt is a 7.8 km road race run mainly on asphalt, with a relatively flat course. The race is part of the Hareid Winter Series, which consists of four races held on the first Saturday in November, December, January and February. The first race in the series was held in 1981, and awards are presented after the fourth and final race in February. To qualify for an award, runners must complete at least three of the four races. Scores are based on the three best races, with bonus points for completing all four.
course_highlights: 7.8 km road race, mainly on asphalt
Relatively flat course
Part of the Hareid Winter Series, with four races
additional: Registration takes place at Hareid clubhouse from 13:00 on race day. Changing facilities are available at the clubhouse. A one-time Norwegian Athletics Federation licence is required for races outside a track if you do not have an annual licence. The race starts at 14:00 at Hareid clubhouse, with registration from 13:00. The series consists of four races, and an award requires participation in at least three.

name: Refleksløpet Arendal, Fossbekk
description: Welcome to the Refleksløpet in Arendal, an atmospheric race in the dark held at Fossbekk in Arendal. The race offers two distances: a short 4.8 km course and a long 7.8 km course, as well as the option to walk without timing. The race starts early in the evening, and participants are encouraged to wear a headlamp for a safe and magical experience. This is a social event where friends, family and running buddies can get together for a fun and active evening.
course_highlights: Two distances: a 4.8 km short course and a 7.8 km long course
The race takes place in the dark, so a headlamp is recommended
Start at the Fossbekk parking area, a scenic location between Krøgenes and Longum
additional: The race office opens at 16:30 for registration and bib collection. The long course starts at 18:00, the short course at 18:05, and walkers without timing can start at 17:00. The first 30 people to register will have the chance to win a Mizuno bag. Registering before race day is recommended to avoid stress. Participants receive a 15% discount on headlamps at Brekke sport's physical store. The long course starts at 18:00 and the short course at 18:05. Walkers without timing can start at 17:00. The race office opens at 16:30, and a headlamp is recommended.
